sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: The header comment warning that the VZ_MBLibrary @require must be rewritten before publishing no longer hardcodes which library versions changed the settings dialog (it named only 4.1.0/4.2.0 and had already gone stale against 4.3.0). It now describes this as an ongoing pattern instead, so it stays accurate across future library bumps without needing another edit.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: An ISRC segment entry in the 📊 dropdown ("» country: QM" and the registrant/year/designation entries) that exists only inside a COLLAPSED list item now carries a ▶ marker and a tooltip saying so. Such entries are still offered — ticking one still shows the row and tints the ▶ toggle — the marker just explains why nothing on screen shows the code yet. Expanding the cell drops the marker — `_isCollapsedHiddenItem()`, `collapsedOnlyKeys`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Ticking an ISRC segment entry ("» country: GB", registrant, year, designation) filtered correctly but marked nothing. `initIsrcFormatting()` ran after the highlight and rebuilt every `<code>`, wiping the mark, and on a multi-table page the highlight ran on an unformatted clone with no segment spans to scope to. `_formatIsrcAnchor()` is now idempotent (an already-formatted `<code>` is left alone) and `_formatIsrcAnchorsIn()` formats a clone before it is matched.
"» year: 2005" could never mark anything: the entry value is the 4-digit year but the cell displays the 2-digit "05". The highlighter now marks the displayed segment.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Ticking "valid ISWC format" (and, the same omission, "valid ISRC format" and "valid barcode format") narrowed the rows but highlighted nothing — only the invalid flags had a highlighter. Added `_highlightIswcValidMatch()`, `_highlightIsrcValidMatch()` and `_highlightBarcodeValidMatch()`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Ticking "BUMA" and then "STEMRA ID" (or any two entries that mark the same text) highlighted only the first. `highlightCrossTag()` inserted a virtual space wherever an earlier highlight had split one text node, so a regex spanning the split ("(BUMA/STEMRA ID)") read "(BUMA /STEMRA ID)" and never matched. It no longer adds a gap between two text nodes that were one node before a highlight wrapper split them. Generic to every column's multi-value highlight, not just identifier types.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown for a "Time" column (events listings) now offers a "Time info - Time of day" section with five fixed buckets — Morning (04:00-11:59), Lunch (12:00-12:59), Afternoon (13:00-17:59), Evening (18:00-23:59) and Night (00:00-03:59) — `_findCellTimeBucket()`.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: "Attributes - Identifier type" now also lists the parts of a slash-separated identifier type separately: a `BUMA/STEMRA ID` badge is offered as `BUMA/STEMRA ID`, `BUMA` and `STEMRA ID` — `_workAttrTypeLabels()`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The 📊 dropdown for a "Length" column now offers a "Length info - Milliseconds" section: "ms ≠ .000", "ms = .000" and "no ms data". Shown only once at least one cell carries milliseconds (after ⏱) — `_findCellLengthMsState()`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The 📊 dropdown for a "Relationship types" column now offers a "Relationship types - Credited as" section listing each `(as “credit”)` separately, prefixed with its relationship type (e.g. "» instrument as: lead guitar") — `_findCellRelTypeCredits()`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The 📊 dropdown for a "Tracks" column now offers a "Tracks info - Total" section with the summed track count over all mediums (the same number as the synthetic "Total Tracks" column), e.g. "5 + 5 + 5" → 15.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Native "Barcode" columns now get a GS1 mod-10 format/check-digit validity pass — `initBarcodeValidation()`, page-agnostic, self-detecting via the native `td.barcode-cell` class. A barcode that doesn't match a known length (EAN-8/UPC-A/EAN-13/GTIN-14) or whose check digit doesn't match renders with a ⚠️ warning glyph and an explanatory tooltip. It NEVER rewrites the displayed value, for either valid or invalid entries — unlike ISRC's own reformatting of valid codes.

The 📊 unique-values dropdown for a "Barcode" column now offers three new sections: "Barcode - Validity" (✅/⚠️ valid/invalid counts, mutually exclusive per row since a Barcode cell holds 0 or 1 value), "Barcode - Format" (which GS1 format — UPC-A/EAN-13/EAN-8/GTIN-14 — a STRICTLY CONFORMING entry matches), and "Barcode - Same As" (an open value family, one entry per canonical-equivalence GROUP, labeled with the actual raw representations involved — e.g. "0196587565725 / 196587565725" — rather than a flat count; deliberately independent of the release's own Format column, unlike the existing `sa_enable_barcode_highlight` merge-checkbox feature's grouping) — `_parseBarcodeCode()`/`_findCellBarcodeParts()`/`_getBarcodeCanonicalGroups()`.
New `sa_enable_barcode_validation` setting (default on) gates the whole feature in one place.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: "ISRCs" columns (native `ul.isrcs` listing pages such as artist-recordings, and this script's own release-tracks synthetic column) now always display the hyphenated `CC-XXX-YY-NNNNN` form, with the country/year segments lightly tinted, regardless of whether MusicBrainz's own native markup or the third-party jesus2099 script produced the cell — `initIsrcFormatting()`, page-agnostic, self-detecting via `a[href^="/isrc/"]`.
A code that doesn't match the CC-XXX-YY-NNNNN shape now renders with a ⚠️ warning glyph and an explanatory tooltip instead of being silently reformatted or left unremarked — `data-mb-isrc-invalid`.

The same validity check now applies to native "ISWC" columns against ISO 15707's `T-NNNNNNNNN-C` format (including the computed check digit) — `initIswcValidation()`. MusicBrainz's native ISWC display is already correctly formatted, so this only ever adds the ⚠️ glyph to a malformed code, never rewrites a valid one.

The 📊 unique-values dropdown for an "ISRCs" column now offers five new sections: "ISRC - Country", "- Registrant", "- Year" (resolved to a 4-digit year), "- Designation", and "- Validity" (✅/⚠️ valid/invalid counts) — `_findCellIsrcParts()`.
The 📊 dropdown for an "ISWC" column now offers an "ISWC - Validity" section — `_findCellIswcParts()`.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Credited jesus2099's `mb_INLINE-STUFF.user.js` (`coolifyISRC()`) in the third-party attribution block — this script's ISRC hyphenation/tinting is modelled on, not copied from or dependent on, that function.
`sa_enable_release_tracks_isrc_column`'s description now notes that column-existence gating is independent of the (unconditional) ISRC reformatting/validity behavior.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: New 'iswc' pageType for /iswc/<code> pages: consolidates the works sharing an ISWC into the usual filterable/sortable table (Title, Authors, Recording artists, Other artists, Type, Language, plus an on-demand Relationships column), the same treatment already given to /isrc/<code> pages.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: 🎹 Keyboard Shortcuts and ❓ Application Help (Shift-click) now have a lower-right resize handle, and remember their own position and size across reopens — the same `createInfoDialog()` shell both dialogs share now supports an opt-in `geoKey` that persists and restores geometry, mirroring `showLoadFilterDialog()`'s own `_saveGeo`/`_clampGeo`/`ResizeObserver` idiom.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The ❓ dialog's **🔍 Filter help text…** input works again: it used to only recognize `[data-qf-item]` rows and `<pre>` blocks (the shape of the old plain-text help format), so it silently found nothing in the Markdown-rendered content (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables). It now highlights matches anywhere in the rendered body, without hiding any of it — same as it always did for a `<pre>` block.

Dragging the title bar (or the native resize handle) on either dialog no longer closes it: the browser's mouseup can synthesize a `click` whose target lands outside the dialog once it has moved, which the outside-click handler read as a real outside click. Fixed with the same inside-mousedown tracking guard `showStatsPanel()` already carried for this exact bug.

🎹 Keyboard Shortcuts couldn't grow past its own default size in either dimension, and ❓ Application Help couldn't grow taller: both dialogs' content naturally sits right at the `maxWidth`/`maxHeight` those same options were also being reused as the resize ceiling for, leaving zero headroom to drag outward — it visibly did nothing. A resizable dialog now gets its own generous grow ceiling (95vw/95vh), independent of the comfortable default size `opts.maxWidth`/`opts.maxHeight` still control on first open.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Barcode highlighting's on/off toggle moved out of the h1 toolbar's 🛠 View ▾ menu into the "Barcode" column header itself, as a ▶/▼ toggle mirroring the Length column's ⏱ toggle. `Ctrl+B` (and prefix-mode `b`) still toggle it directly; `#mb-barcode-highlight-btn` no longer exists.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The fetch progress bar now appears after the ❓ Help button, at the very end of the h1 toolbar — it previously sat between the fetch buttons and the ⏹ Stop button, a leftover position from the toolbar redesign.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: ⚙️ Settings and ❓ Help are now drawn as one control beside the 📦 Data and 🛠 View menus — a single rounded pill with a divider between the two halves, instead of two separately-coloured buttons. Both keep their own tooltip and their own action; the pill is a visual grouping, not a merge.

Their default colours now match the pull-down menu buttons. If you had already chosen your own colour for either button, you keep it — only the defaults moved, and the old values are recorded as a migration so an existing choice is never overwritten. Both are still configurable separately under 🖌️ ELEMENT UI STYLES.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: ❓ now opens the help page on GitHub, where it is rendered with a table of contents, working anchors and collapsible sections. Shift-click ❓ to read it inside the page instead, as before.

The help text is rewritten as ShowAllEntityData_HELP.md — a hand-written guide organised around what you are trying to do, rather than the 2448-line plain-text file it replaces. It is roughly a third of the length: the reference detail is folded into collapsible sections, and material that had accumulated over three years of resyncs was re-triaged rather than carried across.

The in-page help dialog renders that Markdown properly — headings, tables, lists, code blocks and links — where it used to drop the file into a <pre>. Its quick-filter still searches the whole document, and its title bar gained a 📖 Open on GitHub link.

The keyboard route is unchanged: the prefix key then H still opens the in-page dialog. Prefix mode cannot carry Shift, so the keyboard keeps the route it can reach and the dialog's own link covers the other one.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The barcode-highlight row in 🛠 View ▾ was the only menu row not showing its keyboard shortcut. It has one — Ctrl+B, configurable — and now displays it like every other row.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt is retired. The mirror keeps serving it for now, so anyone still on an older version keeps working help until Tampermonkey updates them; scripts/check-publish-ready.py reports it as a leftover to remove later rather than as a problem.

scripts/check-publish-ready.py now also fails when a companion file the published script fetches is MISSING from the mirror, not only when it differs. That is the half-finished-rename case this change could have shipped: the script goes out, its renamed help file does not, and the ❓ dialog 404s for everyone already updated.

The settings section of the help file is now a table of setting GROUPS, one row per group in the Settings Manager, and `scripts/audit-config-defaults.py --docs` checks it against the schema's own section list. Its first run found four groups the new help file had folded away or renamed: the unique-values dropdown configuration, the threshold settings, expand-truncated-cells, and the CAA/EAA illustrated discography.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The controls bar beside the page heading is now three groups instead of one long run of buttons. On an artist's Events page it went from 13 controls — nine of them carrying a text label, wrapping onto two lines on a normal window — to five.

📦 Data ▾ holds 💾 Save to Disk, 📂 Load from Disk and 💾 Export. 🛠 View ▾ holds 📏 Density, 📊 Statistics, the barcode-highlight toggle and 🎹 Keyboard shortcuts. Each row shows its own keyboard shortcut on the right, and the menus are navigable with ↑/↓/Home/End, closed with Escape or a click outside.
⚙️ Settings and ❓ Help stay pinned in the bar, one click away as before: they are what you reach for when something is wrong, and burying them would be the opposite of the point.

↔️ Resize and 👁️ Visible moved out of the bar altogether, to the table's own heading beside the filter box — glyph-only, exactly where the per-sub-table ↔️/👁️ pair has always been on a multi-table page. They act on one table, so they now sit next to it. Tooltips and keyboard shortcuts are unchanged.

On an artist's release-group page the four discography views are now one 📀 Discography ▾ menu, and its button names the view you are in — "📀 Discography: Official". The flat run could only tint the active button, which told you nothing until you had looked at all four. That page has the widest heading the script renders; this removes five slots from it.
Every control kept its keyboard shortcut and its tooltip. Pressing Ctrl+D, Ctrl+E or Ctrl+S opens the owning menu for you rather than reporting that the button is missing.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: New setting "Toolbar menu button colors" under 🖌️ ELEMENT UI STYLES, matching the existing per-button colour settings.
The three " | " separators the old bar used are gone; only the one between the fetch buttons and the tools remains, because it still separates two different things.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: A release tracklist now has columns for the relationships of the WORK each track records — publisher, lyricist, composer, arranger, sub-publisher, "is based on", and whatever else a given release uses. MusicBrainz nests those inside the track's "recording of:" relationship, one level below everything that was being extracted, so until now they appeared nowhere but the raw "ARs" column. They are auto-discovered, so a relationship type this script has never heard of gets a column without an update.

Work columns are named with a "Work " prefix — "Work lyricist", "Work publisher label" — so a relationship the recording itself also has (an "arranger:" on both) stays a separate column instead of the two being mixed into one.

A relationship naming several roles at once ("lyricist and composer:") becomes one column per role, so it lines up with tracks that credit the roles separately. On Born to Run that turns three part-filled columns into a full "Work lyricist" and "Work composer".

A work relationship crediting more than one kind of entity across the release splits into one column per kind, the way "Phonographic copyright (℗) by artist"/"…by label" already does — Born to Run credits both an artist publisher and label publishers under the one "publisher:" phrase.
Cells with several credits render as multi-row lists with the usual ▶/▼ per-cell toggle: Thunder Road's three separate "is based on:" relationships are three rows, not just the first one.
Each column's header carries the entity icon MusicBrainz shows beside the names in that relationship — artist, label or work — and the shared "extracted column" header tint.
The columns sit between "Recorded in area" and "Performer", so a track reads left to right as the recording, then the work it records, then who played on it, then the full raw "ARs".

New setting "Add columns for the recorded WORK's own relationships" (on by default) under RELEASE TRACKS. Independent of the other relationship-column settings, and of whether "Recording of work" itself is shown. "ARs" is left completely unchanged either way — every extracted link still appears there too.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ❓ Help's release-tracklist section now describes the "Work …" columns, and its "auto-discovered column" example no longer uses "Publisher" — on a release that is the work's relationship, and it now has its own "Work publisher" column rather than an unprefixed one.
The "Enable collapsible ARs column" setting no longer calls everything in that column a recording-level relationship: it holds both the recording's own relationships and the recorded work's.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A release tracklist saved with 💾 Save to Disk and reopened with 📂 Load from Disk no longer loses its track-vs-recording LENGTH flags. Every ⚠️/❌ tint, its tooltip and both (N) LENGTH buttons used to vanish on the reopened table, because the flag lives on the cell itself and only the cell's contents were saved. They now come back exactly as saved, and the buttons count and filter them as before.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ❓ Help's release-tracklist section now says what a reopened file shows: the flags as they were when saved, not recomputed under a threshold changed since (the millisecond lengths behind them are not in the file); switching flagging off still hides them; and a file saved by an older version has none until it is re-saved from the live page.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Typing into a filter no longer re-counts the whole table for the ⏳ pending-edits and LENGTH ⚠️/❌ summary buttons on every keystroke. Those counts are taken once per set of rows and reused until the rows themselves change — a new fetch, a sort, a Load from Disk — so they cost nothing while you type. On Bruce Springsteen's 4174-row Events page that was 8 348 lookups per keystroke, whether the filter left 4000 rows or 26. The buttons show exactly the same numbers as before, including while a filter hides the rows they count.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The ⏳ pending-edits filter no longer erases the thing it filtered on. Pressing it — or checking "⏳ has pending edits" / a "» pending edit:" entry in the 📊 dropdown — used to paint each matching entity with the ordinary column-filter background, which covered MusicBrainz's own orange "modification pending" marker completely. The rows were right and the one signal you had pressed the button to find was gone.

Those matches are now RINGED instead: the text is left exactly as it reads unfiltered and a bold outline is drawn around the whole marker, orange and all. Same idea as the red ring a matching relationship icon already gets, and for the same reason — the target carries a visual of its own that a background would destroy.
The ring encloses the entity-kind icon too, where MusicBrainz's marker wraps one. On a joined credit only the half with open edits is ringed, exactly as before.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: New "Pending-Edits Match Outline Color" setting, next to the other filter-highlight colours, picks that ring's colour. Dark red by default: MusicBrainz's own pending-edit marker is a pale yellow, so a yellow ring drawn on it is very nearly invisible — which is exactly what the first attempt at this looked like.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ❓ Help's ⏳ PENDING-EDITS FILTER TOGGLE section and the 📊 dropdown's "Pending edits" entry now describe the ring, and say why the pending-edits filters are the only ones that get one: for every other filter the highlight COLOUR is what tells you which filter matched, so typing a query that happens to match inside a pending entity still highlights it the usual way.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The five editable lookup tables — Default Hidden Columns, the three Relationships icon tables and the Unicode Character Picker — now receive rows added in a later version. Until now they were filled in from the built-in list the first time each was used and never looked at it again, so a row shipped afterwards reached nobody who already had the table. The only escape was to delete every row in the table editor, save and reload so it refilled — throwing away everything you had entered by hand to gain one line you had not.

A row you DELETED is never handed back, which is what makes the rest safe. The script now records which built-in rows it has already offered you, because a row you removed on purpose and a row you have never seen look identical in the table itself. Rows you added or edited yourself are untouched, and if you had already added a row that a later version ships as a built-in, yours is kept exactly as it is.
That record travels in a saved configuration file, so importing one on another browser carries your deletions with it instead of quietly reversing them.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: A new row announces itself only when it changes what you see. A new character in the Unicode picker or a new relationship icon simply appears. A new row in Default Hidden Columns hides a column, so that one shows a notice naming it, with ↩︎ Undo to remove it again — and undoing means it is not offered a second time.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: The three Relationships icon tables' built-in rows were written out twice — thousands of lines apart, with nothing keeping the two copies equal. A row added to one and not the other would have made the table you get disagree with the fallback used when the shared library fails to load. They are one list each now, read by everything that needs them.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ❓ Help gained a NEW ROWS IN THE EDITABLE LOOKUP TABLES section explaining what arrives, what never comes back, and why the script has to keep a record rather than just compare your table against the built-in list.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The ⚙️ Settings dialog's header now tells you what you are running: the script version and the shared library's version side by side, how many settings and sections there are, and a live badge counting how many settings currently differ from their default. The library number is the one you could not get anywhere else — it is pulled in behind the scenes and has no entry of its own in Tampermonkey's list, so a script paired with an older library than it was built against behaved differently with nothing anywhere saying so. RESET and CLOSE became proper buttons you can reach with the keyboard, and the note about what SAVE does moved into a line of its own.

Everything you can click, type in or drag in the ⚙️ Settings dialog now has a tooltip. Each setting's name, control, Default cell and Description share one, carrying the description, the default, and the storage key the setting is kept under — that key appears nowhere else, and it is what you need when editing a saved configuration file by hand. Controls whose behaviour is not obvious say so: a 🔧 button runs at once and has nothing for SAVE to store, and a 📋 table editor's own 💾 writes immediately rather than waiting for SAVE. "Collapse all" now explains why it is unavailable while a search is running, instead of just being dead.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Pressing a button in the ⚙️ Settings dialog's header no longer starts dragging the dialog. Every control except SAVE sits on the drag bar, so the dialog used to follow the pointer while you were deciding whether to release on the button — and that could also swallow the click meant to close it.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 💾 Save configuration now also saves your workspace — the things you built up by using the script rather than by opening a settings dialog. Above all your PINNED FILTER LIST, which you edit from inside the ⚙️ Settings dialog via 🔧 Edit Pinned Filter List and which therefore always looked like part of the configuration, and was not in the file. Also: which columns you have hidden on each page type (the 👁️ Visible menu's own memory, each sub-table included), your filter history, the Statistics- and Load-dialog positions and sizes, the Settings- and ChangeLog-dialog sizes, the Settings dialog's column widths and which of its sections you leave open, the 📊 dropdown's collapsed sections, and the shared library's display preferences. 📂 Load configuration restores all of it and tells you, group by group, what it restored. Moving to a second browser or a new profile no longer means re-hiding columns one page type at a time.

Column visibility now travels per sub-table as well as per page type. A page that renders several tables keeps a separate visibility state for each, and those states are found by sweeping storage rather than by guessing their names, so nothing is silently left out of the file.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The file-format version moved from 1 to 2, and reading across the two works in both directions. A file saved by an earlier version imports exactly as before — your column visibility, pinned filters and window positions are left as they are here, rather than being cleared by a file that has no opinion about them. A file saved by a newer version imports everything this one understands and leaves the rest alone. The summary says which of the two happened, so "my window positions did not come across" is never a mystery.
The export dialog's FILE METADATA block now counts the workspace keys alongside the settings keys, so you can see before saving whether the file contains what you expect.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A configuration file can no longer write to anything outside the settings and workspace this script owns. Every key in the file is checked against the list of things that are importable at all, and anything else is reported as skipped rather than stored — so a file that has been hand-edited, or picked up from somewhere unfamiliar, cannot reach into this installation's own bookkeeping.

The record of which one-time settings repairs this installation has already run is deliberately NOT in the file. Carrying it across would tell a browser that still needs the repair that it had already had it, and would offer to undo a repair that never ran there.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ❓ Help's SAVE / LOAD CONFIGURATION section now lists what the file carries and what it does not, explains reading an older or newer file, and notes that saved window positions are clamped to the window they are restored into — so a file written on a large monitor cannot strand a dialog off-screen on a small one.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Opening ⚙️ Settings from the Tampermonkey script menu or from MusicBrainz's own "Editing" menu now gives you the same dialog as the ⚙️ toolbar button. Those two routes used to be second class: the 💾 Save configuration and 📂 Load configuration buttons were missing, and 🔧 Edit Pinned Filter List did nothing at all when pressed — with nothing on screen to say why.

The Default column now says what a setting's default actually is. The five editable lookup tables showed the literal word "undefined", the 🔧 button entry showed an internal function name, and every "pipe-separated" setting showed the text "(pipe-sep.)" instead of its value — the format rather than the default, for exactly the settings whose defaults are hardest to reconstruct by hand.

SAVE no longer reloads the page when you changed nothing. The reload is how a changed setting takes effect, but it also throws away whatever the page had already fetched, so paying it to apply nothing was pure loss. The dialog header's claim that settings are "applied IMMEDIATELY upon saving" was never true and now says what really happens.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: You can now see what you have changed. A setting that differs from its default is marked with an orange edge and a bold name, every section header carries a ● badge counting the changes inside it — visible while the section is still collapsed — and a new ● Changed only button in the toolbar filters the dialog down to just those settings. Across 238 settings there was previously no way to answer this short of exporting the configuration and diffing it against a fresh one.

Sections remember whether you left them open. Every one of the 38 used to re-collapse on every open, so finding the setting you adjust regularly meant the same hunt every time. The first open is still all-collapsed.

Search and collapsing no longer fight each other. Searching now hides sections that contain no match, instead of leaving all 38 headers standing with nothing under most of them, and opens the ones that do — a match inside a collapsed section used to appear underneath a header still drawn as closed. Clearing the search puts every section back exactly as you left it, and a search that matches nothing now says so rather than showing an empty dialog.

Each section header has a ↺ button that resets just that section — and only the settings in it that actually differ, telling you how many first. The single global RESET across 238 settings was the button nobody dared press. Like RESET, it changes only the dialog: nothing is stored until you press SAVE.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ❓ Help gains FINDING YOUR WAY AROUND THE SETTINGS DIALOG, RESETTING and SAVING sections, and its note that the 💾/📂 buttons are missing from two of the entry points is replaced — that was the bug, and it is fixed.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Only the settings you have actually changed are now stored. Pressing SAVE in ⚙️ Settings used to write down all ~232 settings even when you changed nothing — and from that moment on, every improved default a later version shipped was invisible to you, permanently. Ten settings had already drifted that way, including the collapsed sidebar, auto-resizing columns, the 📊 dropdown's row count and the row hover colour.

The first run of this version repairs a profile that had already frozen, once. Settings still holding a default this script used to ship adopt the current one; a notice in the top-right corner names them, with ↩︎ Undo to put everything back and ✓ Keep to dismiss it. Anything you chose yourself is left alone — a value is adopted only when it exactly matches a default this script once shipped for that setting, checked against the whole version history rather than guessed.

Four settings that were removed from the script weeks ago were still occupying storage on every profile that had ever pressed SAVE, with no way to find or clear them. They are now cleaned up in the same pass.

📂 Load configuration no longer re-freezes your profile. The saved file is a full dump of every setting, so importing one used to write all of them back down — undoing the fix above through the back door. An imported value that matches the current default is now applied without being stored, and the summary says how many.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ❓ Help gains a KEEPING UP WITH NEW DEFAULTS section explaining what is stored, what the one-time repair does and how to undo it.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Four descriptions in the ⚙️ Settings dialog described a colour the setting no longer uses, and now describe the real one. The H3 sub-table header background said "Default is a light green" when it is a pale rose; both the H2 and H3 hover backgrounds said "Default is the original MusicBrainz light grey (#f9f9f9)" when both are oranges; and both non-hover heading settings promised "the existing grey hover background is preserved", which those orange hover colours had already replaced. The table column-header setting also claimed its default matches the grey MusicBrainz uses, which stopped being true when it was darkened.

Fifteen places in the script carried a hardcoded colour or number that no longer matched the setting it was standing in for — so the same setting could resolve two different ways depending on which part of the script asked. The hardcoded copies now match the settings. This is normally invisible, and nobody's colours have been wrong: the stand-in value is only reached if you CLEAR a colour field and save it, or set a numeric setting to 0, or if the shared library fails to load. In those cases you now get the setting's real default instead of a value left over from an earlier release.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: A cleared "Unique-Values Dropdown Visible Rows" now falls back to 30 rows rather than 8 — 8 was the default until it was raised to 30 in an earlier release, and this copy of it was missed at the time.
Likewise the auto-resize row limit falls back to 10 000 rather than 2 000 when the shared library is unavailable.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt` needed no change: it documents these settings by name and never quotes their colour values, so nothing in it had gone stale.

The configuration-defaults audit added in the previous release is what found all fifteen, and its list of known mismatches is now empty — a new one fails the audit rather than sitting unnoticed until someone reads two files side by side.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 📂 Load configuration no longer wipes your hand-edited lookup tables. Importing a configuration file silently discarded every row you had entered in Default Hidden Columns, the three Relationships icon tables (relation type / other database / streaming service) and the Unicode Character Picker catalogue — the five settings that take the longest to re-enter — and refilled them with the built-in defaults. The summary dialog counted them as applied, so nothing indicated anything had been lost until you noticed your rows were gone.

The cause: those five settings are stored as tables of rows, and the importer ran every value through a text conversion, turning a table into a single comma-joined string. Anything that is not a real table is now rejected and reported as invalid instead of being written, so a damaged or hand-edited file can no longer overwrite good rows with nonsense.

💾 Save configuration now exports your lookup tables as they are RIGHT NOW, not as they were when the page loaded. Editing a table (say adding a symbol to the Unicode picker) and pressing 💾 Save in the table editor stores it immediately, but the rest of the settings are only re-read on a page load — so a configuration file saved in that same session silently contained the rows from before your edit, and loading that file back put the old rows in place again. Adding a symbol, saving a configuration and loading it back therefore lost the symbol. If you have a configuration file saved from before this version and it is missing a recent table edit, re-save it.

💾 Save configuration no longer exports an internal entry (the 🔧 Edit Pinned Filter List button) that was never a setting, and the importer skips it in files saved by earlier versions. It used to write that entry's internal function name into your stored settings as though you had chosen it.
A table you have never edited is now left out of the saved file altogether rather than recorded as empty, so importing it cannot suppress the built-in rows you would otherwise get.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt`: new SAVE / LOAD CONFIGURATION section, next to Settings dialog safety guards. The feature has shipped since 9.99.273 and had never been documented. It states what the saved file contains, what it deliberately does NOT contain (per-page-type column visibility, the pinned filter list, filter history, dialog geometry and sizes, the 📊 dropdown's collapsed sections, library preferences), and that importing reloads the page.

The same section records where the two buttons appear: they exist only when Settings is opened via the ⚙️ button, Ctrl+, or the prefix key followed by ",". Opened from the Tampermonkey menu or the MusicBrainz "Editing" menu, you get the shared library's own dialog, without 💾/📂 and with 🔧 Edit Pinned Filter List inert.

The configuration-file format comment in the source claimed the export held only settings that differ from their defaults. It never did, and a full dump is what makes a saved file diffable against another one — corrected to say so.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Picking a value from a column's 📊 panel now NARROWS text already typed into that column's filter box instead of replacing it, so the number on an entry's badge is the number of rows you get. The panel counts the rows currently VISIBLE, so with "bruce" typed into the Artist column its "» join phrase: with" entry read (3) — and clicking it returned 9, because the typed filter was thrown away.

The filter box now shows both halves, e.g. `bruce + » join phrase: with`, or `bruce + 2 selected` with several ticked. Unticking the last box restores the typed text and leaves the column filtered on it rather than clearing the column, and the typed text keeps its own match highlighting alongside the picked value's.
Typing into a box that is showing a selection still replaces that selection. That asymmetry is deliberate: the box's text IS the selection's summary, so editing it can only mean editing that text.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Every place that clears a column filter's checkbox selection now goes through one helper, so the newly stored typed text cannot be orphaned at one of them. "Clear ALL filters" was in fact already leaving the selection behind and relying on the next filter pass to tidy it up.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt`: the 📊 panel's "whichever you use last wins and clears the other" rule is no longer true in one direction, and has been replaced with the new behaviour and the retained asymmetry. Its "🔀 Join phrases" description was re-read against the code and needed no change — it already described the feature correctly; the defect was that one phrase never reached it.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A join phrase is no longer dropped when MusicBrainz marks one of the two credited entities as having pending edits. On a credit like "Guns N’ Roses feat. Bruce Springsteen", MusicBrainz wraps the pending entity's link in its own `<span class="mp">`; the join-phrase finder only accepted a link that was a DIRECT child of the shared name element, so it saw one entity instead of two and " feat. " simply did not exist — no entry in the 📊 "Join phrases" section, nothing to filter on, nothing to highlight.

The boundary is now resolved structurally rather than by a list of known wrapper classes: for each pair of credited links the finder takes their nearest common ancestor and reads the nodes between them. That covers MusicBrainz's `mp` wrapper, jesus2099's `name-variation` wrapper, the two nested in either order, one wrapper around BOTH links, and whatever comes next.

This was a disagreement between two finders looking at the same cell: the entity finder already walked through the wrapper, which is why the very same row still offered its "» artist name: Guns N’ Roses" entry while its join phrase was missing.

The highlight for a picked join phrase now lands on the phrase itself. Where each credited entity carries its own disambiguation comment — MusicBrainz's ordinary shape — the text between the two links is split across several nodes, and the mark was going onto the non-breaking space in front of the previous entity's comment instead.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A sub-section with no Relationships column no longer offers a 🔗⟳ retry button for it. A place's Performances tab groups by relationship type, so its recording sections have no Relationships column while its release section does — and all five sections were being given a retry button, four of which could only ever have re-fetched nothing. Both places that create the button asked "does this PAGE have the column" instead of "does this table have it".
The same applies to the ⚠⟳ "retry only what failed" button, which attaches itself to the 🔗⟳ and so followed it onto those sections.

This is older than it looked: the buttons were always created there, but until 9.99.1131 they were inserted inside the sub-section's own filter box, where they were easy to miss. Putting them in the right place is what made them visible.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt` needed no edit: it never claimed the retry buttons appear on every sub-section, and its description of what they do was and remains correct.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The ⏳ pending-edits filter now MARKS what it matched. Every other filter highlights its match; this one could not, because MusicBrainz's open-edits marker is a colour with no text behind it, so the filter tested a property of the row instead of a string. It now highlights each pending entity inside that orange marker, in every column of every matching row — the same marking the 📊 dropdown's "⏳ has pending edits" entry already applied to a single column.

A collapsed multi-row cell now tells you when the pending entity is one of the items it is hiding. Collapsed cells show only their first item, so a pending author sitting in item 2 of an "Authors" cell looked exactly like a cell with nothing pending. Its ▶N▤ expander is now tinted while the ⏳ filter is on, and so are the sub-section's ▤ button and the global collapse button — so you can see which cells are worth opening without opening all of them. Expanding a cell clears its own tint, because nothing is hidden any more.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt`'s "⏳ PENDING-EDITS FILTER TOGGLE" section describes the new marking and the collapsed-cell tint.

`CLAUDE.md` gained a section on the collapsed-cell tint: it is computed ONLY from the four filter-highlight classes found in a cell's HIDDEN items, which is why a structural filter gets no tint until it writes one — and why the fix is one hook rather than an edit to the ten places that read them.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The per-table Relationships retry buttons (🔗⟳ and ⚠⟳) appear on pages where they were silently missing. MusicBrainz wraps many listings' table in a `<form>` for its merge checkboxes — an artist's Works tab is one — and the code looked for the section heading by walking backwards through the table's own siblings, which never leaves that wrapper. It gave up and threw the button away. The heading is now located the same way the artwork buttons already located it, which does not care what the table is nested inside.

On a sub-section whose heading has no artwork buttons, the 🔗⟳ retry button no longer lands inside the sub-table filter's input box. It was inserted after "the heading's last button", which in CSS terms picks the first button that is the last one among its own parent's children — on a heading carrying a filter panel, that is the filter's own ✗ clear button, several levels down. Measured on a place's Performances tab: 4 of 5 sub-sections. It now goes at the end of the heading's own row of controls, next to the row count.
Because both ⚠⟳ "retry only what failed" buttons attach themselves to the 🔗⟳ button, they were missing or misplaced in exactly the same cases and are fixed with it.
On a page carrying both cover art and event art, the page-wide 🔗⟳ no longer wedges itself between the two artwork button groups.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `CLAUDE.md`'s Relationships-retry section records both failure shapes with the snapshot each was measured on, and the rule that replaced them; the segmented-pill section documents `_hdrCtlAnchor()` — where the FIRST control in a heading goes, as distinct from `_ctlRunEnd()`, which places the ones after it.

`ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt` needed no edit here: it describes what the two retry buttons do and never claimed where they sit. Its "TWO retry buttons" paragraph was simply untrue on the affected pages, because there were none, and is now true.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Numeric settings are honoured again after you have pressed SAVE once. The settings dialog stores every non-checkbox value as a string, and it writes ALL settings on the first SAVE — not just the ones you edited — so every numeric setting became a string in storage. Four settings read their value through a `typeof v === 'number'` check, which a string fails, so your value was silently discarded in favour of the built-in default: the Relationships auto-collapse threshold, the Relationships auto-retry "too many failures" limit, and the two completion-toast durations. The visible symptom was an auto-collapse threshold of 0 ("never auto-collapse") still collapsing a large table, because the read fell back to 200. Values are now coerced back to real numbers on read, which also repairs profiles that are already stored as strings — no re-save needed.

"0 to disable" now works for the Large Dataset Threshold and the Chunked Rendering Threshold. Both were read with `|| <default>`, and `0 || 5000` is 5000, so the save-or-render prompt could not be switched off and "always use simple render" could not be selected. Both now read with `??`, matching the Render Warning Threshold, which was always written that way. This had to ship together with the coercion above: before it, the stored string "0" was truthy, survived the `||`, and then failed the `> 0` test — so the setting worked by accident, and coercing it to a real 0 alone would have broken it.

An emptied numeric settings field falls back to that setting's default instead of being read as a deliberate 0. `Number('')` is 0 in JavaScript, which for a threshold documented as "0 to disable" would have silently switched the feature off.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Added `org/config-handling.org` (on `main` since the previous version): the end-user analysis of configuration handling, findings F1-F6, and the decision to commit a generated defaults snapshot that nothing reads at runtime. This change is its F2.

`ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt` needed no edit: it already documented "set the threshold to 0 to never auto-collapse" and "0 to disable" for both render thresholds. Those statements were simply untrue for anyone who had pressed SAVE, and are now true.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 📊 artwork-summary button stood taller than the buttons beside it, so the group it sits in no longer read as one control with a straight top and bottom edge. All of them are the same height again.

The rule that keeps those buttons aligned used to list them one by one, which is why a button added later was left out of it. It now matches them the way the grouping itself does, so anything added next is the right height without a further change.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The ⚠⟳ "retry only what failed" buttons — for cover art, event art and relationships — now also appear on each sub-table, counting that sub-table's own failures. The page-wide one beside the main heading stays, so you can repair one section or the whole page, exactly as the ⟳ and 🔗⟳ reload buttons have always worked.
Each of them joins its own group's pill, so a sub-table with failures reads as one control: toggle, count, reload, and retry-what-failed.

The counts are taken from the rows themselves rather than from what is currently on screen, so filtering the table does not make them shrink — and a button never disappears while a filter is hiding the very rows it would repair.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Loading a file from disk on a page that had already been rendered used to quietly throw away the heading this script adds above the table and build a replacement. Nothing looked wrong afterwards — the replacement landed in the same place — but anything attached to the original heading went with it. The heading is now left alone, which is what the code always intended.

This changes nothing you can see. It is recorded because the page was only coming out right by accident: a later clean-up step happened to remove the leftover, and that had never been written down or tested anywhere.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The little buttons beside a table's heading — the ▶🖼 artwork toggle with its count, ⟳ reload, 📊 artwork summary, and 🔗⟳ for relationships — are now drawn as joined-up pills instead of a row of separate boxes. Buttons that belong together sit in one pill with a hairline between them and rounded ends only at the two ends of the group, so it reads as one control with several parts.
Artwork and relationships stay two separate pills even when they sit side by side, because they reload two different things. A page showing both cover art and event art keeps those apart too.
The ⚠⟳ buttons keep their yellow: the point of that colour is that something failed, and flattening the group to one shade would have thrown the signal away for the sake of tidiness.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 🔗⟳ relationships button no longer lands in the middle of the artwork buttons. It and the 📊 summary were both being inserted next to the same ⟳, so whichever feature finished loading last took the spot and the order came out differently depending on timing. Both now attach to the end of their own group, which gives the same order every time.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: When a page of a multi-page listing finally fails and the run stops short, the status line now offers a "↻ Load remaining pages" button beside the "⚠️ Loaded 37 of 40 pages — INCOMPLETE" it explains. Pressing it carries on from the page that failed and keeps everything already on screen; the 37 pages that did arrive are not fetched again. Hover it to see exactly which page it will start at.

Repeat it as often as you like: if the next page fails too, the offer comes back pointing at that one instead. When the run finally completes the warning and the button both disappear on their own, and the status line goes back to saying how many pages it loaded.

This replaces the only answer available before, which was to press the button again — and still is, if you want a genuinely fresh start. That path reloads the page and re-fetches everything from page 1, and it is unchanged.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Resuming asks MusicBrainz for nothing it already knows: the page count is reused rather than re-requested, so the "⚠️ High Page Count" confirmation does not appear a second time for pages you already agreed to.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: A handful of Relationship rows that the Web Service refused are now quietly asked about once more, by themselves, about half a minute after the rest of the column has finished — and again once after that if they still fail. MusicBrainz refuses requests in bursts rather than steadily, so a burst is usually over by then and the ⚠ cells simply turn into icons while you are reading the page. Nothing else changes on screen.

It is deliberately hard for this to become a nuisance, because it is the only thing in the script that goes to the network without you asking. It never starts until everything else has finished, so it cannot slow a page down; it runs at most twice; it does not start at all when more than 25 rows failed, because that many is the Web Service being down rather than briefly busy; and it gives up on the spot after five refusals in a row without asking about the rest. Any one of those is enough to stop it.

Both ceilings are yours: "Relationships: retry failed lookups once, automatically" turns it off, and "Relationships: largest failure count still worth retrying automatically" (default 25, 0 to disable) sets the outage limit. The ⚠⟳ button is unaffected either way and still retries exactly what failed, however many that is.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: A 📊 button next to each table's cover-art controls opens a summary of what that table's artwork actually is — and it costs nothing, because every word of it was already fetched and then thrown away. It reports how many entities have artwork, have none, could not be fetched or have not been looked up yet; the images broken down by type; which images the archive marks as THE main front or main back (not the same thing as being typed "Front", a distinction nothing else in the script shows you); how many are still unapproved; which thumbnail sizes exist, so a missing 1200 on an old upload stops being a mystery; the MusicBrainz edit that added each cover, linked;.

It reads the current state when you open it, so it works while artwork is still loading. That is the point rather than a detail: the completion message it replaces is page-wide, vanishes on its own, and on a large listing never appears at all — so on exactly the pages where you most want to know what happened, there was nothing to look at.
Anything that could not be fetched is named and linked at the bottom, with a button to retry just those.
The panel counts the rows currently SHOWN, and says so at the top when a filter is active rather than passing a filtered subset off as the whole table.
Fixed before release: on single-table pages the 📊 button jumped out of the artwork-control run after filtering, landing between the heading and the row count.

On a big discography the "pending" count can sit still for a long time, and the panel now explains why instead of looking stuck: cover-art lookups are deliberately queued behind every image on the page so the pictures appear first, and on a 2 000-release artist that is half an hour before the first lookup even runs. The panel shows how many jobs are still queued.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Cover art now gets the ⚠⟳ button the Relationships column got yesterday: ask again about only the entities the Cover Art Archive could not answer, instead of reloading every image in the table. The existing ⟳ button is unchanged and still reloads everything — right when you think what is on screen is stale, wrong as a way to recover three failed lookups out of two hundred. The button appears only when something has actually failed, and carries the count.

This needed a distinction the script could not previously make. A release the archive has no artwork for (a 404) and a release the archive could not answer about (a 503) both end up as "no artwork" on screen, and since the last release both were also remembered identically for the rest of the session. The transient ones are now marked as such — which is what the new button counts, and why a page full of releases that genuinely have no cover art shows no button at all rather than a large and useless number.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: A new ⚠⟳ button recovers only the Relationship lookups that FAILED. The existing 🔗⟳ button reloads everything in its table, which is right when you think the data is stale but very wrong as a way to recover a few failures: on a 2 000-release page with three failed rows it meant 2 000 requests at one per second — about forty minutes to repair three seconds of trouble. The new button asks about the three. It appears only when something has actually failed, and carries the count, so it doubles as the answer to "did anything go wrong?". Both buttons are kept, deliberately: "force a genuine refetch" and "recover the failures" are different intentions and each is worth having.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A retry skipped the rows a filter was hiding, and left them marked as failed for good. Pressing a Relationships retry button cleared the failure markers only on rows currently on screen — and a row still carrying that marker is deliberately passed over by the loader, so a failure you had filtered out was stranded permanently, with nothing to say so. Markers are now cleared on every row, on screen or not. Such a row cannot be re-fetched while it is hidden, but it is no longer stuck: clear the filter and it loads like any other unloaded row.

On single-table pages with cover art switched off, the Relationships retry button was built and then never placed on the page at all — it looked for the artwork retry button to sit beside, and gave up when there was none instead of falling back to the section heading.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The "Release events" column gave up on the first refusal, and said nothing. It is filled by a single request for the whole page, so one "503 Service Unavailable" from MusicBrainz left the entire column empty — with no message, no marker, and no way to ask again short of reloading the page. The request is now retried up to three times like every other Web Service call the script makes (503, 502, 504 and 429, honouring a "Retry-After" header), so most refusals pass unnoticed. A 404 is still taken at face value.

A failed lookup no longer counts as an answer. The cells are left genuinely empty rather than marked as finished, so a later attempt fills every one of them instead of skipping over cells it thinks it has already done.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The "Release events" column header now says what happened, and lets you retry. While the lookup is in flight it shows ⏳; if it finally fails it shows a yellow ⚠ instead — hover for the reason ("HTTP 503"), click to ask again. A successful retry fills the column and the ⚠ disappears. It survives filtering and sorting, so you cannot lose the retry by typing, and nothing at all is added to the header when the lookup works. This is the first retry the script offers at the level of a single column.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A fetch that did not finish was reported in exactly the same words as one that did. MusicBrainz refuses requests in bursts when it is busy, and a single refusal on page 4 of 40 ended the whole run at page 3 — after which the status line read "Loaded 4 pages", counting the page that had just failed. Nothing anywhere said the table was short. It now stops at the failed page and says so: "⚠️ Loaded 3 of 40 pages (287 rows) — INCOMPLETE", in orange, with the reason on hover. The rows that did arrive are kept and stay fully usable; press the action button again to retry.

Page fetches are now retried. A page that comes back "503 Service Unavailable", "502 Bad Gateway", "504 Gateway Timeout" or "429 Too Many Requests" is asked for again, up to three times, with a growing pause (about 2 and 5 seconds) between attempts, and a "Retry-After" header from the server is honoured up to 30 seconds. Most bursts now pass unnoticed rather than truncating the table. An answer that is genuinely final, such as a 404, is not retried. Pressing Stop during one of those pauses takes effect immediately instead of waiting it out.
When the PAGE COUNT itself could not be read, the script quietly fetched page 1 and called it a complete one-page listing. It now says "of an unknown total" and marks the run incomplete.

On an artist's release-group page, the Official / Non-Official discography buttons are built from a preparatory pass of their own. If that pass was cut short, the buttons were still built — and a partial list there does not shorten the "Official" view, it silently files genuinely-official releases under "Non-Official", including in any file you then saved. That partial list is now discarded and the buttons are left out, with the reason in the status line. The rows themselves are unaffected, so this case is flagged but not called INCOMPLETE.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Saving an incomplete fetch to disk now warns you first, and the file remembers. The Save dialog says the file will be a partial copy of the listing, and loading that file later shows the same orange "INCOMPLETE" marker — without it, a short file is indistinguishable from a complete one forever. Files saved before this existed load exactly as they did before.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The Relationships column and the ⏱ millisecond Length feature gave up on the first try whenever MusicBrainz answered anything other than "503 Service Unavailable". Both already knew to keep asking through a 503 burst, but a "502 Bad Gateway" or "504 Gateway Timeout" — which MusicBrainz's front-end returns for a minute or two whenever a new version is rolled out — and a "429 Too Many Requests" from the rate limiter each ended the request immediately and were reported as a settled failure. All three are now retried exactly like a 503: up to three attempts with a growing pause. A deploy that used to leave a page full of ⚠ cells, or a yellow ⏱ button, now mostly passes unnoticed.

An answer that is genuinely final is still taken at face value. A 400 or a 404 is not retried, because asking again would only produce the same answer, and spending three attempts on every one of them would make a bad page slower for no benefit.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: When MusicBrainz says how long to wait before asking again (a "Retry-After" header), that wait is now honoured rather than ignored. It acts as a floor: the pause is never shorter than the normal one, so a server asking for half a second still gets the polite one-request-per-second spacing MusicBrainz asks of every client, and it is capped at 30 seconds so a maintenance window saying "come back in an hour" cannot park a request for an hour. This is the first time the script has read a response header at all.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A Cover Art Archive outage was recorded as "this release has no artwork" and kept on disk for a week. Any non-OK answer from the archive's metadata API — a 503, a 429, a gateway error — was written to the IndexedDB cache exactly like a genuine "no such release" 404. Every later visit to any page listing that release then read the stored zero, showed no artwork, and made no request and no warning at all. Only a definitive 404/410 is persisted now; a transport failure is remembered for the current session alone, so a reload or the ⟳ retry button asks again. This is the same distinction the image-byte path, the ⏱ millisecond Length feature and the Relationships column already made — the oldest network path was the one that never got it.

The ⟳ artwork retry button could not recover such a release. It cleared the in-memory caches but never the IndexedDB record, so the re-fetch it triggered read that record straight back and issued no request — the button did nothing at all for every entity that had a stored result. It now evicts the table's cached archive metadata first, which is what the help text already promised it did.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The archive metadata cache now keeps entries for 30 days instead of 7 (⚙️ Settings → 🗄️ ART ARCHIVE INDEXEDDB CACHE → "Metadata (JSON) cache TTL (days)"), matching the image, Relationships and millisecond-length caches, which were all already 30. Fewer repeat requests to coverartarchive.org on pages you revisit. This was only safe to raise once the fix above landed — otherwise one bad minute at the archive would have hidden real artwork for a month rather than a week. If you have ever pressed Save in the settings dialog your stored value is still 7; reset that one field to pick up the new default.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: In the 📊 unique-values dropdown, the "Country details - Name" entries showed no country flag while the "Country details - Code" entries right below them did — the same countries, listed twice, decorated once. A "Country" cell renders both halves of one value ("United States (US)"), so both sections now show the flag.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: In the 📊 unique-values dropdown, the "Release events - Country" and "Country details - Code" entries showed the country flag in front of the entry instead of after it, so one panel could display two different conventions at once — "[flag] country: GB" directly above "[icon] area name: California [flag]". Country entries now match every other entry: the generic entity icon leads, and the flag follows the name.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On a place's performances page and a label's relationships page, the "Release events" column could occasionally list every release event twice — and so could the "Release country" and "Release date" columns beside it. Two passes could reach the same cell before either had marked it filled, and the second added a second copy rather than replacing the first. It showed up only when the MusicBrainz web service answered unusually quickly, which is why it was easy to miss.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: With a flag userscript installed ("MusicBrainz: Right Side Flags Everywhere"), entries in the 📊 unique-values dropdown could show the same country flag twice — once before the country name and once after — while the table cell itself showed one. When that userscript replaces a flag it cannot simply delete MusicBrainz's original, so it empties it and leaves it in place; the dropdown was counting both the emptied original and the replacement as separate icons. Only one of the two shapes that userscript uses had been recognised. A flag it has emptied is now left out entirely, and the flags this script copies into the dropdown are marked so that userscript does not redecorate them a second time.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On a place's performances page and a label's relationships page, the 📊 unique-values dropdown offered far less for the "Release events" and "Release country" columns than the same columns get everywhere else: no country flags, and none of the "Release events - Country", "- Date" or "- Weekday" groupings, nor "Country details - Name" and "- Code". Filtering by country on those pages meant typing the value by hand. These two columns are built by this script rather than read from the page, and they were being built in a shape of their own that none of the dropdown's country and date recognisers could read — everything else on the page uses MusicBrainz's own markup, and they now do too. The columns look and read exactly as before; what changes is that the dropdown can finally see into them.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Filtering and sorting a multi-section page that shows cover-art thumbnails is much quicker. Every re-render has to copy each visible thumbnail back onto the row it came from, so it survives the next one, and finding that row meant searching the whole table once per thumbnail. On a 4174-row page that search cost about 1.5 seconds of frozen page per keystroke, and about 13 seconds on a 10 000-row one; it now builds one lookup table per pass instead, costing about 2.4 milliseconds. Thumbnails behave exactly as before.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On a release's track listing, most columns' 📊 unique-values dropdown was missing its "▶ collapsed multi-row cells" and "◀ expanded multi-row cells" entries — so there was no way to list, say, the 9 tracks whose Instruments cell holds more than one credit, even though the column header said "▶9▤" right above it. Where the column also had empty cells the dropdown showed a "Structure" section containing only "○ empty cells", which made it look like the section existed and those tracks simply did not; where it had none, the section was absent entirely. Every affected column was one carrying an entity icon next to its name (Instruments, Vocals, Performer, Engineer, Recorded at place and the other relationship columns), because the invisible spacing character behind that icon was being read as part of the column's name.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Filtering is a little quicker on every page, and noticeably less wasteful on big ones: the check behind the (N) WARNING ⚠️ / (N) ERROR ❌ summary buttons used to look for those icons in every cell of every row each time you typed, on every kind of page — even though only a release's track listing can have them. On a 4174-row events page that was 87 654 fruitless searches taking 64 ms per keystroke. It now looks once per row instead of once per cell, and on a page with no such icons it stops looking at all after the first pass. The buttons themselves count exactly what they counted before, including while a filter hides the rows they refer to.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Relationships column: loading a single row by clicking its cell, and then choosing that row's relationship from the 📊 unique-values dropdown, filtered correctly — but after loading a SECOND row with the same relationship and choosing it again, only the first row was shown. The dropdown counted both rows; the table did not, because the previous result for that identical choice was remembered and re-used. Loading relationship icons now also discards that remembered result, so the next filter re-examines every row.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Relationships column: after collapsing the column with ▼🔗 and expanding it again while another column's filter was active, picking an entry from the Relationships 📊 unique-values dropdown no longer marked the matching icons with their red outline — and on some pages stopped narrowing the table at all — for that pick and every later one, until the page was reloaded. Collapsing cleared each row's cached column text using a value the cache did not recognise as "cleared", so the next filtering pass read that value back as if it were real text and failed part-way through, skipping the icon-highlighting step that runs after it.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Relationships column: the 📊 unique-values dropdown has a new "Relationships - Load state" section with four entries — 🔗 not loaded yet, ✓ has relationships, – no relationships, ⚠ request failed — each with its row count. Checking one narrows the table to those rows, so in a large table with only a few relationships you can list the rows still waiting, the ones that actually have icons, or the ones whose request failed. It is offered on a collapsed column too, where the collapsed note now says how many rows are already loaded, and its counts stay current as more rows load.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Relationships column: the ▶🔗 / ▼🔗 header toggle now shows how far the column has got — e.g. "340/2301" distinct entities loaded — updating as rows load by hand, in bulk or one by one, and disappearing once everything is loaded. A request that failed does not count as loaded, and the toggle's tooltip says how many failed.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Relationships column: on an artist's releases, release groups and works, a label's releases, a release group's and a recording's releases, and an area's labels, the column now asks MusicBrainz's Web Service for up to 100 rows per request instead of one request per row — about 24 requests instead of 2 300 for a large discography, i.e. under a minute instead of about 42 minutes when the service is not busy. The bulk answers carry the same relationships as per-row lookups (checked on 51 entities across these 7 page types) and go into the same cache, so other pages listing the same entities get them for free. Rows a bulk answer does not contain, such as a Various Artists view, are still looked up one by one, and bulk fetching stops by itself as soon as one-by-one would be cheaper. The completion toast says how many rows came from bulk requests.
New setting 'Relationships: fetch whole pages at once where MusicBrainz allows it' (sa_rel_browse_batch_enable, default on) switches bulk fetching off.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Relationships column: every cell now shows a small, faint glyph saying where that row stands — 🔗 not loaded yet, ⋯ queued (the column is still fetching), ◌ loading, – loaded but nothing with an icon, ⚠ the request failed. In a huge table where only a few rows have relationships, you can now see at a glance which rows have been looked up and which are still waiting, without the debug console.

Relationships column: click a cell to load just that row — one request — even while the column is collapsed; the rest of the table stays collapsed and untouched. Clicking a queued row while the column is still fetching gets it ahead of the queue, and clicking a failed (⚠) row retries it. On a loaded cell, hovering shows ⟳: clicking the cell outside its icons re-fetches that row, bypassing the cache. Rows loaded by hand survive filtering, sorting and multi-table re-renders, and emptying the column (▼🔗) while a row is still loading discards its late answer.

New setting 'Relationships: show a load-state glyph in each cell' (sa_rel_cell_state_glyphs, default on) hides the glyphs and turns click-to-load off. The glyphs are drawn purely by CSS, so filters, sorting, the 📊 dropdown, exports and Save to Disk never see them.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Relationships column: the icon writer and the failure marker moved out of the column's fetch pass into shared module-level functions (_relWriteResult, _relWriteFailure, _relMasterCellsFor), so a bulk pass and a single-row load write cells through the same idempotent code.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Relationships column: a failed MusicBrainz Web Service request (an HTTP 503 while the service is shedding load, or a network error) was shown exactly like 'this release has no relationships', and stayed that way for the rest of the session because the failure was cached in memory. A failed request is now retried up to 3 times with a widening backoff and is never cached; the cell is marked failed rather than done; it is not re-requested on every filter keystroke; and it is retried when the column is collapsed and expanded again, or with the 🔗⟳ retry buttons. The completion toast and status bar say how many requests failed.

Relationships column: every request, including retries, now waits on one shared one-per-second rate limit, and a lookup already answered from the in-memory cache no longer waits a second before being shown. The millisecond Length batch source shares the same retry code, with unchanged behaviour.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Settings: the 'Enable Relationships column' description no longer claims the column applies only to four page types (artist-releasegroups, artist-releases, label-releases, releasegroup-releases) — it applies to every page type that declares it, including collections, series, tag pages, reports and search results — and now says what the icons come from (URL relationships of the row's release, release group, label or work, plus release/release-group relationships that have an icon).

Statistics panel: the 'Rel WS2 TTL evictions' row said cached relationship records expire after a '7-day TTL'; the default has been 30 days all along. It now shows the configured 'Relationships IDB cache TTL (days)' (sa_rel_idb_ttl_days) value.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Live-recording date checks: the "(N) WARNING ⚠️" and "(N) ERROR ❌" summary buttons counted only the rows a filter happened to leave on screen, so any filter that hid the flagged tracks made the button vanish — taking away the only way back to them — and a filter that hid some of them quietly understated the count.
Both buttons now count the whole tracklist, so they stay available with their real numbers whatever is filtered, exactly as the track/recording length mismatch buttons already did.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt says the counts describe the whole tracklist rather than the filtered view.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 📊 "Structure" filters: after expanding or collapsing one cell, picking "▶ collapsed multi-row cells" (or "◀ expanded multi-row cells") again showed the rows from before the toggle — the count in the dropdown had already updated, so it read e.g. 45 while 46 rows stayed on screen.
Expanding a cell while one of those entries is filtering now removes that row, instead of leaving it listed under a state it no longer has.
The five places that record a cell's expand/collapse state are now one, so the dropdown counts and the filtered rows cannot drift apart again.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt: the Structure entries now state that they follow the ▶/◀ toggles live.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Locality/Region columns: when a separately-installed flag userscript ("More Flags Everywhere" and friends) marks a bare subdivision — a US state, a UK nation — the value moves from "Locality" to "Region" seconds after the table appears. Filters did not follow it: a "Region" filter typed and retyped afterwards still found only the rows that had that value before the move, and even a freshly typed one did, because each row was still being matched against its pre-move text.
A filter that is active when the move happens is now re-applied on its own, so rows stop being listed under a Locality value the move has taken away from them.
Only pages with split Locality/Region columns (events, performances, area listings) and only with such a userscript installed were affected.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt: the Locality/Region split now states that the move can happen seconds after the table appears and that an active filter is re-applied to the new values.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Release events column: filtering or sorting a table while the column was still loading made it come back EMPTY for the rows that were hidden at that moment — permanently, because the column is filled once per fetch. On a label's or place's relationships page, typing a country code into "Release country" before the data arrived and then clearing the filter left every one of those rows blank for the rest of the visit.

The same filter, retyped after the data arrived, also kept showing the pre-load result (no rows), because the rows it had already tested were remembered by what you had typed, and typing the same thing again reused that answer.
A filter left active while the column loads is now re-applied on its own once the values arrive, instead of leaving the table filtered on data that had not loaded yet.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt: the Release events section said "one WS2 call per release row"; it is one call for the page's own entity. Corrected, and it now states that filtering and sorting while the column loads is safe.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Global filter: typing a cover-art image type or comment — "Booklet", "Back", "Matrix/Runout" — found no rows on multi-table pages (a release group's releases, an artist's release groups, a tag listing, …), while the very same word found them with the Rx box ticked, or when typed into the CAA/EAA column's own filter box. Only the plain (non-regexp) global filter was affected, and only for artwork text; every other column matched normally.

Root cause: image types and comments are not visible cell text, and the plain global filter looked for them in the rendered copy of a row instead of in the row it actually tests — a distinction that only exists on multi-table pages. All three filter paths now read them through one shared lookup.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt now states that the global filter box searches image type/comment text too. CLAUDE.md records the resolver and why reading the artwork list element directly is wrong.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: ⏱ millisecond Length toggle: an active filter on the Length column — or a global filter for a length value — kept its old answer after pressing the toggle. Filtering "." then switching to milliseconds still showed no rows although every length now read e.g. "3:11.666"; filtering ".666" in milliseconds and switching back to seconds still showed the row, now reading "3:12". The toggle now makes every active filter re-test the new text.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: CLAUDE.md: the millisecond-precision notes now name all three caches the toggle must drop, and why. DEBUG-NOTES.md: dated root-cause entry with the fixture results and mutation outcomes.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 📊 "Structure - Inline artwork": on multi-table pages (a release group's releases, an artist's release groups, …) "🖼️ front-image available" and "∅ NO front-image available" filtered to ZERO rows while showing the right count. A typed "caa-inline-yes"/"caa-inline-no" column filter did the same. The thumbnail's settled state was only ever written to the rendered copy of a row, never to the row the filter actually tests.
