On single-table pages the same entries silently missed every row whose thumbnail finished loading AFTER you had sorted or filtered once — the entry counted it, the table did not show it.

Picking the same inline-artwork entry again, or the same "CAA info - Type" entry (e.g. "» image type: Front"), after more artwork had loaded replayed the first pick's row list instead of re-testing: rows whose thumbnail or image metadata arrived in between were left out.

Root cause and fix: a settled thumbnail is now also recorded where the filter can read it (keyed by row and column, like the per-cell expand state), and the dropdown's counts read the same record, so a count and the rows it filters to cannot disagree. When artwork arrives late, only the cached filter results that can read artwork are dropped — typing an ordinary filter while artwork is still loading keeps its cache.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: CLAUDE.md: CAA/EAA section records why inline-art presence is matched through one resolver and not the cell's span, and the three guards not to undo. DEBUG-NOTES.md: dated root-cause entry with the fixture results and mutation outcomes. tests/MEASUREMENTS.org: the per-settle master-row lookup cost that ruled out mirroring the span, and the per-row cost the fix does add.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Load from Disk: restore the Relationships column for a file that was saved without it. Since 9.99.1086 such a table came back with a Relationships header but no Relationships cells — so every cell from that column rightward was shifted by one, putting the Picard button under the Relationships header, and no icons, no ▶🔗 toggle and no collapsed-column filter hint were ever built. Files saved WITH the column already populated were unaffected, as were normal (non-disk) page loads.

Root cause: the three places that BUILD the column were gated on a Relationships cell already existing in the page, but on the Load-from-Disk and "Show single-table" paths those cells are created by the very function being gated — so the check could only ever be false for exactly the files that needed it. The gate now also accepts "this page type declares the column", which is what the disk path knows before the cells exist. The places that merely act on an already-rendered column keep the stricter check they were given in 9.99.1086.

This makes the script agree with its own documentation again: ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt already stated that a disk round-trip is network-free only when every Relationships cell was fully populated at save time, and that saving a collapsed column saves it empty.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: DEBUG-NOTES.md: dated root-cause entry with the bisect (the parent commit renders 2090 icons and 22 header cells against 22 body cells; the next commit renders 0 and 22 against 21), the blast radius, and why no existing test caught it — the one committed disk fixture that carries relationship data is also the only one any relationship-aware spec loads.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Relationships column: on release listings that have a Label column — an artist's releases, a release group's releases, a recording's releases and similar pages — every row was looked up as a LABEL (/ws/2/label/<release id>) instead of as a release, so the column showed no relationship icons at all. The row's own record-label link was mistaken for the entity the row stands for. Release rows are now always looked up as releases; work- and label-targeted sub-tables on relationship pages are still detected as before.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Unique-values (📊) dropdown debug logging (see 9.99.1087/9.99.1089/9.99.1090): the 'Uniq-drop col N' debug lines from those fixes are now gated behind their own dedicated setting, 'Enable unique-values dropdown debug logging' (sa_enable_uniq_drop_context_debug, default off) — off means none of these lines appear at all, independent of every other channel the 'Enable debug logging' master switch controls; on means each line always carries the real column name and the owning table's name (page h2 in single-table mode, sub-table h3 in multi-table mode), with no 'on, without context' variant. Still requires 'Enable debug logging' to also be active.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values (📊) dropdown: replaced the per-item-count formula estimating the panel's needed height with a real measurement of its own rendered content (drop.scrollHeight). The formula assumed a flat +50px of section-header overhead regardless of how many distinct synBox sections actually rendered — measured live: a 'Date' column with 4 sections estimated 262px against a real 849px, capping the panel far below what the viewport had room for and forcing an unnecessary internal scrollbar (reported on 'Artist'/'Length'/'Recording date' columns). Since the panel's content is already fully built by the time this positioning code runs, scrollHeight can't drift from actual layout the way a formula can.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values (📊) dropdown: fixed the panel, when opening UPWARD (see 9.99.1087), sizing itself to fill ALL available space above the button instead of to what its own content actually needed — on a real release-tracks page this pushed a 13-value column's panel flush against the top of the page, dozens of rows away from the header it belonged to, whenever spaceAbove was generous (worsened by a user-raised sa_uniq_dropdown_visible_rows, which widens the cap that used to be the limiting factor). Now caps max-height to the content's own estimated height too, not just the cap and the available space, so the panel opens close to its button.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: artist-recordings: removed the native 'Showing all recordings (Show only standalone recordings / Show only videos)' paragraph — redundant with this script's own '⊚ All recordings'/'♫ Standalone'/'🎬 Video' toolbar buttons.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values (📊) dropdown: fixed the panel getting silently clipped past the bottom of the browser window when a column header sits low enough on screen that neither the space above nor below it can hold the panel's full natural height. The old 'flip upward' logic only fired when the WHOLE panel fit above the button; otherwise it fell through to opening downward with no clamp at all, and since the panel is position:fixed on document.body, the overflow was genuinely invisible rather than reachable by scrolling. Now clamps the panel's max-height to whichever side (above/below) actually has more room, so its existing internal scrollbar takes over instead.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Relationships column: fixed it also missing on /user/<user>/ratings (Labels/Release groups/Works), on artist-credit pages (Release groups/Releases), and on artist-relationships/label-relationships/place-performances' work/label-targeted sub-tables — three more instances of 9.99.1085's 'a shared value read after whichever group ran last' bug family, one of them a genuinely new mechanism for pages with no entityFeatures map at all (grouped by relationship type, not entity kind).

Fixed a page-wide instance of the same bug: several functions (_relInitColHeaderToggles, _relPublishCollapsedStatus, _initRelationshipsColumnImpl's own entry guard, _relCreateRetryButtons, both initRelationshipsColumn() call sites) gated on the shared activeInjectedColumns.length to decide whether the PAGE has a Relationships column at all — since that variable reflects whichever group's rebuild ran last, a page whose last-processed group declares no injectedColumns (e.g. artist-credit's 'Recordings') silently skipped the WS2 fetch, the toggles, and the retry buttons for the WHOLE page, even though earlier groups' tables genuinely have the column. Replaced with a DOM-based check (does any td.mb-rel-cell exist).

artist-credit: 'Recordings' was also missing its own Video/Event-* column headers entirely (cloning whichever group's header the fetch loop processed last instead of its own) — renderGroupedTable()'s per-group <thead> rebuild was missing 'artist-credit' from its pageType list even though the fetch-loop's equivalent rebuild already covered it.

_suppressRelationshipsIfNoReleaseOrReleaseGroupLinks() now dynamically sniffs a table's own /work/ or /label/ link (for pageTypes with no entityFeatures map to resolve an entity-kind hint from) instead of relying on a page-wide default that never varies per sub-table — scoped to pageTypes with no entityFeatures map so it cannot second-guess an already-correctly-resolved entityType (a release listing's own 'Label' record-label credit column briefly caused a regression here, caught by the existing rel-ws2-seed-warm-cache regression test).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Relationships column: fixed two stacked bugs that hid it on release-group/release/label/work tables. On tag-value/user-tag-value pages (/tag/<value>, /user/<user>/tag/<value>), activeInjectedColumns was resolved exactly ONCE, page-wide, from whichever entityFeatures key the page's own <h2> happened to match — and since that heading ("Entities tagged as X") never matches any per-entity key, resolution always fell back to the first declared key ('Areas', which declares no injectedColumns), hiding the column across the WHOLE page including 'Release groups'/'Releases' groups that DO declare it. buildActiveInjectedColumns() also picked the WS2 entityType from a pageType-string switch alone (defaulting to 'release' for anything not artist-releasegroups/artist-works), which can't distinguish 'Release groups' from 'Labels' from 'Works' when they share one pageType. Both the per-group column-presence rebuild AND the per-group entity-type resolution (fetch loop, render-time header build, and the Relationships fetch pipeline itself) now key off each group's own resolved entity kind, so Labels/Release groups/Releases/Works each get the column and query their own correct WS2 entity type simultaneously on the same page.

Relationships column: added it to area-labels, area-works/area-works-filtered, collections-releases ('Labels'/'Works'), series-releases ('Works'), search ('Labels'/'Works'), and — dynamically, per report, based on the report's own main column — the whole report-multiple-linked/report-detail family (e.g. ASINsWithMultipleReleases, DiscogsLinksWithMultipleReleaseGroups). A report whose main column isn't Release/Release group/Label/Work (Recording, Artist, Place, Collaborator, …) correctly gets no column at all rather than defaulting to 'release'.

_extractMbidFromRow() now also recognizes /label/<mbid> links, and _suppressRelationshipsIfNoReleaseOrReleaseGroupLinks() no longer wrongly strips the column from a Labels table — its only entity link lives in the sticky title column, the same reason 'work' was already exempted.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: tag-value/user-tag-value: a sub-table category that DOES have a native "See all N …" overflow link (e.g. Events) got a redundant "Show single-table" button rendered alongside its correct "Show all N rows" one (see 9.99.1083). Both button-insertion sites gated on group.seeAllUrl alone, which is only the field name artist-relationships/label-relationships/place-performances-style pages use — tag-value/user-tag-value set group.tagSeeAllUrl instead. Fixed by also checking !group.tagSeeAllUrl/!group.ratingsViewAllUrl at both sites.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: tag-value/user-tag-value: sub-tables without a native MusicBrainz overflow link (e.g. Areas, Instruments, Labels, Places, Series, Works on most tags) never got a "Show single-table" button, since that pageType pair was simply absent from the button's hardcoded allow-list. Added them, plus a new category→entity-slug map so the new tab routes to the tag-value-entity/user-tag-value-entity single-table sibling via the correct singular MusicBrainz URL segment (e.g. "Release groups" → /tag/<value>/release-group).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: tag-value/user-tag-value/user-ratings/instrument-list/artist-credit: a group whose own entityFeatures was empty (e.g. tag-value's Areas/Artists/Series/Works) could silently inherit a PREVIOUS group's synthetic-column extractor, since the shared active extractor registries were only rebuilt when the current group's entityFeatures was non-empty. On /tag/<value> this made Areas/Artists render their entity name/comment under Event-Type/Event-Date/Event-Detail instead of MB-Name/Comment, and made Series/Works grow a spurious Event-Additional-Info column duplicating Comment. Instruments/Labels/Places happened to inherit a harmless no-op extractor instead, masking that they were leaked too. Fixed by always rebuilding the active extractor registries per group, collapsing back to the page-level feature baseline when a group has no entity-specific overrides of its own.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks/many pageTypes: "Event-Date" (the synthetic column produced by the `eventParts` extractor, e.g. release-tracks' live-performance "Disambiguation" parsing, or work-recordings'/artist-relationships' "Comment" parsing) never showed the "Date info - Precision/Decade/Month/Year/Weekday" section family, because `_dateExprColumnNames()` only ever collected names from `dateParts`/`dateTimeParts` entries, never `eventParts`. Also extended the shared date-token match to recognize `eventParts`' own uncertain-day "YYYY-MM-DD/DD" shape (MusicBrainz's "recorded on one of these days" convention) as a complete date with no single resolvable weekday, rather than not matching it at all.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks: the "Recorded at event" column's 📊 dropdown never showed the "Date info - Precision/Decade/Month/Year/Weekday" section family every other date-bearing column gets — the same gap the "Recording date" fix closed, but this column's own cell text is "<event name> (YYYY-MM-DD)", not a bare date, so `_findCellDateExpressionParts()` now also falls back to the cell's `.mb-credit-date` sentinel (the trailing date annotation) when the whole-cell text isn't itself a date expression.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks: the "Recording date" column's 📊 dropdown never showed the "Date info - Precision/Decade/Month/Year/Weekday" section family every other date-bearing column gets. That family is gated on a column's name appearing in a declarative `columnExtractors`/`syntheticColumnExtractors` entry with `extractor: 'dateParts'`, but "Recording date" is built entirely inside `applyExtractTrackTitleData()`'s bespoke AR-column pipeline, outside that mechanism, so it was never registered. Its `<th>`-creation site now also registers the name (with an empty `syntheticColumns`, so it can never inject an unwanted derived column) — the same "column whose existence isn't known at authoring time" registration pattern `_picardRegisterCollapsableColumn()` already uses.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The "Release info - Data quality" 📊 dropdown section never appeared on a relationship listing's "Title" column (e.g. an artist's Relationships tab) even when the relationship's target is a release carrying MusicBrainz's own native high/low-data-quality marker — the section's eligibility check was gated on the column being literally named "Release", which a relationship-target column never is (it can point to any entity kind, so MusicBrainz always calls it "Title"). The gate now also accepts "Title", additionally checking each cell's own native `<span class="releaselink">` marker so a relationship targeting a non-release entity is never miscounted as "normal quality".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks: the "Recording of work" cell rendered completely empty when the credited work currently has open/pending edits on musicbrainz.org. MusicBrainz wraps the work anchor one level deeper in its own native `<span class="mp">` open-edits marker in that case, which the `:scope > a` direct-child lookup didn't accept — the lookup now filters by `href^="/work/"` instead (mirroring `_recordedAtDdAnchor`'s existing fix for the equivalent name-variation-wrapping case), and clones the wrapping `<span class="mp">`/`<span class="name-variation">` (via the new shared `_outerCreditAnchorWrapper()`) so the pending-edits highlight survives into the cell too.

release-tracks: a track's own Title cell silently lost its pending-edits highlight (the recording name itself still rendered) whenever that recording currently has open/pending edits — the Title-cell rebuild in `applyExtractTrackTitleData()` moved back only the bare recording `<a>`, discarding the `<span class="mp">` wrapper it came from.

release-tracks: Performer/Vocals/Instruments/engineer-mixer-etc. credit columns (`_buildCreditListItem()`/`_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem()`) silently lost the pending-edits highlight for a credited artist with open/pending edits — the name rendered correctly either way, only the `<span class="mp">` marker was dropped from the clone.

release-tracks: the millisecond-length WS2 backfill (`_msStampFullReleaseRows()`) silently skipped a row entirely when that row's own recording currently has open/pending edits — its `:scope > a[href*="/recording/"]` lookup found nothing once the Title-cell fix above started preserving the `<span class="mp">` wrapper, so the row never got backfilled to millisecond precision even though the WS2 answer for it had arrived. New shared `_titleRecordingAnchor()` tolerates the wrapper while keeping the existing direct-child scoping (still required to avoid matching a nested `/recording/` link from an unrelated relationship like "DJ-mix of").

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Sorting the Relationships column did nothing: `_sortCellText()` returns '' for every relationship cell (its icons carry no visible text), so both comparators compared '' against '' regardless of icon count. `_sortColumnKind()` now classifies 'Relationships' as a new 'count' kind, sorted by the number of relationship icons (`.mb-rel-filter-key` spans) in each cell instead of cell text.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Every multi-row column grew a little wider on each click of a column's sort glyph — reported on a release page, where `release-tracks` declares 18 collapsable columns and the whole table crept sideways. `initCollapsableColumns()` measured the first `<li>` of each multi-row cell as `li.scrollWidth` with `white-space: nowrap`, and applied `that + 28` as `th.style.minWidth`. An `<li>` is a block box and MusicBrainz's own `<ul>`s carry `padding: 0`, so it fills its `<td>`'s content box exactly — and for a block box with no horizontal overflow `scrollWidth` returns `clientWidth`, i.e. the column's CURRENT rendered width rather than the item's own. A sort re-render reuses the existing `<thead>` untouched, so each click read back the width the previous click had forced, added 28 px and committed it: measured at +12 px per click per column on the reported page. The measurement is now `width: max-content`, which sizes to the content and is independent of the containing block — the same cure `_measureHeaderMinWidth()` already applies to the column drag floor.

A collapsable column's minimum width could never come back down. The value was only ever raised, and nothing cleared it, so a column stayed as wide as the widest first item it had ever rendered even after a filter removed that row. This feature's own floor is now stamped on the `<th>` as `data-mb-collapse-min-px` and released by the pass that recomputes it, so a fresh measurement replaces it. An auto-resize floor written to the same property is deliberately left alone — it is measured across the whole cell rather than its first item, is legitimately the larger of the two, and continues to win.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown's outside-click handler closed the panel and immediately reopened it when the click landed on the count badge (`.mb-col-uniq-count`) instead of the glyph (`.mb-col-uniq-btn`) — the glyph's own `pointer-events: none` made a click there resolve to the wrapper element, which the handler recognized, while the count badge (which must keep `pointer-events` for its tooltip) does not. A second click on the counter now closes the dropdown, matching the glyph.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `#sanojjonasRoot` (sanojjonas third-party userscript container) could survive on a fully-rendered `/series/<mbid>` page: the pageType whitelist gating its cleanup/late-injection watcher never included `series-releases`. Removed the whitelist entirely — cleanup now runs unconditionally on every page, so this bug class can't recur for the next page type sanojjonas decides to support.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The "Relationships" column is now loaded on demand on big listings, from a new ▶🔗/▼🔗 button in its own column header. Until you press it the column is there but empty, and — this is the point — NOTHING is fetched. That column asks MusicBrainz's Web Service about every distinct release, release group or work on the page, one request at a time with a mandatory one-second gap between them, so a 2 300-release artist page quietly spent about 42 minutes trickling requests in the background before you had even scrolled, whether or not you wanted the icons. Pressing ▶🔗 loads that one table; pressing ▼🔗 empties it again.

New setting "Relationships auto-collapse threshold (unique entities)" (`sa_rel_collapse_threshold`, default 200) decides which tables start collapsed. Small listings are unaffected and keep loading immediately, because at a dozen entities the whole thing costs a few seconds. Set it to 0 to never auto-collapse and get exactly the old behaviour back. The button is always available either way — the setting only chooses the starting state.

The decision is made per table, not per page, so on a multi-section page a small section can load itself while a large one waits for you. Multi-section pages also get a page-wide "▶🔗 Load all Relationships" / "▼🔗 Empty all Relationships" button next to the existing collapse-all, cover-art and Picard buttons.

Emptying a collapsed column keeps everything already fetched, in memory and in the browser cache, so pressing ▶🔗 again is instant and costs no requests at all. Only the "🔗⟳ Retry" buttons clear that data, which is what they are for.
A table restored from a saved snapshot always starts expanded, whatever the threshold says: its icons are already in the file, so there is nothing to save by hiding them.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: A collapsed Relationships column now says so instead of quietly matching nothing. Its column-filter box is tinted and reads "collapsed — press ▶🔗", its 📊 unique-values dropdown shows a "Collapsed — press ▶🔗 in the column header to load" line rather than an empty section, and the status bar reports "🔗Rels: collapsed" instead of claiming a completed load. Neither the filter box nor the dropdown starts the fetch — a glance at a dropdown should not be able to queue a multi-minute run.

The ▶🔗 tooltip says what pressing it will actually cost, in requests and in expected time (e.g. "12 distinct entities to look up, about 13 seconds"), so "load this" is never a blind choice between two seconds and forty minutes.

The six little controls that live in column headers — ▶🖼 cover art, ▶⏱ millisecond length, ▶♪ Picard, the new ▶🔗 Relationships, the ▶N▤ multi-row expander and the 📊 unique-values button — are now readable. They used to be drawn at 55-60% opacity directly on the header, which worked on the plain grey header they were designed for but not on the blue-grey one injected columns use: 🔗 renders as a blue-grey emoji, so the glyph and the header behind it were the same colour at the same lightness, and sorting the column made it worse rather than better by washing a warm tint over both. They now sit on a small light pill of their own, slightly larger, and the 🔗 and ⏱ glyphs are drawn as outlines instead of as colour emoji. That works on any header colour, including one you have changed yourself in the settings, and it makes them look pressable before you hover them.

The multi-row count in the ▶N▤ expander — the number telling you how many cells in that column have more than one row — is bigger. It was the smallest thing in the whole header: font sizes compound, so a count set to 0.82em inside a button set to 0.80em came out at two thirds the header's size. It is about 29% larger now, and still slightly smaller than the ▶ and ▤ around it. The 📊 button's own count went the same way — it was 0.72em at 60% opacity beside a 📊 glyph at 45%, which made the pair the faintest thing in the header; both are at full opacity now and the count is about 18% larger.

The ⇅ ▲ ▼ sort buttons in each column header are now drawn as ONE control instead of three loose glyphs: a single pill, divided into three segments by thin vertical rules, matching the other six header buttons. The currently-applied sort direction keeps exactly the green-on-yellow it always had — it just fills its whole segment now instead of sitting as a ragged patch behind the glyph, so a sorted column is easier to spot when scanning a wide table. Clicking, Ctrl+Click multi-sort, Alt+Click sort-by-length and the Ctrl+↑/↓/# shortcuts all behave exactly as before.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Relationship icons could be rendered SEVERAL TIMES in the same cell. The column fetches one entity per second in the background, and anything that asked it to load again while that was still running started a second background run over the rows the first had not reached yet — so both runs added their own copy of every icon. Two such overlaps gave two copies, three gave three. Typing in the filter box while the column was still loading was enough to trigger it. Each run now REPLACES a cell's icons instead of adding to them, so overlapping runs can no longer multiply anything, and a run whose rows are no longer waiting for it now stops instead of continuing to request data nobody is going to use.

Every keystroke in the filter box could kick off a redundant Relationships pass — re-reading three settings tables and walking every row of the page three times — on any page containing a row with no release, release group or work link at all. Such a row gets a Relationships cell that can never be filled, and the check for "is anything still unloaded?" counted it forever. The check now ignores cells that have nothing to look up, and skips collapsed tables entirely.

Dragging a column down to its minimum width could cut off the 📊 unique-values button at the right edge. The minimum was measured once, early in the page build — before the ▶🔗, ▶🖼 and ▶⏱ header buttons are added and before the unique-value counts have been computed — so it was smaller than the header actually needed and the column was allowed to become too narrow for its own contents. On a real page 20 of 21 columns were affected, the worst by 126 pixels. The minimum is now measured at the moment you start dragging, when everything in the header exists. This also fixes the opposite case: a column whose minimum had been recorded AFTER auto-resize widened it could not be narrowed at all (one measured at 765 pixels for a header needing 211).

The ⇅ ▲ ▼ sort control sat flush against the column name with no gap. The name is written with a trailing space, which used to provide it, but that space is trimmed by the browser because the name is an anonymous item inside a flex row — it went unnoticed while the glyphs were bare text sitting where the space had been, and showed up as soon as they gained a border. The gap is now a real margin.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Unique-values dropdown: the "Editor info" family (Deleted/Recorded name/Membership/Comment), previously scoped only to `*/annotations`' "Editor" column, now also applies to `/elections`' Candidate/Proposer/1st seconder/2nd seconder columns and `/election/<n>`'s Voter column, via a new `EDITOR_INFO_COLUMN_NAMES` Set (was a single fixed-name check).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: "Date info" family (see 9.99.1069) now also applies to `dateTimeParts`-derived pure-date synthetic columns, not just `dateParts`-fed ones — `_dateExprColumnNames()` extended to recognize a `dateTimeParts` entry's own date-only output column. New `Date`/`Start date`/`End date` → `dateTimeParts` wiring on `/election/<n>` ("Date" → "Vote date"/"Vote time") and `/elections` ("Start date"/"End date" → "Election start/end date"/"time"). This also fixes `*/annotations`' existing "Revision date" column, which previously got NO "Date info" sections at all since the gate only recognized `dateParts`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown: the "Date info" family gains two new sections, "- Year" (exact calendar year) and "- Weekday" (COMPUTED day-of-week, via `Date.prototype.getDay()` — contrast with the unrelated, third-party-scraped "Release events - Weekday"), via new `_dateAtomYear()`/`_dateAtomWeekday()` bucketers alongside the existing `_dateAtomDecade()`/`_dateAtomMonth()`. `_highlightDateAtomMatch()` extended to highlight the matching YYYY substring for Year (same mechanism as Decade) and the whole matching date atom for Weekday (since the weekday name is never literal cell text).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown: `top-cd-stub`'s Title column gets two new sections, "Title info - Added" and "Title info - Modified" — one entry per distinct "N <unit> ago" age phrase, decomposed from the row's own `.comment` span ("Added N ago, last modified M ago") via a new `_findCellTitleAgeParts()` extractor. Deliberately not built on the generic `comment:`/`entityComment` machinery — a `/cdstub/<hash>` href is never recognized as an entity ref (`cdstub` is absent from `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH`), and the two facets (Added vs. Modified) need independent tracking. A new `_highlightTitleAgeMatch()` uses lookbehind/lookahead anchoring so an identical Added/Modified phrase (e.g. both "9 years ago") highlights only the matching half.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown: "Catalog info - Prefix" (the "Catalog#" column) silently dropped the prefix for any real-world catalog number ending in embedded punctuation with no space (e.g. "SOPL-248"), separated by a bare hyphen/dot/slash instead of whitespace ("40-32210", "138.645", "746.225/2-032210"), or with no separator at all ("CDCBS65480") — `_findCellCatalogParts()`'s old `/^(?:(.+?)\s+)?(\d+)$/` grammar required the entire trailing portion to be pure digits with whitespace separation. Replaced with a first-digit-index split that recovers all of these shapes while reproducing identical output for every shape that already worked. A multi-word prefix (e.g. "CBS S") is now also split on internal whitespace into independent TOKENS — "CBS" and "S" each become their own separately filterable dropdown entry, since a short token like "S" recurs across unrelated labels and is independently meaningful; `_highlightCatalogPrefixMatch()` is now word-boundary-anchored so checking a short token never lights up a substring inside an unrelated prefix (e.g. "S" inside "CDCBS").

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Unique-values dropdown: every "Catalog info - Prefix" entry now carries a generic explanatory tooltip on hover, covering catalog-number anatomy (prefix/main number/suffix, non-standardized separators) and the historical — but explicitly non-universal — "S"/"M" stereo/mono letter convention. One static explanation for every entry; no per-prefix lookup table, since no reliable source maps specific letter codes to specific label meanings.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown: `artist-works`' "Attributes" column (MusicBrainz's own identifier-badge shape — ACAM ID, SUISA ID, BUMA/STEMRA ID, PRS tune code, …) gets a new "Attributes - Identifier type" section — one entry per identifier TYPE, via a new `_findCellWorkAttributeIdentifiers()` extractor. Deliberately a distinct label/glyph from the existing "Attributes" section (free-text recording-attribute words like "live"/"cover") and gated by DOM shape (`.work-attribute` badges), not column name, so the two families never collide even though both can appear under a column literally named "Attributes". Reads the live, already-`expandShowAllCells()`-expanded DOM, so a truncated cell's hidden identifiers (behind MusicBrainz's own "(show N more)" placeholder) are still fully counted.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown: the native "Attributes" column (work-recordings, artist-relationships, place-performances, area-recordings, …) gets a new "Attributes" section — one entry per atomic recording-attribute word (e.g. "live", "cover", "partial"), decomposed from MusicBrainz's own natural-language-joined cell text (e.g. "cover and live") via a new `_findCellRecordingAttributeWords()` extractor, reusing the existing `REC_OF_ATTRIBUTES` vocabulary.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown: `/series/{mbid}` links (e.g. a user's "Series subscriptions" table) never surfaced an "Entity info - Series name"/"- Comment" section, even when carrying a real disambiguation comment (e.g. "3CD (Sony Music)") — `series` was absent from `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH`, so `_findCellEntityRefs()` silently returned nothing for every series cell.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `/cdstub/browse`: the duplicate-row fix from the previous release could leak a skipped duplicate's "Added N years ago..." text onto an unrelated, earlier row's Title cell (via unbounded appendChild), instead of dropping it along with the duplicate row it belonged to — on a real fetch, one row accumulated over 44,000 characters this way, making its column render artificially wide.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `/cdstub/browse`: the same CD stub could appear twice in the consolidated table. This listing ranks by a live, constantly-changing lookup count with no stable secondary sort key, so two page fetches a few seconds apart can return heavily overlapping results (measured ~90% overlap between page 1 and page 2) — an upstream ranking artifact, not something sorting introduced (sorting only made the pre-existing, scattered duplicates collate together and become visible). Rows are now deduplicated by their Title link as they're fetched.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `/cdstub/browse` ("Top CD stubs"): the native "Added N years ago, last modified M years ago" info row's text was landing in the "Primary alias" column instead of "Comment" — extractMainColumn always appends MB-Name/Comment/Primary alias in that order, so Primary alias (not Comment) is the row's real last cell.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown's own quickfilter search box highlighted only the FIRST occurrence of the typed substring inside each entry's label (e.g. typing "as" against "» alias: Southside Johnny & The Asbury Jukes at The Stone Pony" highlighted "as" in "alias" but not "As" in "Asbury"), unlike the main table's global/column filter, which always highlights every occurrence. Fixed for all three affected entry shapes — synthetic entries ("» alias:", "» comment:", etc.), plain unique-value list entries, and flag-icon (Country/Area) entries — via one shared helper.

sections.label: ⚡ Performance
items: Typing in a filter, clearing one, and sorting are all substantially less work per pass. The internal pass that resets each cell's transient state before it is re-rendered (`_stripTransientCellState`) used to make about a dozen separate searches of every cell — one per feature it might have to clean up (cover-art markers, expand buttons, collapse toggles, icon backgrounds, inline thumbnails, three kinds of cache-hint overlay, the ▶ release-expand buttons, and a link sweep) — and each of those searched the whole cell again, whether or not the page has that feature at all. It now searches each cell ONCE and sorts what it finds, and skips the search entirely for a cell that contains no elements, which most cells do. Measured: on a 4174-row × 21-column single-table page one filter clear went from 1 079 876 element searches to 83 680 (−92%), and on a 2143-row page split across 47 sub-sections from 323 422 to 107 099 (−67%). The cell-by-cell behaviour is unchanged, which a new test pins family by family, and every other kind of DOM work the same pass does came out identical to the digit.
The measured page had cover art switched off entirely and still paid every cover-art search — the cost was not doing the work, it was asking a dozen times per cell whether there was any.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Unique-values dropdown: renamed the 'Roles' section (SYN_SECTION_META's `roles` entry, exact-combined-role-string match) to 'Entity info - Role (combined)' — it was the only label in the table breaking the "Topic - Capitalized subtopic" naming convention, which made it read as an unexplained duplicate of the sibling 'Entity info - Role' (decomposed, OR-matching) section next to it on any Artist column carrying role credits (e.g. a place's /events page). No behavior change — both sections keep their distinct filter semantics.

Unique-values dropdown: renamed 'Event info - Event date'/'Event info - Event cancelled' (SYN_SECTION_META's `eventInfo`/`eventCancelled` entries, e.g. a user's own /ratings/event/ page's Event column) to 'Event info - Date'/'Event info - Cancelled' — dropped the redundant repeated "Event" word after the dash, since the section's own topic prefix already says "Event info". Left the unrelated 'Entity info - Event name'/'Entity info - Event cancelled' entries (a different topic family, sibling of Entity info - Artist name/Label name/etc.) untouched — they already follow the entity_* family's own established convention of repeating the entity-type word.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The "Picard" column now has a ▶♪/▼♪ toggle in its own column header, and ships COLLAPSED: the column and its cells are always there, but the ♪ buttons are built only when you press it. Each table has its own toggle and controls only its own cells, so on a multi-section page you can open the ♪ buttons for the one section you are tagging and leave the rest empty. Multi-section pages also get a page-wide "▶♪ Show all Picard" button in the action bar, next to the existing Collapse-all and CAA/EAA all-buttons.

New setting "Start the Picard column collapsed" (🎵 PICARD TAGGER, default ON). Building the ♪ buttons means walking every row for taggable entities, on the initial render and again on every filter keystroke and every sort; leaving this on keeps that cost off pages where you are not tagging. Turning it OFF reproduces the previous behaviour exactly — every button built during the render — while keeping the header toggle available. It decides the STARTING state only; the master "Enable Picard Tagger column" switch is still what adds or removes the column.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: While the Picard column is collapsed, a filter keystroke or a sort no longer drops the 📊 unique-values dropdown's cached per-table data (and with it the column-header count cache). That cache was being invalidated on every render pass on the grounds that the Picard cells had just been rebuilt; a collapsed column rebuilds nothing, so there is nothing for the cache to have missed.

The "Enable Picard Tagger column" setting's description no longer lists a set of supported page types. The guard became purely data-driven some time ago — a table gets the column when its body contains at least one /release/<mbid> link, whatever page it is on — and the old list said otherwise.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Column-name resolution no longer reads the "Picard" header as "Picard▶3▤" once that column has multi-row cells. The per-column multi-row header button is appended directly to that <th> (it is the one header with no flex layout to insert into) and was not being stripped, so any consumer resolving the column name while the button was present got the glyphs with it. Latent until now — the collapse pass removes the button before its own name lookup — but it is what a text glyph in the new toggle would have turned into a real breakage, which is why that glyph comes from CSS instead.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt: new "PICARD TAGGER COLUMN" section — the release-link guard, the per-table and page-wide toggles, the new default, and the previously undocumented host/port settings. 🎵 PICARD TAGGER added to HELP's settings list. The cross-tab snapshot section no longer claims the Picard icons "work identically to the live page": the capture strips the whole column, so the destination tab applies its own default.

ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt now says explicitly that a release's own tracklist gets NO Picard column: the guard asks whether a table's body links a /release/<mbid>, and a tracklist's rows link recordings. Nothing changed there — it was simply never written down, and the plan for this work had assumed otherwise.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Multi-table pages (release-group releases, series releases, tag/user-tag value listings, artist-relationships, …) no longer lose the whole "Picard" column the moment anything re-renders. The ♪ buttons appeared on the initial render and then vanished on the first global-filter keystroke or sub-table sort, while the "Picard" header stayed put — leaving the affected sub-table one column short of its own header. The Picard cell is now given to the captured SOURCE rows as well as the live ones, in BOTH table modes, so every re-render clones it along with the row.

Sorting one sub-table no longer needlessly rebuilds the ♪ buttons of every OTHER sub-table. Only cells that were actually re-cloned are re-wired, which is the scoped-render behaviour the rest of the table already had.

Switching discography view (Complete / Official / Non-Official / merged) now re-wires the ♪ buttons it re-renders. That code path re-populates sub-tables without going through the normal render, so its buttons were previously left inert.

The "Release events" and "Relationships" placeholder cells can no longer be inserted to the RIGHT of the Picard cell, which would have swapped those columns' data against their headers. Both now anchor on the Picard cell the same way the injected-column cells already did.

A Load-from-Disk after a live fetch in the same session no longer leaves the "Picard" header missing while every row still gets a Picard cell, and a second full render can no longer inject a duplicate "Picard" header. Either one desynced the header and body column counts, which in turn produced a stray column-filter input.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "More Flags Everywhere": an area anchor with no flag of its own (e.g. a neighbourhood/city not in that userscript's region map, like "Midtown Manhattan" or "Gelsenkirchen"), chained immediately before a DIFFERENT, flagged area anchor, no longer wrongly "borrows" that neighbour's flag icon into its own Locality cell. Region correctly keeps both distinct areas, each with its own correct icon.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The synthetic "Locality"/"Region" columns (split from "Location") could render the same area's flag/subdivision icon in a DIFFERENT order on different rows — e.g. "Praha" with the icon before the name on one row and after it on another. Root cause: a race between this script's own synchronous extraction and a flag-decorating userscript's asynchronous, continuous re-scanning of the page for undecorated `/area/` anchors — including anchors this script had just cloned into its own synthetic columns. Fixed two ways: `_routeAreaLink()` now always renders the area name BEFORE its icon (matching the dropdown's own "name, then flag" convention), and stamps the cloned anchor with the same `data-flag-processed` marker "MusicBrainz: More Flags Everywhere" and "Right Side Flags Everywhere" both already check, so neither script re-decorates it afterward in a different order. `_findAreaLinkIcon()` was widened to recognize an icon on either side of the anchor, since it now needs to recognize its own reordered output as readily as a live source page's native placement.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "MusicBrainz: Right Side Flags Everywhere" wraps a country's area anchor in its own `span.mfe-flag-wrapper` and, when that anchor already sat inside a native `<span class="flag flag-XX">`, explicitly neutralizes that native flag's background rather than removing the now-empty span. `_findAreaLinkIcon()` checked the (now hollow) native flag ancestor before RSFE's own wrapper, so the dropdown's "Entity info - Area name" trailing icon — and the cell-preview row's icon segments — showed a blank/duplicate flag in front of the name instead of RSFE's real icon after it. Fixed by checking RSFE's wrapper first. Separately, `_buildFlagSegmentsForRoot()`'s `iconSel` used a bare `span[class*="flag-"]` substring check, which also accidentally matched RSFE's own `mfe-flag-wrapper` class (it merely contains the characters "flag-"), adding a second bogus icon segment; tightened to require the literal `flag` class token, and to skip a native flag span RSFE has already hollowed out via `:not(:has(...))`.

The unique-values dropdown's cell-preview row could also render a country name with an artificial space in the middle (e.g. "Israel" → "Isra el") when a partial column-filter match highlighted part of it, splitting one logical word across two adjacent DOM text nodes that `_buildFlagSegmentsForRoot()`'s `textParts.join(' ')` then joined with a synthetic space. `getCleanColumnText()` already solves this exact class of bug (clone + unwrap the highlight/`.mb-ic-wrap` spans + `.normalize()`), but that function's text-only approach can't be reused directly here since flag-icon baking needs `getComputedStyle()` on the LIVE, attached elements. Fixed by baking every icon from the live root first (in document order), then walking a normalized clone for text only and consuming the pre-baked icons by position — icon-matching elements never overlap the unwrapped selectors, so their count and order are unaffected by the clone.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A `<div id="sanojjonasRoot">` (a third-party userscript's container) could survive indefinitely on a fully-rendered `artist-events`/`area-events`/`place-events` page. Root cause: the guard on both sanojjonas-cleanup call sites checked `pageType === 'events'`, a value that never actually occurs — `pageDefinitions` only ever assigns `'artist-events'`/`'area-events'`/`'place-events'`. This silently disarmed `_watchForLateSanojjonasInjections()`'s MutationObserver on every real events page, the one mechanism that catches sanojjonas injecting its container AFTER this script's own one-shot cleanup has already run. Both call sites now go through a single `_shouldCleanupSanojjonas()` helper checking the real pageType values.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown's "Entity info - Area name" section only ever showed a trailing flag for the country-level area (e.g. "Spain"), never a subdivision (e.g. "Catalunya"), even with a flag-decorating userscript installed. Root cause: the icon-detection logic only recognized the OLD `span.area-icon` shape, not "MusicBrainz: More Flags Everywhere"'s current `span.custom-area-icon` shape or "MusicBrainz: Right Side Flags Everywhere"'s `span.mfe-flag-wrapper` + trailing `img.mb-hq-flag-img` shape. A new shared `_findAreaLinkIcon()` helper now recognizes all three shapes (plus the native country flag), used consistently by the table's own area-chain rendering, the entity-info dropdown population, and the dropdown's cell preview icons — so a subdivision now renders "[glyph] » area name: Catalunya [icon]" whenever either userscript decorates it.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown's "Entity info - Area name" section rendered a country's real flag icon in place of the generic area glyph, and before the name (e.g. "[flag] » area name: Spain"). The generic glyph is now always shown, and the flag — when the area has one — is appended after the name instead: "[glyph] » area name: Spain [flag]".

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Column-header count badges (the unique-value count before 📊 and the ▶N▤ multi-row count) are now memoized per table and only recomputed when the set of visible rows actually changes. On a 4174-row, 21-column page that scan is roughly 88 000 cell-text extractions; restoring the full table after clearing a column filter measured 29% faster (12.6 s → 8.9 s). Implements PERFORMANCE.org Step 3.
The cache key is deliberately order-independent, so re-sorting a column is a cache hit: a sort changes row order and never the row set, and the counts do not depend on order.
The last four row sets are kept rather than only the most recent one, so the filter → clear → filter cycle hits on every leg instead of missing on all of them.

A scan that is superseded part-way through no longer records its partial result as the cached answer, so the columns it never reached are recomputed by the next pass instead of keeping a stale number for as long as the row set stays put.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On multi-table pages, only the last sub-table's column-header counts were ever computed. Every sub-table scheduled its own scan but they shared one cancellation token, so each new one silently aborted the previous sub-table's scan before it wrote a single badge — leaving, for example, 1 of 423 badges filled on an artist's release-groups page. The token is now per table. Implements PERFORMANCE.org Step 22.

The Locality→Region correction applied to flag-decorated area cells (which lands up to six seconds after the render, once a third-party flag userscript has decorated them) now invalidates the affected table's cached column data. Previously the unique-values dropdown and the column-header counts could keep serving values read before the correction moved them between columns.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Two long-lived project documents were renamed, and every live cross-reference to them inside the userscript's own comments and JSDoc was retargeted: `debug/NOTES.md` → `DEBUG-NOTES.md` (24 references) and `pageTypes-testing-reference.org` → `PAGETYPES-TESTING-REFERENCE.org` (1 reference). Comment-only; no runtime behaviour changes.

`DEBUG-NOTES.md` moved out of `debug/` deliberately. That directory is excluded by a bare `debug/` in the root `.gitignore`, and the file was tracked only because it had been force-added to the index — there is no `!` negation for it, and one could not work, since git never descends into an excluded directory. At the top level it no longer depends on that fragile arrangement.
Fixed a stale symbol name in a comment: `_msIdbPutLength` → `_msIdbPutLengths` (the function has been plural since it was written; the singular form appears nowhere in the code).
The changelog's own historical entries were deliberately left pointing at the old filenames — they describe what shipped at those versions, and rewriting them would falsify the record.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: CAA/EAA column: typing "no" or "yes" into the column's own filter box no longer secretly filters by artwork PRESENCE. It used to mean two unrelated things at once — the rows whose image types/comments really contain that text (e.g. "no" inside a "Matrix/Runout" type), PLUS every row with no artwork at all. Presence is now exclusively the unique-values dropdown's '✓ has artwork' / '✗ no artwork' entries; a typed filter matches only what the cell actually says.

This also removes an inconsistency between the plain and regexp filter modes: the sentinel shortcut lived only in the non-regexp code path, so an anchored `^no$` matched nothing while a plain `no` matched presence. Both now agree.

CAA/EAA column: sorting now actually sorts. Ascending lists the rows WITHOUT artwork first, descending the rows WITH artwork first. Previously the column had no sort basis at all — its every element (the artwork icon, the count badge, the per-image rows, and the hidden presence sentinel) is excluded from the text the comparators read, so every row's sort value was the empty string, all rows compared equal, and clicking the header silently left the order untouched.

Both comparators now share one `_sortCellText()` resolver instead of each inlining the same text lookup — the same single-source-of-truth split `_sortColumnKind()` already exists to prevent. Deliberately scoped to the CAA/EAA presence sentinel: the "Video" and "Cancelled" columns' own sentinels are not excluded from the visible text, so they already sorted correctly and are left exactly as they were.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Corrected three JSDoc blocks that documented behaviour which had not happened since the artwork sort keys were first excluded from the extracted text (PERFORMANCE.org Step 21's own fix-shape list): the `caa` extractor's sortability claim and its inner `appendSortKey` note (both still said the sort keys were walked by `getCleanColumnText()`/`getCleanVisibleText()`), and `_artSetInlineSortKey()`'s claim that the strip pass excludes its class and that no bypass is required — both false; it is stripped, and it works only because of an explicit bypass.

Also corrected one stale PERFORMANCE.org cross-reference in `_visibleRowSetSignature()`'s JSDoc, which described Step 3 as "not part of this branch" — written while that helper itself lived on a branch.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown (📊) on a CAA/EAA column: every entry now actually filters. On `tableMode: 'multi'` pages (e.g. any release-group's release list) the panel listed entries with correct, non-zero count badges and clicking them narrowed to ZERO rows — '✓ has artwork', every 'CAA info - Type' / 'CAA info - Comment' entry, and every per-image '▤' item entry. '✗ no artwork' was the only one that worked.

Cause: the dropdown COUNTS from the live table rows, but `runFilter()` MATCHES against the source rows in `groupedRows`, which on multi-table pages are permanently separate DOM elements that never receive the async artwork markup (no `ul.mb-caa-art-ul`, no image `<li>`s, no type badges, no comment spans). Every matcher behind those entries is a DOM query against exactly that markup. '✗ no artwork' was right only by accident — a row with no artwork has nothing to find either way.

`_artSyncSearchTextToSourceRow()` now mirrors four structural facts onto the source cell alongside the flat search text it already carried (image-`<li>` count, per-`<li>` texts, distinct type labels, distinct comments), read back through the new single-parser `_findCellSyncedArtFacts()`. `_classifyCollapseCell()` and the `arttype:`/`artcomment:`/`▤` matchers consult it only when their live-DOM query comes up empty — the same ordering `getCleanColumnText()` already used for the search text.
Typing a substring directly into a CAA/EAA column's filter input was already fixed earlier and is unchanged.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Removed the dead `injectedColumns: ['Relationships']` declaration from the `'Release groups'` entityFeatures block on `user-ratings`/`user-ratings-type` (see debug/user-rating-no-relationship.html — the column never rendered). No behavior change: the declaration was already inert, since `resolveEntityFeaturesFromH2()` resolves the page's FIRST entityFeatures key ('Artists', which declares no `injectedColumns`) at fetch time, and `renderGroupedTable()`'s per-group thead rebuild never re-derives `activeInjectedColumns`/`activeReleaseEventColumns` per group the way it does `activeColumnExtractors` etc. Even fixing that staleness wouldn't make the column correct here: `buildActiveInjectedColumns()` picks its WS2 entity type by pageType alone (user-ratings/-type fall through to its generic 'release' branch — wrong namespace for a release-group MBID), and `_initRelationshipsColumnImpl()`'s `_ensureRelCell` scans every `table.tbl` row on the page unconditionally, so a single resolved entityType would mis-tag every OTHER sub-table's rows (Artist/Event/Label/Place/Recording/Work ratings) as release-groups too. The 'Relationships' column's own setting description already scopes it to artist-releasegroups/artist-releases/label-releases/releasegroup-releases only; making it work on a multi-entity-type page like user-ratings would need a per-table-scoped redesign, not a bug fix.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The "Release group ratings" sub-table on `user-ratings`/`user-ratings-type` desynced every appended MB-Name/Comment/Primary-alias cell one position late — the release group's own name rendered under the "Comment" header instead of "MB-Name", which also meant the CAA hover tooltip's `tooltipColumns: ['MB-Name', 'Artist']` showed only the artist, never the release group's own name. Root cause: that entityFeatures block declared `columnExtractors: [{ sourceColumn: 'Release group', extractor: 'artistCredit', ... }]`, but Structure H's native `<li>`→`<table>` conversion for this entity type already splits "ReleaseGroup by Artist" into two NATIVE columns (Release group, Artist) — exactly like `'Recordings'`, which never declared this extractor for the same reason. The redundant extractor read the now-artist-free "Release group" cell, produced a permanently EMPTY synthetic "Artist" cell that was never excluded, leaving one extra unaccounted-for cell that shifted everything appended after it. Removed the extractor from both `user-ratings` and `user-ratings-type`; also reordered `tooltipColumns` to `['Artist', 'MB-Name']` per user request, so the hover tooltip now reads artist name first, then the release group's own name.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown's "Date info - Decade"/"- Month" sections were missing on `user-ratings`/`tag-value`/`user-tag-value`'s per-entity-type sub-tables (e.g. the "Event ratings" table's "Date" column) whenever more than one entity-type section with its own `entityFeatures` was present on the page. `openUniqDrop()`'s `isDateExprCol` gate read the shared `activeColumnExtractors`/`activeSyntheticColumnExtractors` module state, which `renderGroupedTable()`'s per-group rebuild leaves reflecting whichever group rendered LAST by the time a later click opens the dropdown — not necessarily the group the clicked column belongs to. `renderGroupedTable()` now also snapshots each group's own dateParts-fed column names onto `table.dataset.mbEntityDateExprColumns` (new `_dateExprColumnNames()`), mirroring the existing `mbEntityTooltipColumns`/`mbEntityExtractMainColumn` per-table annotations; `isDateExprCol` prefers that snapshot when present and falls back to the original check everywhere else, unchanged.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The CAA/EAA inline-thumbnail and big-picture-strip hover tooltip crashed with `TypeError: features.extractMainColumn.toLowerCase is not a function` and never appeared, on every pageType declaring `extractMainColumn` as a numeric column INDEX (`user-ratings`, `user-ratings-type`, `report-multiple-linked`, `tag-value`(-entity), `user-tag-value`(-entity)) rather than a column-name string. `_renderBigboxTooltipFromColumns()` now only reads `extractMainColumn` as a name when it actually is a string, treating the numeric form the same as "absent" (no tooltip spec entry can match a numeric marker by name) instead of crashing the whole hover handler.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On `tag-value-entity`/`tag-value`/`user-tag-value-entity`/`user-tag-value` pages (e.g. `/tag/rock/recording`), the "MB-Name", "Comment", and "Primary alias" columns rendered empty, with the recording's own name and disambiguation comment instead appearing as unlabeled trailing cells (see debug/tag-rock-recording-final.html). Root cause: `cleanupHeaders()` gated its `_resolvedPrimaryCols` set (which decides whether a `syntheticColumnExtractors` entry sourced from 'MB-Name'/'Comment'/'Primary alias', e.g. the `eventParts` extractor's nine `Event-*` columns, gets a header at all) on a plain truthy check of `features.extractMainColumn` — but these four pageTypes declare it as the numeric index `0` (their single native column is always first), which is falsy even though genuinely active. A second, correct check 30-odd lines below the same function already used strict `!== undefined && !== null` and DID inject the MB-Name/Comment/Primary-alias headers themselves — so the header row ended up 9 columns short of the row's actual cell count, and the browser's positional header/cell alignment shifted every column from "Artist" onward. Fixed by hoisting that one strict check to the top of the function and reusing it for both gates, so a single source of truth answers "is extractMainColumn active" consistently.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Sorting one sub-section on a multi-table page (artist discographies, release-group release lists, relationship pages, …) now rebuilds only that sub-table. Previously every sub-table on the page was torn down and re-created to re-order one — 124 rows across 3 sub-tables to sort a single 119-row one, or all 123 rows across 17 sections on an artist page.

Technical: the sort handler mutates exactly one `groupedRows[i].rows` array, then called `_invalidateFilterCache(); runFilter();`. The wholesale cache clear forced a full `testRowMatch()` membership pass over every row of every group even though a re-order cannot change which rows match, and `runFilter()` then re-cloned, re-stripped, re-highlighted and re-inserted all of them. New `_renderDirtyGroupIdxs` names the groups a sort actually disturbed; `runFilter()`'s multi branch skips the clone/strip/highlight pass for the rest, and `renderGroupedTable()`'s reuse branch leaves their `<tbody>` — and their whole per-group decorate pass, including `initCollapsableColumns()`'s full unique-value column scan — untouched.

New `_invalidateFilterCacheForGroups()` drops only the disturbed groups' cached match sets, and does so across ALL `discographyViewState` values rather than just the current one: the multi cache key is `m:<view>:<groupIdx>`, so keying on the current view alone would leave a pre-sort ordering cached under another view, ready to be resurrected on the next switch. Single-table sorts keep the wholesale invalidation — `allRows` is one array under one key, so there is nothing to narrow.

Merged discography view is the deliberate carve-out. It renders a category from the union of every same-category group, re-sorted through `mergedSortComparatorRegistry`, so `_sortDirtyGroupIdxs()` adds those co-contributors to the dirty set. Verified they cost nothing: they are the hidden duplicate tables whose rows are already folded into the visible one, so re-rendering them empties their `<tbody>` and inserts no rows at all — measured, not assumed.

The colon-alignment finalizers (`finalizeSplitAlignedColumns`/`finalizeRLCColumnWidths`) are skipped on a scoped pass. They measure one shared column width across the whole rendered row set, which a re-order does not change; running them against a `filteredArray` with the undisturbed groups emptied would have narrowed every column to what the sorted sub-table alone needs.

Measured: rows re-inserted by a sort went from 7 to 6 on the small pilot release group and from 124 to 119 on a 124-row/3-sub-table one. On the shape this is actually for — a 123-row artist discography across 17 sub-sections, sorting a 61-row one — 123 re-insertions became 61 and the sort went from a 114 ms median to 83 ms (3 runs each, same page, same section, toggled in place). Artwork is unaffected: icons and inline thumbnails still arrive already painted, and the sort still issues zero requests to the archive.

Side effect, found while checking why a saved file grew: the 📊 unique-value count badges and their tooltips now SURVIVE a sort of an unrelated sub-section instead of blanking back to a placeholder and being recomputed. `initCollapsableColumns()`'s per-column scan is part of the per-group work that is now skipped for an undisturbed table, and its counts were still correct — a sort changes a group's row ORDER, never its row set. Measured on a saved payload: 19 of 22 badges populated afterwards, against 0 of 22 before.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Inline cover-art thumbnails (the 20×20 image inside each Release/Title cell) no longer vanish and pop back on every sort or filter keystroke on multi-table page types (artist-releasegroups, releasegroup-releases, …). Rows re-inserted by a re-render now arrive with their thumbnail already showing. This completes the artwork-preservation work started in 9.99.1038, which covered the icon column only.

Technical: the icon fix could not cover this. Painting an icon writes a VALUE (`background-image`) onto a `span.caa-icon` the source row already owns, and `cloneNode(true)` carries values through; an inline thumbnail is a NODE (`.mb-caa-inline-ph` / `.mb-eaa-inline-ph`) that `_artInitInlinePics()` injects only into the live rows, so `groupedRows[i].rows` never held one and `_stripTransientCellState()`'s `preserveLiveArt` placeholder branch had nothing to match. New `_artMirrorInlineThumbToSourceRow()` mirrors the whole placeholder onto the matching source row, constructing it there rather than copying a value.

The mirrored placeholder rides through `renderGroupedTable()`'s row-insertion clone (which deliberately does not strip), so the live row arrives with the image in place and lands in `_artInitInlinePics()`'s Case C1 — hover preview and bigbox tooltip re-wired (`cloneNode(true)` copies no listeners), live image kept, nothing re-resolved. Measured: inline thumbnails present at row insertion went from 0 of 7 to 7 of 7 on the small pilot release group, and from 0 of 119 to 119 of 119 on a 124-row/3-sub-table one — with zero requests to the archive in both cases.

`_artResolveSourceCounterpart()` is split: its row/cell half becomes `_artResolveSourceCell()`, since the icon mirror resolves an element that already exists on the source row while the inline mirror has to build one. Both keep the `_findMasterRowByIdx()` lookup, which is what makes merged discography view work — it folds other groups' rows into the first-occurrence table, where a group-index lookup silently misses exactly those rows.

Placement matches the live injection: after the container's own `[data-erg-btn]` when there is one, else first. Source rows carry no ERG button (that feature injects into the live DOM), so the mirrored placeholder lands first — and on the next render `initExpandRGsFeature()` runs before the inline-thumbnail pass and prepends its ▶ ahead of it, giving the same order as a freshly built page.

No live `blob:` URL and no placeholder can reach a saved file: Save-to-Disk serialises through `getCleanCellHtml()` → `_stripTransientCellState()` WITHOUT `preserveLiveArt`, which removes both unconditionally. The `_hadInlineArtPh` jesus2099 gate cannot misfire on a mirrored cell either — `ColumnDataExtractor.caa`'s Path A MOVES a jesus2099 anchor into the synthetic "CAA" column, and no page definition ever names "CAA" as its `addCAA`/`addEAA` inline-thumbnail column, so the two are never in the same source cell.

Still not changed: sorting one sub-table re-renders all of them. It issues no network request — every row comes back carrying both its icon and its inline thumbnail — but the DOM work itself is still wasted.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: CAA/EAA artwork icons no longer blank out and repaint on every sort or filter keystroke on multi-table page types (artist-releasegroups, releasegroup-releases, artist-relationships, …). Rows re-inserted by a re-render now arrive with their thumbnails already in place.

Technical: on multi-table pages renderGroupedTable() always inserts clones, so artwork was painted onto the rendered clone while the source rows in groupedRows stayed blank — which made _stripTransientCellState()'s existing preserveLiveArt option a no-op on that path, since there was never anything on a clone to preserve. A new _artMirrorIconToSourceRow() mirrors a painted icon's background-image back onto the matching source row (same write-back shape as _artSyncSearchTextToSourceRow()), and the multi clone loop now opts into preserveLiveArt. Measured on a 17-sub-table artist-releasegroups page: icons already painted at row insertion went from 0 of 123 to 85 of 123 — every icon that had artwork.

The source-row lookup uses _findMasterRowByIdx() rather than the group-index lookup its sibling uses. Merged discography view combines several groups' rows into the first-occurrence table, so an index-based lookup silently misses exactly those rows and would drop their artwork.

Not changed: inline thumbnails are still rebuilt on a re-render (their placeholder is injected into live rows only, so a source row has no counterpart to mirror onto), and sorting one sub-table still re-renders all of them. Neither issues any network request — both repaint from the in-session memory cache.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Artwork that does not exist is no longer re-requested on every sort. A sort of a page with cover-art now issues ZERO requests to the archive: images that exist come from the session memory cache, absences are remembered, and the JSON metadata is already in `ctx.countCache`. Previously each re-render fired one doomed request per art-less entity — 20 of them per sort on the pilot page — each with a ⌛ the user watched until it failed.

Root cause: every tier of `_artFetchCachedImage()` recorded successes ONLY. The `_artIdbMemCache.set()` and `_artIdbPut('images', …)` lines sit *after* the `await` that throws, so a URL that 404s left no trace in memory, in IndexedDB, or anywhere else. "This artwork does not exist" and "this artwork has not been fetched yet" were therefore the same state — an absent memory entry — and the only possible response to an absent entry is to ask again.

New per-session negative cache (`_artMissCache`), the Tier-1 sibling of `_artIdbMemCache`, consulted immediately after it. Only a DEFINITIVE absence is recorded (HTTP 404/410, per `_ART_MISS_STATUSES`): a 5xx, network error or timeout is deliberately left uncached, because the Cover Art Archive fails in bursts and treating a bad minute as "this artwork does not exist" would hide real images for the rest of the session. This is the same distinction `_msFetchWs2RecordingLengths()` already draws between a successful-but-empty answer and a transport failure. `_artGmFetchBlob()` now carries the HTTP status on its rejection so the two can be told apart at all.

`_artInitBigPics()` additionally consults `ctx.countCache` before building a wrapper at all. `_artEnrichIcon()` has always stored a 0 there (and persisted it to IndexedDB) the moment the archive reports an entity has no images — with a comment about suppressing exactly these repeated requests — but the stripe builder never read it, and went on deriving a `front-{size}` URL for every anchor in the table regardless. Self-correcting by ordering rather than by guesswork: `_artInitBigPics()` runs BEFORE `_artEnrichTable()`, so the first render still attempts every entity exactly as before and only re-renders skip.

The two overlap deliberately, and each covers a case the other cannot. The URL-level miss cache catches an entity that HAS images but no front cover — its count is non-zero, so the metadata check would pass it through. The metadata check catches an art-less entity whose image URL answers 5xx rather than 404, which the miss cache must never record. Verified by mutation: with only the metadata check, one hourglass survives; with only the miss cache, the 5xx case rebuilds its wrapper on every render.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The ⟳ per-table retry button now clears `_artMissCache` wholesale. Its cache-busted `?_cb=…` URLs would sidestep the miss cache on their own, but the un-busted URL would stay marked missing afterwards — so a retry that actually recovered an image would have been undone by the next ordinary render.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The CAA/EAA big-picture image stripe no longer empties out to a row of ⌛ hourglasses on every sort, refilling a few images at a time. Unlike the icon column and the inline thumbnails, this strip legitimately IS rebuilt on each re-render — it has to follow the table's new row order — but every one of its images was then re-resolved through `_caaQueue`, waiting for one of `sa_caa_fetch_concurrency` slots even though the image was already sitting in the session memory cache. An image already resolved in that cache is now painted at build time, from a plain Map lookup with no I/O, and gets no hourglass. Only images that genuinely have to be fetched still show one — on a page with releases that have no cover art at all, those wrappers really are re-attempted (and removed again) on each render.

New `_artMemCachedObjectUrl()` answers "is this image already resolved in memory?" synchronously. `_artFetchCachedImage()` can only answer as a Promise, which is too late to decide whether to build a holding glyph in the first place.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `_artUpdateBigBoxForTable()` now counts bigbox images via an explicit `data-art-big-loaded` marker set by `_onBigLoaded()`, instead of inferring "has this image loaded" from `img.style.display === 'inline'`. The two were equivalent only while nothing could paint an image before its load callback ran; painting memory-cached images at build time broke that equivalence and inflated the per-table badge — and through it the page-wide global badge — after a sort with a sub-table filter active. Caught by `subtable-filter-sort-caa-interaction.spec.js`'s global-badge assertion.

The queued fetch task is still dispatched for every image, unchanged, including ones already painted. It is visually idempotent but keeps ALL the bookkeeping on its original schedule: the per-table badge increment, the render-generation guard, the STF-hidden check, the toggle-button thumbnail and the cache-hint overlay. That ordering is load-bearing — the global toggle button is created synchronously before any image resolves and its count is driven entirely by these callbacks — and an earlier attempt that let memory hits skip the queue outright double-counted against the wrong render generation.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Inline CAA/EAA thumbnails (the small images injected into the Release/Title column) no longer vanish and pop back on every sort and every filter keystroke on `tableMode: 'single'` pages. `_stripTransientCellState()` deleted each `.mb-caa-inline-ph`/`.mb-eaa-inline-ph` placeholder outright — taking its `` with it — and `_artInitInlinePics()` then re-injected and re-resolved every one of them. As with the icon column, nothing was re-fetched: the images came back out of the session memory cache. Under `preserveLiveArt`, a placeholder still showing an image from a live object URL is now kept.

The `done` marker (`data-caa-inline-done`) is deliberately still stripped, which is what makes the surviving placeholder correct rather than merely present. Keeping both marker and placeholder would land the cell in `_artInitInlinePics()`'s Case A — the "already processed, skip" branch, which does NOT re-wire — leaving a thumbnail that looks perfect but whose hover preview is dead, since `cloneNode(true)` copies no listeners. Stripping the marker routes the cell into Case C1 instead: re-wire hover and bigbox tooltip, keep the live image, skip the fetch, and only then stamp the marker. That branch already existed and already did exactly this; it was simply unreachable from the re-render path, because the placeholder it needs had been deleted a moment earlier.

New shared `_artIsLiveBlobUrl()` underpins both liveness checks (`_artIconBackgroundIsLiveBlob()` for the icon column's CSS background, `_artInlinePhIsLiveBlob()` for an inline placeholder's `.src`), so "is this object URL still ours" is answered in exactly one place.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Split `_artWireImageLi()` out of `_artBuildImageLi()`: the per-image art `<li>`'s broken-image handler, hover-preview popup and type-badge tooltip are now attached by a function that can be re-applied to an `<li>` that already exists. No behavioral change on its own — the builder calls it as its last step, so the same listeners land on the same elements as before. Groundwork for preserving art rows across a re-render instead of rebuilding them, which is impossible while the listeners close over `_artBuildImageLi()`'s locals.

The wiring now reads everything it needs back off the element (`data-li-tooltip-types`, `data-li-tooltip-comment`, and the new `data-li-big-src` hover-preview URL) rather than from the archive payload. The first two were already stamped; the third was trapped in the closure, and is the reason a cloned `<li>` could never be re-wired. It is stored regardless of `sa_caa_hover_preview`, so toggling that setting no longer implies rebuilding the cell from the archive response.

Deliberately no "already wired" marker: `cloneNode(true)` copies attributes but not listeners, so a marker would be inherited by every clone and report wiring that no longer exists — exactly the trap `_artInitInlinePics()`'s Case C1 documents for `hoverWiredAttr` and defuses by deleting the inherited value first. A clone is a fresh instance with no listeners, so re-wiring one is always correct.

Covered by new tests, since the per-image hover preview and type-badge tooltip previously had none at all — which made them the riskiest part of the extraction: the listeners are attached with `addEventListener`, so a broken split would leave the `<li>` looking completely correct and fail only on hover. Mutation-verified (disabling the wiring fails the new test and nothing else).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The "🎨 All CAA/EAA artwork loaded" toast no longer pops after every sort and every filter keystroke. `_artInitQueue()` resets `_caaFetchStats` at the start of each render pass, so those counters describe that pass alone — and a re-render re-enqueues every image but resolves all of them from the Tier-1 session memory cache. Announcing a completed load there told the user their artwork had just been re-downloaded when nothing had left the machine, which was a large part of why sorting *looked* like a reload. The toast is now shown only when the pass actually fetched something (`idb`/`network`/`browser` tiers; `memory` is the only no-cost tier — `browser` is the native `img.src` path and still hits the network stack). A pass that genuinely fetches — initial load, disk restore, newly-rendered rows — still reports exactly as before.

Setting `sa_caa_completion_toast_duration` to 0 no longer switches off three unrelated things. `_showCaaCompletionToast()` does four jobs, and the duration check was an early return at the very top, so disabling a cosmetic toast also disabled the `#mb-info-display-caa` status-bar segment, the one-time global status summary and the Statistics-panel refresh — and with them the completion signal the Playwright harness waits on (`waitForCaaEaaComplete()`). Those three now always run; the setting gates the toast alone. The Relationships sibling (`sa_rel_completion_toast_duration`) already had this ordering right, writing `#mb-info-display-rel` before its own early return — this brings CAA/EAA in line with it.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The CAA/EAA icon column no longer flashes empty on every sort and every filter keystroke on `tableMode: 'single'` pages. Sorting a column is not a DOM reorder — it re-enters `runFilter()`, which re-clones every row and ran `_stripTransientCellState()` over each one, and that helper unconditionally removed the `background-image` from every artwork icon. The icon was then immediately repainted with the *identical* object URL, served from the session's Tier-1 in-memory cache — no network request, no new blob, nothing actually re-fetched.
