The whole column simply blanked and refilled, once per keystroke, which is what made sorting look like it was re-downloading every image. A live icon background is now left alone instead: `_stripTransientCellState()` takes a new opt-in `preserveLiveArt` option, and only `runFilter()`'s single-table branch passes it.

The check is deliberately narrow. A background is preserved only when it is a `blob:` URL still tracked in `_artIdbBlobUrls` (new `_artIconBackgroundIsLiveBlob()`), which is the `background-image` twin of the `blobIsAlive` test `_artInitInlinePics()`'s Case C1 already applies to an inline placeholder's `.src`. A blob-*shaped* string is not enough — after a `pagehide`, or on a row hydrated from a disk snapshot, the URL survives in the serialised style while the object behind it is gone, so a prefix test alone would have "preserved" broken images. Anything else (dead blob, plain http(s) URL, no background) is still cleared and re-fetched exactly as before.

`preserveLiveArt` defaults to false, and that default is load-bearing rather than cautious: `_stripTransientCellState()` has five call sites and three of them serialise the cell — `getCleanCellHtml()` (Save-to-Disk and the sub-table snapshot), `loadTableDataFromDisk()` and `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()`. Every object URL is alive by definition in the tab that created it, so an unconditional liveness check would have written `url(blob:…)` into saved files, where it is guaranteed dead on load, and persisted the `.mb-art-cache-hint-*` indicators so a restored file misreported which cache tier its images came from. Only a caller re-rendering into the same live document may opt in.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Added a standing warning to `_artInitSmallPics()` against adding an idempotency guard that skips icons which already carry a background-image. It now looks like free work-avoidance, but `_artLoadIcon()`'s completion path (`_onIconLoaded`) both paints the background and re-attaches the icon's hover-preview listeners, which `cloneNode(true)` drops on every re-render — so skipping a painted icon would leave it looking correct while its hover preview silently stopped working.

Two additions to the test-mode-only `__saTest` surface (`window.__SA_TEST_MODE__` gated; no UI, no user-visible behavior outside the Playwright harness): `artMintBlobUrl(register)` mints and optionally registers a real object URL the way `_artFetchCachedImage()` does, and `stripTransientCellState(selector, opts)` drives the real helper over a live cell and reports the artwork state back. Both exist because the interesting states here are unobservable from the DOM — the strip runs on a DETACHED clone between `cloneNode(true)` and insertion, and "is this blob still live" is answerable only from `_artIdbBlobUrls`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The release-tracks millisecond-precision ⏱ toggle now backfills the `Length`/`Recording length` columns for tracks MusicBrainz's own embedded page payload doesn't cover — confirmed on a real 1209-track release whose SSR hydration blob only ever carries data for the first 100 (the overflow-loading "Load all tracks..." call fills the live DOM but never updates that blob). Pressing the toggle now fires one supplemental `/ws/2/release/<mbid>?inc=recordings` request — verified live to return the release's COMPLETE, unpaginated tracklist regardless of size — only when some cell is still unstamped after the embedded payload's own pass, so a normal small release costs nothing extra. New `_msFetchFullReleaseTrackLengths()`/`_msStampFullReleaseRows()`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The release-tracks track-vs-recording length-mismatch tint (`td[data-mb-len-flag="warn"/"severe"]`) silently failed to render on any row that happened to land on MusicBrainz's own zebra-striped "even" `<tr>` — its native `tr.even > td { background: … }` rule (specificity 0,0,1,2) outranks a plain `td[data-mb-len-flag="…"]` background-color declaration (0,0,1,1) and painted right over it, leaving only the ⚠️/❌ glyph visible with no tint. Confirmed live (screenshot: an odd "far over" row showed its red tint fine, two even "warn" rows showed none) and reproduced by simulating MusicBrainz's real zebra rule against the local test fixture, which — lacking musicbrainz.org's own stylesheet — never exercised this conflict before. Both declarations now carry `!important`, the same fix already used for the identical class of conflict in `_ensureDetableifyStyle()`'s own zebra-vs-diff-color rules.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The "Show single-table" sub-table button (and, transitively, the real "Show all N rows" overflow button it stands in for) was missing entirely on `work-recordings`, `area-recordings`, `area-works` and `area-releases` whenever every relationship/link-type category on the page stayed under MusicBrainz's own 100-row-per-category cap — e.g. https://musicbrainz.org/area/a36544c1-cb40-4f44-9e0e-7a5a69e403a8/recordings. These four pageTypes share the exact same grouped-by-link-type, MB-capped shape as `artist-relationships`/`label-relationships`/`place-performances` (the "7 pairs" cluster in pageTypes-testing-reference.org) but had never been added to `SA_SNAPSHOT_SUPPORTED_PAGETYPES`/`SA_SNAPSHOT_LINK_TYPE_ID_PAGETYPES`, so `renderGroupedTable()`'s fallback branch silently skipped them. Added all four to both Sets.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: jesus2099's "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL Ⅱ X TURBO" (`RECORDING_LENGTH_COLUMN`) writes its own millisecond-precision `M:SS.mmm` Length values into the native page on pageTypes MusicBrainz itself renders no Length column for (`place-performances`, `work-recordings`, `artist-relationships`, ...). `purgeJesus2099Artifacts()`/`_stripJesus2099InTable()` already stripped the `treleases` class/title/text-shadow, but never touched the cell's own TEXT, so the leaked millisecond value rode straight through into the final rendered table — indistinguishable from genuine content, and leaving ShowAllEntityData's own ⏱ millisecond-precision toggle honestly unpressed while some cells already showed decimals (confirmed via a live-interop investigation against a real page, `tests/support/run-live-interop.js`, and three real captures: `debug/place-perf-initial-with-jesus-milliseconds.html`, `debug/place-perf-final.html`, `debug/place-perf-single-tabbed-final.html` — the last of which showed the leak was PARTIAL, only on rows from the page's first real navigation, since Tampermonkey never runs jesus2099 against ShowAllEntityData's own internal AJAX pagination fetches). New `_adoptJesus2099MsLength()` (wired into both `_stripJesus2099InTable()` and the live `_repairTreleasesTd()` mutation-observer path) now ADOPTS the leaked value into ShowAllEntityData's own `data-mb-ms`/`data-mb-sec-text` ms-toggle tracking instead of leaving it as unmarked text — displayed at MusicBrainz's own ROUNDED seconds precision by default (not jesus2099's raw truncated minutes:seconds), with the real millisecond value preserved for the ⏱ toggle to use instantly, no re-fetch needed. `_msToggleLengthPrecision()`'s `needFetch` logic also gained a `'ws2'`-source branch (`_msHasUnstampedLengthCell()`) so a page mixing adopted and un-adopted rows resolves BOTH in a single press instead of silently stranding the un-adopted ones once anything was already stamped.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `_titleHasRecNameMismatch()`'s JSDoc and its call-site comment (near `showStatsPanel`'s `titleMismatchCount` tally) now name the actual source of the '≠' track/recording-name-mismatch marker explicitly — jesus2099's "mb. INLINE STUFF" userscript — instead of a generic "e.g. jesus2099's userscript". Confirmed by scanning that script's real source directly while building the new `tests/support/run-live-interop.js` live third-party-userscript harness (see `tests/fixtures/live-userscripts/manifest.json`'s `jesus2099-inline-stuff` entry) — its `jesus2099userjs81127` class-name fragment, already cited in the comment, turned out to be that exact script's own internal id.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: New ⏳ pending-edits filter toggle in the filter bar: shows only rows crediting an entity that currently has OPEN EDITS on musicbrainz.org. Reads MusicBrainz's own native `<span class="mp">` marker via the new `_rowHasPendingEdits()`, so no extra request is made. Structural rather than text-based, like the length-mismatch buttons and unlike the live-date ones — `.mp` is a CSS-only orange highlight carrying no text of its own, so there is nothing to type into the global filter; `testRowMatch()` consults a predicate instead.

On multi-table page types every sub-section with pending edits gets its OWN toggle next to its filter panel, and the filter-bar button becomes a tri-state master: plain (nothing filtered), bold (all filtered), dashed (some). Pressing it while partial COMPLETES the set rather than clearing it, so the sub-sections already chosen are never silently discarded; pressing it while bold clears everything. `aria-pressed` carries `false`/`true`/`mixed` so the partial state is announced, not merely drawn differently.

Self-scoping throughout: a sub-section with nothing pending gets no button, and a page with nothing pending shows nothing at all — so the button's mere presence is the signal that something on the page is mid-edit. Same idiom as the live-date and length-mismatch summary buttons, needing no page-type check.

This is the first filter in the file that is BOTH structural and scoped per sub-table. Length-mismatch runs on a multi-table page type but is strictly page-wide (one module scalar that `testRowMatch()` reads directly), so two things are new: per-sub-table state lives in the DOM on each button (`data-mb-pending-active`), surviving every re-render for free because `renderGroupedTable()`'s reuse branch never rebuilds the `<h3>` — the same reason the sub-table filter can stash `container._mbApplySubFilter`; and `testRowMatch()` reads the flag off `ctx`, never a module variable, since the answer differs per group. `runFilter()` resolves it once per group into `matchCtx`, right beside `matchCtx.table`, keeping it O(1) per row instead of a DOM walk.

Per-sub-table buttons are class-only, with no id: merged discography view renders duplicate category names, and the `mb-stf-${safeId}-…` id scheme produces genuine duplicate ids there. Every lookup is `<h3>`-scoped, so an id would buy nothing and break in exactly that case.

Counts read SOURCE rows (`groupedRows[i].rows` / `allRows`), never the live `<tbody>` — `runFilter()` REMOVES non-matching rows on the multi-table path, so a live-DOM tally reports only what the current filter left behind, which is how the length-mismatch ❌ button once vanished as soon as you filtered to ⚠️. `_msSourceRows()` could not be reused: it flattens every group into one array and so cannot answer a per-group question.

Gated by the existing `sa_enable_pending_edits_section` setting, so one switch governs both this and the 📊 dropdown's "Pending edits" sections. Renamed to "Enable 'Pending edits' Filtering" and its description rewritten to cover both. The two compose and complement: the dropdown filters ONE column to a named entity, the toggle filters whole ROWS across every column.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: `updateFilterButtonsVisibility()` now counts the toggles as an active filter (so "✗ Clear all filters" appears while one is engaged — they are held by no input, exactly like the length-mismatch filter), `clearAllFilters()` releases every sub-table button as well as the module flag, and `_updatePendingEditsButtons()` is called from that one function alongside its two siblings, inheriting all six existing render/filter-completion hooks rather than adding call sites of its own.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: New `tests/fixtures/pending-edits-filter.spec.js` (8 tests) over a new three-sub-table fixture (`pending-edits-multi.html`, shaped after `tests/snapshots/artist-releasegroups/raw.html`: Album 2 of 3 rows pending, Single 1 of 2, Live none — two eligible groups being the minimum that can produce a partial state). Covers self-scoping, per-sub-table independence, the full tri-state cycle, broadcast, clear-all, composition with a typed query in both orders, and the setting's off state.

Every sync point was mutation-tested rather than assumed, which caught two weaknesses. The counting test originally passed even when counting the live `<tbody>`, because in that fixture the pending count happened to equal the filtered row count; it now narrows a sub-table to its one NON-pending row and asserts the button still reports 2, which fails against a live-DOM tally. And `_buildIncrPartialKey()` turned out NOT to be reachable: removing the flag from it fails no test, because toggling always re-runs the filter with an unchanged query and `_canNarrow` demands a strictly longer one, so a toggle press always forces a full scan first. The line stays as defence in depth and its comment now says so plainly instead of claiming a bug it does not fix.

`ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt`: new "⏳ PENDING-EDITS FILTER TOGGLE" section covering the tri-state master, the per-sub-section buttons, why the count does not shrink under other filters, and how it composes with the dropdown sections.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: The global filter bar (`#mb-filter-container`) now groups its own children into four semantic containers instead of holding every control as one flat run of 16 direct children mixing four unrelated concerns: `.mb-global-summary-container` (the live-date ⚠️/❌ and length-mismatch summary buttons), `.mb-global-filter-container` (the filter input wrapper, pin/history widget and the Cc/Rx/Ex labels), `.mb-global-actions-container` (prefilter message and toggle, collapse-all, highlight toggle, and the two clear buttons), and `.mb-global-status-container`. This mirrors the shape the sub-table bar has always had via `.mb-subtable-filter-container`, and gives the global bar the stable anchor for inserting new controls that it previously lacked.

`#mb-status-display` takes the fourth group's class directly rather than gaining a wrapper — it already IS a container holding exactly the filter- and sort-status spans, so a fourth nesting level would have added nothing.

The three new grouping spans are `display:contents`, which is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Every child of the summary group and of the actions group starts `display:none`. A `display:none` CHILD generates no flex gap, but a rendered wrapper whose children are all hidden is itself a zero-width flex item that DOES generate the bar's `gap:5px` on both sides — so a normal `inline-flex` wrapper would have added dead space to the bar on every page type that isn't release-tracks, and again whenever no filter was active. `display:contents` removes the wrapper's box entirely, leaving its children direct flex items of the bar with the same gap, alignment and font-size reset as before: no nested flex context, no second baseline resolution, no wrapping change.

Verified layout-neutral by measurement, not by eye: the bounding box of every rendered element in the bar is identical before and after, on both a page with a visible summary button and one where every summary and action button is hidden. The only DOM difference on that second page is the added class name.

`_artInitGlobalCaaColHdrToggle()`'s button now lands inside `.mb-global-actions-container`, since it is inserted with `.after()` on `#mb-col-collapse-all-btn`, which moved there. That is the semantically correct group for it and is visually identical; its JSDoc records the new location.

Naming note carried in the code: none of these may be shortened to `mb-global-filter`. A dead `document.querySelector('.mb-global-filter input')` targets a class that exists nowhere, and creating it would silently make that code live and match `#mb-global-filter-input`.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: New `tests/fixtures/filter-bar-containers.spec.js` (4 fixture tests): group membership and ordering, the `display:contents`/`flex` computed values, that `#mb-col-collapse-all-btn`'s `insertBefore` still resolves inside its group rather than throwing, and — the real guard — that no dead space appears when a whole group is hidden. That last test deliberately ignores zero-width boxes, because an empty rendered wrapper is itself zero-width and consecutive gaps either side of it still read 5px; ignoring it collapses them into one 10px gap between the real controls, which is what fails. Confirmed to fail against an `inline-flex` wrapper and pass against `display:contents`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: New "Pending edits" family in the 📊 unique-values dropdown, split into "Pending edits - Presence" (⏳ the binary `pending-edits-yes`/`pending-edits-no` flag pair) and "Pending edits - Entity" (✏️ the open `pendingedit:` per-value list, one entry per distinct entity, counted by ROWS). Both read MusicBrainz's OWN native `<span class="mp">` marker — the orange highlight it paints on an entity whose `/open_edits` list is non-empty — so no extra request is made. New `_findCellPendingEdits()` extractor, two `_cellMatchesStructureMode()` branches plus the `pendingedit:` compound one, and `_highlightPendingEditsMatch()`.

Unlike every other section family, these two are COLUMN-AGNOSTIC: the marker is a property of the entity, not of a column's grammar, so they are offered on every column of every page type with no `is…Col` gate — which is what the request asked for. That is also exactly why they are suppressed wholesale whenever nothing in the open column is pending (`pendingEditsYesCount > 0` at both emit sites): without that gate, every column on the whole site would grow a meaningless "○ no pending edits (N)" row. The upside is that the section appearing at all is itself the signal that a column has in-flight edits.

`_findCellPendingEdits()` reads each `span.mp` via `getCleanColumnText()`, not raw `textContent` — that helper already unwraps live `.mb-column-filter-highlight` spans, so re-running the extractor over its own previous output (a second filter pass, or reopening the dropdown while a pending-edits filter is still active) reports the same names instead of fragmenting or dropping them. It also reads straight through the extra nesting levels seen in real data: a `<span class="name-variation">` between the wrapper and the `<a>`, and a wrapper on only ONE artist of a joined credit.

Highlighting is scoped to the `span.mp` element itself, so on a "Queen & David Bowie" cell where only Bowie has open edits, checking his "» pending edit:" entry marks Bowie alone. `pending-edits-no` gets no highlighter — an absence has nothing to point at, same as `locale-not-primary`/`catalog-has-prefix`.

Gated by the new `sa_enable_pending_edits_section` setting (checkbox, default on). `_cellMatchesStructureMode()` re-checks it defensively on all three modes, so a pending-edits filter restored from a persisted/URL state saved while the setting was on cannot keep matching after it is turned off — same guard `lengthdeviation-*` already uses.

Both new counts and the per-entity value counts feed `panelBadgeChWidth`; "○ no pending edits" is normally the largest count in the whole panel, so omitting it there would have visibly clipped the badge column.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt`: new "⏳/✏️ Pending edits" entry in the unique-values dropdown section list, documenting the column-agnostic behaviour, the hidden-unless-pending rule, the two highlighting modes, and the new setting.

New `tests/fixtures/uniq-drop-pending-edits.{html,spec.js}` (6 fixture tests): the section split and its row-counted values, the emit gate on a column with nothing pending, both highlighting modes, the re-open-after-filter pass that would catch a self-corrupting extractor, and the setting's off state including the defensive matcher guard. Four of the six fail against the previous revision.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The Picard column is now a multi-row cell in its own right — one `<li>` per entity — so on a merged recording-search row each ♪ sits on the line of the release it sends, rather than all of them crowding onto one line. Always a `<ul>`, even for a single entity, so the column has one uniform cell structure (the same always-wrap rule `applyRenderMultiRowCells` documents); with the list reset, a one-item cell renders exactly as the bare button did, so no other page changes visually.

It also collapses and expands with the rest: `initPicardTaggerColumn()` registers "Picard" on `activeDefinition.features.collapsableColumns` (only when some row actually produced more than one button, so nothing runs on the pages where the column is one button per row) and re-runs `initCollapsableColumns()` itself. That extra call is the price of the column being injected LAST on every render path — it has to be, since its `<td>` must land after the Relationships cells to stay rightmost, which puts it after each path's own collapse pass; and rewire mode rebuilds each cell's `innerHTML`, which would wipe a toggle that pass had added. `initCollapsableColumns()` is idempotent and never calls back, so there is no loop.

Registration uses `concat`, not `push`: `activeDefinition.features` is rebuilt per fetch but its `collapsableColumns` VALUE is the page definition's own array, so pushing would mutate that definition for the rest of the session.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: One Picard ♪ button per release on a merged recording-search row, instead of one for whichever release happened to be listed first. `_picardExtractRowEntity()` became `_picardExtractRowEntities()`: the first taggable anchor in document order still decides both the entity type and the cell to read — so nothing changes on any other page — but the whole of THAT cell is now harvested rather than just its first anchor. Anchoring on the first match's own cell is what keeps this from over-collecting: a `release-tracks` AR column can hold a dozen unrelated `/recording/` links, but it is never the row's first entity cell.

Each button names its own entity in its tooltip ("Send to Picard (Hotel Diablo — release)"). With several buttons in one cell an 8-character MBID prefix does not tell you which release a given ♪ would send.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Track" and "Medium" on the recording search results did not line up across the table. `td.mb-has-collapse-toggle` sets `padding-right:22px` so cell content never slides under the absolutely-positioned collapse toggle, but it lands only on cells that HAVE a toggle — which in a centred or right-aligned column makes a value's position depend on whether its own row happens to be multi-row. Measured: the same "1" in "Medium" sat 10.5 px (half the padding) further left in a row with a toggle. A new `td.mb-collapse-col-pad` reserves the same space on every other cell of a toggle-bearing column. A no-op for the left-aligned text columns this mechanism is usually applied to, and it costs no width — the auto-resize pass already budgets the toggle's space once per column.

`applyRenderMultiRowCells()` built a bare `<ul>` and relied on MusicBrainz's own stylesheet to neutralise the UA defaults — the only list builder in the script that did not reset the list it creates (`splitCountryDate`'s two lists and the CAA art list all do). That is a real bug, not just an inconsistency: the UA's `padding-inline-start:40px` is added to the width of whatever box contains the list, so an integer column's `min-width:Nch` — set on the `.mb-ic-val` span AROUND the list — never binds, and a centred column's values then sit at a position that depends on their own text width. Now reset like every other one.

A `<li>` appended by `mergeContinuationRows` never received its column's integer-alignment treatment. `applyIntegerColumnStyling()` is the last step of row assembly and guards on a per-CELL `data-mb-int-col-styled` flag, but a continuation row is not parsed until after the base row is fully assembled — so in a split-aligned column each cell ended up with exactly one separator, on its first item, while every merged item kept raw text. The merge now styles the items it appends (new `_styleIntColListItem()`, resolving the column's `align` from `activeIntegerColumns` by the destination index).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: "Track" ("N/M", track N of M) is now split-aligned on its "/" the way "Length" is on its ":", so the separator sits at one horizontal position for the whole column. Right-alignment alone lined "5/13" and "23/39" up on the 3 and the 9, which reads as noise.

Split-character alignment works on multi-row cells at all now: `applyIntegerColumnStyling()` builds one `.mb-ic-wrap` unit per `<li>` instead of one per cell (the old code read the cell's CONCATENATED text, split it at its LAST separator, and cleared the cell to rebuild it — destroying the list outright), and `finalizeSplitAlignedColumns()` measures and widens every span pair in a cell rather than just the first. So a cell's own items align with each other as well as with the rest of the column.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: The three-span split-align unit is now built by `_buildSplitAlignWrap()` and multi-row detection by `_intColListItems()`, both shared between `applyIntegerColumnStyling()`'s two branches and the measurement passes — previously inline, and impossible to reuse per `<li>`. The 'L'/'R'/'C' branch deliberately stays whole-cell: it wraps the cell's entire `<ul>` in one `.mb-ic-val`, so a later-appended `<li>` lands inside that span and inherits its alignment and width for free.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Recording search results (`/search?type=recording`) rendered every release after a recording's first one as a broken row. MusicBrainz paginates those results by RECORDING (25 per page) but emits one `<tr>` per (recording, release) pair, with the recording's own four columns rendered only on the first — every further release arrives as a "continuation" row whose leading four columns are a single empty `<td colspan="4">`. That row has 5 cells for an 8-column table, and the row-import loop addresses cells POSITIONALLY, so all of its content was read four columns to the left: release TITLES landed in the Length column, Track in Artist, Medium in ISRCs, Type in Release. Page 1 of a `roulette` search is 25 real rows plus 17 of these.

The most expensive part of that was invisible as a cause: a release title inside the Length column was wrapped in that column's `:`-alignment spans, which made `finalizeSplitAlignedColumns` size EVERY Length cell in the table to the longest title — 51ch — and blew the rendered table out to 5557 px wide.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: New page-definition feature `mergeContinuationRows`, enabled on the recording search results. A continuation row is now folded into the preceding data row instead of being imported as its own, one extra `<li>` per column, so "Release", "Track", "Medium" and "Type" become multi-row cells with the collapse toggles, per-cell counts, filter-match tinting and unique-values entries every other multi-row column already has. The rendered row count is now exactly MusicBrainz's own "Found N results", instead of that plus one broken row per extra release.

The merged columns are derived from the data, not declared: they are exactly the columns NOT covered by the continuation row's own `colSpan`, which is what MusicBrainz's markup already says they are. The detection (`_isContinuationRow`) is structural — an empty spanning first cell — rather than keyed on a page type, so the feature is a flag away for any other page MusicBrainz renders this way.

The four columns are also declared in `renderMultiRowCell`, which is what gives EVERY row the same uniform `
  • ` shape — a recording with one release now has exactly the cell structure of one with ten, which is what `_classifyCollapseCell`, `testRowMatch` and the statistics panel all assume. It is safe against comma-splitting here because a release title lives inside `…`, an element child rather than a top-level text node, so a title like "2001-12-06: Copper Dragon, Carbondale, IL, USA" is left whole.

Two features fall out for free, because both already understood `ul > li` cells: each release in a merged cell gets its own inline cover-art thumbnail (`_artInitInlinePics`) and its own ▶ entity-page toggle (`initExpandRGsFeature`).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: `finalizeRLCColumnWidths()` now sizes an L/R/C integer column from the longest SINGLE list item rather than the cell's concatenated text (new `_rlcValueLength()` helper). "Track" and "Medium" are integer columns AND multi-row columns on this page, so the old measurement read a three-release cell as `"7/1012/254/9"` — 12 characters instead of 5 — and stretched the whole column by a factor of the row count. Each `<li>` is its own visual line inside the value span, so the longest item is the width the column actually needs.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: The merge reuses the ordinary pipeline rather than reimplementing it: `_buildContinuationSourceRow()` pads the continuation row back out to the table's ORIGINAL, pre-deletion column indices (`colSpan` empty leading cells, then its own trailing cells), which lets `applyColumnErasers()` and `applyRenderMultiRowCells()` run over it verbatim with their already-resolved `colIdx` values. The destination index is then computed by subtracting the excluded columns that precede it — the base row is already post-`deleteCell` — rather than assuming `indicesToExclude` is empty, so a foreign userscript column or a setting-gated removal (Rating, checkbox-cell) can't silently shift the merge one column over.

Exactly one `<li>` is appended per column per continuation row, empty when the source cell is empty, so the four parallel lists stay row-aligned with each other. A destination column that is NOT declared in `renderMultiRowCell` has its existing content wrapped on the fly, so the feature degrades to "correct, just only wrapped where a merge happened" instead of dropping data.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: New "MULTI-ROW CELLS FROM REPEATED-SUBJECT ROWS" section in the help text, and a dated `debug/NOTES.md` entry recording the two snapshots this was diagnosed from and why the symptom looked like a Length-column bug.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Track-vs-recording length mismatch flagging on `release-tracks`, building on 9.99.1019's "Recording length" column. When a track's two lengths differ by more than a configurable threshold, BOTH duration cells are tinted and marked — `⚠️` past the threshold, `❌` past `threshold × multiple` — and both carry a tooltip. Five new settings in 💿 RELEASE TRACKLIST: an on/off master (`sa_enable_release_tracks_length_mismatch_flag`, default on), `sa_release_tracks_length_mismatch_threshold_ms` (default 1000), `sa_release_tracks_length_mismatch_severe_factor` (default 3), and a configurable tint per level.

The threshold is in MILLISECONDS, not seconds, for two reasons: it is the unit MusicBrainz stores lengths in, and the settings dialog's number input has no `step` (implicit `step=1`), so a seconds-based field could not express a sub-second tolerance at all without a change to `VZ_MBLibrary.user.js` — a different project. 1000 ms is the default because one second is the smallest difference actually VISIBLE at the columns' default seconds precision; below it both columns can read "4:50" while the stored values differ, so flagging would look arbitrary until the ⏱ toggle is pressed. On `Born to Run`, 1000 flags 1 of 8 tracks and 0 flags 6 of 8.

The severe level is `threshold × factor`, and is DISABLED (never reached) whenever that product is not strictly greater than the threshold. Two settings reach that state — a factor of 1, and a threshold of 0 — and in both cases promoting every flag to `❌` would be the opposite of what the numbers ask for.

Each flagged cell's tooltip is written from THAT cell's point of view rather than sharing one neutral sentence: the Length cell reads "Track length 3:19.000 is 3 s LONGER than the recording's own length, 3:16.000" and the Recording length cell reads the mirror image. The two columns are easy to mix up, so naming the direction relative to the cell being hovered removes the ambiguity instead of restating it. Durations are always quoted at full millisecond precision regardless of what the column currently displays — at seconds precision the two values can read identically, which is exactly when the numbers behind the flag are least visible.

New `(N) LENGTH ⚠️`/`(N) LENGTH ❌` summary buttons in the filter bar, counting TRACKS (each flagged track marks two cells, so a per-cell tally would report double) and filtering to them on click. Unlike the live-recording WARNING/ERROR buttons they are TOGGLES with a pressed state, and they compose with a typed query rather than clearing it — press ⚠️, then type to narrow further.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: The marking is carried ENTIRELY by a `data-mb-len-flag` attribute, with both the tint and the `⚠️`/`❌` glyph coming from CSS (`td[data-mb-len-flag]::after`); no marker element exists in the cell at all. Three independent reasons, two of them silent if broken: `applyIntegerColumnStyling()` rebuilds these cells with `cell.textContent = ''` to build the `:`-alignment spans, so a child marker would simply be deleted; a glyph in the cell TEXT would reach `_compareDurations()` — which parses this column's rendered text to sort it — making a flagged row sort as if its duration were unparseable, besides widening that one row's colon-split segment; and attributes survive `cloneNode(true)`, so the marking needs no re-wire hook on any render path, where a JS-painted marker would need one on every path.

`_msRecordingLengthForRow()` renamed to `_msLengthForRow()` and made map-agnostic. The row-resolution rule (recording MBID first, displayed `mN·nN` position as fallback) is identical for the track-length and recording-length maps, and the mismatch check needs one row looked up in BOTH; two copies that could drift apart is exactly how a row would end up compared against another track's length. It also now takes the row's cells as an ARRAY captured before insertion rather than reading `tr.children` live — both indices come from the pre-insertion header list, and the caller has already inserted Video/Disambiguation/Recording artist cells by then. Those all land after "Title" today so a live lookup still resolved, but only by luck.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `_buildFilterKey()` now includes the length-mismatch filter state. It appears nowhere else in the key, so "no query, no column filters" hashed identically whether the structural filter was engaged or not — `_filterResultCache` returned the previous pass's rows, and pressing a summary button a second time to clear it did nothing at all. Found in testing, before shipping.

`_countLengthMismatchRows()` counts the captured source rows (`_msSourceRows()`), not the live tbody. `runFilter()` REMOVES non-matching rows from a multi-table tbody rather than hiding them, so a live-DOM tally reports only whatever the current filter left behind: filtering to `⚠️` made the `❌` button disappear, since no `❌` row was still rendered. A summary button has to state a stable fact about the release and stay reachable while the other severity is engaged.

`updateFilterButtonsVisibility()` counts the length-mismatch filter as active, so "Clear ALL filters" is offered while it is on. It is the one active filter with NO input holding it, so without this the rows narrowed while every clear affordance stayed hidden — leaving the pressed summary button as the only way out. `clearAllFilters()` resets it explicitly for the same reason.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: HELP gains a "Length-mismatch flagging" block under RELEASE-TRACKS PAGE (worked example, both severity levels and their defaults, why the threshold is in milliseconds, and how the toggle-style summary buttons differ from the live-recording ones). CLAUDE.md's track-length section gains the attribute-only marking rationale and the three pieces of state that must stay in sync with `_lenMismatchFilterKind`, each of which broke in testing.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: New "Recording length" column on `release-tracks`, showing the length MusicBrainz stores on the RECORDING each track links to — `tracks[].recording.length` in the release payload the page already inlines, so it costs no request of any kind. It sits immediately after the native "Length", because reading the two side by side is the entire point: "Length" is `tracks[].length`, THIS release's own tracklist value, while a recording's length belongs to the recording entity every release using it shares. The two disagree constantly — on `Born to Run` six of eight tracks differ, `Meeting Across the River` by three whole seconds (track 3:19 vs recording 3:16).

Named to match the pair the tracklist already has: native "Artist" (the release-level credit) alongside the injected "Recording artist" (the recording's own). "Length"/"Recording length" now reads the same way, and matches MusicBrainz's own data-model terms.

Added only when at least one track's recording length actually disagrees with its track length — the same page-wide-decision pattern as Video/Disambiguation/Recording artist (`renderGroupedTable()` clones ONE `<thead>` template from the first `table.tbl`, so a column can only be decided for the whole release, never per medium). Where every recording length matches, the column would be an exact duplicate of "Length" and is not added at all rather than costing a full column's width. Measured over every release snapshot in `debug/` (scripts/scan-track-vs-recording-length.py), 2 of 11 releases fall on that side.

A track length with NO recording length behind it (`4:37` vs `?:??`) deliberately does NOT earn the column on its own: it is a difference, but a column added on that basis alone would be every row `?:??`, stating only "MusicBrainz has no recording lengths here". Where the column is earned by some other row, those rows still render `?:??` — the informative half is kept, the empty column is not. The reverse case (`?:??` under Length, a real value under Recording length) is exactly where the column shows something "Length" structurally cannot, e.g. `The Rising: Tour Edition`'s DVD track `Lonesome Day (music video)`.

The existing ⏱ millisecond toggle in the "Length" header now switches BOTH duration columns together, rather than gaining a second button. This falls out of the mechanism rather than being bolted on: `_msApplyLengthPrecision()` rewrites every `td[data-mb-ms]` on a row, not one resolved column index, so stamping the new cells with the same `data-mb-ms`/`data-mb-sec-text` pair is all it takes. Comparing the two at different precisions would be meaningless anyway — and milliseconds are where most of their differences actually live (`4:50.293` vs `4:49.826` both round to `4:50`). The column itself is independent of `sa_enable_ms_track_length`: with that off the column still renders seconds, just unstamped and with no toggle.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Both duration column headers on `release-tracks` now carry an explanatory native tooltip, each leading with WHICH entity owns the value rather than with how it is displayed — that being the distinction the two columns exist to draw. "Length" explains that the value belongs to the release and is displayed rounded to the nearest second; "Recording length" explains that it belongs to the shared recording entity, that it was read from data already in the page, why the column is present at all, and what `?:??` means there. Both mention the shared ⏱ toggle, and both drop that sentence when `sa_enable_ms_track_length` is off rather than pointing at a button that isn't there.

Scoped to `release-tracks` on purpose, exactly like `_initColHeaderGlyph()`. A "Length" column appears on ~20 other pageTypes where it means something else — the recording's own length on `work-recordings`, a TOC/sector-derived value on `release-discids` — so a page-agnostic tooltip would confidently state something false on most of them.

Injected from the tail of `makeTableSortableUnified()`, alongside `_initMsLengthColHeaderToggle()`, and for the identical reason: that function is what rebuilds every `<th>`, so it is the one site guaranteed to run after the header exists on every render path (single-table, grouped, and sub-table-in-its-own-tab alike).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `_isJesus2099Treleases()` hardened against a `title` this script writes itself. Its discriminator is literally "does this `treleases` cell have a `title`?" — sound when written, because MusicBrainz puts none on its own Length `<th>` and jesus2099's `RECORDING_LENGTH_COLUMN` always does. Adding the Length tooltip above broke that assumption from a completely unrelated direction: the predicate began reporting the release tracklist's own NATIVE header as jesus2099's, so `purgeJesus2099Artifacts()` stripped MusicBrainz's `treleases` class off it and removed the tooltip again on every render — precisely the destructive outcome the predicate's own JSDoc warns about, and which three earlier call sites had already caused once each.

Our own tooltips now carry `data-mb-col-tip`, and both places that key off bare `title` presence — `_isJesus2099Treleases()` and `_stripJesus2099InTable()`'s disposition-3 title removal — consult the new `_isOwnColumnTooltip()` instead. Anything that puts a `title` on a `treleases` `<th>`/`<td>` in future must mark it the same way; the predicate's JSDoc now says so.

Regression coverage for exactly this: `tests/fixtures/release-tracks-recording-length.spec.js` asserts the Length header keeps MusicBrainz's `treleases` class AND its tooltip, both on first render and after a re-render (which is when the purge runs again).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: HELP gains a "Recording length" bullet under RELEASE-TRACKS PAGE (with a worked Born to Run example, the not-added-when-identical rule, and what `?:??` means there), and TRACK LENGTH PRECISION now states that one ⏱ button drives both duration columns and that the embedded release data feeds the new column too.

`scripts/build-ms-length-fixture.py` now carries `tracks[].recording.length` into the fixture — the field was trimmed out as unread, which is no longer true — and emits a second fixture, `tests/fixtures/release-tracks-recording-length-match.html`, with every recording length forced equal to its track length. That is the other side of the gate: the column must NOT appear. Forced rather than borrowed from a release that genuinely agrees, because the payload has to keep keying THIS DOM — rows are matched by recording MBID, so another release's payload would match nothing and the column would be absent for the wrong reason, passing the test while proving nothing.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `integerColumns` alignment could be stamped onto columns it was never configured for, most visibly centring `place-performances`(-filtered)'s free-text `MB-Name` column. The styling is applied POSITIONALLY (`applyIntegerColumnStyling()` reaches for `row.cells[entry.colIdx]`) against indices resolved once from a reconstructed list of the final column names — and that list's synthetic-column-extractor step guarded on `_finalColNames.includes(entry.sourceColumn)`, while `eventParts` sources from `'Comment'`, which the MB-Name/Comment/Primary alias step only appends AFTERWARDS. The entry therefore looked unresolved, its nine `Event-*` names were dropped from the list even though the cells were still rendered, and every column resolved past that point came out nine indices too low: `R-YYYY` (align `'C'`) landed on `MB-Name`, `R-DD`/`R-MM` (align `'R'`) on two `Event-*` columns. The guard now also counts the `extractMainColumn` trio, which at row-assembly time genuinely does exist before a synthetic-column extractor reads it — that is how `eventParts` works at all.

The defect needed three ingredients at once — `extractMainColumn`, a `syntheticColumnExtractors` entry sourcing from its synthetic `Comment`, and an `integerColumns` entry resolved AFTER it (i.e. fed by `injectedColumnExtractors`). An audit of all 23 pageTypes declaring `eventParts` confirms `place-performances` and `place-performances-filtered` are the only two that combine all three, via `R-DD`/`R-MM`/`R-YYYY` off the injected `Release events` column; every other one's integerColumns resolve before the gap and were never affected. It was latent until those two pageTypes gained `eventParts`.

Regression coverage: `tests/fixtures/place-performances-intcol-align.{html,spec.js}`, which fails on the pre-fix code and passes after. Its main assertion is the general invariant — NO column outside `features.integerColumns` may carry the styling marker — rather than the narrow "MB-Name is not centred", so any future recurrence is caught wherever it lands. Note the fixture must keep `sa_enable_relationships_column` ON: that column contributes one more name to the reconstructed list, and it is precisely what makes `R-YYYY` land on `MB-Name` rather than one column earlier, so with it off the reported symptom does not reproduce.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The ⏱ millisecond-Length toggle is now offered on a series' Recordings listing (`series-releases`' `entityFeatures.Recordings`), where the Length column previously had no glyph at all. Source is `'batch'`, not `'ws2'`: `_msWs2PageKey()`'s regex covers only work/artist/place/area, and a series' recordings are its PARTS rather than a relationship list that one `inc=recording-rels` answer would cover — so the batched search endpoint, keyed on the recording MBIDs the page actually renders, is the only source that applies. HELP's "where the data comes from" list resynced to name series-recordings alongside the other batched pageTypes.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The `eventParts` syntheticColumnExtractor now runs on ELEVEN further recording-listing pageTypes, closing an audit gap: `place-performances`, `place-performances-filtered`, `artist-relationships`, `artist-relationships-filtered`, and the `'Recordings'` entityFeatures of `search`, `collections-releases`, `series-releases`, `tag-value`, `tag-value-entity`, `user-tag-value` and `user-tag-value-entity`. A recording's disambiguation comment on these pages encodes live-performance metadata in MusicBrainz's usual free-form shape (e.g. "live, 1975-10-18, early show: The Roxy Theatre, West Hollywood, CA, USA"); it is now split into the nine `Event-Type`/`Event-Date`/`Event-Detail`/`Event-Venue`/`Event-Venue-Detail`/`Event-City`/`Event-State`/`Event-Country`/`Event-Additional-Info` columns, the same treatment the twelve already-wired recording pageTypes (`work-recordings`, `area-recordings`, `artist-recordings`, `instrument-recordings`, `isrc`, `release-tracks`, `user-ratings`, `artist-credit`, and their siblings) have had all along. Every one of the eleven already produced the synthetic `Comment` source column via `extractMainColumn` — no new plumbing was needed, the extractor was simply never declared.

No pageType needed a new mechanism for this. The nine `entityFeatures`-based entries rely on the existing merge precedence in `startFetchingProcess` — `entitySpecificFeatures` is spread BEFORE `baseDef.features`, so a per-entity `syntheticColumnExtractors` survives only while the base definition declares no key of that name. Verified for all four tag-value-family pageTypes plus `search`, `collections-releases` and `series-releases`: every existing `syntheticColumnExtractors` in those definitions already lives inside an `entityFeatures` entry (e.g. `'Events'` → `dateParts`), never in the top-level `features` block, so nothing is shadowed.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: HELP resynced: the Event-* derived-column entry no longer names two example page styles but describes the actual rule — every page that lists recordings — with the concrete surfaces enumerated.

`scripts/add-eventparts-to-recording-pagetypes.py` records the edit rather than being run and discarded. It addresses each of the eleven insertion points by LINE NUMBER, not by a text anchor, because four PAIRS of the target blocks are byte-identical to one another (`collections-releases`/`series-releases` Recordings, `user-tag-value`/`tag-value` Recordings, both `place-performances` variants, both `artist-relationships` variants) and so cannot be told apart by content. Each insertion is guarded by an assertion on both the block's opening line and its `columnExtractors` closing line, and the script refuses to write if any guard fails.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Ruled OUT as non-candidates during the same audit, recorded so the next pass does not re-derive them: `recording-releases` (its rows are RELEASES — the `Comment` there is a release disambiguation, not performance metadata), `label-relationships`/`-filtered` (release-shaped: no `Length` column, no `msTrackLengthWs2`), `recording-fingerprints`, `release-discids`, `cd-stub`, `top-cd-stub` (whose `Comment` is synthesised from the "lastupdate" info row, not a native disambiguation span), `entity-aliases`, `annotations`, `ratings-entity`, and `report-detail` (its `extractMainColumn` candidate list does include `Recording`, but across 117 differently-shaped reports that column is not live-performance metadata).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Repaired two unresolved `WIP.N` placeholders left in shipped changelog entries by hand-folds that predate `scripts/fold-wip-changelog.py` — they rewrote each entry's own `version` field but not the cross-references buried in its prose, which is precisely the defect that script now treats as a hard error. 9.99.932's `WIP.1` now reads 9.99.931, confirmed twice over: 9.99.931 is the entry that introduced the `window.__saTest` hook the sentence cites, and replaying that fold's own WIP file from git maps `WIP.1` to 9.99.931 exactly.

9.99.783's two `WIP.26` citations were DELETED rather than repointed, because no such version exists to point at. `WIP.26` never appeared in any committed WIP file — the pre-fold file jumps `WIP.25` to `WIP.27`, no commit in the repository's history contains a `"WIP.26"`, and no shipped entry introduces the "Phonographic copyright (℗) by artist/label" columns the sentence refers to: the commit that first put that column name into the userscript is the very commit that entry describes. It was a mis-numbered reference from the moment it was written, and inventing a plausible target would have been worse than removing one.

Gave a `version` to the two entries that had none, which made any tool reading `entry['version']` bail: the 2026-03-06 entry between 9.99.46 and 9.99.44 is now 9.99.45, and the 2026-02-24 entry between 9.91.0 and 9.90.0 is now 9.90.1. The first is unambiguous — one free integer slot in a strictly descending sequence. The second is a RECONSTRUCTION rather than a recovery: its neighbours are all `9.9x.0`, no integer fits between 90 and 91, and both entries entered git in the initial import, so nothing records what they actually shipped as. 9.90.1 is the only value that keeps the sequence strictly descending without colliding.
The repair is `scripts/repair-changelog-integrity.py`, committed rather than run and discarded: it is the record of which shipped release notes were edited and on what evidence.

Removed three duplicate version numbers, which were three different accidents and so took three different fixes. 9.99.338 was the SAME entry stored twice, byte-identical — one copy deleted. 9.99.247 and 9.99.547 were each two different write-ups of one release, a rewrite appended instead of replacing its predecessor; both texts are kept, merged into a single entry. Renumbering was not an option for either: 9.99.547's neighbours leave no free slot, and while 9.99.247 has a free 9.99.246 beside it, BOTH of its write-ups cite "the previous attempt (v9.99.246)" as the thing they replace, so numbering either of them 9.99.246 would have made it cite itself. Dropping one would have needed a judgement about which write-up is authoritative, and nothing in the data says.

Normalised the two non-numeric versions `9.99.483-dbg`/`9.99.482-dbg` to their plain numeric form — they broke any tool doing `int(version.split('.')[2])`, which is the exact class of bail this pass exists to remove. Both slots were free and the surrounding sequence had room for exactly those two. Their five in-prose citations were normalised with them, which needed a WHOLE-FILE pass rather than a per-entry one: a citation names some other entry's version, so `v9.99.482-dbg` appears in 9.99.483's text, and a scoped rewrite left every one of them behind. Nothing is lost — both entries still open by calling themselves a temporary debug build, which is all the suffix conveyed.

The changelog now passes a full hygiene audit: 1,186 entries, every one with a parseable `version` and a `date`, no duplicates, no unresolved placeholders, and strictly descending version order end to end. The repair was verified not to lose anything — every item text present beforehand is still present, the only reduction being the byte-identical duplicate's second copy.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: `merge-push-remove`'s post-fold sanity check is a whole-file `grep` for `WIP.` again. It had just been narrowed to the fold's own added lines precisely because those two historical stragglers made the whole-file version fire every time — and a check that always fires is one you learn to ignore. With the file clean, any hit is now a live defect.

The repair script is `scripts/repair-changelog-integrity.py` (renamed from `repair-changelog-placeholders.py` once it grew past placeholders). Idempotent, refuses to act if the entries it targets have shifted, and treats a pair it expects to be byte-identical no longer being so as a hard error rather than deleting the wrong one.

`scripts/fold-wip-changelog.py` now treats a backtick-quoted `WIP.N` as a LITERAL and rewrites only bare ones. Found by this very entry: it discusses placeholder tokens as strings, and the fold aborted on the ones naming numbers no batch contains. The quieter half is worse — a literal naming a token the batch DOES contain was being silently rewritten into a version number, turning a sentence about a placeholder into a false claim about a release. Backticks are how this file quotes every other identifier, so the rule costs nothing to follow, and the error message now names it when a citation really is dangling.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Millisecond "Length" precision now reaches the pageTypes that no single Web Service lookup can cover: `artist-recordings`, `instrument-recordings`, `isrc`, and recording search results. These are fetched in batches keyed on the recording MBIDs the page actually renders — `/ws/2/recording?query=rid:(…)`, 100 at a time, one request per second — so a page of 100 rows or fewer costs a single request. The ⏳ glyph counts the batches off ("⏳2/5") and the tooltip quotes the cost before you spend it.

A batched lookup rather than the `?artist=` browse endpoint, because a browse loop's cost is set by the ENTITY's whole catalogue instead of by the page: Bruce Springsteen's `recording-count` is 74,540, i.e. 746 requests and roughly fourteen minutes, whether the table lists ten rows or ten thousand. It also cannot serve `instrument-recordings` at all — `/ws/2/instrument/<mbid>?inc=recording-rels` returns zero relations for a page listing 100 recordings, because MusicBrainz models instrument credits as artist-recording relationships carrying an instrument attribute. 100 MBIDs per request is the measured ceiling, not a guess: 150 is accepted but silently capped by the endpoint's own limit, and 200 is rejected as `HTTP 414 URI Too Long` (scripts/probe-ms-rid-batch-size.py).

Fetched lengths are cached per RECORDING in IndexedDB (`ms-rec-len` store), not per page, so a recording already seen on one page is free on every other page that lists it and free again after a reload. New settings `sa_ms_idb_enable` (default on) and `sa_ms_idb_ttl_days` (default 30) control it, and the 📊 Statistics panel reports the store's size alongside the existing art and relationship caches. Each batch's answers are written in ONE IndexedDB transaction rather than one per recording, which at a hundred rows per batch is the difference between one write and a hundred.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: `area-recordings` and `area-recordings-filtered` gained the ⏱ toggle through the existing SINGLE-request path rather than the new batched one. An area's own `inc=recording-rels` answer covers its recordings page exactly — Asbury Park returns 24 relations with lengths for a page listing those same 24 recordings — so one request beats chunking the rows.

A partly-failed batched run now shows the rows that did arrive and says the column is incomplete (the same yellow tint the retry state uses), instead of either discarding usable data or presenting a half-filled column as finished. Failed batches cache nothing, so switching the toggle off and on again re-requests exactly the missing MBIDs and fills the gaps rather than starting over. Worth having rather than theoretical: the Web Service was returning 503 for roughly one request in three while this was being built.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The background IndexedDB sweep has never actually swept the `rel-ws2` store. `sweepStore()` measured every record's age from a `storedAt` field, which only the `images` and `metadata` records carry — a `rel-ws2` record timestamps itself as `ts`, so it always read as age 0 and was never deleted. Those entries did still expire, but only lazily and one at a time, whenever `_relIdbGet()` happened to read one. It now reads either field, which also lets the new `ms-rec-len` store be swept properly rather than inheriting the same silent no-op.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `recording-releases` is now documented in the source as deliberately having NO millisecond source, so it does not acquire one later by analogy with its neighbours. Its rows are releases rather than recordings and carry no `/recording/` link at all, and its "Length" is the per-release TRACK length — a different stored field from the recording's own length, which genuinely differs (4 of `Born to Run`'s 8 tracks disagree, one by 3 s). Substituting the recording length would be showing a different measurement rather than more precision on the shown one, the same objection that already keeps `release-discids`' TOC-derived lengths out. Doing it properly needs a release-keyed source, which is its own mechanism.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: New fixture-based coverage for the batched source (`tests/fixtures/artist-recordings-ms-batch.spec.js`, 130 generated rows over two batches) asserting what the mechanism is actually about: how many requests go out, which MBIDs each asks for, that a "?:??" row is never requested, that answers are cached across sorting/filtering/re-toggling, and both failure shapes. Plus `area-recordings-ms-length.spec.js`, which pins the one-regex-token `area` path a typo would otherwise disable silently. Both were verified by mutation — reverting the code they cover makes them fail.

`__saTest.msPendingLengthLookups()` exposes how many recordings are still outstanding, because the interesting case is invisible from the DOM: a row answered as "no length on record" is never stamped and so looks identical to an unanswered one.

`tests/support/idbFixture.js` resynced to IndexedDB version 3 and the new `ms-rec-len` store. It seeds the database before the userscript opens it, so a stale version there would have left the userscript holding a handle to a database it believed current with a store missing — its own comment already asked for exactly this re-check whenever the version drifts.

`tests/fixtures/length-column-filter-colon-gap.spec.js` now identifies its column by `data-col-name` instead of stripping decorations out of the header text — `artist-recordings` headers now carry the ⏱ toggle, which that helper's strip list did not know about.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Test coverage for the cross-tab sub-table handoff — `openSubtableAsSingleTableTab()` through to `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()` — which had none at all despite several features crossing it: CAA/EAA art cells, the Relationships column, collapse state and now millisecond Length precision. New `tests/support/subtableTab.js` drives the real thing in the same spirit as `diskFixture.js`: the source page captures its own snapshot and nothing is hand-built. Asserts both that the payload really lands in GM storage under the documented key shape carrying just that sub-table's rows, and that the opened tab hydrates from it, starts with milliseconds hidden, and round-trips the ⏱ toggle cleanly.

Verified meaningful rather than merely green: with BOTH millisecond resets disabled the round-trip test fails. Disabling either one alone does not, because the capture-side and hydration-side resets are redundant by design — each is sufficient on its own.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The ⏱ toggle could flip its glyph without the "Length" column moving at all. The cause was a poisoned baseline: both stampers read the cell's current text as the seconds to restore when the toggle goes off, and if that text was ALREADY at millisecond precision the stashed baseline was itself a millisecond string — so switching off dutifully restored milliseconds. Visible in the reported capture as `data-mb-sec-text="11:17.000"`. They now refuse to record a millisecond-shaped string and derive the seconds form from the milliseconds instead, rounded the way MusicBrainz rounds (5:34.866 gives "5:35", never "5:34"). This holds however the millisecond text reached the cell.

Separately, and correct on its own terms though not what fixed the report: a "Length" cell that arrives already rendered at millisecond precision is now reset to MusicBrainz's seconds form, recovered exactly from the text. `captureSubtableSnapshot()` stores `cell.innerHTML`, so a cell's own `data-mb-*` attributes never cross the sub-table handoff — only the rendered text does — and the destination would otherwise re-stamp that text as if it were MusicBrainz's own seconds.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: A sub-table opened in its own tab via "Show single-table" now always starts with milliseconds hidden, whatever was showing on the page it was opened from. Precision is a per-page view setting rather than something that follows the data around — and it makes the behaviour uniform with a paginated sub-table, which is re-fetched from MusicBrainz and so always started in seconds.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `CLAUDE.md` records that this reset belongs ONLY on the capture and hydration paths and must NOT be added to `_stripTransientCellState()`: that helper looks like the obvious home, but `runFilter()` also calls it on the live re-render clones, so putting it there silently undoes the toggle on every keystroke.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The ⏱ millisecond toggle was missing entirely from the "Length" header on a sub-table opened in its own tab, so a column showing milliseconds had no control to switch it back. Same root cause as 9.99.1010 — the button is injected from a hook that ran before the header layout existed — in a path that fix did not reach: `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()` calls `renderFinalTable()` well before `makeTableSortableUnified()`, which is what builds the `.mb-col-hdr-flex` the button lives in.

Rather than patch a third caller, the injection now hooks the END of `makeTableSortableUnified()` — the function that actually builds the `.mb-col-hdr-flex` the button lives in, and so the one place guaranteed to run after that layout exists. Every other candidate site had to know it ran late enough, and two of them didn't: `startFetchingProcess()`'s single-table branch and `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()` both call `renderFinalTable()` — whose tail also tries — several steps earlier. This covers the single-table path, the multi-table group loop and snapshot hydration alike, and the 9.99.1010 per-caller workaround has been removed in favour of it. The hook is scoped to the table being processed, so a page with many sub-tables doesn't re-scan them all once per group, and its cheap `_msLengthSource()` check now runs before the row-walking `_msAnyStamped()` fallback.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A failed millisecond-length request is no longer cached as if MusicBrainz had answered "there is no sub-second data here". MusicBrainz's Web Service is intermittently flaky — a 503 while it is being hammered by bots is routine — and caching that turned a few seconds of upstream trouble into a permanently dead ⏱ button for the rest of the page's life. Reported from a live console log: one `HTTP 503` followed by nothing but `cache hit` lines, so every later press was a silent no-op. Only a SUCCESSFUL answer is cached now; a transport failure (any non-OK status or thrown error) leaves nothing behind, so pressing the button again really does retry.

The tooltip in that situation was also flatly wrong: it read "Millisecond precision unavailable here — MusicBrainz has no sub-second length on record for these recordings", a claim about the DATA, when what had actually happened was that the service could not be reached. The button now distinguishes the two. A transient failure turns it YELLOW, names the error (e.g. "Could not load millisecond lengths (HTTP 503) — the MusicBrainz Web Service is temporarily unavailable, which happens when it is under heavy load. Click again to retry.") and stays fully clickable, with no `aria-disabled`, because clicking again is exactly the right response. The dimmed, `aria-disabled` "no sub-second length on record" state is now reserved for what it actually describes: MusicBrainz answered, and the answer is that it holds no lengths here — a settled fact, so that one stays cached.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The ⏱ millisecond toggle was missing entirely from the "Length" header on single-table pageTypes (`place-performances-filtered`, `work-recordings-filtered`, `artist-relationships-filtered`, and every other `tableMode: 'single'` page). Those pages build their header layout AFTER `renderFinalTable()` returns — `startFetchingProcess()` only calls `makeTableSortableUnified()`, which creates the `.mb-col-hdr-flex` the button is inserted into, several steps later — so the render tail's own injection found no flex row and silently did nothing. The button then appeared only if some unrelated later re-render happened to run that tail again, which is why the same page could have it or not depending on whether anything had been filtered or sorted yet: reported live on `place-performances-filtered`, where the 398-row "Recording location for recording" sub-table had no button at all while the 1-row "Shooting location for recording" one did. Now also injected right after `makeTableSortableUnified()`/`initCollapsableColumns()` in the single-table path; the injection is idempotent, so the two call sites never fight. The multi-table path was never affected — `renderGroupedTable()` calls `makeTableSortableUnified()` inside its own group loop, well before its tail.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Expanded the "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL Ⅱ X TURBO" third-party attribution block: it now credits `RECORDING_LENGTH_COLUMN` alongside `RELEASE_EVENT_COLUMN`, records that the ⏱ millisecond track-length feature and the "Release events" column are both INSPIRED BY and modelled on jesus2099's code — not copied from it, and not dependent on it at runtime — and names the two ideas taken directly from his implementation (the single per-page-entity Web Service call rather than one request per row, and the `[H:]M:SS.mmm` display shape his `time()` helper produces, which `_msFormatDuration()` reproduces so both scripts read consistently where both are installed). Also notes that jesus2099 in turn credits loujine's `mbz-showperformancedurations.user.js` as the inspiration for `RECORDING_LENGTH_COLUMN`, and refreshes the recorded `@version` from 2026.1.9 to 2026.5.21.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Millisecond track lengths now also work on the six pageTypes that have no sub-second data in the page itself — `work-recordings`, `artist-relationships`, `place-performances` and their `-filtered` twins (verified: `"length"` does not appear in a single one of a work page's embedded JSON blobs). They are fed by one MusicBrainz Web Service call, `/ws/2/{work|artist|place}/{mbid}?inc=recording-rels`, which returns every recording relationship of the page entity with its length — one request for the whole table, not one per row.

That request is made ONLY when the ⏱ toggle is first pressed, never while the page renders, so a page you don't ask for precision on costs nothing. The glyph shows ⏳ while it is in flight, and the response is cached for as long as you stay on the page: sorting, filtering and switching the toggle off and on again all work from that single response. A failure is cached too and dims the toggle with an explanation, rather than retrying on every click or quietly doing nothing. The tooltip says in advance whether a press will fetch, since on a release page it never does.

Declared per pageType via the new `features.msTrackLengthWs2`, so the toggle is only offered where a source actually exists — a page with neither an embedded payload nor that declaration gets no button rather than a dead one.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Same discard rule as the embedded source, and it earns its keep here: a Web Service value whose rounded seconds disagree with what MusicBrainz already displays is thrown away rather than rendered, since that can only mean the row was matched to the wrong recording. MusicBrainz does populate this column natively on these pages and it rounds there too (5:34.866 is displayed as "5:35"), so the check is meaningful — and it doubles as a guard against a mis-resolved column index, which would then stamp nothing instead of writing durations into some other column. Rows MusicBrainz shows as "?:??" have no length on record and stay unknown in both modes.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Millisecond track lengths on release pages. MusicBrainz stores every track length in milliseconds but only ever displays it rounded to the nearest second — a new ⏱ toggle at the left edge of the "Length" column header re-renders the whole column at full precision ("4:50" → "4:50.160") and back. It costs no network request at all: the values are already embedded in the page MusicBrainz served, in the tracklist component's own `<script type="application/json">` payload. The toggle is page-wide, so on a multi-medium release every medium switches together instead of leaving one disc reading seconds and another milliseconds. Gated by "Enable millisecond track lengths" (default: ON, new ⏱️ TRACK LENGTH PRECISION section); with it off no toggle is injected, nothing is stamped, and the column renders exactly as before.

Sorting, filtering, highlighting and the 📊 unique-values dropdown all follow whatever precision the column is currently showing, with no per-consumer work — they already read the column's rendered text. So you can filter for ".666", and "Length info - Deviation" simply becomes finer-grained. Toggling rewrites the captured source rows and re-renders through `runFilter()`, which is what keeps the active filters, their highlighting and the current sort order intact.

New "Hide a '.000' millisecond part" setting (default: OFF). MusicBrainz stores a length entered as plain "m:ss" with zero milliseconds, so ".000" means "no sub-second data on record" rather than "exactly zero"; switching this on renders those as plain "3:19". Off by default because uniform width keeps the column easier to scan.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: The value revealed is the TRACK length (`tracks[].length`), never the underlying RECORDING's length — two different MusicBrainz fields that differ constantly: on `Born to Run` four of eight tracks disagree, one by three whole seconds. MusicBrainz renders the track length, ROUNDED, which is provable from that same release (`Tenth Avenue Freeze‐Out` displays "3:12", a value only 3:11.666 rounds to and never 3:11.000). The feature's contract is therefore "reveal more precision in the number already on screen", never "show a different measurement", and it is enforced at runtime: a stamped value whose rounded seconds disagree with what MusicBrainz rendered is discarded rather than displayed. Toggling back restores the original string verbatim rather than recomputing it, since recomputing could not reproduce MusicBrainz's rounding.

Resynced `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt` (new "TRACK LENGTH PRECISION" section, the ⏱️ settings block, and a note on the new duration-aware Length sorting under "NUMERIC COLUMN ALIGNMENT") and `CLAUDE.md` (new "Track length precision and the `treleases` trap" section, plus the new `length` debug channel).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Stop deleting MusicBrainz's own `treleases` class from release tracklists. `treleases` is genuine MusicBrainz markup there — a release page natively renders its Length column as `<th class="treleases">` plus one `<td class="treleases">` per track (verified in `tests/snapshots/release-tracks/raw.html`, which the Playwright harness captures with only this script loaded: 9 occurrences, and not one `jesus2099` string, plugin `title` or yellow `text-shadow` in the whole file). jesus2099's `RECORDING_LENGTH_COLUMN` merely reuses the same class name on the page types MusicBrainz does NOT mark (work, artist-relationships, place-performances), and never adds it alone — the same statements also set its own script name as the `title` and, on the header, a yellow `text-shadow`. New `_isJesus2099Treleases()` tests for exactly that co-occurrence, so a bare `treleases` is now recognised as MusicBrainz's and left alone.

Three places keyed on the bare class and are now gated on that predicate: the 9.99.1005 artifact purge (which had started stripping it from the Length `<th>`), `applyColumnErasers()`'s `'jesus2099-any'` Strategy 3b (which had been emptying `class`/`style`/`title` on all eight Length `<td>`s of every release tracklist — a pre-existing defect, visible in the committed `release-tracks` snapshot baseline as `<td class="">`), and `initTreleasesObserver()`'s dispatch (which fired `_repairTreleasesTd()` on our own freshly-rendered native cells, rebuilding them from plain `textContent` and so discarding any filter-highlight spans inside them). The predicate is conservative by construction: with no corroborating evidence the class is left in place, so the failure direction is "a stale third-party class survives", never "native markup is deleted".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Sorting a "Length" column no longer treats MusicBrainz's own "?:??" unknown-duration placeholder as a zero-length recording. It was compared with `parseFloat(text.replace(/[^0-9.-]/g, '')) || 0`, which collapsed "?:??" to 0 and so floated every unknown-length row to the TOP of an ascending sort (descending already put them last, by the same accident). Unknown length is absent data, not zero length, so those rows are now pinned LAST in both directions — in single-column sorts and as a tie-breaker inside a Ctrl+Click multi-column chain alike.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: New explicit duration comparator for "Length" columns: `_parseDurationToMs()` parses `M:SS`, `M:SS.mmm` and `H:MM:SS[.mmm]` (right-padding a short fractional part, so ".5" is 500 ms), and `_compareDurations()` orders on real milliseconds. The previous digits-only `parseFloat` path happened to order genuine durations correctly — seconds are always zero-padded, so "5:05.146" became 505.146 and stayed monotonic — but only by relying on that undocumented invariant.

`createSortComparator()` and `createMultiColumnComparator()` now resolve a column's comparison kind through one shared `_sortColumnKind()` (`'duration'`/`'numeric'`/`'text'`) instead of disagreeing: the single-column path consulted the page definition's own `integerColumns` descriptors and only then a name heuristic, while the multi-column path used the raw header text alone and never looked at the page definition at all. `createSortComparator()`'s third argument changes from an `isNumeric` boolean to that kind string. Duration detection is data-driven — `integerColumns`' `align: ':'` descriptor already means "colon-split duration" — plus an exact `"Length"` name match, so a pageType that renders durations without declaring an `integerColumns` entry for them (`release-discids`' per-disc totals) sorts as a duration too. Alt+Click "sort by column length" still outranks the column's kind, durations included.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The final rendered table no longer carries any leftovers from jesus2099's userscripts. The reported case was the "Length" column header arriving as `<th class="treleases mb-original-column" title="SUPER MIND CONTROL Ⅱ X TURBO" style="text-shadow: yellow 0px 0px 2px; …">` — jesus2099's "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL Ⅱ X TURBO" mutates the native header and cells in place before this script scrapes them, and `makeTableSortableUnified()` rebuilds `th.innerHTML` without ever resetting `className`/`title`/`style`, so all three rode straight through into our own header. Same for every Length `<td>` and, on release pages, for the whole `jesus2099userjs81127*` tracklist family (`toolzone`/`editbutt`/`openEdits` hover buttons, plus markers stamped onto the recording title link and Title cell). New `purgeJesus2099Artifacts()`/`_stripJesus2099InTable()` now clean every rendered `table.tbl` — header row included — on both render paths.

The purge also runs over the captured source rows in `groupedRows`/`allRows`, not just the live DOM. `runFilter()` re-renders by inserting `cloneNode(true)` copies of those rows and classes/attributes survive cloning, so cleaning only the live table would have pasted every marker back in on the next filter keystroke.

Three dispositions, so nothing real is ever destroyed: jesus2099's cover-art icon family is skipped entirely (it already has its own deliberately gated handling in `applyColumnErasers()`'s Strategy 2 and `_stripTransientCellState()` — re-stripping it here would have reintroduced the artwork-loss regression documented in `debug/CAA-missing-doubled.org`); pure-decoration elements are removed outright; everything else keeps the element and loses only the marker class, because those markers sit on genuine MusicBrainz content (`jesus2099userjs81127recording` is stamped on the recording title anchor itself). An unrecognised future marker defaults to the safe "strip, don't remove" path. The plugin `title` and its yellow `text-shadow` are dropped from marker-carrying `<th>`/`<td>` only — native MusicBrainz puts meaningful `title`s on `<a>`/`<abbr>`, and a `text-shadow` with no jesus2099 marker belongs to an unrelated third-party script (30 such elements in `debug/therising.html` alone), so neither may be stripped blind.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Scope note: the purge is confined to the `table.tbl` elements this script renders. Everything jesus2099 puts outside them — its sidebar/sub-header search links, pending-edit counters and its own toolbar (108-123 such markers per page in the sampled snapshots) — is left completely untouched, so the initial page keeps working exactly as before.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
