items: Fixed "Date info - Decade"/"- Month" checkboxes highlighting the matching atom's WHOLE date text (e.g. all of "2008-07-15") instead of just the specific component that made it match — checking a decade now highlights only that atom's own "YYYY" (e.g. "2008"), and checking a month now highlights only its own "MM" digit pair (e.g. "07"), via lookbehind/lookahead-anchored regexes in `_highlightDateAtomMatch()` that never touch the surrounding date text (nor, for a range, the OTHER side's atom).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Date info" family to the unique-values (📊) dropdown, applying automatically to every column fed into a `dateParts` extractor on every pageType (e.g. "Date", "Begin", "End", "Release date" — no per-pageType feature flag needed): "- Precision" is a fixed 3-flag count (📅 complete dates / 🌓 partial dates / ↔️ date ranges, from the new `_findCellDateExpressionParts()`'s own classification of each cell's raw "YYYY[-MM[-DD]]" or dash-joined-range text — never one entry per distinct date value, since that already duplicates the plain column-value list); "- Decade" and "- Month" are open per-value lists bucketing each date's own year (`_dateAtomDecade()`, e.g. "1970-1980") and calendar month name (`_dateAtomMonth()`, e.g. "August", sorted calendar order not alphabetically). A range contributes BOTH its start and end independently to Decade/Month (deduped per row), so e.g. "1973-08-09 – 1973-09-23" counts toward both "August" and "September". Checking an entry narrows the table and highlights the matching text — the whole date expression for a Precision flag, or only the specific matching atom for a Decade/Month entry (so an unrelated side of a range stays unhighlighted).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Length info - Live status" section to the "Length" column's unique-values (📊) dropdown, sibling to "Length info - Deviation": surfaces the same live/studio classification that section already computes internally as its own two directly checkable entries ("🎙️ Live recording" / "⚪ Not live"), only shown when the page has a recognized live-flag column. Checking "🎙️ Live recording" narrows the table and highlights the word "live" in each matching row's Attributes cell.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Length info - Deviation" section to the "Length" column's unique-values (📊) dropdown: buckets each row by how far its Length deviates from the page's average Length (within 10% / 10-25% / 25-50% / 50%+ shorter or longer). Rows flagged "live" in the page's "Attributes" column (or a per-pageType-configurable equivalent, via a new `features.lengthDeviationLiveColumn` key) are excluded from the average — so extended live versions don't skew what counts as "normal" for studio tracks — while still being bucketed against that studio average. Toggleable via the new `sa_enable_length_deviation_section` setting (default on), since this is the first dropdown section that needs a table-wide average rather than a pure per-cell computation.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "Length" column's split-align "M:SS" cell text (rendered as three sibling `.mb-ic-left`/`.mb-ic-sep`/`.mb-ic-right` spans) reading as "5 : 05" instead of "5:05" to both the plain-text filter matcher and the highlighter, so a manually-typed column or global filter like "5:0" never matched any row even though the cell visibly shows "5:05".

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Length info - Duration" section to the "Length" column's unique-values (📊) dropdown: recordings/tracks are bucketed into fixed "N to N+1 minutes" ranges (e.g. "0 to 1 minutes", "5 to 6 minutes"), with MusicBrainz's own "?:??" unknown-duration placeholder mapped to its own "Unknown length" entry. Checking a bucket filters the table to matching rows and highlights the matched duration text.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "Video" column's video-indicator icon rendering left-aligned instead of centered inside its data cell across all pageTypes that use it (e.g. release-tracks, work recordings, various *-recordings listings).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed a "Relationships" column bug on 'label-relationships'/'place-performances' pages: after clicking a sub-section's "Show single-table" button while that page's own Relationships fetch was still in progress, every relationship icon fetched by the new tab appeared doubled. Caused by initRelationshipsColumn() being invoked twice in close succession during snapshot hydration (once internally by runFilter(), once directly by the hydrate tail) — both runs raced over the identical not-yet-populated cells and each appended its own copy of the icons. Fixed by making initRelationshipsColumn() a re-entrancy-guarded wrapper that lets a concurrent call await the in-flight run instead of starting a second overlapping pass.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed a column swap on 'label-relationships'/'place-performances' pages: after clicking a sub-section's "Show single-table" button (or a Load-from-Disk round trip), the "Release events" column showed the "Relationships" column's data and vice versa. Caused by initReleaseEventsColumn()'s _ensureReCell() blindly appending the recreated Release events placeholder cell after the already-restored Relationships cell instead of inserting it before, one column out of step with the fixed header order.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown "Entity info" name-collision split (added in the previous release for two different MusicBrainz areas sharing a display name, e.g. a city and a state both named "New York") was being applied to every entity type instead of just areas — on pages like `work-recordings`, many different recordings sharing one track title exploded the dropdown into one numbered entry per recording instead of staying a single merged entry. Scoped the split to area collisions only.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: CAA/EAA column-header collapse glyph (`.mb-caa-col-hdr-btn`, the ▶/▼+thumbnail toggle in a CAA/EAA column's header): no longer shown until artwork metadata has finished loading. Previously it rendered immediately and permanently, even before any image data was known — now it starts hidden on a page's first render pass and is revealed once the CAA/EAA fetch queue drains, or removed outright if the column turns out to have no artwork at all.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Unique-values dropdown "Event info - Event cancelled"/"Entity info - Event cancelled" entry (e.g. `/user/<username>/ratings/event`, `artist-events`, `place-events`, `area-events`, `tag-value`/`user-tag-value`): now renders in red, reusing MusicBrainz's own native `.cancelled` CSS class — matching the "(cancelled)" marker's own red styling in the "Event" column cell instead of plain text.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Artists with collaboration relationships" report (`/report/CollaborationRelationships`): the "Collaboration" column rendered empty for every collaborator row. The report shares the exact colspan group-header/empty-first-cell table shape as the `report-multiple-linked` family (e.g. `ASINsWithMultipleReleases`), but its URL doesn't follow that family's `...With(Multiple|Many)...` naming pattern, so it fell through to the generic `report-detail` catch-all, which has no group-header merge logic. Now explicitly routed to `report-multiple-linked`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Location/Area splitting (`_routeAreaLink()`/`_maybeCorrectAreaFlagRegion()`): when a "More Flags Everywhere"-decorated area link's bare anchor text collides with a DIFFERENT entity's name (e.g. MusicBrainz's own area "New York" the city vs. area "New York" the state both render bare "New York"), the city was wrongly force-routed into the "Region" column alongside the state instead of staying in "Locality". Fixed via new `_flagIconSubdivisionLabel()`, which reads the decorating icon's own disambiguated `alt`/`title` (e.g. "New York City") instead of the anchor's own ambiguous text.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown "Entity info" `» name:` family: when two DISTINCT MusicBrainz entities share the exact same display name on one column (e.g. the area-name collision above), a single flat `» name: New York` entry used to silently match BOTH real-world entities with no way to isolate either. Split into one entry per underlying href instead (`New York (1)`/`New York (2)`, …), each independently selectable via a new href-scoped `namehref:` compound filter mode — new `_emitNameSynItem()`, `_findCellEntityCommentParts()`'s added `href` field, and matching `_cellMatchesStructureMode()`/`_highlightEntityCommentPartMatch()`/`_structureModeLabel()`/`_structureModeTooltip()` branches.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown: the `instrument-list` pageType's per-family first column (e.g. "Wind instrument", "Family" — see `INSTRUMENT_LIST_COLUMN_NAMES`) gets two new independent binary-flag sections — "Instrument info - Comment" ("💬 has comment", a direct-child `<span class="comment">`) and "Instrument info - Description" ("📝 has description", free text after the "—" separator, which may itself contain nested `<a>` links). New `_findCellInstrumentFacets()` extractor and `_highlightInstrumentCommentMatch()`/`_highlightInstrumentDescriptionMatch()` highlighters.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Unique-values dropdown: the "Event" column's already-existing "Event info - Event cancelled" section (native `span.cancelled` marker, e.g. `/user/<username>/ratings/event/`'s Event ratings sub-table) now also applies to the `user-ratings-type` page type — `_eventCancelledKind`'s page-type gate extended alongside its existing `tag-value`/`user-tag-value` entries. No new extractor/highlighter — reuses `_findCellEventCancelled()`/`_highlightEventCancelledMatch()` unchanged.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown: the alias-table "Locale" column gets a new "Locale info" section — "- Language" (one entry per distinct locale language, e.g. "English", "Chinese (China)", via new `_findCellLocaleInfo()`) and "- Primary" (fixed "🥇 primary"/"◦ not primary" flags, from MusicBrainz's own `(primary)` marker). New `_highlightLocaleLanguageMatch()` highlights the matched language text, and new `_highlightLocalePrimaryMatch()` highlights the "primary" marker's own text when that flag is checked. Alias Types with no Locale at all (e.g. "Legal name", "Search hint") contribute to neither facet.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed by 9.99.986: a SOLO entity (not joined with anyone else) whose own MusicBrainz-rendered `<bdi>` also carries a sibling `.comment` span — e.g. "David Bowie (English singer‐songwriter)" appearing alone in the Artist column, not just in the "Queen & David Bowie" joined credit — had its name computed as the WHOLE bdi text (name + comment combined) instead of just its own name. This broke the "» name: David Bowie" row filter for every solo occurrence (comparing the clean selected value against a comment-polluted name never matched), and kept those rows' name/comment from merging into the same "Entity info - Artist name"/"Entity info - Comment" entries the joined row already offered. `_findCellEntityRefs()` now always scopes an entity's `name`/`nameNode` to its own anchor alone whenever the governing `<bdi>` is an ancestor of it — never the whole bdi — regardless of whether that bdi is shared with another joined entity.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A joined artist credit (e.g. "Queen & David Bowie") silently dropped any entity whose own link MusicBrainz wraps in `<span class="mp">` — its native marker for an entity with open/pending edits — from the "Entity info - Artist name"/"Entity info - Comment" sections of the 📊 unique-values dropdown. `_findCellEntityRefs()` only recognized a credited name as a direct child of its shared `<bdi>` or containing its own nested `<bdi>`; it now resolves the governing `<bdi>` via an ancestor walk instead, so any incidental wrapper is transparent to it.

`_findCellEntityCommentParts()` also mis-attributed comments when a cell has more than one independently-commented entity sharing a `<bdi>` with no `<li>` boundary between them (the same "Queen & David Bowie" shape) — every entity after the first silently inherited the FIRST entity's own comment instead of its own. It now resolves each entity's own adjacent `.comment` span instead of taking the first match in the whole cell.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: recording-fingerprints: the "AcoustID" column's 📊 unique-values dropdown now offers an "AcoustID info - Link status" section (🔗 linked / 🚫 unlinked), letting you filter to just the AcoustIDs that are still linked to this recording or just the ones that have been unlinked. The unlinked entry reuses MusicBrainz's own "disabled-acoustid" styling directly.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks: "Recorded at place"/"Mixed at place" — a single "recorded at:"/"mixed at:" credit listing two or more places, each individually bounded by its own "(from … until …)" date range, appended a duplicate copy of the LAST place's date onto every earlier place's row instead of keeping each place's own date.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: release-tracks: the "Part of series" column's 📊 unique-values dropdown now offers "Part of series - Name"/"- Date"/"- Number" sections, letting you filter by one credited series' own name, disambiguation-comment (usually a date), or numeric series position individually.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks: a track's "Part of series" column glued multiple credited series (comma/"and"-joined in one native relationship) into a single unsplit row instead of listing each series on its own row, unlike the equivalent multi-artist/multi-label AR columns.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A column hidden via the 👁️ "Visible" Column Visibility button reappeared, fully populated with its cell data, the moment any filter or sort re-rendered the table — the toggle only set `display: none` on the `<tr>` elements live in the DOM at toggle time, but every filter/sort/disk-load re-render replaces `<tbody>` content wholesale with fresh clones of the captured source rows, which never saw that mutation. Each table's own header row (never rebuilt) is now used as the source of truth to re-apply hidden columns after every such re-render.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks: the third-party "MB: Inline per-recording streaming & download links" userscript's own `<dl class="ar">` container isn't always a sibling of MusicBrainz's native `<div class="ars">` relationship block — when nested inside it instead, the emptied shell (its own "▼ Streaming/Downloads:" toggle button and label) was left stranded inside the "ARs" column's cell after its actual link data was correctly extracted into the dedicated "Streaming/Downloads" column. Now detached from the DOM the moment it's found, regardless of its original nesting depth, so it's discarded cleanly either way.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Column filter highlighting no longer misses a match that spans a real comma-separator text node between two linked entities — e.g. filtering an artist's Events tab Location column for a query like "k, n" against a native "place in area, area, area" chain (`Midtown Manhattan, New York, New York, …`) correctly narrowed the row count but left the matching area-link boundary with zero visible highlight spans, even though a same-node match elsewhere in the same cell (inside a plain-text comment) highlighted correctly.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Column filter highlighting no longer misses a match that spans a comma/parenthesis/bracket boundary between two DOM text nodes — e.g. filtering an artist's Events tab for a query like "USA, bleach" against an Event cell whose native comment markup places a disambiguation alias directly before a bare comma (`…USA, Bleachers)`) correctly narrowed the row count but left the matching row with zero visible highlight spans.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Column headers on large single-table pages no longer report counts taken from a fraction of the table. On a page like an artist's Events tab (4177 rows), clearing a column filter left the 📊 unique-value badge stuck at a bare multiple of 500 — 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500 depending on the machine — instead of the real 4161, and the ▶N▤ multi-row badge equally wrong (1 instead of 5 for 'Location'). A Load-from-disk hydration showed the wrong number immediately, without any filtering at all. The row-count stat next to the heading was always right, which is what made the mismatch so visible.

Root cause: `runFilter()` is synchronous and so could not await its own `renderFinalTable()` call. Above the chunked-render threshold (`sa_chunked_render_threshold`, default 1000 rows) that render appends rows 500 at a time, yielding to the browser between chunks — so when `runFilter()` continued, only the FIRST 500 rows were in the table. Its entire post-render pass then ran against that fragment, and the deferred header-count scan it schedules measured whatever multiple of 500 had arrived by the time it fired. Nothing recomputed the counts once the remaining chunks landed.

The badges were only the visible tip. The same 500-row window starved every other post-render pass on those pages, so after a filter-clear or a sort the rows past the first chunk kept no per-cell ▶ collapse toggles, no release-group ▶ expand buttons, no CD-TOC tracklist toggles, no re-enabled annotation compare radios, no re-wired Picard tagger cells, no nested-heading toggles, no CAA/EAA artwork enrichment, and no zebra striping, sticky-column or barcode-highlight repaint. All of that now runs against the finished table.

The sticky first column is the clearest example, and was the most visible of these in daily use: re-capturing the committed artist-events sort baseline shows the sticky-column marker going from 502 cells to 4176 — so on a 4174-row table, scrolling past roughly row 500 after a sort or a filter-clear left no sticky column at all.

`renderFinalTable()` gained an optional completion hook, invoked once every row is actually in the table, and `runFilter()`'s single-table post-render work moved into it. Tables below the chunked-render threshold are unaffected down to the last detail: that path executes no `await` at all, so the hook still fires synchronously, in the same call stack, exactly where the code used to run. A render superseded by a newer one (fast typing) never fires its hook — the winning render fires its own.

Load-from-disk had a second instance of the same race: its own ~200-line tail ran immediately after the synchronous `runFilter()` call, i.e. also against 500 rows. It now waits for the render to finish first, so the Release-events, Relationships, Picard, expand-RG, annotation-radio, CD-TOC, barcode and sticky-column passes it drives all see the whole table.

The header-count scan is now scheduled through one entry point that holds it back until any in-flight render has settled and collapses repeat requests into a single pass — `initReleaseEventsColumn()` alone triggers it three times in a row. Two callers that never went through `runFilter()` (the Release-events column population and the column-visibility toggle) were exposed to the same partial-table race and are covered by this too.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The per-column header-count scan no longer runs as one unbroken task. Now that it covers the whole table rather than a 500-row prefix, a full pass over a page like artist-events is roughly 88,000 cell-text extractions (4174 rows × 21 columns); it is now sliced one column per event-loop turn and abandons itself as soon as a newer scan is queued, so the tab stays responsive while the counts fill in. A scan interrupted this way leaves the columns it already reached updated and the rest showing the previous numbers until the newer scan catches up.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown: the panel no longer closes itself the instant it opens when the 📊 button had to be scrolled into view first. Scroll events are dispatched asynchronously (at the next rendering opportunity), so a scroll that happened BEFORE the panel opened was still delivered AFTER it opened, and the close-on-scroll listener acted on it. Because `.mb-col-uniq-wrap` is focusable, this was reachable in normal use: clicking — or tabbing to — a 📊 button that is only partially in view makes the browser scroll it into view on focus, and that scroll event lands one tick later, right after the click handler already built and positioned the panel. The panel flashed open and vanished, with focus bounced back to the previously-focused column filter input.

The close-on-scroll listener now compares the owning 📊 button's CURRENT viewport rect against the rect the panel was positioned against at open time, instead of closing on any scroll event unconditionally. An unchanged rect means nothing actually moved (a stale, pre-open scroll event) and the panel stays open; a changed rect means the page really has scrolled since, the fixed-position panel is no longer anchored to its button, and it closes as before. As a side benefit this also stops an unrelated inner scroll container — one that doesn't move the column header at all — from dismissing an open panel.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown (📊) cache: also invalidate it when a CAA/EAA artwork cell finishes loading. `_artBuildMultiRowArtCell()` rebuilds a cell's image `<li>`s, its per-image type/comment badges and its `ul.dataset.mbArtSearch` search text asynchronously, long after the initial render and with no row show/hide — invisible to the cache's visible-row-set signature. The dropdown reads all three: `valueCounts` picks up the search text via `getCleanColumnText()`, and `artTypeValueCounts`/`artCommentValueCounts` read the badges. Without this, a dropdown opened for a CAA/EAA column before its artwork resolved kept serving pre-enrichment counts on every reopen. Invalidation added to both the REBUILD and FIRST-BUILD branches, so it covers single-table and multi-table pages alike (unlike the neighbouring `_artSyncSearchTextToSourceRow()`, which is multi-table-only by design). Same class as the 9.99.974 sites; this one surfaced after rebasing onto main's v9.99.971/v9.99.972 CAA/EAA multi-table filter fix, which introduced the search-text sync and its own `_rowTextCache` invalidation alongside it.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown (📊) cache: invalidate it for columns whose cells are populated asynchronously, after the initial render. The 9.99.973 cache keys off which rows are currently visible, which cannot see a column that fills previously-empty cells in place with no row show/hide — so a dropdown opened while such a column was still loading would cache a near-empty bundle that nothing ever refreshed (until an unrelated filter or sort happened to change the visible-row signature). New table-wide `_invalidateUniqDropDataCacheForTable(table)` is now called from `initReleaseEventsColumn()` (both post-population re-scan sites), `initRelationshipsColumn()`'s completion handler, and `initPicardTaggerColumn()`; `_artSetInlineSortKey()` additionally invalidates just its own column, since it stamps the `.mb-inline-art-sort-key` sentinel that the dropdown's inline-artwork scan reads, from ~8 CAA/EAA fetch-completion callbacks. Affects the Release events / Release country / Release date, Relationships, Picard tagger and inline CAA/EAA columns.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 4 (`openUniqDrop()` per-open caching): the unique-values dropdown's 5 full `tbody.rows` scan passes (whole-cell value counts, flag-icon segment map, relationship-cell detection, relationship icon counts, inline CAA/EAA-thumbnail counts) are now cached per (table, column) in a `WeakMap`, keyed by a cheap O(rows) signature of the currently visible rows' `data-mb-row-idx` values. Reopening the same column's dropdown with no filter/sort change in between skips straight past all 5 passes. Measured on `artist-events` (4174 rows, 21 columns, median of 5, script 9.99.970 both sides, captured back-to-back on one machine): warm dropdown open 31 347 ms → 581 ms (**54x faster**), with global filter (1242→1292 ms), column filter (1201→1239 ms) and sort (2995→2906 ms) all unchanged within noise. Cold (first) open is unchanged within noise too — 30 649 → 32 985 ms, against an observed ~20% run-to-run spread for that same 30-second 5-pass scan; a cache miss adds only one O(rows) signature build plus one `Map.set`. Each Map/counter declaration became a `_uniqCacheHit ? … : <original>` ternary in place and each scan loop got a `!_uniqCacheHit` guard, so none of the hundreds of `.set()`/`.get()`/`++` call sites inside the loop bodies changed. Keying by the live `<table>` element means a brand-new table (new fetch, disk-load, multi-table sub-table) is always a cache miss, with no manual reset needed.

Landed WITHOUT PERFORMANCE.org Step 3, which it was originally written alongside: `_updateAllColHeaderCounts()` — the function Step 3 caches — is never reached from `openUniqDrop()`, so it contributes nothing to the win above. The one thing Step 4 genuinely needed from Step 3, the shared `_visibleRowSetSignature(table)` helper, is carried here standalone; a later Step 3 can key off the same primitive unchanged.

Found and fixed one correctness gap while implementing: the "Cell structure" section's collapsed/expanded split is read from `expandedCells` (individually-toggled cells), not derivable from the visible-row signature, so a lone cell expand/collapse click would otherwise leave a reopened dropdown showing a stale split. Added `_invalidateUniqDropDataCache(table, colIndex)` and wired it into all 5 places `expandedCells` is mutated by user interaction (`_applyCollapseState()`'s two branches, `ensureCollapseDelegate()`'s three inline toggle branches).

Found and fixed a second gap that the earlier `perf-steps-1-4` / `perf-steps-3-4` versions of this change still carry: 10 further symbols populated inside the (now skipped) first scan pass were neither defaulted from the cache nor stored into it — `editorDeletedValueCounts`, `editorAnyDeletedCount`, `editorRecordedNameValueCounts`, `editorMembershipValueCounts`, `editorCommentValueCounts`, `changelogHasMessageCount`, `changelogNoMessageCount`, `releaseQualityHighCount`, `releaseQualityLowCount`, `releaseQualityNormalCount`. Left as-is they read 0/empty on every warm reopen, silently dropping the "🗑️ any deleted editor", "📜 has changelog message", "🚫 no changelog specified" and "🟢/🟠/⚪ data quality" entries plus every Editor-info value entry — and, since those same counters gate their sections' visibility conditions, potentially collapsing a whole section to empty. Affects the `annotations` pageType (Editor / Version history columns) and every page carrying a "Release" column. Same failure mode as the previously-recorded `roleTokenValueCounts` miss.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: releasegroup-releases (and every other tableMode:'multi' page): an explicitly-uncollapsed CAA/EAA column cell silently re-collapsed on every filter keystroke (single-table pages were never affected). Root cause: v9.99.971's fix forces `_artBuildMultiRowArtCell()`'s FIRST-BUILD branch on every filter/sort re-render, and that branch hardcoded the new cell to collapsed, ignoring the `expandedCells` map the rest of the collapse/expand system already consults. Fixed by making that branch look up `expandedCells` too.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: releasegroup-releases (and every other tableMode:'multi' page): a column filter typed against the CAA/EAA column's per-image type/comment text (e.g. "cassette case") always matched zero rows, even when a row genuinely had matching artwork. Root cause: `renderGroupedTable()` always inserts `row.cloneNode(true)` copies into the DOM, so the "source" rows `runFilter()` matches against never received the async CAA/EAA enrichment applied to the live, rendered clone. Fixed by syncing each enriched image's search text back onto the source row via a new `_artSyncSearchTextToSourceRow()` helper.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: CAA per-image type/comment filter highlighting: fixed a confirmed duplication bug where matching text got wrapped in `.mb-column-filter-highlight` TWICE (nested, visually indistinguishable from a single highlight, but a real DOM defect) — `_artHighlightImageLi()` is legitimately called twice by design (once during cell build, once from an async post-build catch-up) and neither cleared the other's spans first; now idempotent.

CAA per-image highlighting also never fired at all on a page loaded via Load-from-Disk — its saved CAA cell markup is baked in directly and never goes through the enrichment pipeline that used to be the only place highlighting was applied; a new post-filter sweep (`_artHighlightAllBuiltCaaCells()`) now re-applies highlighting to every populated CAA cell regardless of how its content got there.

Removed the literal en-dash (" \u2013 ") separator between a CAA image's type badge and its comment, replacing it with a plain space — as a side effect this also fixes cross-tag highlighting for filters spanning both (e.g. typing a type followed immediately by the start of its comment), which the en-dash previously broke.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Extended the `artist-releases` (BoDeans) Playwright regression suite: CAA type/comment substring cases, a real chaban day-of-week third-party-interop case, a Catalog# multi-row collapse-indicator assertion, a Relationships substring case, filter-status/tooltip/button UI-state assertions folded into every existing case, and a genuine exercise of the opt-in pre-filtered-disk-load (§J) and column-visibility (§K) sections — the latter previously used a checkbox selector that never matched real DOM and had never actually run against live markup before.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `highlightCrossTag()` now correctly highlights a plain-text filter match that spans a comment boundary (e.g. an entity's `<bdi>` name into a separate sibling `<span class="comment">`, joined only by a synthesized/` ` space) — confirmed on Release, Label, and Country/Date columns. Root cause: `String.trim()` strips ` ` identically to regular whitespace, so `highlightCrossTag()` dropped the connecting text node and joined the surviving fragments with no separator, unlike `getCleanColumnText()`'s own unconditional space-joining behavior used for the actual row match — the row count narrowed correctly, but the highlight regex never matched inside `highlightCrossTag()` itself.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `runFilter()`'s CAA/EAA artwork initialization never registered the queue-idle completion callback (`_caaQueue.onIdle(_showCaaCompletionToast)`) that `startFetchingProcess()`'s equivalent block already had — so the "🎨 All CAA/EAA artwork loaded" toast and the `#mb-info-display-caa` status-bar segment never appeared after *any* call to `runFilter()` (every ordinary filter/sort action, and every Load-from-Disk hydration), even though the artwork itself always loaded correctly. Fixed by registering the same callback in `runFilter()`, mirroring `startFetchingProcess()`'s pattern; `makeCaaQueue()`'s own `onIdle()` already fires safely even when the queue is already idle at registration time, so this is safe on every `runFilter()` pass.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed a bug on `tag-value`/`user-tag-value`/`artist-credit`/`user-ratings` pages where a sub-table's trailing overflow row ("See all N entities"/"View all ratings", already replaced by a "Show all N rows" button on first render) secretly survived in the in-memory row arrays and reappeared as a real, permanently visible row — in EVERY sub-table with an overflow button, not just the one being acted on — the instant any column in any uncollapsed sub-table was sorted, flipping that sub-table's row-count badge from `(N)` to `(N+1 of N)`. Root cause: the removal code matched the row by DOM reference (`indexOf`) against a `cloneNode(true)` copy that is never reference-equal to the original stored in `group.rows`/`group.originalRows`, so the removal silently no-op'd every time. Fixed by marking the row with a `dataset` attribute at creation time (`applyListToTable`) and stripping it from the row arrays by that marker instead.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Resynced `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt` against every user-facing change from 9.99.888 through 9.99.964: added the new `annotations` pageType's own ANNOTATION HISTORY PAGE section (Editor/Version-history columns, relocated "Compare versions" button, always-selectable Old/New radios), documented the two new 📊 unique-values dropdown sections ("Entity info - Role" atomic role tokens, "Release info - Data quality") plus the annotations-only "Editor info"/"Version history - Changelog" sections and the Ctrl+Click collapse/expand-all-sections behavior, corrected several stale default-value claims (Flag Icons In Unique-Values Dropdown OFF→ON, Unique-Values Dropdown Visible Rows 8→30, "Show single-table" button OFF→ON, Annotation-section auto-expand OFF→ON, "ARs" column collapse ON→OFF, auto-resize-on-load default noted as ON), added the missing "Event-Additional-Info" synthetic column and the new uncertain-day "/DD" date format to the Event-Parts extractor description, added the new "Default Hidden Columns per Page Type" setting to COLUMN MANAGEMENT/SETTINGS, and updated RELEASE-TRACKS PAGE for Vocals' vocal-range consolidation, the new colored/italicized credit-attribute-word styling, and the Relationships column's disk-round-trip-without-refetch behavior.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The `eventParts` synthetic column extractor's Event-Date now recognizes MusicBrainz's own "uncertain day" date convention — a full date followed by one or more `/DD` segments, e.g. `2001-12-22/23` (recorded on the 22nd or 23rd, exact day unclear). Previously this shape wasn't recognized as a date at all and the whole string fell through to Event-Detail instead of Event-Date.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the `eventParts` synthetic column extractor (Event-Type/Event-Date/Event-Detail/Event-Venue/Event-Venue-Detail/Event-City/Event-State/Event-Country/Event-Additional-Info, parsed from a recording's "Comment" field on Work-Recordings/Artist-Recordings-style pages) mis-parsing rows whose Event-Additional-Info text (after the ';') itself contains a comma — e.g. "...OH, USA; YouTube – X, from Y". The location string used to be comma-split before the ';' boundary was located, so an extra comma inside Additional-Info fragmented it into bogus extra location segments, silently dropping the venue name and shifting City/State/Country by one field. The ';' boundary is now located in the full location string first, before any comma-splitting.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the third-party "sanojjonas" userscript's clutter container (`#sanojjonasRoot`, plus the unrelated "Taggregator" panel) sometimes still being present on the final rendered page after a normal fetch or a "Load from Disk" load — happened when the action button (or disk load) was triggered before sanojjonas' own asynchronous script had rendered its container yet, so it finished injecting after this script's one-shot cleanup passes had already run. The late-injection watcher that already existed for the fast cross-tab "Show single-table" snapshot path is now also armed on the normal fetch path (events/artist-releasegroups/collections-releases-multi pages) and on the "Load from Disk" path.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the discography-view (Complete/Official/Non-Official/Complete (merged)) master-toggle "Show/Hide all sub-sections" button getting permanently out of sync with the actual collapse state after switching views — most visible on a view where nothing auto-expands (e.g. the Non-Official view with no "Album" category). Clicking the desynced button was worse: it unconditionally showed/hid every sub-table on the page, including ones belonging to a currently-filtered-out view, dumping unexpected headerless content into the page while that view's own section headers correctly stayed hidden. The button now resyncs on every render (not just the first) and its click handler now correctly skips sub-tables that aren't part of the current discography view.

Fixed sorting a column in a multi-table page's sub-table, then switching discography views, losing the sort's visual indicators (column header tint, sort-glyph highlight, body zebra striping, and per-table sort-status text) even though the underlying row order correctly stayed sorted. All of these now persist across a view switch exactly like the row order already did — a view switch no longer resets sort-related state at all, only genuinely view-specific state (filters, highlighting, collapse state, CAA visibility).

Fixed body zebra striping (the alternating per-value-change background shade in a sorted column, as opposed to the column header's own tint) getting lost specifically after visiting the Complete (merged) view, persisting for one further view switch even after leaving it. Both the merged-view row-combining pass and the pass that restores a table's rows when leaving merged view are separate code paths from the normal render pipeline and were never re-applying the active sort's tint to their own freshly-inserted rows; they now do.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Shortened the four discography-view buttons on artist-releasegroups pages (Complete Discography → Complete, Official Discography → Official, Non-Official Discography → Non-Official, Complete Discography (merged) → Complete (merged)) and added a shared "Discography:" label after the button-group divider so the repeated word only appears once.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed a broken sub-table filter (STF) input selector used in 14 places across the script (`input[type="text"]` instead of the STF input's actual `type="search"`, forced by `_hardenFilterInputAgainstAutofill()`). This silently made every STF-active check inert — the per-sub-table `<h3>` "Clear all filters" button never appeared while only an STF filter was active, the "Clear ALL filters" bulk button never cleared STF inputs, and the internal re-apply-after-render pass never fired at all.

Fixed the CAA/EAA "big picture" image stripe and its per-sub-table count badge reverting to the full, unfiltered set after sorting a column on a multi-table page (e.g. release-group "Show all Releases") while a sub-table filter (STF) was active. The sort's full re-render now correctly starts each STF-filtered-out row's image wrapper hidden, and the row-count/highlighting reapply now runs synchronously as part of that same render instead of via a debounced, dead-selector code path — so the stripe/badge never visibly revert in the first place. The global, page-wide CAA/EAA toggle-button count intentionally still shows the unfiltered total regardless of any STF filter, matching existing behavior.

Fixed clearing a sub-table filter (STF) after a column sort leaving the table permanently stuck showing only the previously-filtered rows, with stale row counts and stale highlighting, and no way to get back to the full row set. Root cause: the first render of a multi-table page inserted its row elements by direct reference rather than by clone, so STF's own row-hiding markers leaked permanently into the canonical row data the moment a later re-render (e.g. a sort) rebuilt the table from it. Row insertion on first render now clones, matching how every subsequent filter/sort re-render already worked.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Added `REFACTORING.org`, a structural-refactor review of the userscript's architecture (single IIFE, `pageDefinitions` registry, `configSchema`, extractor registries) independent of `PERFORMANCE.org`'s filter/sort/cache work. Ranks 9 candidates found by direct file survey — worth doing: consolidating the 11-entry `*-tags` pageDefinitions cluster and the 7 filtered/unfiltered pairs (mirrors the already-proven `entityFeatures` pattern), adding a startup-time validator for typo'd `features` keys/`extractor:` strings (currently fail silently), and de-duplicating the `dateParts` and `video`/`caa` `appendSortKey` extractor logic; conditional: extracting `configSchema` to its own `@require`'d file (closure-safe but inherits Tampermonkey's known `@require` URL-caching staleness risk); rejected: a full bundler-based module split (no existing build tooling, shared mutable module state crosses every proposed boundary, and only ~12% pageType snapshot coverage makes it unverifiable at this size), further `pageDefinitions` reorganization, and merging `renderFinalTable`/`renderGroupedTable`. Docs only; no userscript runtime changes.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Introduced `SA_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT_VERSION` ('1.1'), replacing the two hardcoded `version: '1.0'` literals in `saveTableDataToDisk()`/`captureSubtableSnapshot()`. Load-time hydration (`_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()`) now checks the saved format version via a new `_snapshotVersionAtLeast()` helper before applying the 9.99.956/9.99.957 fast-path restoration below, so pre-existing `.json.gz` files (format 1.0) keep loading exactly as before — full Relationships re-fetch, no cdtoc tracklist-toggle restore — with no behavior change and no new user-facing warning dialog. This is distinct from the script's own `// @version` — it's a save-file format version, now actually meaningful instead of an inert label.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `cdtoc` pages' tracklist show/hide toggle now survives a Save-to-disk/Load-from-disk round trip. Previously `data-cdtoc-tracklist-html`/`-visible` (row-level dataset attributes read by `_cdtocInitTracklistToggles()`) were never captured by `saveTableDataToDisk()` — only `<td>` cell HTML was serialized, never `<tr>` dataset — so the toggle silently no-opped after every disk-load. Fixed via a new top-level `cdtocTracklistData` field (index-aligned with `dataToSave.rows`, mirroring the existing `discOfficialCategories` pattern), restored onto each reconstructed `<tr>` in `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()` before `_cdtocInitTracklistToggles()` runs (gated by format version — see 9.99.958).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The "Relationships" injected column (`td.mb-rel-cell`) now round-trips through Save-to-disk/Load-from-disk with **zero** network/IndexedDB activity when every cell was already fully populated at save time. Previously `mb-rel-cell` was explicitly excluded from serialization, so every disk-load re-triggered a live WS/2 fetch to repopulate it — even though its icons are plain hotlinked `` URLs (never `blob:`), so nothing actually prevented a verbatim restore. `saveTableDataToDisk()`/`captureSubtableSnapshot()` now serialize `mb-rel-cell` cells via a shared `_buildDiskCellData()` helper, adding `mbid`/`relDone` fields (mirrored from the live cell's own dataset) only for that column. `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()` applies those fields to the reconstructed `` (class + dataset) so `_ensureRelCell()`'s existence check and `initRelationshipsColumn()`'s `td.dataset.mbid && !td.dataset.relDone` candidate filter both correctly treat a restored cell as already done — a row saved mid-fetch (rare) still completes normally on load. Also fixes a latent completion-signal gap this change would otherwise have introduced: when every candidate cell is already done, `initRelationshipsColumn()` previously returned before ever showing the completion toast/status segment, meaning `#mb-info-display-rel` — what `waitForRelationshipsComplete()` (Playwright test helper) and real users both watch for — would never become visible for an all-done page; it now fires the same signal (with 0 elapsed time, 0 fetches) on that path too. New `sa_rel_idb_ttl_days` setting (default 30, mirrors the existing `sa_art_idb_image_ttl_days` for CAA/EAA) replaces the hardcoded 7-day `_REL_IDB_TTL_MS` constant for the Relationships WS2 IndexedDB cache.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: tests: added artist-events performance-comparison instrumentation — `tests/live/artist-events-interactions.spec.js` (global/column filter, sort both directions, header-badge sanity, uniq-dropdown cache-invalidation correctness), `tests/support/capture-interaction-perf.js` (median-of-5 timing for global filter/column filter/sort/uniq-dropdown cold-vs-warm-open, written per-branch to `tests/snapshots/artist-events/interaction-perf-<branch>.json` so `main` and a performance-focused branch can be compared side by side), and `tests/support/capture-snapshots.js` extended with `post-filter.html`/`post-sort.html` full-DOM regression snapshots for `artist-events` (catching a rendering regression a canonical filter/sort action could introduce that no single correctness assertion would catch). All three load via the newly-captured `tests/fixtures/saved-data/artist-events.json.gz` disk fixture (`tests/support/capture-fixture.js`, extended with an `artist-events` entry and `seedGmValues`/`renderTimeout` support) rather than a live 42-page fetch. Canonical filter/sort/uniq-drop targets shared across all three via new `tests/support/artistEventsFixture.js`, so they can't drift apart. New `waitForActualRowCount()` helper in `tests/support/filterSortAssertions.js` — a stronger completion signal than the existing status-text-based waits for an action that narrows a large single-table page then widens it back out (confirmed empirically that `#mb-filter-status-display`/`.mb-row-count-stat` both update before the tbody rebuild and the `#mb-render-heading` chunked-render overlay have actually finished catching up, on `artist-events`' 4174 rows). No `ShowAllEntityData.user.js` changes — pure test-infra additions, per this project's existing precedent for test-only commits.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: sanojjonas cleanup: sanojjonas' own userscript now wraps all of its infinite-scroll `load`/`load2`.../`bottom1`-`bottom7` placeholders inside a single `<div id="sanojjonasRoot">` container (confirmed via debug/sanoj-initial.html, debug/sanoj-new.html). Replaced the whole-document `[id]` sweep and `/^(load\d*|bottom\d+)$/` ID-shape regex in `_isSanojjonasContainerId()`/`_findSanojjonasContainers()` with a fixed 3-ID lookup (`#sanojjonasRoot` plus the two Taggregator IDs), used by both the one-shot `removeSanojjonasContainers()` pass and `_watchForLateSanojjonasInjections()`'s late-injection watcher. Also fixes a latent bug where removing only the wrapper's individual descendants (never the wrapper itself) could leave an empty orphaned `#sanojjonasRoot` shell behind.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Corrected a mis-attribution in the sanojjonas cleanup code's comments: the "Taggregator" tag-aggregation panel (`#taggregator-settings`/`#taggregator-import-button`) is a separate, unrelated userscript by zabe (`@namespace https://github.com/zabe40`), not a second script by sanojjonas — the comments previously described both as "two unrelated userscripts by that [sanojjonas] author".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks: stopped stripping the "VZ: MusicBrainz - Generate Recording Comments For A Release" userscript's `button.work-button-style` and `span#settings-icon` out of `h2.tracklist` via `removeSelectors` — those two entries were removed from the `release-tracks` pageDefinition. The header cleanup previously fired on every `finalCleanup()` pass (i.e. every time the "Show all Tracks for Release" action re-renders), silently deleting that other script's button/settings-icon each time. They now survive and continue to render inside `h2.tracklist`, right after the "Tracklist" text.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed sanojjonas userscript artefacts still surviving on the "Show single-table" cross-tab snapshot page (v9.99.951's `removeSanojjonasContainers()` fix alone wasn't enough there) — confirmed via debug/sanoj-debug.log/debug/sanoj-page.html that sanojjonas' own script(s) are asynchronous and noticeably slower than jesus2099's: on this fast snapshot-hydration bootstrap (settles within one `setTimeout(...,0)` tick of the tab opening), only 2 of 11+ real sanojjonas elements had appeared by the time the one-shot `finalCleanup()` cleanup ran, leaving everything injected afterward to survive as visible artefacts. Added `_watchForLateSanojjonasInjections()`, a 15-second `MutationObserver` mirroring the existing `_watchForLateJesus2099Injections()` pattern, wired into the same cross-tab snapshot bootstrap call site. Refactored `_findSanojjonasContainers()`/`removeSanojjonasContainers()` to share the new `_isSanojjonasContainerId()` predicate with the observer, so the one-shot and late-watch removal logic can't drift apart.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed leftover "sanojjonas" userscript artefacts (the "Taggregator" tag-aggregation tool's own sidebar panel, `#taggregator-settings`/`#taggregator-import-button`) appearing after the table on `artist-relationships-filtered` (`/artist/<mbid>/relationships?link_type_id=<n>`) — its consolidated `Relationships` column sits right before a run of sanojjonas' own infinite-scroll placeholder `<div>`s (`#load`, `#load2`, …, `#bottom1`, `#bottom2`, …) directly after the table, followed by the Taggregator panel further down. `removeSanojjonasContainers()` previously only targeted a fixed `load`/`load2`-`load4`/`bottom1`-`bottom6` ID list and never included the Taggregator IDs at all; `debug/sanoj.html`'s own snapshot goes up to `bottom7`, one past that list, confirming it was already silently missing artefacts even for its original targets. Replaced the fixed list with a new `_findSanojjonasContainers()` helper that matches `load`/`bottom` containers by ID SHAPE (`/^(load\d*|bottom\d+)$/`, no suffix cap) plus the two fixed Taggregator IDs, shared by both `removeSanojjonasContainers()` and the final-cleanup presence check (previously a separately hardcoded, now-eliminated duplicate list) so the two can never drift out of sync again.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The "Release" column now offers a "Release info - Data quality" (⭐) unique-values dropdown section — three fixed entries for MusicBrainz's own native data-quality marker: 🟢 high, 🟠 low, and ⚪ normal (normal = no `high-data-quality`/`low-data-quality` marker span present at all, matching MusicBrainz's own convention of never emitting an explicit "normal" marker). New `_findCellReleaseDataQuality()` extractor and `release-quality-high`/`release-quality-low`/`release-quality-normal` structure modes, gated by column name only (`isReleaseCol`, no page-type check) so it applies automatically on every page type with a "Release" column — release listings, release-group overview pages, the `LowDataQualityReleases` report, etc. No highlighter (the marker span is empty/decorative, nothing visible to wrap), mirroring `catalog-has-prefix`'s own no-highlight precedent.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The `annotations` pageType's native "Editor" column now also splits into five new synthetic columns via a new `ColumnDataExtractor.editorActivity()` extractor: "Deleted editor" (literal `true` when the editor is a deleted-account placeholder, empty otherwise), "Active for"/"Active since" (the visible `.comment` span's duration phrase and bare trailing year, e.g. "active 10 years until 2015" → `10 years`/`2015`), and "Active start date"/"Active end date" (the two ISO dates parsed from the editor link's own tooltip membership line, e.g. "active 10 years (2005-07-28 〜 2015-09-21)" → `2005-07-28`/`2015-09-21`). Reuses the existing `_findCellEditorInfo()` helper directly (the same one backing this column's "Editor info" unique-values dropdown sections from the previous version) rather than re-deriving its own DOM/tooltip parsing.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The `annotations` pageType's 📊 unique-values dropdown now offers four new "Editor info" sub-sections for the "Editor" column — "- Deleted" (🗑️, one entry per distinct deleted-editor placeholder identity, e.g. "Deleted Editor #135888", plus a sibling "any deleted editor" aggregate flag that matches every deleted-editor row regardless of which specific ID), "- Recorded name" (🏷️, the tooltip's own historically-recorded editor name, only offered when it differs from the row's current name), "- Membership" (🕰️, the tooltip's own "active N years (start 〜 end)" span), and "- Comment" (💬, the visible `.comment` span's differently-worded restatement of the same membership fact) — plus a new "Version history - Changelog" (📜) section for the "Version history" column, a binary "has changelog message"/"no changelog specified" flag pair (never enumerating the actual free-text messages, matching this file's existing free-text-prose convention). New `_findCellEditorInfo()`/`_findCellChangelogPresence()` extractors, `_cellMatchesStructureMode()` branches (`editordeleted:`/`editor-any-deleted`/`editorrecordedname:`/`editormembership:`/`editorcomment:`/`changelog-has-message`/`changelog-no-message`), and `_highlightEditorDeletedMatch()`/`_highlightEditorCommentMatch()`/`_highlightChangelogNoneMatch()` (the recorded-name/membership/has-message facets are sourced from a hover-only `title` attribute or intentionally untracked free text, so they deliberately get no highlight, same as this dropdown's other pure-state flags). Deliberately bespoke, not built on `_findCellEntityRefs()`/`KNOWN_ENTITY_LINK_KINDS` — a `/user/{name}` editor link is a non-MBID reference those catalog-entity-only helpers never recognize anyway, so there's no overlap with the generic "Entity info" family.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Added `extractMainColumn: 'Editor'` to the `annotations` pageType — splits the Editor cell into synthetic `MB-Name`/`Comment`/`Primary alias` columns via `_extractMainColumnParts()`, the same treatment already applied to every other page's main entity-link column.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the multi-table `.mb-master-toggle` ("Show/Hide all sub-sections") button on `release-tracks` (and any other page where one or more sub-tables start expanded by default — a single sub-table, or a small `album`/`official` group) always initially reading "Show all sub-sections" even though every medium's tracklist was already visible on screen. Root cause: the button is created, hardcoded to `dataset.state = 'collapsed'`, BEFORE the `dataArray.forEach` loop that actually decides each sub-table's `shouldStayOpen` state runs — so its label never reflected the real DOM. Now synced once, right after that loop, against each table's actual `display` value: if any sub-table is visible the button starts as "Hide all sub-sections" instead.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed `tests/support/browser.js`'s `waitForRenderComplete()` (used by the HTML-snapshot regression harness's `capture-snapshots.js`) returning before a `tableMode: 'single'` page's render had actually finished, on any pageType whose row count exceeds `sa_chunked_render_threshold` (default 1000) — reported live on 9.99.944's `artist-events` capture (4174 rows): the committed `rendered.html` still showed the "🎨 Rendering rows... 2,000 / 4,174" chunked-render progress overlay on screen, and the auto-resize button was missing from the action bar entirely. Root cause: `startFetchingProcess()` sets `#mb-filter-container` visible — the only signal this function previously waited on — SYNCHRONOUSLY, in the same tick it calls `renderFinalTable()`, which for a large table `await`s a `requestAnimationFrame`-yielding batched-insertion loop; `addAutoResizeButton()` and the `sa_auto_resize_columns` auto-resize pass both only run strictly after that loop resolves. Now additionally waits for the render-progress overlay (`#mb-render-heading`) to be absent (no race — confirmed both DOM mutations happen in one synchronous JS burst, so if the overlay was going to appear it already has by the time this check can run) and, gated by a new configurable `waitForAutoResize` option (`tests/pagetypes.json`, default `true`, added explicitly to all four registered pageTypes), for the Resize button's title to reach its "Restore…" completed state. Re-captured `artist-events` (both overlay/button symptoms confirmed gone, deterministic on first repeat) and re-verified `artist-releasegroups`/`release-tracks`/`releasegroup-releases` all still report `unchanged` — they happened to already be timing-safe by luck, not by any prior guarantee. Also refreshed `artist-releasegroups`' `perf-baseline.json` (`medianWallMs` 21660 → 33436) since `measureOnce()`'s wall-clock now legitimately includes the resize wait — the old baseline would otherwise falsely WARN as a regression on the next `--perf` run for a measurement-completeness reason, not a real slowdown. Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

sections.label: ⚙️ Internal
items: Added `artist-events` (Bruce Springsteen) to the HTML-snapshot regression harness (`tests/pagetypes.json`, `tests/snapshots/artist-events/{raw,rendered}.html`, `tests/snapshots/registry.org`) — a deliberately large, paginated (42 native MB pages, 4174 rows), single-table pageType, earmarked as a future performance-comparison target for repeated sort/column-filter/unique-values-dropdown interactions against a later performance-focused branch (no new perf instrumentation for those specific interactions built yet — scoped as a separate task by explicit agreement). `sa_enable_caa_pics` forced off for this capture only (EAA queue too slow at this row count, same rationale as the existing `artist-releasegroups` row); deterministic (`unchanged`) on the very first repeat capture, no other drift sources found. Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

sections.label: ⚙️ Internal
items: Added `releasegroup-releases` ("Tougher Than the Rest") to the HTML-snapshot regression harness (`tests/pagetypes.json`, `tests/snapshots/releasegroup-releases/{raw,rendered}.html`, `tests/snapshots/registry.org`). Found and fixed real capture non-determinism specific to this pageType before committing a baseline: the "Relationships" injected column's real, unstubbed WS/2 fetch produced different purchase-link order/content across runs, and the CAA completion toast's visibility raced the snapshot timing — both features are forced off for this capture only (seedGmValues), mirroring the existing `artist-releasegroups` row's own precedent; both are covered separately by `idb-cache-hit-bigbox.spec.js` (9.99.942) via direct IndexedDB seeding instead of live network. Confirmed via a byte-level diff before disabling, and re-verified deterministic (`unchanged`) across repeat capture runs after.

Added `tests/live/registry.org`, a dashboard indexing every spec under `tests/live/` (page/URL/title/what it verifies/why that page), distinct in scope from `tests/snapshots/registry.org` (which only covers pages with a committed HTML-snapshot baseline pair — no functional/behavioral live spec, including the new IDB one above, belongs there). Manual dashboard data only; no code changes.

sections.label: ⚙️ Internal
items: Added IndexedDB-tier live test coverage for CAA cover-art image caching (`tests/live/idb-cache-hit-bigbox.spec.js`, `tests/support/{capture-idb-fixture,idbFixture}.js`, `tests/fixtures/idb-state/releasegroup-releases-caa-bigbox-images.json`), on the `releasegroup-releases` pilot page (7 real releases across its two sub-tables, not 6 — confirmed live after an initial miscount). Covers both DOM locations fed by the same IDB-backed `images` store: the "bigbox" / big-picture image stripe (`_artInitBigPics()`) and the inline thumbnail rendered in front of each release name in the Release column (`_artInitInlinePics()`, `addCAA: 'Release'`/`sa_caa_pics_inline`) — both default to the identical `front-250` fetch size, so they resolve through the same cache entries, but each is asserted independently rather than one standing in for the other. Confirmed empirically (and in Playwright's own source) that `storageState({indexedDB: true})` cannot round-trip Blob-valued IndexedDB records — a captured `images`-store record decodes on restore to a non-Blob placeholder, which made the userscript's own `URL.createObjectURL()` throw and silently fall through to a stubbed, always-404 network fetch. Worked around this by capturing real coverartarchive.org image bytes once (`capture-idb-fixture.js`, via a custom network-passthrough `GM_xmlhttpRequest` since GM_xhr bypasses CORS and a plain `fetch()` can't read the response cross-origin) into a plain base64 JSON fixture, then seeding IndexedDB directly inside the page (`idbFixture.js`'s `seedArtIdbFixture()`, via `indexedDB.open()`/`put()` in a `page.addInitScript()`) before the userscript's own DB open — sidestepping `storageState`'s serializer entirely. The new spec includes a control test (no IDB seed) proving the network-stubbed fixture-restored test is genuinely exercising the IDB tier for both DOM locations rather than trivially passing regardless. Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

sections.label: ⚙️ Internal
items: Added `tests/fixtures/thirdPartyScripts/` (`jesus2099-title-mismatch.js`, `rogue-filter-writer.js`) and `tests/support/thirdPartyScripts.js` (`injectThirdPartyScript()`) — hand-built DOM-mutation snippets simulating specific known third-party userscript side effects (not vendored copies of any real script), injectable before or after our own script's render. Backs two new live specs: one confirming the Structure/Flags detection correctly picks up a jesus2099-style title/recording-name mismatch marker, one confirming `_isGenuineFilterInputEvent()`'s guard against an untrusted column-filter write still holds (the real debug/fail.debug incident this guard was added to fix) — found empirically that the guard's rejection actively resets the poisoned input rather than just ignoring it. Promoted `seedGmValues()` out of `capture-snapshots.js` into `tests/support/gmStubs.js` as a shared export, now used by both. Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

items:
Added a "page title" column to `tests/snapshots/registry.org` (third column, after URL) — the entity name/title from each pilot page's `

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed `tests/support/snapshot.js`'s capture functions leaking this userscript's own injected `<script>` source into saved `rendered.html`/`raw.html` snapshots — opening a saved file directly in a browser showed the raw JS source dumped as literal page text (a `</script` substring inside the source prematurely closed the real script tag). Now strips every `<script>` element and inserts a `<base>` tag before serializing, matching `tests/support/test.js`'s existing precedent. Also switched `captureRaw()` from `domcontentloaded` to `load` — a native MusicBrainz page-JS widget was found racing that event, causing false diffs unrelated to any real change. Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

sections.label: ⚙️ Internal
items: Added `performance.mark()`/`performance.measure()` instrumentation ('sa-fetch-phase'/'sa-render-phase') at `startFetchingProcess()`'s existing internal `fetchingTimeStart`/`renderingTimeStart` boundaries, readable via `performance.getEntriesByType('measure')` — backs the HTML-snapshot harness's `--perf` timing mode (`tests/support/capture-snapshots.js`). No sort-phase mark added — confirmed by reading the function that sorting never happens during the initial fetch/render, only later via a separate user-triggered column-sort click. Adds no UI and changes no user-visible behavior.

sections.label: ⚙️ Internal
items: Added the HTML-snapshot regression harness pilot (`tests/support/{snapshot,browser,capture-snapshots}.js`, `tests/pagetypes.json`), covering both `artist-releasegroups` and `release-tracks`: captures MB's raw page + the script's fully-rendered output, scrubbing known-volatile content (build-hashed asset URLs, this script's own self-reported timing text, and MusicBrainz's own per-request-randomized embedded JSON key order) before diffing against the committed baseline in `tests/snapshots/`. Also adds a `--perf` timing mode (5-sample median wall/stage timing vs. a committed baseline, 25%/3x warn/fail thresholds) and `tests/snapshots/registry.org`. Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

sections.label: ⚙️ Internal
items: Added `tests/support/diskFixture.js` (`loadFromDiskFixture()`) and `tests/support/capture-fixture.js`, a reusable capture script producing `tests/fixtures/saved-data/<pageType>.json.gz` baselines via the script's own Save-to-disk dialog. Added `tests/live/disk-fixture-load.spec.js` and a committed `releasegroup-releases.json.gz` pilot fixture, verifying disk-loaded renders are immune to MusicBrainz data drift (exact row/group counts asserted). Corrected the original design's file-input selector (`accept*="json"`, not `accept*="gz"`, to disambiguate from the vestigial dead `#mb-file-input`) and traced the dialog's real 2-click sequence — see task-playwright-test-infra-expansion.md's Part 6 implementation notes. Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

Corrected the original design's settle-wait against real, variable debounce timing (see task-playwright-test-infra-expansion.md's Part 5 implementation notes) and the STF input's real selector. Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

Test tooling only; no userscript runtime changes.

sections.label: ⚙️ Internal
items: Added a `window.__saTest` debug hook (`getUniqDropSections()`, `closeUniqDrop()`), gated behind `window.__SA_TEST_MODE__` — a read-only introspection surface for the Playwright test harness, inert outside test runs. Adds no UI and changes no user-visible behavior.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'annotations' pageType: fixed the Old/New "Compare versions" radios becoming completely unselectable under certain filter conditions — the previous "Old must be strictly older than New" range restriction (re-implementing MusicBrainz's own native client-side JS, since this script's row rebuilding drops it) was re-applied against only the currently-filtered/visible rows, and could end up disabling every remaining radio in one column with no valid pair reachable without first clearing the filter. Replaced with simply keeping every Old/New radio always enabled — every combination is now selectable regardless of the active filter or which pair is currently checked.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'annotations' pageType: fixed the "Compare versions" h2-header button swapping sides with the row-count stat span on every sort/filter re-render (button-after-count on initial load, button-before-count afterwards) — updateH2Count() removes and recreates that span on every re-render, always re-inserting it immediately before filterContainer, which displaced a button anchored on filterContainer itself. Anchoring the button on the count span (when present) instead keeps it consistently positioned right after the h2's native text and before the count, on every render.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'annotations' pageType: added an 8px left margin (matching .mb-row-count-stat's own left-margin convention) to the relocated "Compare versions" h2-header button — it previously sat flush against the h2's native "Annotation history" text with no visible gap.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'annotations' pageType: fixed "Compare versions" only ever being able to compare the newest revision against another — MusicBrainz's native Old/New radio range restriction is client-side JS tied to the original DOM nodes, which this script's cloneNode/importNode-based row rebuilding silently drops on every sort/filter re-render (leaving only the static initial-page disabled attributes: New locked to the newest row, Old unrestricted). initAnnotationCompareRadios() re-derives and re-wires the "Old must be strictly older than New" constraint after every (re)render, matching native behavior: selecting an Old row now correctly widens the selectable New range up to (but not including) it, and vice versa.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: 'annotations' pageType: moved the "Compare versions" button from the bottom of the page into the h2 header bar (styled like the other header buttons, e.g. "🎨 Toggle ALL highlighting"), via the new initAnnotationCompareButton(). Clicking it now navigates directly to the diff URL (built from the native form's own action + the checked old/new values) rather than relying on native form submission, opening in a new tab by default — configurable via the new 'Open "Compare versions" in a new tab' setting (sa_annotations_compare_new_tab, default on).

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Added two new debug-logging toggles for the CAA/EAA artwork pipeline, both default off: `sa_enable_art_fetch_debug_logging` gates per-image fetch logging (inline thumbnails, the big-picture strip/column icon, and details/expand JSON enrichment) across ergInjectCaaInlineThumbnails, _artInitInlinePics, _artSetInlineSortKey, _artLoadIcon, _artEnrichIcon, _artBuildMultiRowArtCell, _artInitSmallPics, _artEnrichTable, _artInitBigPics, and caaUpdateBigBoxForTable/eaaUpdateBigBoxForTable; `sa_enable_art_cache_fetch_debug_logging` gates the shared low-level cache/network fetch helper _artFetchCachedImage's memory/IDB/network-hit logs. Previously these Lib.debug() calls fired unconditionally whenever the global 'Enable debug logging' setting was on, making the console noisy for any other debug channel — most visibly _artSetInlineSortKey, which logs once per inline-thumbnail cell on every render. Existing sa_enable_art_diagnostic_logging-gated calls (snapshot/watchdog/counter diagnostics) are unaffected.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Added clickMasterToggleAndExpandAll() to tests/support/liveAssertions.js — clicks the page's single .mb-master-toggle button ("Show all sub-sections") instead of an individual <h3> group header, and asserts data-state/label flip to 'expanded'/"Hide all sub-sections" and every table.tbl (not just one group) becomes visible with rows. Both release-group live tests (release-group-fetch.spec.js and release-group-paginated-fetch.spec.js) now use this in place of the previous single-group "Promotion release" <h3> click, exercising the all-sections-at-once toggle path instead.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Added tests/support/auth-setup.js (`npm run auth:login`) — an interactive, non-test helper that opens a real visible browser at musicbrainz.org/login for you to log in yourself (solving any CAPTCHA), then saves the session via Playwright's storageState to playwright/.auth/vzell.json. Never handles credentials directly. playwright.config.js's chromium-live project picks that file up automatically when present, so live tests run logged in as you (matching real usage, e.g. the "Log in"/"Create account" header links vs. a logged-in username) instead of anonymous; absent by default, so nothing changes until you opt in. playwright/.auth/ is gitignored — a saved session is equivalent to a password and must never be committed.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: tests/live/release-group-paginated-fetch.spec.js: after the render-completion check, now clicks the "Promotion release" sub-table's <h3 class="mb-toggle-h3"> toggle icon and asserts it uncollapses (was collapsed by default) and its rows become visible — exercises renderGroupedTable()'s per-group collapse/expand click handler with a real Playwright click. Locates the group's <table> by walking forward from the h3 (mirroring findH3ForTable()'s own backward walk) since a div.mb-caa-bigbox can sit between them when sa_enable_caa_pics is on (the live default). As a side effect, a SAVE_HTML=1 run of this test now saves the section already expanded.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: tests/support/test.js: the SAVE_HTML feature now strips <script> elements from the saved snapshot and adds a <base href> tag instead of saving page.content() verbatim. loadPage.js inlines ShowAllEntityData.user.js/VZ_MBLibrary.user.js as raw <script> text via addScriptTag({ path }) — harmless live, but <script> content serializes completely unescaped, and that multi-megabyte source contains a literal `</script` substring somewhere; re-opening the saved file in a browser ended the script tag right there and rendered the rest of the source as garbled visible page text, with the real page markup only appearing far down the document after the parser recovered. Stripping scripts (they serve no purpose in a static snapshot anyway) fixes the corruption and also shrinks saved files from several MB down to well under 1MB; the added <base> tag keeps MusicBrainz's own root-relative CSS/image URLs resolving correctly when the file is opened directly.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Added tests/support/test.js — a Playwright `test` extended with an auto-saving `page` fixture: when the SAVE_HTML env var is set, every test's final page.content() is written to test-results/rendered-html/<test-name>.html and attached to the HTML report, with no per-test code needed. All spec files now import test/expect from this module instead of '@playwright/test' directly. Added an `npm run test:live:save-html` script. The saved file is a static DOM snapshot for visual review in a real browser — the userscript isn't re-injected against it, so it isn't interactive.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: tests/support/gmStubs.js: buildGmStubsScript() now accepts an optional initialValues map, pre-seeded into the GM_getValue store before the userscript runs. tests/support/loadPage.js uses it to force sa_enable_caa_pics/sa_enable_relationships_column off for every fixture test — the "Relationships" injected column fetches via plain fetch() (not stubbed, unlike GM_xmlhttpRequest-based CAA/EAA) straight to musicbrainz.org's WS/2 API, so without this override a fixture test that clicks a "Show all" button would silently leak a real network call. Live tests are unaffected (both settings keep their true configSchema defaults there).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Added tests/live/release-group-paginated-fetch.spec.js — a live test against a release-group whose release list spans 2 of MusicBrainz's own native pages, exercising startFetchingProcess()'s pagination loop. Extracted the shared render-completion/self-consistency assertions (previously only in release-group-fetch.spec.js) into tests/support/liveAssertions.js so both tests share the same checks.

tests/support/liveAssertions.js: narrowed collectPageErrors() to only listen for uncaught JS exceptions (pageerror), not every browser console 'error' — a live test hitting real infrastructure can see an unrelated transient asset-load error (e.g. a momentary 503 on a favicon request) that has nothing to do with script correctness; the broader console-error capture made the release-group-fetch.spec.js test flaky.

playwright.config.js: added an 'html' reporter (view via `npm run report`) alongside 'list', plus trace/screenshot capture on failure (trace: 'retain-on-failure', screenshot: 'only-on-failure'). Added package.json scripts test:ui (interactive UI mode) and test:headed (visible browser).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: tests/live/smoke.spec.js: added a comment clarifying it only checks that the action-button toolbar renders and deliberately never clicks a button (the artist's /recordings listing is ~476 native pages).

Added tests/live/release-group-fetch.spec.js — a live test that actually clicks "Show all" and fetches a real release-group's release list (bounded, so cheap to run). Since it hits real mutable MusicBrainz data, it asserts self-consistency invariants (fetch/render completes without page errors, at least one row rendered, the script's own per-group .mb-row-count-stat counts sum to the actual rendered row count) rather than a fixed expected row count/dataset, which would break on unrelated MusicBrainz edits.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Added a Playwright test harness (package.json, playwright.config.js, tests/) scoped to ShowAllEntityData/ — a fixture-based suite (`npm test`) that stubs the Tampermonkey GM_* APIs and intercepts navigation to inject a local HTML snapshot at a real musicbrainz.org-shaped URL (so pageDefinitions[].match() behaves exactly as it would live) with zero network dependency, plus an opt-in live smoke test against musicbrainz.org (`npm run test:live`). No changes to script runtime behavior.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: isPrefixKeyEvent()/isShortcutEvent(): guarded against synthetic `keydown` events with no `key` property (e.g. `new Event('keydown')` dispatched by other page scripts/extensions) — isPrefixKeyEvent() runs as a document-level capture-phase listener on every keydown on the page, so `e.key.toLowerCase()` crashed with 'Cannot read properties of undefined' whenever such an event reached it, as seen on release pages.

The visibility menu's real keyboard-focus highlighting is implemented separately and completely in buildColVisMenuKeyboard()/moveFocusTo(), which already handles this correctly.

All CSV/JSON/HTML/org-mode exports now go through showExportDialog() (filename-confirmation dialog) and the Save-to-Disk path through showSaveDialog(); both superseded this pair some time ago but the dead functions and their stale JSDoc cross-references ("Triggers showExportNotification() on success", etc.) were left behind. Confirmed dead via its own comments ("...instead of the old single-value applyUniqVal()...") and by tracing makeInlineArtItem(), which actually delegates through _wireStructureCheckbox()/applyUniqValueSet(), not applyUniqVal() as its own comment claimed. Removed duplicated dead local variables otherListId/otherVisible/otherEl (computed but never read) from both pin-list and LRU-list arrow-key keydown handlers in the filter-history dropdown — leftover scaffolding for a cross-list wrap-around feature that was never implemented.
Removed three orphaned CSS rules with no element ever carrying the class: .mb-show-all-btn-active, .mb-subtable-status-display, .sa-history-item:hover.

Removed five CSS classes assigned via className/classList.add that no stylesheet rule or selector ever matches: mb-cdtoc-inner-tracklist, mb-col-uniq-syn-box, mb-column-visibility-menu, mb-density-menu, mb-filter-wrapper. sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Unique-values dropdown: Ctrl+Click (or Ctrl+Enter/Ctrl+Space) on any section header now collapses/expands EVERY section at once, using that header's own new state — a plain click still toggles just the one section clicked. Mirrors the existing column-header collapse button's own 'this modifier means apply to everything' Ctrl+Click convention. Each header now also shows a tooltip describing what a click (and Ctrl+Click) will do, kept in sync by a new shared _applyUniqSectionState()/_uniqSectionTitle() pair that both the click handler and _applySynBoxQuickFilter()'s quickfilter-driven section show/hide go through, so the tooltip never goes stale relative to the section's actual expand/collapse state.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown: new 'Entity info - Role' (🎭) section for the 'Authors'/'Other artists'-style artist-roles columns (e.g. artist-works pages), alongside the existing 'Roles' section. 'Roles' still matches a credit's exact combined role string (e.g. selecting 'composer, lyricist' only matches that exact combination); the new section instead offers each ATOMIC role word (composer, lyricist, writer, arranger, …) as its own selectable value, and selecting one matches any row where an artist has that role, alone or together with others — e.g. selecting 'composer' now also matches an artist credited as 'composer, lyricist'.
