New _splitArtistRoleTokens() (comma-split, since MusicBrainz's real markup joins multiple roles with a comma, not the '/' _findCellArtistRoles() itself splits on) is the single source of truth for this decomposition, feeding a new 'roletoken:' compound structure-mode (_cellMatchesStructureMode(), testRowMatch()'s highlight dispatch via new _highlightRoleTokenMatch()) and the new 'entityRole' SYN_SECTION_META/MB_UNIQ_KIND_TO_SECTION entries.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: _findCellArtistRoles(): fixed a self-corrupting extraction bug that broke re-filtering on an artist-roles column (Authors/Other artists) after the FIRST match highlight was applied. Cause: this function only summed a <li>'s DIRECT TEXT-NODE children (deliberately skipping a `.comment` disambiguation span), but _highlightEventRoleMatch()/the new _highlightRoleTokenMatch() wrap the matched substring in a `<span class="mb-column-filter-highlight">` — turning it into an element-node child that the text-node-only loop silently skipped on every SUBSEQUENT filter pass. Symptom: selecting a second 'Roles'/'Entity info - Role' value (or otherwise re-triggering a filter pass after the first one highlighted a cell) corrupted the re-extracted role text (e.g. 'composer, lyricist' → ', lyricist'), which could zero out matches entirely instead of the expected OR of both selections. Fix: the extraction loop now also recurses into (only) `.mb-column-filter-highlight`/`.mb-global-filter-highlight` element children, treating them as transparent text; `.comment` and the credited-artist `<a>` link still carry neither class and stay excluded exactly as before.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: New table-style setting `sa_default_hidden_columns` (Page Type → comma-separated, quoted column list) lets you pre-hide columns the first time a given pageType's table renders, without touching the 👁️ Visible popup manually. Ships with one default: `release-tracks` → `"ARs"`, so the ARs column starts hidden on release-tracks pages instead of visible by default. A configured column is tracked as hidden-by-default per pageType (`vz-mb-colvis-{pageType}` GM storage) and re-asserted on every render, UNLESS you explicitly touch that specific column yourself — a genuine click on its checkbox, or Select All / Deselect All / Choose current configuration (tracked separately via `vz-mb-colvis-touched-{pageType}`) — in which case your choice is remembered forever and the default never overrides it again. This per-column tracking is what lets the default survive simply opening and closing the 👁️ Visible popup without touching anything, which (by pre-existing design) still snapshots every checkbox's current value on close.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: '👁️ Visible' column-visibility popup: clicking the toggle button threw `Uncaught ReferenceError: selectedCheckboxIndex is not defined` in the browser console on every open, from a dead assignment left over from an earlier refactor of `buildColVisMenuKeyboard()` (which now tracks keyboard focus via `menuFocusables.indexOf(document.activeElement)` instead of a separate index variable). The variable was never declared and never read anywhere else in the file. Removed the stray assignment; `moveFocusTo(0)` on the next line already resets keyboard focus to the first checkbox correctly on its own.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': a dynamic-fallback AR column crediting MULTIPLE distinct source recordings in one `<dd>` (e.g. "DJ-mix of" — confirmed via `debug/DJ-mix-of-original.html`, a 26-target credit on https://musicbrainz.org/release/a24eb845-0b82-44a7-8227-d13d4c1200dd) collapsed all of them into a single `<li>` instead of one row per recording — the column's own multi-row count badge silently read "1". Root cause: `_collectEntityKinds(dd)` only detects a DIRECT-child `<span class="recordinglink">` marker (the credited artist's own `<span class="artistlink">` sits nested inside a `<bdi>`, one level deeper, so it's never itself detected here), yielding `{recording}` — but `PEER_SPLIT_KINDS` (the set `_filterPeerKinds` restricts peer/row-boundary markers to) only listed `artist`/`label`, so `recording` was stripped to an empty set and `_buildKindSplitListTd` fell into its `kinds.size === 0` "no recognized marker — clone the whole `<dd>` verbatim into one `<li>`" branch. Added `'recording'` to `PEER_SPLIT_KINDS`: every `recordinglink` marker in a dynamic-fallback AR's `<dd>` is always a genuine distinct credited recording (never a recording's own nested "decoration", unlike the already-excluded place/event/work/area/series chain-shaped kinds), so it's safe to always treat as a row boundary. Affects every recording-to-recording dynamic column with 2+ targets (DJ-mix of, Samples, remix of, edit of, Music videos, …), not just this one release; single-target cases were already correct by coincidence (one clone into one `<li>` looks right when there's only one item) and remain unaffected. The column name stays unsuffixed ("Dj-mix of", not "Dj-mix of recording") since `_collectEntityKinds` still only ever reports the single `recording` kind for this shape.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: `release-tracks`: credit "attribute" words (e.g. "lead"/"solo" on a Vocals credit, "additional"/"assistant" on Engineer/Producer/Mixer, "live"/"cover" on "Recording of work") now render in italics and in a configurable color (new "Credit attribute color" setting, default a medium-dark green #2e7d32 chosen for readable contrast against the table's alternating row backgrounds) — applies to every column sharing the `.mb-credit-attr` sentinel, not just Vocals/Instruments. A credit's "credited as" alternate name (e.g. "drums" for "drums (drum set)", Vocals/Instruments only) now renders in italics too. All pure styling changes — unique-values dropdown per-attribute/per-credited-as filter entries are unaffected.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: `artist-releases` and every other page splitting a "Country/Date" column: release events MusicBrainz truncates behind a native "(show N more)" toggle (common for widely-released digital releases) are now fully reconstructed before row extraction, from the same JSON data MusicBrainz already embeds in the page — no click simulation or extra network requests needed, so it works identically for fetched pages, not just the current one. New "Auto-expand truncated \"Country/Date\" release-event cells" setting (default: on, ▶️ EXPAND TRUNCATED CELLS section) lets you opt out on very large discography pages if this adds noticeable overhead.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Unique-values dropdown: split six more flat "Cell structure" sections the same way "Credit details" was split last version — "Structure" (core cell-shape states vs. a new "Structure - Inline artwork" sub-section), "Flags" ("- Title mismatch"/"- Name variation"), "Format info" ("- Size"/"- Medium count"/"- Combo"/"- Type"), "Tracks info" ("- Tracks"/"- Multi-medium"), "Catalog info" ("- Prefix"/"- Presence"), and "CAA info"/"EAA info" (each into "- Type"/"- Comment") — each independently collapsible with its own remembered state. Also normalized two older section-label deviations onto the now-established "Topic - Capitalized subtopic" convention: "Release events - country/date/weekday" → "- Country"/"- Date"/"- Weekday", and the previously dash-less "Country name details"/"Country code details" merged into "Country details - Name"/"- Code".

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: `ShowAllEntityData/CLAUDE.md`: added a new section documenting the unique-values dropdown's `SYN_SECTION_META`/`MB_UNIQ_MODE_TO_SECTION`/`MB_UNIQ_KIND_TO_SECTION` section-splitting mechanism, its naming convention, and a split-history table, plus a full accuracy pass against the current codebase — corrected every stale line-number anchor in the "File structure" table, two fabricated/wrong settings-key names (`sa_enable_eaa_pics`, `sa_enable_picard_tagger_column`), an incomplete debug-channel list, missing DOM-convention classes, an inaccurate "alphabetical grouping" checklist claim, a dangling `debug/user-edits-wrong.org` reference, and several sections that no longer fully described current behavior (ARs/Edit-details prose-clamp carve-outs, a 4th clone-rewire function, `KNOWN_ENTITY_LINK_KINDS`'s 8th entry).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Unique-values dropdown: split the flat "Credit details" section into independently-collapsible "Credit details - Attribute"/"- Task"/"- Date"/"- Instrument"/"- Credited as" sub-sections (mirroring the existing "Entity info"/"Release events" splits), so columns with many credit annotations — e.g. "Vocals" now that vocal-range/type credits are consolidated into it — stay readable instead of one long mixed list.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `release-tracks`: vocal-range/type credits (e.g. "alto vocals", "bass vocals [Gaoler]", "soprano vocals [Soprano I]", "guest baritone vocals") no longer spawn their own one-off throwaway columns — they're now recognized and consolidated into the shared "Vocals" column alongside the existing "choir vocals"/"lead vocals"/etc. credits, each rendered with a "(range)" or "(attribute/range)" parenthetical.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Removed references to the obsolete "MusicBrainz: Canadian Province Flags Everywhere" companion userscript from code comments — only "MusicBrainz: More Flags Everywhere" remains current.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Adjusted several configuration setting defaults to more sensible out-of-the-box values: `sa_sidebar_collapsed` ("Start with sidebar collapsed") false→true; `sa_enable_dropdown_flag_icons` ("Show Flag Icons In Unique-Values Dropdown") false→true; `sa_uniq_dropdown_visible_rows` ("Unique-Values Dropdown Visible Rows") 8→30; `sa_auto_resize_columns` ("Auto-resize columns on load") false→true; `sa_enable_show_single_table_btn` ("Enable 'Show single-table' button") false→true, and dropped its now-stale "Off by default while this feature is new" description text; `sa_enable_ars_collapse` ("Enable collapsible 'ARs' column") true→false; `sa_enable_annotation_auto_expand` ("Auto-expand native 'Annotation' section") false→true. Only affects fresh installs / users who haven't explicitly overridden these settings — anyone with an existing explicit value keeps it.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 📊 unique-values dropdown: fixed "Join phrases" entries (e.g. "&") disappearing after closing and reopening the dropdown on a column with an active join-phrase filter. `_findCellJoinPhrases()` required the separator text to be a bare DOM text node, but `_highlightJoinPhraseMatch()` wraps that same text node in a `<span class="mb-column-filter-highlight">` once the entry is checked — a re-scan on reopen (which runs without an intervening filter pass to clear the highlight first) then found nothing between the two credited artists. `_findCellJoinPhrases()` now also recognizes its own highlight-wrapper span in that position and reads its text content, so reopening the dropdown keeps showing join-phrase entries that still match the currently-filtered rows.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Resynced `ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt` against every user-facing change from 9.99.864 through 9.99.887: documented the six new 📊 unique-values dropdown "Cell structure" sub-sections (Join phrases, Name variations, Format info, Release events - country/date/weekday, Country name/code details, Tracks info, Catalog info), the "Entity info" section's split into per-entity-type collapsible sub-sections plus its two page-specific variants (Tag count, Event cancelled), the mouse-hover/keyboard-focus sync and post-close filter-input focus restoration, the new "Locale language"/"Primary locale" columns on Aliases pages, the "Video"/"Cancelled" columns now also covering tag-value/user-tag-value's Recordings/Events sub-tables, and the "MB-Primary alias" → "Primary alias" rename (including report pages' now much broader automatic MB-Name/Comment/Primary-alias extraction). Also corrected stale text describing the long-removed `tagCount_*`/`primaryAlias` legacy extractor family.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Added the `video` columnExtractor (synthetic "Video" column, e.g. `debug/tag-2024.html`'s Recording cells carrying `<span class="video" title="This recording is a video">`) to the "Recordings" sub-table's "Recording" column on `tag-value` and `user-tag-value`, alongside the existing `artistCredit` extractor already there — matching the same `video` extractor already used for the "Recording" column on `report-detail`/`user-ratings`.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Added a new "Entity info - Event cancelled" section to the unique-values dropdown for `area-events`/`place-events`/`artist-events`'s "Event" column, and a new "Event info - Event cancelled" section (sibling of the renamed "Event info - Event date") for `tag-value`/`user-tag-value`'s "Events" group's "Event" column — both list the "(cancelled)" marker with how many events carry it, and highlight the matched "cancelled" text when checked. `_findCellEventCancelled()` re-derives the marker the same way `ColumnDataExtractor.cancelledEvent` already does for the synthetic "Cancelled" column. Deliberately scoped to only these 5 named page types (via `activeDefinition.type`, reliable even on `tag-value`/`user-tag-value`'s `tableMode: 'multi'` pages where `activeColumnExtractors` itself is not) even though several OTHER page types (`user-ratings`/`user-ratings-type`/`user-tag-value-entity`/`collections-releases`/`search`/`series-releases`) also have a `cancelledEvent` extractor on their own Event column — their dropdown behavior is intentionally left unchanged.

Renamed the unique-values dropdown's "Event info" section to "Event info - Event date", and its `date: <value>` entries to `event date: <value>`, to disambiguate now that a sibling "Event info - Event cancelled" section exists alongside it. Unrelated to `revdate:` (the "Release events - date" family's own `date:` entries), which keeps its existing label.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Added a new "Entity info - Tag count" section to the unique-values dropdown for `tag-value-entity`'s original per-entity-kind column (Artist/Label/Area/Event/...) — mirrors the existing "Entity info - Comment"/"Entity info - Alias" sections, showing each distinct leading tag-vote count (e.g. "26" from "26 - Johnny Cash") with how many entities carry it, and filtering the table to those rows when checked. Scoped via `activeColumnExtractors` (reliable here since `tag-value-entity` is `tableMode: 'single'`), so it only ever appears on the column the `tagCount` extractor actually ran against — never on `user-tag-value-entity` (no `tagCount` extractor there) or any other page type. Also wired `tagcount:` into `runFilter()`'s per-mode highlight dispatcher (`_highlightTagCountMatch`, alongside the other structure-mode highlighters), which the initial implementation missed — checking a "» tag count: N" entry now visually highlights the matched leading count the same way every other structural entity/value entry already does, re-deriving from `_findCellTagCount()` itself before highlighting so a comma-formatted original count (e.g. "1,234") is matched correctly even though the filter's own stored value has commas stripped.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Replaced the legacy `Name_Comment`/`Name_Comment_Artists`/`Name_Date_Comment` column extractors with `features.extractMainColumn` (matching the generic "MB-Name"/"Comment"/"Primary alias" shape already used by `report-detail`) on `user-ratings-type`, `user-ratings`, `user-tag-value-entity`, `user-tag-value`, and `tag-value`. `extractMainColumn` is read-only against the native entity cell, so the original column is never mutated. Two new small, read-only companion extractors — `eventDate` (the trailing date after an Event's entity link) and `artistCredit` (the artist credit after "by" on Release/Release group/Recording) — restore the extra columns those legacy extractors also used to produce. `Name_Comment`, `Name_Comment_Artists`, `Name_Date_Comment`, and the (now-unused) `primaryAlias` extractor were deleted as dead code. `instrument-list` (`Name_Comment_Description`) is untouched — instruments cannot have a MusicBrainz primary alias. No change to `_extractMainColumnParts()` itself.

Fixed a header/cell-count-mismatch bug in `renderGroupedTable`'s per-group `<thead>` build for `tag-value`/`user-tag-value`/`instrument-list`: `activeColumnExtractors.find(e => e.sourceColumn === group.colName)` only resolved `colIdx` for the first `columnExtractors` entry when a group declared two or more entries on the same `sourceColumn`, silently dropping that entry's header (row extraction, run earlier, already resolved every matching entry, so its cell still got appended) — a `.forEach()`-based resolver now sets `colIdx` on every matching entry, matching the pattern already used everywhere else in the file.

Fixed the same class of header/cell-count mismatch on `user-ratings`'s Artist/Label/Place/Work ratings sub-tables: their per-group `<thead>` build only called `cleanupHeaders()` (which injects the MB-Name/Comment/Primary-alias headers) when the group declared its own non-empty `entityFeatures`, but `extractMainColumn` is a page-level feature applying to every group uniformly — every row still grew 3 MB-Name/Comment/Primary-alias `<td>`s regardless. `cleanupHeaders()` (and the colIdx re-resolution feeding it) now runs unconditionally for every group, matching the tag-value/user-tag-value/instrument-list per-group thead path.

Restored a `_synthColTooltip` case for `Name_Comment_Description` (the `instrument-list` extractor) describing its Name/Comment/Description columns — previously fell through to the generic per-extractor fallback tooltip.

Reordered the Events `columnExtractors` from `[eventDate, cancelledEvent]` to `[cancelledEvent, eventDate]` everywhere both appear, so the "Cancelled" column renders before "Date". Also added the `cancelledEvent` extractor to `tag-value`/`user-tag-value`'s Events blocks, which previously only had `eventDate` — bringing all five page types' Events blocks in line.

Migrated `tag-value-entity` off the `tagCount_*` extractor family onto the same `features.extractMainColumn` design as the other five page types, fixing the same missing-primary-alias gap those had (`tagCount_*` never surfaced a primary alias, just silently stripped it out of Comment). Reused `eventDate`/`artistCredit` unchanged for Date/Artist, and added one new small read-only companion extractor, `tagCount`, for the leading integer tag-vote count. `tagCount_Name_Comment`, `tagCount_Name_Comment_Artists`, and `tagCount_Name_Date_Comment` were deleted as dead code.

Consolidated 10 of the 11 `*-aliases` page definitions (`instrument-aliases`, `area-aliases`, `place-aliases`, `series-aliases`, `label-aliases`, `work-aliases`, `releasegroup-aliases`, `release-aliases`, `recording-aliases`, `event-aliases`) — byte-for-byte identical apart from the entity name — into a single `entity-aliases` entry, using the existing `labelFromPathEntity` button-label mechanism to keep each page's "Show all Aliases for `<Entity>`" wording (release-group's label now reads "Release group" instead of the previous "Releasegroup"). This also fixes a real bug: all 10 were missing the `localeParts` columnExtractor that `artist-aliases` already had, so their alias tables' Locale column never got split into "Locale language"/"Primary locale" — now fixed for all of them at once. `artist-aliases` is left untouched (its `/artist/<mbid>/aliases` page has a second "Artist credits" section, needing two buttons with their own `targetHeader`/`tableMode` — a shape nothing else shares).

Removed `_tagCountBase`, whose only remaining caller (`Name_Comment_Description`, `instrument-list`) used just 2 of its 3 outputs (Name, Comment — never Tag count) and never needed its flag-span-before-the-link fallback (instruments are never flagged) or its primary-alias stripping (instrument is not an aliasable MusicBrainz entity type). `Name_Comment_Description` now does its own minimal, inline Name/Comment extraction instead of going through the shared helper.

Renamed the synthetic "MB-Primary alias" column (and every internal reference to it — header text, `dataset.colName`, `primarySyntheticCellMap` key, tooltip case, debug logs, comments) to plain "Primary alias", matching the `MB-Primary alias`-less casing MusicBrainz itself uses for the native `<i title="Primary alias">` marker this column is extracted from. This is a global, file-wide rename — the column is produced by `_extractMainColumnParts()`/`features.extractMainColumn`, shared by every page type using it (roughly 70-85), not just the ones touched earlier in this branch; also updated the 6 pre-existing, unrelated page types (`collections-releases`, `search`, `area-events`, `place-events`, `series-releases`, `artist-events`) whose own `tooltipColumns` arrays hardcoded the old name. No collision with any existing column name; the `MB-` prefix carried no functional meaning anywhere in the file.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Added a new `columnErasers` sentinel, `'expandEvents'`, that strips `<button class="expand-events-toggle" data-event-gid="…">▸</button>` — the inline expand/collapse control Dvir Yitzchaki's "Expand events" userscript injects into an Event cell, already present on the page before this script's own fetch/scrape runs — from the consolidated table's Event column. Matches on the stable `expand-events-toggle` class only, not the userscript's own CSS-modules-generated hash class (which changes between its versions/builds). Wired into all 5 page types that render an Event main column via native MusicBrainz markup: `area-events`, `place-events`, `artist-events`, and the `Events` sub-block of `collections-releases` and `series-releases`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: All four `@include` header patterns now tolerate a trailing slash (e.g. `/instruments/` as well as `/instruments`). Previously only patterns using a bare `.*` alternative (like `tags.*`, `report/.*`) happened to already allow it; every alternative built from the stricter `(?:\?.*)?` optional-query suffix — `/instruments`, `/genres`, `/elections`, `/privileged`, `/doc/Edit_Types`, `/account/applications`, `/search/edits`, `/edit/subscribed(_editors)?`, `/edit/notes-received`, every `/user/<name>/...` subpage, and the entire `/<entity>/<mbid>[/<subpath>]` family (11 entity types × 17 subpaths) — silently failed to inject the script at all on a trailing-slash URL, since Tampermonkey never even loads the script when no `@include` matches. Paired with matching trailing-slash tolerance added to the 12 `pageDefinitions` match functions that were anchored with a bare `$` (no `\/?`) and would otherwise have loaded the script via the fixed `@include` but then matched no page type: `ratings-entity`, `user-ratings-type`, `user-ratings`, `edits` (including its `/search/edits` and `/edit/subscribed(_editors)?` exact-path checks), `notes-received`, `user-open-edits`, `user-edits`, `artist-releasegroups`, `artist-releases`, `artist-recordings`, and `release-tracks`.

Added the missing `event-tags` page type for `/event/<mbid>/tags` — the only one of the 11 taggable core entity kinds (artist, release-group, release, recording, work, label, series, place, area, instrument, event) that had no dedicated `*-tags` page definition, so the "Show all Tags" button never appeared on an event's tags page even though the page loaded fine.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The "Event" column's own unique-values dropdown now shows a "» date:" entry (new "Event info" section) for each distinct trailing date found in its cells — e.g. "2024-05-28" from native tag-value Event listings like `… (2024-05-28)` (confirmed against debug/data-missing.html, reported on /user/vzell/tag/england and /user/vzell/tag/rescheduled). This was previously only extracted into the separate synthetic "Date" column (`Name_Date_Comment`); the dropdown's existing "date:" entries are fed exclusively by the `.mb-credit-date` sentinel used for AR-credit relationship annotations (e.g. release-tracks credits), a different code path a plain Event cell never goes through, so the new `eventDateValueCounts`/`_findCellEventDateParts()` pair reads the native markup directly instead — gated to the "Event" column only.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `/report/PlacesWithoutCoordinates` rendered empty "Locality"/"Region"/"Country" cells for every row (confirmed against debug/coordinates.html): its 'Place' column carries only the place name, with the district/region/country chain instead living in a separate native 'Area' column that report-detail's `columnExtractors` never read. Added a `splitArea`-based extractor for the 'Area' column, named 'MB-Locality'/'MB-Region'/'MB-Country' (not the usual 'Locality'/'Region'/'Country' other pages' own 'Area' entries use) specifically because this report has both 'Place' and 'Area' as real columns at once, and reusing those names would have appended duplicate cells per row and desynced every column after them.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `/report/ArtistsWithMultipleOccurrencesInArtistCredits` coincidentally matches the `report-multiple-linked` page type's "...With(Multiple|Many)..." URL pattern (v9.99.879 and earlier), but its table is actually report-detail's flat, one-row-per-artist shape — the report's subject entity ("Artist") is the URL segment before "With", not a linked entity derivable from the suffix the way that page type expects, so `mainColIdx` never resolved and the injected "MB-Name"/"Comment"/"MB-Primary alias" columns stayed empty for every row (confirmed against debug/a.html). This report is now excluded from `report-multiple-linked` and falls through to the generic `report-detail` definition instead, whose `extractMainColumn` candidate list (added in 9.99.879) already includes 'Artist'.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The generic `report-detail` report page (`/report/<Name>`) now extracts the "MB-Name", "Comment", and "MB-Primary alias" synthetic columns from whichever main entity column is present — Release, Release group, Recording, Label, Artist, Event, Place, Series, Work, or Collaborator — mirroring the extraction already done for the `report-multiple-linked` family (e.g. ISRCsWithManyRecordings). Covers reports such as ReleasesWithDownloadRelationships, SetInDifferentRG, ReleaseGroupsWithoutVALink, AnnotationsEvents, DuplicateRelationshipsRecordings, DeprecatedRelationshipLabels, CollaborationRelationships, PlacesWithoutCoordinates, SeriesContainingDuplicates, and WorkSameTypeAsParent.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On alias-listing pages, `normalizeAliasTable()` (v9.99.877) removed the invisible "Actions" (Edit/Remove) `<td>` from every body row but left its `<th>` header in place, so the rendered table still showed an "Actions" column — with sort buttons and a unique-values dropdown — that was now always empty in every row (confirmed against debug/action.html). The header cell is now removed too, so the column disappears entirely instead of rendering dead.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On alias-listing pages, whenever a row's Alias text equals its Sort name, MusicBrainz renders that row's leading cell with `colspan="2"` — one fewer real `<td>` than the header count, which silently shifted every later column's positional cell lookup left by one for that row. The existing fix for this (`normalizeAliasTable()`, which also strips the invisible Actions/Edit-Remove column) was gated behind a manually-curated allowlist that covered only 6 of the 11 `*-aliases` page types and explicitly excluded `artist-aliases` — so on that page the "Edit | Remove" Actions text leaked into the Type/Locale/"Locale language"/Actions columns' cell data and unique-values dropdowns (most visibly since the new `localeParts` "Locale"/"Locale language"/"Primary locale" extraction landed, but the same column-shift already silently corrupted Begin/End-date extraction there too). `work-aliases`/`releasegroup-aliases`/`release-aliases`/`recording-aliases` had the identical latent gap. Normalization now runs unconditionally for every `*-aliases` page type — `normalizeAliasTable()` is already a no-op for any row/table that doesn't actually have the Actions column or a colspan'd cell, so this is safe everywhere.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The artist Aliases page (`/artist/{mbid}/aliases`) now splits the native "Locale" column into two synthetic columns: "Locale language" (the plain locale text, e.g. "English", with any locale that already legitimately has its own parenthetical, e.g. "Chinese (China)", preserved intact) and "Primary locale" ("true" when that row's locale carries MusicBrainz's own "(primary)" role indicator, left empty otherwise — including alias types like "Legal name"/"Search hint" that have no locale at all, e.g. "English (primary)" → language "English" + primary "true"; "English" → language "English" + primary empty).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown's "Entity info" section (the collapsible "» area name: …"/"» place name: …" groups) now shows a country's real flag instead of the generic area icon for entries backed by a flagged area/country cell (native `<span class="flag flag-XX">`, or a third-party "More Flags Everywhere"-style subdivision icon) — a non-country area (e.g. "Ohio") still shows the generic icon as before. Gated behind the existing `sa_enable_dropdown_flag_icons` setting (off by default), the same one that already puts flags in the dropdown's plain value list for Location/Country/Locality/Region/Area-type columns. Since flag and generic-icon markers can render at different sizes, both are now centered inside a small fixed-width slot so the "»" label text lines up consistently regardless of which icon a given entry shows.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: MusicBrainz's "...With(Multiple|Many)..." report family (e.g. "Amazon URLs linked to multiple releases" at /report/ASINsWithMultipleReleases, "Discogs URLs linked to multiple labels/artists/release groups", "ISRCs with multiple recordings" at /report/ISRCsWithManyRecordings) groups its rows under a shared identifier rendered once, followed by one plain row per linked entity with an empty first cell — the identifier row was either silently dropped (URL-style reports, whose identifier cell alone spans every column) or, worse, kept as a spurious extra row with blank Artist/Recording/Length cells (ISRC-style reports, whose identifier cell is followed by a separate empty colspan filler cell), and every real per-entity row's identifier column stayed blank either way. A new page type, report-multiple-linked, now recognizes any /report/*With(Multiple|Many)* report by name, detects both group-header row shapes, carries the identifier forward (across pages too, since a group's rows can span a pagination boundary) into each following row's empty first cell instead of emitting it as its own row, and derives the linked-entity column to auto-split into MB-Name/Comment/MB-Primary alias from the report's own URL (not a fixed column position) — needed because that column's position varies per report (e.g. ISRCsWithManyRecordings renders ISRC/Artist/Recording/Length, where Artist sits before the true target column Recording).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown now offers several new synthetic sections extracting finer-grained structure from columns that previously only offered a whole-cell value: "Format info" (💿 — distinct disc sizes like 7"/10"/12", medium counts, a type entry (e.g. "Vinyl"/"Acetate") that matches regardless of size, and combined "2xVinyl"-style entries for filtering an exact count+type combination in one click), "Release events - country"/"- date"/"- weekday" (🌐/📅/📆, on "Country/Date": distinct country codes with their native flag icon, date text, and chaban weekday abbreviations, each independently optional, now each its own collapsible section), "Country name details"/"Country code details" (🌍/🏷️, on the synthetic "Country" column splitCountryDate() produces, likewise split into two sections), "Tracks info" (🎵, distinct per-medium track counts, plus a "multiple mediums" flag for rows joined by "+"), and "Catalog info" (🏷️, distinct catalog-number prefixes like "CBS"/"S CBS", plus three independent flags: "has prefix" / "no prefix" (a single row's catalog list can match both) and a new "no catalog number" flag for list items that are literally MusicBrainz's own "[none]" placeholder. Checking any of these new entries now correctly highlights the matching text/number/prefix/placeholder within the full cell content, not just the filtered rows themselves — including "Release events - date" and "- weekday", whose highlighting was missing an element reference to scope to and has now been added.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown's shared badge-width computation (panelBadgeChWidth), which right-aligns every "(N)" count badge across every section in the panel: it was missing numerous value-count maps and counters added across this session (Join phrases, Name variations, and the newest Format/Release-events/Country/Tracks/Catalog# sections), so any section whose own counts happened to exceed whatever width the panel HAD been sized from rendered with inconsistent right-alignment — reported as the "Format info" section's count numbers looking center-aligned. The computation is now comprehensive over every value-count map/counter in the panel.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown's "Entity info" section — previously one flat collapsible list mixing every "» name:"/"comment:"/"alias:" entry together — is now split into one independently-collapsible sub-section per entity type actually present ("Entity info - Artist name", "Entity info - Event name", "Entity info - Place name", etc., using the same native MusicBrainz entity-type icon shown per entry), plus separate "Entity info - Comment" and "Entity info - Alias" sections. Each collapses/remembers its own state independently, same as every other section in the panel. Entry labels and filtering/highlighting behavior are unchanged.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown's "Entity info" and "Join phrases" sections were both blind to a credit whose artist(s) are wrapped by the third-party jesus2099 userscript's name-variation marker (`<span class="name-variation">`, injected directly between `<bdi>` and `<a>` when a credited display name differs from the entity's real name) — such rows contributed no per-artist "» artist name: …" entries and no join-phrase entry at all, even though a plain (non-wrapped) multi-artist credit already worked correctly. Both extraction functions now recognize a `<span class="name-variation">` wrapping a single artist link as transparently equivalent to that `<a>` itself, so these rows are found like any other. As a side effect, the artist's actually-displayed credited name is now offered as its own "Entity info" entry for the first time (previously only the tooltip-derived real/sort name strings were exposed, via the separate "Name variations" section).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown now offers a dedicated "Name variations" (🪪) section when the third-party jesus2099 userscript marks a credited name as differing from the entity's real/canonical name (`<span class="name-variation">`). Each marker's `title` attribute (MusicBrainz's own "RealName – SortName" tooltip convention) is offered as three checkable/filterable entries: the full "RealName – SortName" string, and each half on its own (e.g. "山崎千裕" and "Yamazaki, Chihiro" separately, in addition to "山崎千裕 – Yamazaki, Chihiro" as one entry) — prefixed "» name variation: ". Checking an entry highlights the credited display text itself, since the matched value only ever lives in the tooltip, never as visible cell text.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown's "Entity info" (👤) section never offered individual entries for entities credited jointly in one cell (e.g. the native "Artist" column's "Bruce Springsteen & The E Street Band", or a 4-artist "A / B / C / D" credit) — the section was silently empty for every such row, even though each entity is independently filterable/checkable in every other way. Root cause: _findCellEntityRefs() resolved each entity's own "name" from the whole shared `<bdi>` wrapping ALL joined entities, rather than from that one entity's own `<a>` — every joined entity ended up reporting the full combined credit string as its own name, making the internal "is this a bare cell" check trivially true for all of them and hiding them from Entity info entirely. Each entity's name/highlight scope is now correctly isolated to its own `<a>` whenever it shares a `<bdi>` with other entities; a `<bdi>` wrapping just one entity (the common case) is unaffected.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown now offers a new "Join phrases" (🔀) section on any column whose cells credit two or more entities joined by a literal separator inside one shared name element (e.g. the native "Artist" column's "Bruce Springsteen & The E Street Band", "... with The Sessions Band", or free-text editor phrasing like "... w/special guest ..."). Each distinct observed phrase ("&", "and", "with", "feat.", "/", or any arbitrary text an editor typed) becomes its own checkable, filterable, highlightable entry — phrases are never normalized toward a "canonical" spelling, so "&" and "and" stay distinct. The existing "Entity info" section already offers each individual credited entity (e.g. "Bruce Springsteen" and "The E Street Band" separately) as its own entry on such cells — no change needed there, it already worked correctly.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The Reports index page (/reports) now extracts two new synthetic columns, "Delta" and "When", when the third-party "MusicBrainz: Reports Statistics" userscript (by chaban) is installed and active. That userscript injects a change-indicator into each report link (e.g. "▼ -1 (-0.0%) (1 day ago)"); "Delta" now shows just the arrow/count/percent part and "When" shows the trailing time phrase on its own, with the wrapping parentheses removed (e.g. "1 day ago"). Both columns are colored to match the original indicator (green/red/grey). The columns are always present on this page, same as every other extracted column in this script — they're simply empty for every row when that other userscript isn't active.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: When the per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown was opened with nothing previously focused (e.g. a plain mouse click into empty page space, or straight after page load), checking one or more entries and then closing the dropdown left focus nowhere, even though the column filter's display text now read "<n> selected". Closing now focuses that filter input (cursor placed after the text) whenever the selection actually changed during the session. If nothing was selected before closing — e.g. Escape pressed immediately after opening — focus is left untouched, preserving the state from before the dropdown opened.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Closing the per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown — via Escape, re-clicking the 📊 button, or scrolling — left keyboard focus nowhere, even when a column's filter input had focus right before the 📊 button was clicked. Focus is now restored to that filter input on close, so typing can continue right where it left off. Covers real mouse clicks on 📊 plus the Ctrl+Q and prefix-mode `q` keyboard shortcuts; clicking outside the dropdown to a different element intentionally does not restore focus, so it doesn't fight that click.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown's mouse-hover and keyboard arrow-key highlight were two independent, unsynchronized indicators — hovering one entry while keyboard focus sat on another showed two highlighted rows at once. Mouse hover now drives the same focus state as keyboard navigation (moveFocus()), so exactly one entry is ever highlighted regardless of input method, and Enter/Space after hovering now act on the hovered entry too.

An already-checked entry's background always visually won over the hover/keyboard-focus highlight color, because the two CSS rules had identical specificity and cascade fell back to source order — the reverse of what the adjacent code comments claimed. Added a genuinely higher-specificity combined rule for "checked AND highlighted" with its own distinct in-between color (#e1f1f3, the midpoint of the existing highlight blue and checked green), so a checked entry's highlight is now visible again when hovered or keyboard-focused.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown's Enter key closed the panel when toggling an entry inside a "Cell structure"/"Flags"/"Entity info"/etc. synthetic section, but left it open when toggling a standard value entry — an inconsistency that silently broke keyboard-driven multi-select in those synthetic sections (mouse click already worked fine there). Enter now always toggles the highlighted entry in place and leaves the panel open, in every section — matching mouse-click behavior everywhere. Escape remains the only key that closes the panel.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown now supports the Space key to toggle the checkbox of the currently arrow-key-highlighted entry, identical to Enter and to a mouse click (stays open for continued multi-select). Previously Space only typed a literal space into the quickfilter text field.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Resynced ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt against every user-facing change since 9.99.746 (114 entries, through 9.99.861). Added: a new RELEASE-TRACKS PAGE section covering the new consolidated release-tracklist page type (pre-processing, always-present/conditional columns, the Recording-of/Recorded-at/Recorded-in/Mixed-at column family, credit-role columns, Instruments/Vocals, auto-discovered dynamic AR columns, the live-recording-date ⚠️/❌ consistency check, AcoustIDs/ISRCs, the ARs column, and the relocated Credits section); a new SHOW SINGLE-TABLE BUTTON section covering the opt-in client-side sub-table snapshot feature. Substantially expanded UNIQUE-VALUES COLUMN DROPDOWN with the configurable visible-row-count setting and a full explanation of the collapsible "Cell structure" sub-sections (🔠 Structure, 🚩 Flags, 🎚️ Credit details, 👤 Entity info — now type-labeled/type-sorted, 🎭 Roles, 🔗 Relationship icons — now multi-select, and dynamic "CAA info"/"EAA info"), entity-reference rows, and human-readable multi-item joins. Added cross-reference bullets to SUPPORTED PAGES, RELATIONSHIPS COLUMN, MULTI-TABLE PAGES, and PROGRESS BAR; updated COLUMN MANAGEMENT's extracted-columns list for the new "MB-Primary alias" column. Added the 📑 SHOW SINGLE-TABLE BUTTON and 💿 RELEASE TRACKLIST settings groups to SETTINGS, and extended 🖼️ CAA/EAA ILLUSTRATED DISCOGRAPHY, 🎨 TABLE FILTER CONFIGURATION, and 🛠️ GENERIC SETTINGS with their new settings.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The per-column unique-values (📊) dropdown's "Entity info" section — its "» name:" entries (e.g. `artist-events`' "Location" column, which mixes `place` and `area` references) — sorted purely alphabetically, interleaving different entity types together (e.g. "Albany" (area), "Alberta" (area), "Alice Tully Hall" (place), "American Airlines Center" (place), "Amsterdam" (area), …). Now sorts by entity type first (new `ENTITY_NAME_TYPE_SORT_ORDER`: artist, label, work, release-group, release, recording, event, place, area — creative/production entities first, then event, then geographic entities from most specific to broadest), alphabetically within each type, and relabels each entry from the generic "» name: …" to a type-specific "» place name: …"/"» area name: …"/etc. so the groups read distinctly. Generic across all 9 entity types `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH` recognizes (this section is shared by many other entity-reference columns — Recording of work, Recorded at place, credit-role columns, etc. — not just Location), via a new `entityNameTypeMap` threaded alongside the existing `entityNameGlyphMap` from `_findCellEntityRefs()`'s own `type` field (now also forwarded by `_findCellEntityCommentParts()`). `makeValueSynItem()` gained a new optional `entityType` parameter driving the label; falls back to the previous generic "» name: " when no type is known.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The `series-releases` page definition (bare `/series/<mbid>` overview page) was missing an `'Artists'` `entityFeatures` key — `Releases`/`Events`/`Release groups`/`Recordings`/`Works` were declared, but not `Artists`. When the page's H2 read "Artists", `resolveEntityFeaturesFromH2()`'s fallback silently applied the FIRST-declared feature set (`'Releases'`, `extractMainColumn: 'Release'`) instead — wrong for the Artists sub-table, whose real main column is `'Artist'`. Since `mainColIdx` never resolved, `cleanupHeaders()` still unconditionally created the "MB-Name"/"Comment"/"MB-Primary alias" `<th>` headers (gated only on "is `extractMainColumn` configured at all", not on whether it resolves to a real column on this table) while the row-building code correctly produced no data `<td>`s for them, leaving every row 3 columns short of its own header row — see `debug/artist-series.html`. Added the missing `'Artists'` entry, mirroring `collections-releases`' own already-correct one (`extractMainColumn: 'Artist'`, plus its Area/Begin area/End area/Begin/End column extractors).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On a "Show single-table" cross-tab snapshot of a Work or Recording sub-table from `artist-relationships` (which correctly has NO "Relationships" column on the live multi-table page — it only makes sense for Release/Release-group sub-tables), the hydrated single-table tab artificially injected a "Relationships" column header that could never be populated. Root cause: `artist-relationships`/`artist-relationships-filtered` declare `injectedColumns: ['Relationships']` unconditionally at the page-definition level (no per-sub-table-category scoping) — on the live page, correctness comes entirely from a downstream, per-sub-table, data-driven guard, `_suppressRelationshipsIfNoReleaseOrReleaseGroupLinks()` (and its sibling `_suppressReleaseEventsIfNoReleaseLinks()`), which physically removes the injected column from any table whose rows contain no `/release/`or `/release-group/` links — called from both `renderGroupedTable()`'s per-group loop and the live single-table fetch path in `startFetchingProcess`. `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()`'s own single-table render branch duplicated the rest of that live single-table sequence (`cleanupHeaders`/`addColumnFilterRow`/`makeTableSortableUnified`) but never called either guard, so a hydrated Work/Recording snapshot kept the header (and would have gone on to create empty `mb-rel-cell`/`mb-re-cell` placeholder `<td>`s once `initRelationshipsColumn()`/`initReleaseEventsColumn()` ran later). Added both guard calls to that branch, in the same relative order (after header injection, before the later `init*Column()` calls) as the live single-table path already uses.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values (📊) dropdown entries for flag-decorated columns ("Country/Date", "Country", "Locality", "Region", etc.) had three rendering bugs, all confined to `openUniqDrop()`'s `flagIconMap`/`renderItems()` flag-rendering path (the tooltip, built from `getCleanColumnText()`, was always correct): (1) text glued together with no space, e.g. "ES2009-02-08Sun" instead of "ES 2009-02-08 Sun" — `flagIconMap`'s text accumulation raw-concatenated text nodes instead of joining them with `' '` at each boundary the way `getCleanColumnText()` does; (2) multi-row (multi-`<li>`) cells rendered with no "and"/", " between items, e.g. "AT2003-05-05MonXE2003-05-05Mon" instead of "AT 2003-05-05 Mon and XE 2003-05-05 Mon" — `flagIconMap` walked the whole `<td>` with one flat pass, with no `<li>` item-boundary awareness, so the existing `_joinListItemsForDisplay()`/`displayText` "A, B and C" join (from an earlier session) never applied to the flag-icon rendering branch at all. Fixed by extracting the per-cell walk into `_buildFlagSegmentsForRoot()` (now called once per `_findCellListItems()` item instead of once for the whole cell) and a new `_joinFlagSegmentItems()` helper mirroring `_joinListItemsForDisplay()`'s exact separator rule to splice synthetic `', '`/`' and '` segments between items. (3) The icon-to-text gap in the dropdown didn't match the real table cell's own spacing — `renderItems()` hardcoded `marginRight: '4px'` on every icon clone, while `resolveFlagVisual()`'s `pick()` never captured the live cell's own `marginRight` at all. Now captured and baked onto the clone in `_bakeFlagIconNode()`; the hardcoded `4px` in `renderItems()` is only a fallback for a clone with no baked margin.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On a "Show single-table" cross-tab snapshot of a sub-table from a multi-table page (e.g. `artist-relationships`), filtering ANY column (typed filter text or a unique-value dropdown checkbox) permanently removed the Picard tagger column's icons from every row, never to return — even after clearing the filter. Root cause: `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()` calls `runFilter()` (which clones rows from the `allRows` source array into the live DOM) BEFORE its own full-mode `initPicardTaggerColumn()` call, so the picard `<td>`s only ever landed on that one now-orphaned live-DOM clone — `allRows` itself never got them, so every subsequent filter re-render re-cloned from a picard-less `allRows` and the rewire-only call (correctly, per its own contract) had nothing to rewire. This is the exact same class of bug `initRelationshipsColumn()`'s `_ensureRelCell()`/`allRows` sync already fixed for the Relationships column, for the identical reason — `initPicardTaggerColumn()` now mirrors that pattern: its full-mode pass also applies to `allRows` directly (single-table mode only; multi-table mode's own full-mode call already runs before its first `runFilter()`, so `group.rows` was never affected). Refactored the per-row cell-creation logic into a shared `_picardApplyToRow()` helper used by both the live-DOM pass and the new `allRows` pass, avoiding duplicated logic.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Relationships column's unique-values (📊) dropdown "Relationship icons" section (one entry per distinct relationship base URL, e.g. "https://www.amazon.com/") now supports multi-select checkboxes like every other section in the dropdown, instead of applying a single value and immediately closing the panel. Clicking an entry now toggles a ☑/☐ checkbox and re-applies the OR'd set via `applyUniqValueSet()`, keeping the panel open for continued selection — implemented as a new `rel:` compound structure mode (`_cellMatchesStructureMode()`), wired through the existing `_wireStructureCheckbox()` helper the same way "» name:"/"» role:" entries already work. Extracted a new `_findCellRelIcons()` helper (grouping a cell's relationship-icon URLs into base-URL "domainKey"s, including the existing path-sensitive-host handling for e.g. springsteenlyrics.com) as the single source of truth shared by both the dropdown-building pass and the new row-match branch — previously this grouping logic only existed inline inside the dropdown builder. Per-icon match highlighting (the red-outline `.mb-rel-icon-match` box) now also fires for this new multi-select path via the existing `_highlightRelCellIcons()` helper. Query-string-agnostic matching (e.g. `bootlegs.php?item=2616` still matches a `bootlegs.php` filter entry) is unchanged.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: The TEMPORARY diagnostic instrumentation added in 9.99.845/9.99.846 while chasing a hollow CAA/EAA-icon "Show single-table" bug (cross-tab snapshot capture/hydration fingerprints in `captureSubtableSnapshot`/`openSubtableAsSingleTableTab`/`_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData`, per-call counters and entry/branch logs in `_artInitPics`/`_artEnrichTable`/`_artEnrichIcon`/`_artBuildMultiRowArtCell`, the `_debugDumpCaaColumnState()` pipeline-stage dumper and its 5 call sites in `runFilter`'s single-table branch including 3 delayed `setTimeout` follow-ups, and the `_debugWatchCaaColumnForRegression()` MutationObserver regression watchdog) is being kept permanently rather than removed — useful to have on hand if a similar CAA/EAA regression needs chasing again. Added a new "GENERIC SETTINGS" checkbox, `sa_enable_art_diagnostic_logging` (default `false`), that every one of these sites is now gated behind — `_debugDumpCaaColumnState()`/`_debugWatchCaaColumnForRegression()` early-return (and, for the latter, skip installing their MutationObserver / scheduling their `setTimeout`s) when it's off, and every other individual log call site checks it directly, mirroring the existing `sa_enable_tooltip_debug` pattern (requires the global "Enable debug logging" setting to also be on). No behavior changes when the new setting is off (the default) — purely a toggle, matching the pre-existing behavior of this instrumentation being effectively silent unless deliberately dug into.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `eventParts` synthetic-column extractor (Comment/Disambiguation → Event-Type/Event-Date/Event-Detail/Event-Venue/.../Event-Additional-Info, used by 11 page definitions) unconditionally wrote the first pre-colon comma segment into `Event-Type`, regardless of its content, and would still attempt to split any post-colon text into Venue/City/State/Country even when that leading segment wasn't event metadata at all — so "version 4" landed in `Event-Type`, and "The River: Single Album version" (a release title that merely happens to contain ": ") got incorrectly split across `Event-Country`/`Event-Additional-Info`. Now the whole Type/Date/Detail/Location schema is only attempted when the leading segment is one of the recognized keywords `live`, `soundcheck`, `studio`, `interview`, `audition`, `live rehearsal` — anything else routes the ENTIRE raw disambiguation/comment text verbatim into `Event-Additional-Info` instead, with every other synthetic column left empty.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Unique-values (📊) dropdown's whole-cell entry for a multi-item list cell (e.g. "Producer", "Engineer", "Performer", "Instruments", tags, genres, or any other `<ul>/<li>`-rendered column) now reads as a natural "Jon Landau, Chuck Plotkin and Bruce Springsteen" instead of the ungrammatical space-joined run-on `getCleanColumnText()` previously produced — the CREDIT_ROLES `<li>` builder (like every other list-cell builder) never emits any separator text into the DOM between items, so `getCleanColumnText()`'s bare-space text-node join was the only thing standing in for punctuation. New `_joinListItemsForDisplay()` helper joins each multi-item value's own per-`<li>` texts (captured via a new `valueItemSequence` map, first-occurrence keyed by the raw whole-cell value) for display and tooltip purposes only. The underlying value used for the entry's checkbox key, `checkedValues`, `dataset.mbUniqValues`, and the row-filter equality check in `testRowMatch()` is untouched — still the exact raw `getCleanColumnText(cell)` string — so clicking the entry keeps filtering rows exactly as before.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: "CAA info"/"EAA info" dropdown section (9.99.849-851): superseded 9.99.850's plain font-size bump — "» image type: …" entries now render the value itself as an actual pill (bold, dark-grey background, matching `.mb-caa-type-badge`'s real inline style in the table cell) instead of plain text, via a new `_buildArtTypePillLabel()` helper. `_applySynBoxQuickFilter()`'s generic label rebuild (used by every other entry kind, and previously would have silently flattened the pill back to plain text on the very next quickfilter keystroke or clear) is now gated: entries carrying a new `item.dataset.mbUniqArtType` marker rebuild the pill via the same helper when the search is cleared, restoring it every time; while a search is actively matching text, the entry deliberately falls back to the existing plain-text-plus-`<mark>` rendering unchanged (same as before this pill styling existed) rather than attempting to splice a `<mark>` across the prefix/pill boundary — simpler and lower-risk, and only visible while actively typing in the dropdown's own search box. Checkbox-driven column filtering itself (`_wireStructureCheckbox`/`_cellMatchesStructureMode`) is completely unaffected by any of this, since it only ever depends on the `kind`/`value` strings, never on label DOM structure.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: CAA/EAA cell type-badge pills (e.g. "Schedule"/"Poster" — see debug/font.html, artist-events' "EAA" column) rendered noticeably smaller than the ".mb-caa-art-comment" text right next to them (e.g. "rescheduled dates") — two compounding nested `em` shrinks (the `.mb-caa-type-badge` wrapper's own 0.75em, then the individual pill's inline 0.78em on top of that) worked out to roughly 58% of the comment's size, which just inherits `li.mb-caa-art-li-image`'s own unshrunk 0.85em. Removed the wrapper's font-size (now inherits, no longer compounds) and bumped each pill's own inline font-size from 0.78em to 0.85em, matching the comment's effective size exactly.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: "CAA info"/"EAA info" dropdown section (9.99.849): the "» image type: …" entries read small/pill-like at the dropdown's default ambient font-size (0.87em, same as the source table cell's own small bold type-badge pill), noticeably smaller-feeling than the "» image comment: …" entries next to them. Bumped the image-type label span's own font-size to 1.05em so it reads like ordinary text, on par with the comment entries. `_appendSynLabelText()` now returns the label span it creates (harmless for existing callers that ignore the return) so `makeValueSynItem()` can style this one case without an extra DOM query.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "CAA info"/"EAA info" (named after the actual column header) section to the per-column unique-values dropdown for CAA/EAA art columns, listing every distinct per-image type-badge pill value (e.g. "Front", "Obi", "Matrix/Runout", from `.mb-caa-type-badge > span`) and every distinct per-image free-text comment (e.g. "Front cover, booklet page i", from `.mb-caa-art-comment`) — see debug/single-published-release.html — each independently checkable/filterable/highlightable, following the same pattern as the existing attr/task/date/instrument/altname/name/comment/alias/role families. New `makeValueSynItem` kinds `'arttype'`/`'artcomment'` (compound `MB_UNIQ_STRUCTURE_MODE_PREFIX` modes, so filtering needed zero changes to the generic `getColFilters()`/`testRowMatch()` dispatch — only two new branches in `_cellMatchesStructureMode()`). Since the target section depends on which column is actually open ("CAA info" vs "EAA info"), unlike every other kind these two are deliberately absent from the static `MB_UNIQ_KIND_TO_SECTION` map and instead routed dynamically inside `makeValueSynItem()` from `_caaOrEaaColName` (the `isCaaOrEaaCol` IIFE now resolves and keeps the literal column name, not just a boolean). New `SYN_SECTION_META` entries `caaInfo`/`eaaInfo`. Highlighting required two separate additions, not one: `testRowMatch()`'s dispatch (new `_highlightArtValueMatch()`) for the normal synchronous case, AND `_artHighlightImageLi()` (called from `_artBuildMultiRowArtCell()` when CAA/EAA artwork is (re)built — which happens asynchronously after the table's initial render/filter pass) for the async-rebuild case — without the second one, filtering would work but the highlight would silently fail to appear whenever an art cell (re)builds after a matching filter was already applied, which is the common case for these columns. Also extended `_structureModeLabel()`/`_structureModeTooltip()` for the two new compound modes.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Show single-table" (bug 2, continued — see 9.99.845/846/847): 9.99.847's fix wasn't sufficient — the count badge now survived, but the icon/thumbnail itself still vanished ("the number of images instead of the image itself when collapsed"), and only when the third-party jesus2099 "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL" userscript was installed (confirmed by the reporter: perfect in a browser with only this script). Root cause: a second, independent mechanism — `_watchForLateJesus2099Injections()`'s `_stripJesus2099CaaAnchor`, installed specifically for the cross-tab snapshot bootstrap right before `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData()` runs — has the exact same unconditional-removal bug 9.99.847 fixed in `_stripTransientCellState`, just in a separate code path untouched by that fix. It reactively strips any `<a>` wrapping jesus2099's cover-art icon class the instant it's added anywhere inside `table.tbl` (plus a final sweep at its 5s watch-window boundary), which fires the moment renderFinalTable inserts the hydrated rows — removing the anchor within the same render pass, confirmed via debug/mt2-debug.log / debug/st2-debug.log (anchor present and correct immediately post-hydration, gone moments later, with this function's own "removed a late jesus2099 caa-icon anchor" log in between). Regated `_stripJesus2099CaaAnchor` to skip this script's own synthetic "CAA"/"EAA" column (checked via `cell.cellIndex` against `caaFindColumnByName`) — that column is exactly where ColumnDataExtractor.caa's Path A/B puts a row's one authoritative art anchor, which on pages without a Title-column 'jesus2099' columnEraser (e.g. artist-relationships) legitimately carries the jesus2099 class as the cell's ONLY content, not a duplicate. Every other column (sticky Title, MB-Name, …) never legitimately holds a raw cover-art anchor, so those keep the unconditional strip — this generalizes 9.99.847's `.mb-caa-inline-ph`-presence gate (which only ever sees the sticky Title column) to also cover MB-Name-style columns that gate can't reach.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Show single-table" (bug 2, see 9.99.845/9.99.846): root-caused via the round-2 debug logs (debug/mt-debug.log, debug/st-debug.log) — captureSubtableSnapshot's new RAW-vs-STRIPPED fingerprint showed all 4 "published release" rows had a correct anchor+badge on the LIVE page at the exact moment of capture, but 3 lost their badge and 1 lost its anchor entirely after getCleanCellHtml/_stripTransientCellState ran. Two distinct over-eager cleanup steps in _stripTransientCellState: (1) _artEnrichIcon's "Resource Timing wrapper adoption" moves the CAA/EAA count badge inside `.mb-art-cache-hint-col-wrap` to stack it under the cache-hint emoji, but the wrap's cosmetic cleanup removed the whole wrap — badge included; now the badge is pulled back out as the wrap's own sibling first. (2) The jesus2099 cover-art-icon strip (added in commit 4432890 for artist-releasegroups' sticky Title column, where a LATE-arriving jesus2099 icon duplicates this script's own separate inline thumbnail) ran unconditionally on every cell — but artist-relationships' Title column has no 'jesus2099' columnEraser configured, so ColumnDataExtractor.caa's Path A moves jesus2099's OWN anchor straight into the synthetic "CAA" column, where it is the cell's ONLY art content, not a duplicate; stripping it unconditionally destroyed it outright. Now gated on `_hadInlineArtPh` (captured before the inline-thumbnail placeholder is itself removed) — only strips when this same cell also carries this script's own separate inline CAA/EAA thumbnail, mirroring the same per-cell gate `_stripLateJesus2099CaaIcon()` (9.99.844) already uses for the reactive/live case. All debug-only instrumentation from 9.99.845/9.99.846 is left in place (no behavior effect, gated by sa_enable_debug_logging) pending confirmation this fully resolves bug 2.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: TEMPORARY diagnostic instrumentation, round 2 for bug 2 (see 9.99.845). The first round's logs (debug/sub-table-debug.log, debug/single-table-debug.log) disproved the detached-clone-race theory: the row that ends up hollow (release 8aeb338a, "row 914", published-release category) was built CORRECTLY by _artBuildMultiRowArtCell on the ORIGINAL multi-table page — confirmed via the logged artCell.innerHTML snapshot showing a properly-titled anchor — and no further instrumented call touches that row again before it's captured hollow ~29s later by captureSubtableSnapshot, while three sibling rows built in the same batch survive untouched. Something un-instrumented reverts it. Added `_debugWatchCaaColumnForRegression(table)`: a MutationObserver installed on every table with a CAA/EAA column (wired into `_artInitPics`) that tracks each row's anchor+badge presence and, on any row transitioning from "had both" to "missing either", logs the triggering mutation's removedNodes/addedNodes and a best-effort stack trace — the direct smoking-gun catcher for whatever is reverting it. Also added the missing RAW (pre-getCleanCellHtml) fingerprint to captureSubtableSnapshot's existing per-row debug log, alongside the already-captured post-strip one, to distinguish "already hollow on the live page before capture" from "getCleanCellHtml/_stripTransientCellState broke it during capture" (the first round only logged the post-strip state). No behavior changes — logging only. Remove once bug 2 is root-caused.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: TEMPORARY diagnostic instrumentation for the still-open bug 2 (missing CAA icons + dead collapse-header button on a "Show single-table" hydrated single-table page — non-deterministic per debug/single-published-release-2.html, unlike the first snapshot). Added extensive Lib.debug() logging across the whole cross-tab snapshot path: captureSubtableSnapshot/openSubtableAsSingleTableTab (per-row CAA/EAA marker fingerprint + capture timestamp), _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData (entry marker, per-cell before/after _stripTransientCellState fingerprint, resolved addCAA/addEAA, pre-runFilter timestamp), runFilter's single-table branch (pre/post-renderFinalTable, pre/post-initCollapsableColumns, pre/post-initCaaPics with +500ms/+2000ms/+5000ms delayed follow-up dumps), and the CAA enrichment chain itself (_artInitPics/_artEnrichTable/_artEnrichIcon/_artBuildMultiRowArtCell — call counters, per-anchor row/href/enriched-state, and critically anchor.isConnected/artCell.isConnected right before each DOM write, to catch a suspected detached-clone race where a later re-render replaces a row while an earlier _artEnrichIcon async chain — IDB await or network fetch — is still in flight, landing its result on an orphaned clone). New shared helper `_debugDumpCaaColumnState(label)` snapshots every CAA/EAA cell's live state at a named checkpoint. No behavior changes — logging only, gated by the existing sa_enable_debug_logging toggle. Remove once bug 2 is root-caused.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Show single-table" (openSubtableAsSingleTableTab / _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData): the third-party "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL" userscript's (jesus2099) own cover-art icon reappeared next to this script's inline CAA thumbnail on a snapshot tab, doubling the visible artwork (see debug/CAA-missing-doubled.org, debug/double-caa-icons.html — a Bruce Springsteen artist-releasegroups "Album" sub-table). The existing capture-time strip (`_stripTransientCellState`, WIP-era commit 4432890) only cleans the payload once, on the ORIGINAL tab, before the snapshot is taken — but the "Show single-table" tab is a real MusicBrainz page load, so jesus2099 runs its own fresh, independent cover-art lookup there too, well after hydration, landing the icon right back in the cell. Added `initCaaInlineJesus2099Observer()`/`_stripLateJesus2099CaaIcon()`, mirroring the existing AcoustID/ISRC and Disambiguation late-arrival observers: a MutationObserver watches every table for the jesus2099 icon re-appearing in a cell that already carries this script's own `.mb-caa-inline-ph`/`.mb-eaa-inline-ph` inline thumbnail, and removes it reactively. Wired into all three inline-thumbnail call sites (runFilter's single-table branch, the initial single-table load, and renderGroupedTable's tail — covering artist-releasegroups' `_isReleaseGroupsMultiMode()` branch specifically). New setting `sa_enable_caa_inline_jesus2099_observer` (default on).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Status line (`#mb-status-displays-container`): a Load-from-Disk (or cross-tab "Show single-table") load never seeded the leading `globalStatusDisplay` segment the way a fetch-from-web load does (`Loaded N pages (M rows)`), so the first later CAA/EAA or Rels completion's own leading `, ` separator had nothing in front of it — a stray leading comma before e.g. `🎨CAA: 8.2s`. Added the equivalent leading segment (`Loaded N rows from disk file X.gz` / `Loaded N rows from <sourceLabel>`) in `_hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData`, resetting the same `_caaGlobalStatusDone`/`_relGlobalStatusDone` flags the fetch path resets so later segments still append correctly.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: release-tracks: the "Disambiguation" column (fed by the native title/recording-name comment, and by the third-party "mb. INLINE STUFF" userscript's own async recording-comment lookup — see 9.99.841) is decided once, page-wide, at extraction time: if the button is pressed before that comment has loaded for ANY track, the whole column is skipped, not just the individual row. Added `initDisambiguationObserver()`/`_relocateLateDisambiguation()` (mirroring the existing AcoustID/ISRC late-arrival observer): a MutationObserver now watches each medium's table and, when a comment span shows up after the fact, either moves it into the already-existing Disambiguation column reactively, or — when the column was never created at all — shows a small, dismissable "Rebuild table" notice next to the status line instead of silently doing nothing (deliberately not a hand-spliced column injection into the already-rendered/sorted/filtered table, and not a silent auto-reload that would discard the user's current filter/sort/scroll state — clicking the notice just re-runs the normal, already-correct fetch). New setting `sa_enable_release_tracks_disambiguation_observer` (default on).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: release-tracks: `syntheticColumnExtractors` entries sourcing from `'Disambiguation'` (the `eventParts` extractor, splitting a live-performance comment like jesus2099's "mb. INLINE STUFF" userscript's "(live, 1978‐07‐07: The Roxy Theatre, West Hollywood, CA, USA)" into Event-Type/Date/Venue/City/State/Country columns) were silently never applied on release-tracks, even though the identical config works on other page types (e.g. instrument-recordings). Root cause: both per-row synthetic-column-extractor pipelines inside `startFetchingProcess()`'s fetch loop, AND the header-injection pass in `cleanupHeaders()`, resolved `sourceColumn` only against a map/set populated exclusively from resolved `activeColumnExtractors` outputs and the `extractMainColumn`-only MB-Name/Comment/MB-Primary-alias triad — never from a plain header/cell that a page's own bespoke pre-processing (here, `applyExtractTrackTitleData()`) creates directly, like release-tracks' "Disambiguation" column. instrument-recordings only happened to work because it sources from `'Comment'`, which IS in that triad via its own `extractMainColumn: 'Name'`. Added a page-scoped `headerName → colIdx` lookup (built once from the already-scanned `headerNames`) as a fallback source in all three per-row synthetic-extractor call sites, plus the equivalent "is this sourceColumn already a real header on this table" fallback in `cleanupHeaders()`'s header-injection guard (data cells alone were appearing correctly after the first fix, but with no header above them — see debug/row.html vs debug/header.html) — general enough to fix this for any current or future page type/column, not just this one. Also documented the third-party "mb. INLINE STUFF" userscript (jesus2099) — whose own recording comment/disambiguation span shares the native `.comment` class and selector, so it was already picked up structurally, just never wired through — at the three code sites that build/detect the Disambiguation column.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The unique-values dropdown's standard section showed one small-glyph-icon entry per distinct entity href whenever the same text (e.g. a release title) was credited to more than one distinct entity — e.g. several different releases all titled "18 Tracks", or a release also showing up with a disambiguation comment as a separate entry (see debug/uvd-enhancement.html, debug/uvd-title.html, debug/glyph-entity-entry.html). These entries were visually indistinguishable from each other and from the plain whole-cell value (same text, tiny unlabeled icon prefix), so there was no way to tell which specific entity a given row would filter to without clicking it and checking. Removed the per-href entity-glyph rows from the standard section entirely; the existing "Entity info" section's "» name:" entry now offers exactly ONE entry per distinct entity name (with its entity-type glyph icon), which — unlike the removed rows — matches EVERY row containing that name irrespective of its own disambiguation comment or lack of one, and is no longer restricted to entities that have a comment. `_findCellEntityCommentParts()`'s gate broadened from "has a `.comment` span" to "is not a bare cell-wide name" (`!ref.isBare`), with `comment`/`alias` falling back to `null` for a non-bare entity that has no comment of its own; `_cellMatchesStructureMode()`'s `name:` mode and `_highlightEntityCommentPartMatch()` now match/highlight directly off the ungated `_findCellEntityRefs()` list instead of the comment-scoped helper, so bare occurrences of the name are matched and highlighted too. The now-dead per-href `entityInfo`/`entityHrefCounts`/`entityEntries` aggregation in `openUniqDrop()` and `renderItems()`'s matching render branch were removed; the `MB_UNIQ_ENTITY_HREF_PREFIX`-keyed matching/highlighting/label machinery itself is untouched, so a filter selection saved before this change (e.g. loaded from a saved table export) keeps working.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 9.99.838's CAA/EAA dropdown-highlight fix missed the item-value ("▤") case: a CAA/EAA cell with ≥2 images (summary li + image li's) is itself a qualifying multi-row list to `_findCellListItems()`'s generic ul>li structural detection, so an image's own type text (e.g. "Poster") can also be offered/checked as an item-prefixed dropdown entry, not just a plain whole-cell value. `_artHighlightImageLi()` (the async art-cell-rebuild highlighter 9.99.838 also touched) only re-checked the plain-value case after a rebuild, not the item-value one `_highlightUniqItemMatches()` already handled for cells built before the filter changed — so a cell that (re)built AFTER selecting the item-value entry stayed unhighlighted. Added the same item-value check `_highlightUniqItemMatches()` uses (highlighting the whole matching `<li>`, not just its badge/comment span) to `_artHighlightImageLi()`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Selecting a CAA/EAA image type or comment value (e.g. "Poster") from a column's unique-values dropdown correctly filtered the row but never highlighted the matching `.mb-caa-type-badge`/`.mb-caa-art-comment` text — only typing the same value directly into the column filter box did. `getCleanColumnText()` folds each image's own type(s)/comment (stored out-of-band in `ul.dataset.mbArtSearch`, not as visible text) into the CAA/EAA cell's whole-cell value, so a plain dropdown selection like "Poster" can exact-match a cell whose only content IS that art-search text — but both places that apply column-filter highlighting (`testRowMatch()`'s `isMultiValueFilter` branch and the CAA/EAA-specific `_artHighlightImageLi()`, used for async art-cell rebuilds) explicitly skipped ALL value-set/dropdown filters, since a normal whole-cell value match has no single sub-element worth highlighting. Added `_highlightUniqArtTypeMatches()` (mirroring the existing `_highlightUniqItemMatches()`/`_highlightUniqEntityMatches()` per-`<li>` pattern, scoped to each image's own type-pill/comment span) and wired it into both call sites.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 9.99.836 `columnErasers` fix for doubled CAA inline images didn't actually take effect on `/user/<username>/ratings` (or `tag-value`/`user-tag-value`/`instrument-list`/`artist-credit`) — those pages show several entity types' tables at once (e.g. Artist ratings, Event ratings, Release group ratings, … all on one page), and the per-group table-building pass only rebuilt `activeColumnExtractors`/`activeSyntheticColumnExtractors`/`activeInjectedColumnExtractors`/`activeIntegerColumns` from each group's own `entityFeatures` block — never `activeColumnErasers`. So `applyColumnErasers()` kept using whichever single entity type's erasers (if any) got resolved once at the top of the page, for every group's rows, silently never applying a group's own `columnErasers` entry (including the ones just added). Added the missing `activeColumnErasers` rebuild + per-table colIdx re-resolution alongside the existing extractor rebuild, and added `'artist-credit'` to the pageType list that gets it (it has the same simultaneous-multi-entity-table shape but wasn't in that list at all).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The "Release group ratings" section on `/user/<username>/ratings` (and the matching `/user/<username>/ratings/release_group` "View all ratings" overflow page) showed each release group's cover art TWICE — the jesus2099 "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL" userscript's own native `<a href=".../cover-art"><span class="caa-icon">` icon, plus this script's own `addCAA` inline thumbnail layered on top of it, since nothing erased the native icon first (unlike other pages using `addCAA` alongside a `columnErasers: […, 'jesus2099']` entry for the same column). Added the missing `columnErasers` entry to both page definitions' 'Release groups' entity features, then audited every other `entityFeatures` block combining `addCAA` with a Release/Release-group-shaped source column and found the identical gap copy-pasted across `artist-credit-entity`, `artist-credit`, `user-tag-value-entity`, `user-tag-value`, `tag-value-entity`, `tag-value`, `collections-releases`, `search` (its 'Releases'/'Release groups'/'Recordings' blocks), and `series-releases`'s own 'Releases' block — fixed all of them the same way.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
Fixed a Location-column split bug where two consecutive same-shaped area levels sharing an identical name (e.g. an event at "SiriusXM Studio" in New York City, itself inside New York state — MusicBrainz has separate area entities both literally named "New York") rendered as two SEPARATE `
  • ` lists jammed into the "Region" cell ("…
,
    …") instead of one merged entry, whenever a flag-decorating userscript ("More Flags Everywhere"/"Canadian Province Flags Everywhere") decorated the Locality cell's area link only AFTER this script's own extraction ran (always true for paginated rows 2..Max, fetched via a detached `DOMParser` that userscript never sees). `_forceLocalityToRegion()` — the deferred correction that moves a wrongly-placed Locality entry into Region once its subdivision-name match is confirmed — moved Locality's WHOLE `
      ` wrapper as a sibling of Region's own `
        ` instead of merging their `
      • ` content together. It now detects the `
