        • ` multi-row wrapping both `splitLocation`/`splitArea` cells always use and merges same-indexed `
        • ` pairs' children instead, falling back to the original whole-cell move only when Region has no `
            ` of its own to merge into (i.e. it was genuinely empty).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The unique-values dropdown's "Roles" section now also picks up `» role:` entries for the plain-text "Role" column shown when browsing one artist's OWN events (e.g. `/artist/<mbid>/events`) — previously only the `.artist-roles` list shape (event pages' "Artists" column, e.g. `/place/<mbid>/events`) was recognized. `_findCellArtistRoles()` now falls back to splitting that column's flat comma-joined text (MusicBrainz's `commaOnlyListText()` output, e.g. "main performer, guest performer", confirmed against the `EventList.js`/`tableColumns.js` source) into individual roles, gated strictly on the cell's own column being named "Role" (via `_cleanColHeaderText()`) so no unrelated plain-text column is misread as a role list. Its returned `{li, roles}` shape is renamed to `{container, roles}` since `container` is now a `<td>` for this shape, a `<li>` for the other.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The unique-values dropdown's visible height (how many entries show before it scrolls) is now configurable via the new "Unique-Values Dropdown Visible Rows" setting (default 8, matching the dropdown's previous fixed height) instead of a hardcoded 320px — raise it to see more entries at once. Applied as an inline `max-height` in `openUniqDrop()` (always wins over the unchanged 320px CSS fallback on `#mb-col-uniq-dropdown`), and the same value now drives the upward-flip positioning estimate too, so the flip decision stays accurate at any configured row count.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The unique-values dropdown's synthetic entries no longer sit under one flat, always-expanded "Cell structure" header — they're now grouped into named, independently collapsible sections with their own icon: 🔠 Structure (empty/single/multi-row cell state, artwork/inline-thumbnail presence), 🚩 Flags (track/recording name mismatch, name variation), 🎚️ Credit details (attribute/task/date/instrument/credited-as), 👤 Entity info (name/comment/alias), 🎭 Roles (event role), and 🔗 Relationship icons. Click a section header (or Enter/Space) to collapse/expand it; state is remembered globally by section name across every column and page (GM storage key `mb_sa_uniq_section_collapse`). New `getOrCreateSynSection()`/`SYN_SECTION_META` in `openUniqDrop()` replace the old single `synHdr`/`appendSynDivider()` scattered per family.

The dropdown's quickfilter now covers the "Relationship icons" section too — a pre-existing gap where those entries had no `dataset.mbUniqSynLabel` and were silently skipped by `_applySynBoxQuickFilter()`. Typing a filter also auto-expands any collapsed section that has a match (showing a `(N)` match count in its header) and hides sections with zero matches, so a collapsed section can no longer hide a live search result; clearing the filter restores every section's persisted collapsed/expanded state.

The "Entity info" section's "» name:"/"» alias:" entries (one per distinct bare entity name/primary alias found in cells with a disambiguation comment) no longer duplicate a name/alias that's already independently selectable elsewhere in the same dropdown — as a plain whole-cell value or as an entity-glyph href row. On a page with many disambiguated same-named entities (e.g. an instrument's "Artists" list) this noticeably shrinks the section instead of showing the same name three different ways.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The unique-values dropdown's flag/area icon(s) (Country/Locality/Region/Area/Location/Country-Date/Recorded-at-place/Mixed-at-place columns) now render inline, immediately in front of the place/area/country name each one decorates, instead of every icon being bunched at the very start of the entry — e.g. "Southern Tracks in [flag]Atlanta, [flag]Georgia, [flag]United States" instead of "[flag][flag][flag]Southern Tracks in Atlanta, Georgia, United States" (see debug/place-flags.html, debug/place-flags-ucv.html, debug/uv-dropdown.html). `flagIconMap` now stores an ordered array of text/icon segments (built by walking the live cell with a TreeWalker, mirroring `getCleanColumnText()`'s own document-order text extraction) instead of a flat array of cloned icons; `renderItems()` renders those segments inline, preserving the existing quickfilter `<mark>` highlight for the common case of a match that doesn't straddle an icon.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" section now has per-value entries for an artist's own credited event role (e.g. "main performer", "guest performer", "support act", "participant", "host") in any column rendering a native MusicBrainz `.artist-roles` list — e.g. the "Artists" column on `/place/<mbid>/events` and similar event-listing pages (see debug/event-performer.html). New generic query-time extractor `_findCellArtistRoles()`, reusing `_artTooltipArtistRoles()`'s established direct-text-node-children technique, wired into a new `role:` compound structure-mode alongside the existing `name:`/`comment:`/`alias:` family.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A bare `<dt>instruments:</dt>` (MusicBrainz's own generic, unspecified-instrument credit — no `/instrument/` link at all, e.g. crediting an artist for playing unspecified instruments — see debug/instr.html) was rejected entirely by `_parseInstrumentVocalsDt`, since it neither carries an instrument link nor ends in the word "vocals". This dumped the credit into its own bogus dynamic-fallback column that collided in name with the real shared "Instruments" column. Bare "instruments:"/"additional instruments:" credits (and any recognized attribute-word prefix) now correctly join the same shared "Instruments" column, just without a specific instrument-type prefix on the artist's entry.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The dynamic-fallback "Part of" column (a track's "part of series" relationship) is now labeled "Part of series", and "Edit of"/"Remix of" are now labeled "Edit of recording"/"Remix of recording" (confirmed via MusicBrainz's own embedded relationship-type metadata in debug/g.html: `edit` is a recording-to-recording relationship type, not series) — the bare names read ambiguously next to their own glyph icon. New `DYNAMIC_ROLE_DISPLAY_NAME_OVERRIDES` map, checked by phrase key in `_dynamicRoleDisplayName()`, for any future dynamic-fallback column that needs the same treatment.

`KNOWN_ENTITY_LINK_KINDS` (the entity kinds the dynamic-fallback AR-column glyph/kind-splitting system recognizes) now includes `'recording'` — recording-to-recording relationships like "Samples"/"Music videos"/"Instrumental versions" now get their own recording header glyph, same as every other entity-kind-recognized dynamic column. Confirmed via debug/tracklist-overflow.html's `<span class="recordinglink">` marker on these columns' `<dd>`s.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The "Loading overflow tracks" progress label now shows the total track count MusicBrainz already reports on the medium's own "currently showing 100 out of 1209 total" overflow message (e.g. "medium 1 of 1... (1001 of 1209 tracks) - 1.8s left"), instead of just the live count with no target to compare against.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Dynamic-fallback AR columns whose relationship is chain-shaped (a primary target plus its own nested area/country decoration, e.g. "engineered at:"/"produced at:" — a place credit followed by " in " and its own area, same shape as the dedicated "Recorded at place"/"Mixed at place" columns) never got a header glyph icon, because `_glyphClassForDynamicColumn` required exactly one entity kind to be present and a chain always has 2+ (its target kind plus its area/country decoration kind). Confirmed via debug/soul-days.html's "engineered at:" credit. Since a merged (`'default'`) dynamic column can only ever be chain-shaped when it holds more than one kind (a genuine multi-kind PEER merge is always split into separate per-kind columns instead — see `_splitColumnByEntityKind`), the glyph is now always taken from the first kind present in `KNOWN_ENTITY_LINK_KINDS`' fixed order (which already lists every real target kind before its own decoration kind), rather than requiring exactly one.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
`INSTRUMENT_VOCAL_ATTRIBUTES` (the recognized attribute-word prefixes for the shared "Instruments"/"Vocals" release-tracks columns) was missing `'other'` — a real MusicBrainz credit attribute (e.g. `
Drums (drum set) and other vocals [shout]:
`, `
Other vocals [chant]:
`). Since `_parseInstrumentVocalsDt` rejects the WHOLE `
` when even one component has an unrecognized word, this silently dropped the otherwise-valid "Drums (drum set)" instrument component too, dumping the whole credit into its own bogus dynamic-fallback column (e.g. "Drums (drum set) and other vocals [shout]") instead of splitting cleanly into "Instruments"/"Vocals". Added `'other'` to the recognized list.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `_parseInstrumentVocalsDt()`'s component-splitting (for the shared "Instruments"/"Vocals" release-tracks columns) split on every `,`/` and ` in a `<dt>`, including ones INSIDE a credited-as `[…]` alt-name bracket — MusicBrainz's own bracket can itself be a comma-joined list, e.g. `guitar [1965 Gibson Firebird, Gibson SG, 12 string PRS, Blackface Fender Super Reverb, Silvertone 40]:` (see debug/credited-as-original.html). This split the bracket in two, left an unclosed `[` that failed the bracket-match, and its now-unstripped garbage words failed the attribute-word check — silently rejecting the whole `<dt>` and dumping the credit into its own bogus dynamic-fallback column named after the raw half-bracketed text (e.g. "Electric bass guitar [1961 fender p-bass, ampeg b-15]") instead of the shared "Instruments" column. Confirmed on a 100+-row release via debug/credited-as-final-buggy.html. The component split now skips over whole `[…]` brackets before ever considering a `,`/` and ` inside them a boundary.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: The unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" section now has per-value entries for the "Instruments"/"Vocals" columns' credited-as alternate name — MusicBrainz's own trailing "[…]" bracket on a credit (e.g. `guitar [12-string guitar]`, `synthesizer [synth strings]` — see debug/cr-as-original.html / debug/cr-as-final.html). Previously this text rendered but was plain, unfilterable text; it's now wrapped in a `.mb-credit-altname` sentinel (mirroring the existing `attr:`/`task:`/`date:`/`instrument:` compound structure-modes) so it can be checkbox-filtered and highlighted like every other credit detail.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `extractMainColumn`'s "Comment" column never stripped `<i title="Primary alias">` before reading comment text, so on a row whose entity comment was wholly or partly a primary alias, the alias text showed up mislabeled as a disambiguation comment (e.g. artist-works' "An der schönen blauen Donau, op. 314" → Comment showed its alias "On the Beautiful Blue Danube, op. 314" verbatim — see debug/work-comment-bug.html). The two duplicated inline extraction blocks that built `MB-Name`/`Comment` are now unified into a single new helper, `_extractMainColumnParts()`, which also splits out a new third synthetic column, `MB-Primary alias`. The identical bug in the independent `_tagCountBase()`-backed extractor family (`Name_Comment`, `Name_Date_Comment`, `Name_Comment_Artists`, `tagCount_Name_Comment`, and friends — used by tag-value/tag-count page types) is fixed the same way.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Retired 7 `columnExtractors` entries using `extractor: 'primaryAlias'` whose `sourceColumn` matched their page definition's own `extractMainColumn` — fully redundant now that `extractMainColumn` natively produces `MB-Primary alias`. `tooltipColumns` references to the old `'Primary Alias'` column were updated to `'MB-Primary alias'` on those pages. The 3 page blocks that pair `primaryAlias` with the `_tagCountBase` family (no `extractMainColumn`) keep using it unchanged, since it remains their only source of alias data.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Same gap as 9.99.822, for `release-group`-typed entity links (e.g. a report page's "Release group" column, `/report/SetInDifferentRG"` — see debug/rep-rg.html) — `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH` didn't recognize the `/release-group/{mbid}` URL path segment at all. Added `'release-group': 'rglink'` — note the CSS class is `rglink`, not a hyphenated `release-grouplink`; the map's key (URL path segment) and its value (CSS class name) are independently-confirmed facts about two different things, not derived from each other.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The unique-values dropdown's entity-glyph rows, and the new `name:`/`comment:`/`alias:` "Cell structure" filtering, silently did nothing for `release`/`recording`-typed entity links — e.g. an artist's "Releases"/"Recordings" pages, a label/series/instrument page's "Release" column, or an artist's "Relationships" page "Title" column. Root cause: `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH` (the map `_findCellEntityRefs()`/`_findCellEntityCommentParts()` use to recognize an entity link at all) only listed 6 of MusicBrainz's own glyph-marker types, based on an in-code comment claiming no `recordinglink`/`releaselink` CSS class existed anywhere in real MusicBrainz markup — confirmed WRONG via live page snapshots (`<span class="recordinglink">`/`<span class="releaselink">` genuinely render on an artist's Relationships page) and MusicBrainz's own icons stylesheet, which defines both (plus `serieslink`/`instrumentlink`/`rglink`/`collectionlink`/`genrelink`, not added here since nothing reported needs them yet). Added `release: 'releaselink'` and `recording: 'recordinglink'` to `_ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH` and corrected every stale comment repeating the old 6-type claim.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" section now supports filtering/highlighting by an entity's own anchored name, its disambiguation comment (excluding any primary alias), and its primary alias, independently combinable — e.g. an artist-works page's "Work"/"Authors" columns' `Name (Alias, extra text)` shape. Unlike the existing attr:/task:/date:/instrument: entries (which scan DOM sentinel classes this script injects when building release-tracks' bespoke AR columns), this works on NATIVE, unmodified MusicBrainz markup at query time — via a new `_findCellEntityCommentParts()` helper (extends `_findCellEntityRefs()`) reused identically by the counting pass, `_cellMatchesStructureMode()`'s new `name:`/`comment:`/`alias:` compound modes, and a new `_highlightEntityCommentPartMatch()` — so it works generically across every page/column with this shape (artist Works, report-detail, collection Works tab, search Works tab, and any other column sharing the same native markup), not just release-tracks. Scoped to entities that actually have a disambiguation comment; comment-less entities are unaffected (their name remains independently selectable via the existing href-based entity-glyph rows in the standard section).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown's quickfilter now also filters and `<mark>`-highlights entries inside the "Cell structure" section, not just the standard value list below it — typing narrows both sections together, and Escape/the × button clears both. New `_applySynBoxQuickFilter()` toggles visibility and rewrites each entry's own label span in place (synBox's entries are built once and keep their checkbox/checked state across keystrokes, unlike the standard list which fully rebuilds), and keyboard arrow-navigation now skips quickfilter-hidden "Cell structure" entries the same way it already skipped filtered-out standard entries.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: "Cell structure" section's count badges now right-align with a shared, panel-wide fixed width instead of their own unpadded natural width — symmetric with the standard value list's badges, and now the single source of truth for column-widest-count sizing across BOTH sections, so no badge in the whole dropdown can end up misaligned or overflow its column regardless of which section's number happens to have the most digits.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" section now surfaces the "Instruments" column's own instrument type (e.g. "bass", "guitar", "drum machine") as its own per-value checkbox entry, exactly like the existing per-attribute/per-task/per-date entries — one entry per distinct instrument actually present, checking one filters to matching rows and highlights the instrument link. `_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem()`'s cloned instrument `<a>` is now tagged with a new `mb-credit-instrument` sentinel class (its own href/click-to-instrument-page behavior untouched) alongside the existing `.mb-credit-attr`/`.mb-credit-date` sentinels, wired through the same `instrument:` compound structure-mode used for `attr:`/`task:`/`date:`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Vocals"/"Instruments" columns rendered their attribute word (e.g. "lead") and date/task annotation (e.g. "on 1988-04-27") merged into one shared comma-joined parenthetical — "(lead, on 1988-04-27)" — instead of each in its own separate brackets like every other AR credit column (e.g. "Recorded at place"'s "(additional) (from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03)"). `_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem()` (the actual builder `_buildInstrumentsTd`/`_buildVocalsTd` share — a separate, less-developed twin of `_buildCreditListItem` that 9.99.817's date-range "Cell structure" feature missed entirely) now appends two independent " (…)" parentheticals, symmetric with `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd`/`_buildCreditListItem`'s own convention: "Bruce Springsteen (lead) (on 1988-04-27)". This also closes the gap that made 9.99.817's date-range feature not actually work on Vocals/Instruments at all — the date/task annotation there was still a bare, unwrapped text node; it's now wrapped in `.mb-credit-date`/`.mb-credit-task` (via `_wrapDateAnnotationsInText()`/`_isDateAnnotationText()`) the same as every other AR credit column, so the unique-values dropdown's per-date/per-task "Cell structure" checkbox entries and highlighting now work correctly here too.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" section now surfaces AR credit date/date-range annotations (e.g. "on 1988-04-27", "in 1987", "from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03", and the bare "1988-04-27" shape special to "Recorded at event") as their own per-value checkbox entries, exactly like the existing per-attribute ("additional"/"guest"/"assistant"/"co") and per-task entries — one entry per distinct date expression actually present in the column, checking one filters to matching rows and highlights the actual date text. New `<span class="mb-credit-date">` sentinel (mirroring `.mb-credit-attr`/`.mb-credit-task`) is wired into every AR-credit builder that can carry a trailing date annotation: `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd` (Recorded at place/Mixed at place), the "Recorded at event" bare-date cell, `_buildCreditListItem` (Vocals/Instruments/Performer/CREDIT_ROLES), and the generic `_buildKindSplitListTd`/`_buildLabelCreditListTd` (Phonographic copyright by artist/label, Produced for label, and any other AR column routed through the generic multi-kind-split builder) — the last two also correctly split MusicBrainz's own multi-date shape for a single credit (e.g. "in 1987, in 1988") into two separate date entries. Detection reuses the existing `_parseCreditDateAnnotation`/`_parseBareParenDate` date-shape recognizers from the live-recording-date-check feature, so both agree on exactly the same date forms.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unique-values dropdown's "~ has name variation" Cell-structure entry only ever detected MusicBrainz's `<span class="name-variation">` shape (nested inside a relationship/credit list item, e.g. an artist's "Events" Location column or "Works" Recording artists/Authors columns) — it never detected the CELL-LEVEL `<td class="artist-credit-variation">` shape MusicBrainz uses on release/release-group listings' credited-artist column, so a genuine name variation there produced no entry at all. Replaced the three narrow `span.name-variation` lookups (counting in `openUniqDrop()`, `_cellMatchesStructureMode()`'s `'name-variation'` mode, and `_highlightNameVariationMatch()`) with a new shared `_findNameVariationElements()` helper that checks the cell's own class as well as its descendants, matched by class-name SUFFIX (`[class$="-variation"]`) rather than an enumerated list — generalizes to any current or future similarly-named MusicBrainz `-variation` class, page-type-agnostically, without a new hardcoded selector each time.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': every collapsable AR credit-role column (Recording engineer, Engineer, Producer, Mixer, Recorded at place, Recorded in area, Mixed at place, Performer, Instruments, Vocals, Phonographic copyright …, Produced for label, and any dynamically-discovered AR column) permanently lost its collapse/expand toggle and multi-row collapsed state the moment ANY filter was applied (typed text or a unique-values dropdown selection) — all their cells snapped to fully expanded with no way to re-collapse them, even after clearing the filter. Root cause: `_initColHeaderGlyph()`'s entity-type glyph marker (injected into these columns' headers only, via `_guardGlyphAgainstEmptySelectorHiding()`) embeds an invisible zero-width space (U+200B) that survives both `initCollapsableColumns()`'s glyph-character-class regex strip AND `.trim()` (U+200B isn't JS whitespace). On the very first render this is harmless (`initCollapsableColumns()` runs before the glyph gets injected), but every subsequent filter re-render reuses the already-glyph-decorated `<thead>` without rebuilding it, so `initCollapsableColumns()`'s own `th.textContent`-based column-name lookup permanently failed to match these columns by name, silently skipping their re-collapse step right after its own cleanup pass had already un-hidden every `<li>` table-wide. Fixed by switching that lookup to the already-existing, already-correct `_cleanColHeaderText()` helper (prefers the stable `th.dataset.colName` `makeTableSortableUnified()` stamped once, over a `textContent` re-derivation) — the same helper `_initColHeaderGlyph()` itself already relies on for its own idempotency check.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 9.99.813's "~ has name variation" filter never actually highlighted the matching `<span class="name-variation">` credit itself (e.g. "Nick Didia" on a release's "Recording engineer" column, or "Bruce Springsteen" on an artist's "Recording artists" column) — the checkbox correctly filtered rows but left no visual highlight on the matched name. Added `_highlightNameVariationMatch()` (mirrors `_highlightCreditValueMatch()`'s `attr:`/`task:` handling) and wired it into `testRowMatch()`'s structure-mode highlight pass. As a side effect this also fixes a multi-row cell's collapse toggle (▶N▤) never tinting to signal a hidden match when the matching name-variation credit was inside a COLLAPSED list — the existing `_COLLAPSE_MATCH_SEL`-based hidden-match signalling already looks for `.mb-column-filter-highlight` spans, it just had none to find until this fix started producing them.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-values dropdown (📊): "Cell structure" entries (empty/single/collapsed/expanded/any multi-row cell state, title/name-variation flags, per-attribute/per-task credit-role values, and addCAA/addEAA inline-artwork presence) now get the same ☑/☐ multi-select checkbox behavior as regular value rows — checking one no longer closes the dropdown, and multiple "Cell structure" entries (and regular values) can be OR'd together within a column. Internally this folds the old single-select `dataset.mbMultirowMode`/`applyMultiRowStateFilter()` mechanism entirely into the existing checkbox mechanism via a new `MB_UNIQ_STRUCTURE_MODE_PREFIX` sentinel and shared `_cellMatchesStructureMode()` matcher — the legacy mechanism is fully removed, not left as dead code.
Unique-values dropdown: the column-header 📊 button's tooltip now mentions when that column also has a "Cell structure" section available to filter by.

Unique-values dropdown: entries with a glyph/icon (entity-type marker, flag/area icon, ▤ item marker on regular value rows; ▶/◀/✗/✓/≠/~/🖼️/∅ symbols on "Cell structure" entries) now explain that glyph's meaning in their hover tooltip — previously several of these glyphs (entity-type markers especially) had no explanation anywhere in the script.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: 'release-tracks': swapped which icon 9.99.809's live-recording date check uses for each case, per explicit correction — a credit with NO date attribute at all now gets "⚠️" (was "❌"), and a credit whose date attribute DIFFERS from "Recording date" now gets "❌" (was "⚠️"). Only `_liveDateCheckResult()`'s two icon literals changed; the underlying missing-vs-mismatch detection logic, tooltips' wording, and the 9.99.810/9.99.811 WARNING/ERROR summary buttons (which just tally whichever icon is present) are all unaffected.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': 9.99.810's WARNING/ERROR summary buttons never appeared even when ⚠️/❌ icons were genuinely present on the page (e.g. real "Recording engineer" errors on /release/abc6ad0c-2e02-4141-8275-6943b3553dbf — see debug/h2.html) — both buttons existed in the DOM but stayed permanently empty and hidden. Root cause: `_updateLiveDateFlagButtons()` was only ever called from inside `updateFilterButtonsVisibility()`, and every one of that function's call sites is interaction-driven (`runFilter()`, editing a sub-table filter, "Load from Disk") — none of them fire on a plain initial page load with no user interaction, so the buttons were never populated after the first (and typically only) render. Fixed by also calling `updateFilterButtonsVisibility()` from the tail of `finalCleanup()` — the one page-type-agnostic function already called unconditionally once the initial render (single- or multi-table) is fully complete, as well as after disk-load. Also added `Lib.debug('filter', …)` logging to `_countLiveDateFlags()`/`_updateLiveDateFlagButtons()`/`_applyLiveDateFlagFilter()` to make any future issue in this area easier to diagnose.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': two new buttons in the "Tracklist" header, right before the global filter box — "(N) WARNING ⚠️" and "(N) ERROR ❌" — each only shown when at least one matching icon (from 9.99.809's live-recording date check) exists on the page. Their tooltip breaks the count down by column (e.g. "Vocals (2), Recording engineer (1)"). Clicking one clears every other active filter and shows only the rows containing that icon, reusing the existing global filter/"Clear all filters"/status-display machinery, so clearing back to all rows works exactly as it already does for any other filter.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': for a live-recording track ("Recording of work" carries the "live" attribute) with a known "Recording date", each entity credited in "Recording engineer", "Vocals", "Instruments", "Recorded at event", and "Recorded at place" now gets a small ⚠️/❌ icon (native tooltip) whenever its own date attribute doesn't exactly match "Recording date": ⚠️ when it has a date but it differs (may be from a different performance), ❌ when it has no date attribute at all. Comparison is an exact string match, with no leniency for differing date precision. Deliberately excludes "Engineer"/"Producer"/"Mixer"/"Miscellaneous support"/"Performer"/"Produced for label"/"Mixed at place". New setting: "Flag live-recording credit dates that don't match 'Recording date'" (default on), depends on the existing "Recording of"/"Recorded at"/"Recorded in"/"Mixed at" columns setting for the "Recording date" data itself.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed the "Recorded in area" column header, and any area-typed entry in the 📊 unique-values dropdown (e.g. "Manhattan"/"New York" inside "Recorded in area"'s dropdown), silently rendering with no area icon at all — despite the correct `` marker genuinely being present in the DOM with MusicBrainz's own real background-image glyph correctly resolved (confirmed live via DevTools Computed panel: `background-image` resolved to the actual icon, but `display: none` won). Root-caused via a live DevTools Styles-panel walk (with the user) to a real, currently-installed third-party userscript's own injected stylesheet: `span.arealink:empty, a[href*="/area/"] > span.arealink:empty { display: none !important; }` — that script (a "More Flags Everywhere"-style enhancement) deliberately hides MusicBrainz's generic native area icon whenever the marker span is EMPTY, since it normally replaces it with a real per-area flag `` (which, once inserted as a child, makes the span no longer `:empty` and the rule stops applying). Our own glyph spans — both the column-header one (`_initColHeaderGlyph`) and the unique-values dropdown's generic per-entity-type marker (`_findCellEntityRefs`'s `glyphClass`, rendered in the dropdown's item-building loop) — are always genuinely empty (a header or a generic "this entity is an area" marker has no specific area to show a flag FOR), so they matched `:empty` too and got `!important`-hidden right along with the fallback icon they were never meant to suppress. MusicBrainz's own CSS was never the problem — confirmed via a separately-downloaded, unminified `mb-icons.css`: `.arealink`'s own rule is a plain, unscoped `background-image`, identical in shape/specificity to the already-working `.placelink`/`.eventlink`/`.worklink`/etc.

New shared `_guardGlyphAgainstEmptySelectorHiding(glyphSpan)` appends a zero-width space (`\u200B`) text node to any glyph span we create/clone ourselves — a text node with `data.length === 1` does not satisfy the CSS `:empty` pseudo-class's own spec definition ("no children, or only comment/processing-instruction nodes and zero-LENGTH text nodes"), so this reliably defeats the third-party selector while staying visually invisible. Called from both `_initColHeaderGlyph()` and the dropdown's entity-marker builder. Applied to every glyph class unconditionally (not just `arealink`, the only one currently affected) since it's cheap and harmless — a pure no-op for users without that userscript installed, since MusicBrainz's own CSS never keys off `:empty` at all — and future-proofs against the same third-party treatment being extended to other entity-type classes later.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed "Recorded at event" silently dropping its own trailing date attribute — e.g. the anchor text already spells out "1988‐04‐27: Los Angeles Memorial Sports Arena, Los Angeles, CA, USA", but the separate trailing " (1988-04-27)" sibling text right after the anchor (confirmed in `debug/double-ars.html`) was never read at all, only the anchor itself. Now found and appended the same way "Recording of"/"Recorded at place" already handle their own trailing parentheticals.

Fixed "Recorded at place" silently dropping an ENTIRE second place — reported live against https://musicbrainz.org/release/52c6808b-037d-47d5-b0c7-17331c9d36cd: a track with a separate "additionally recorded at: The Hit Factory…" `<dt>` AND a separate "recorded at: Thrill Hill East…" `<dt>` (two different studios during the same recording — NOT two places joined inside one `<dd>`, which was already handled) only ever showed the first. Root cause: `_findRecordedAtDt` used a first-match-only `.find()`, exactly the same bug class already fixed once for "Phonographic copyright (℗) by:" (see 9.99.783) but never applied here. `_findRecordedAtDt`/`_findMixedAtDt` are now `.filter()`-based, returning every matching `<dt>`; `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd` now accepts and merges the whole array into one cell, checking each source `<dt>`'s own "additionally recorded at:" wording independently (so a merged cell can correctly show "(additional)" on one dt's places but not another's).

Fixed "Recorded at place" (and, since it shares the same builder, "Mixed at place" — 9.99.805) unconditionally DROPPING its own trailing date attribute (e.g. "(from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03)", "(on 1988-04-27)") — this was deliberate for the ORIGINAL "Recorded at place"-only design (no per-place date context existed), but is wrong now that dates are expected here too (see "Recorded in area", 9.99.805, which already keeps its own trailing date). The date is now extracted from each source `<dt>`'s `<dd>` and re-appended AFTER the "(additional)" marker on every place `<li>` that `<dt>` produces, e.g. "The Hit Factory in Manhattan, … United States (additional) (from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03)" — matching the requested format exactly.

Fixed the 📊 unique-values dropdown's flag-icon decoration (9.99.785) not covering the new "Mixed at place" column (9.99.805) — it shares the exact same `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd`-built `<span class="area-icon">`/`<span class="flag flag-XX">` shapes as "Recorded at place", so — like that column — this was purely a missing name-recognition entry in the dropdown's column allow-list, no new scan logic needed. "Recorded in area" needed no equivalent fix — its name already matches the allow-list's generic `endsWith('rea')` check.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed the "Vocals"/"Instruments" columns (9.99.802) silently dropping a credited artist's own trailing date attribute — e.g. "Bruce Springsteen (on 2002-08-29)"/"Toby Scott (from 1987-01-20 until 1987-03)" (confirmed against real data in `debug/therising.html`/`debug/double-ars.html`) rendered as just the bare artist name, date gone — spotted by comparing against a dynamic-fallback column ("Creative direction") built via `_buildKindSplitListTd`'s blanket-clone-the-whole-`<dd>` approach, which had ALREADY been preserving trailing dates correctly the whole time, unlike `_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem`'s selective artist-anchor-plus-known-annotations extraction, which never looked for one. `_buildInstrumentVocalsListItem` now also calls the existing `_findCreditSegmentTextAnnotation` (the same free-text-parenthetical fallback "Miscellaneous support"/bare-role CREDIT_ROLES columns already use for their own annotations) and merges its result into the SAME trailing parenthetical as the attribute words, comma-separated — e.g. "Jane Doe (guest/background, on 2002-08-29)" — mirroring `_buildCreditListItem`'s identical grouping. Deliberately NOT applied to the CREDIT_ROLES columns themselves (9.99.773 already established they drop trailing dates on purpose, and no regression was reported there).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed the dynamic-fallback AR-column machinery (9.99.804) fragmenting a single place/area "chain" credit into multiple columns and/or multiple rows — reported live: "Mixed at place"/"Mixed at area" split "A&M Studios in Hollywood" into two separate columns instead of one (`<span class="placelink">`+`<span class="arealink">` both appearing as direct children of the same `<dd>`, per real markup — `_collectEntityKinds` correctly detected BOTH kinds present, but `_buildKindSplitListTd`'s marker-boundary check unconditionally treated ANY of `KNOWN_ENTITY_LINK_KINDS`'s 7 classes as a segment boundary, regardless of what the caller actually asked to split by), and "Recorded in" showed only "Asbury Park" instead of the full "Asbury Park, New Jersey, United States (on 2002-09-20)" chain (an area's OWN parent-area ancestry legitimately reuses the SAME `arealink` marker class repeatedly — a fundamentally different shape from place-vs-area, where marker-KIND alone can no longer distinguish "the credited target" from "its own decoration"). New `PEER_SPLIT_KINDS` (`['artist', 'label']` — the only two kinds ever proven to have genuine multiple-PEER-entity semantics, e.g. `_buildPhonographicCopyrightTds`'s mixed artist+label case) restricts `_buildKindSplitListTd`'s boundary detection to markers the CALLER's own `kinds` parameter actually requested — any other recognized-but-unrequested kind marker is now left as ordinary content instead of fragmenting the segment. The dynamic-fallback discovery scan now filters its collected kinds through `_filterPeerKinds` before ever calling `_splitColumnByEntityKind`/`_buildKindSplitListTd`, so a place/event/work/area/series-shaped role safely falls back to `_buildKindSplitListTd`'s existing `kinds.size === 0` "clone whole `<dd>` verbatim, one row" behavior — never fragments — protecting any FUTURE unknown relationship shaped this way, not just the two observed cases.

Added "Mixed at place" (new `_findMixedAtDt`, reusing `_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd` as-is — same place-primary/area-decoration shape as the existing "Recorded at place") and "Recorded in area" (new `_findRecordedInDt`/`_buildRecordedInAreaTd` — cardinality-1 per MusicBrainz's own relationship-type metadata, so no segmentation is attempted at all: only the very first `arealink` marker is dropped, everything else — the full ancestor-area chain, flags, AND the trailing date — is cloned verbatim into one row) as their own DEDICATED fixed handlers rather than relying on the generic dynamic-fallback path, so they get exactly the chain-preserving treatment "Recorded at place" already has. `_dtMatchesAnyFixedHandler`/`_classifyArDt` updated to recognize both (plus a bare "performer:" — see the Feature entry below) so none of the three can be shadowed by a duplicate auto-discovered dynamic column.

Wired up the missing column-header relationship glyph icons (`_initColHeaderGlyph`) for "Instruments"/"Vocals"/"Performer" (all `artistlink`), "Recorded in area" (`arealink`), and "Mixed at place" (`placelink`) — these five new/9.99.802 columns never got the same post-render glyph re-injection every other release-tracks AR column already receives from `renderGroupedTable()`'s tail, so their headers showed no icon at all (confirmed via a side-by-side screenshot comparison against "Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/etc., which do). New `_glyphClassForDynamicColumn`/`def.features._dynamicArColumnGlyphs` runtime registration (mirroring the existing runtime `collapsableColumns` registration mechanism) extends the same glyph re-injection to dynamically-discovered fallback columns too, whenever exactly one entity kind is present for that role.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': added a dedicated "Performer" column (each track's bare "performer:" relationship, via the existing `_findCreditDts`/`_buildCreditListTd` machinery, no attribute-word prefix), positioned before "Vocals"/"Instruments" rather than lumped in with the CREDIT_ROLES columns — its own gate/setting reuses `sa_enable_release_tracks_credit_role_columns`.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: 'release-tracks': reordered the release-tracks AR columns to the requested final sequence: Recording of work, Recording date, Recorded at event, Recorded at place, Recorded in area, Performer, Vocals, Instruments, Recording engineer, Engineer, Producer, Mixer, Miscellaneous support, Mixed at place, Phonographic copyright (℗) by artist/label, Produced for label, [dynamic-fallback columns], ARs — swapping Vocals before Instruments (previously Instruments-then-Vocals), and reordering `CREDIT_ROLES` to Recording engineer/Engineer/Producer/Mixer/Miscellaneous support (previously …/Mixer/Engineer/Producer/…) so "Mixer" sits immediately before the new "Mixed at place". The whole header-insertion block now computes its shared "ARs" `<th>` reference ONCE (`_arsHeaderRef`) instead of four separate, identically-computed copies — the final column order is simply the order the insertion blocks now run in, following this same shared reference throughout.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': every AR relationship type not already covered by a dedicated column (Recording of/date, Recorded at event/place, the credit-role columns, Phonographic copyright, Produced for label, Instruments/Vocals — 9.99.801-803) now gets its own auto-discovered column instead of only ever surfacing as raw text inside "ARs" — e.g. "Conductor", "Publisher", "Mixed at", "Lyricist and composer", "Creative direction", "Shot at", "Version of", "Concertmaster" (all observed in `debug/therising.html`/`debug/double-ars.html`), and any relationship type MusicBrainz adds in the future, with zero code changes needed. New `_classifyArDt(dt)` is the single source of truth for what kind of relationship a given `<dt>` is — checked in priority order: an already-handled fixed column (`_dtMatchesAnyFixedHandler`, covering everything above via the same `roleWords`/`_creditDtMatch` machinery those columns already use, plus the "recording of:"/"recorded at:" text+glyph checks), then Instruments/Vocals (`_parseInstrumentVocalsDt`), then the dynamic fallback — used by both the page-wide discovery scan and the per-row `<td>` builder so the two always agree. A page-wide scan (mirroring the existing `_pageHasCopyrightByArtist`-style gates) buckets every track's unclaimed `<dt>`s into a `Map<key, {displayName, kinds}>` keyed on the relationship's own literal phrase text (lowercased, trailing ":" stripped) — so e.g. "strings arranger:" and "cello arranger:" become two distinct columns, never merged, matching the confirmed keying decision — with the display name sentence-cased from the same text. Map insertion order (first-encountered-in-page) becomes the final left-to-right column order, inserted as a block right after "Produced for label", before "ARs": reading order becomes curated specific columns → auto-discovered generic columns → full raw ARs. Each discovered column can itself split by entity kind via the 9.99.803 `_splitColumnByEntityKind`/`_buildKindSplitListTd` machinery (e.g. a hypothetical role crediting both an artist and a place on the same release). Gated by a new dedicated setting, `sa_enable_release_tracks_dynamic_ar_columns` (default on), independent of every other release-tracks column setting, since this is the most exploratory/unpredictable piece of the feature. Dynamically-discovered column names are pushed into `def.features.collapsableColumns` at creation time (dedup-guarded) rather than pre-declared in the page definition, since `initCollapsableColumns()` only matches by exact header-text string and the set of names isn't known at authoring time — `def` is the same object as `activeDefinition`, so this registration is visible by the time `initCollapsableColumns()` actually runs. Verified via a standalone jsdom-free unit test covering every previously-unhandled phrase above, plus regression checks confirming "live recording of:", "assistant engineer:", "producer and mixer:", "phonographic copyright (℗) by:", and "produced for:" all still classify as already-fixed (never shadowed by a duplicate dynamic column), and that a "strings arranger:" `<dt>` — rejected by the Instruments parser (9.99.802) specifically because "arranger" isn't a recognized attribute word — correctly falls through to become its own "Strings arranger" dynamic column instead of silently vanishing.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Generalized the "Phonographic copyright (℗) by artist"/"…by label" column-name-uniqueness pattern (the ONLY place this file previously disambiguated a relationship's column name by target entity kind) into reusable machinery, in preparation for the dynamic-fallback AR columns (9.99.804), which need the identical rule applied to an unbounded, unknown-in-advance set of relationship types. New `KNOWN_ENTITY_LINK_KINDS` (`artist`/`label`/`place`/`event`/`work`/`area`/`series` — every native MusicBrainz `<span class="{kind}link">` marker class confirmed present in `dl.ars` credit data) backs `_collectEntityKinds(dd)`/`_collectEntityKindsAcrossDts(dts)` (which entity kinds does a `<dd>`, or set of `<dt>`s, actually credit), `_splitColumnByEntityKind(baseColumnName, kinds)` (decides the final column name(s) — unchanged when `kinds.size <= 1`, one `` `${base} ${kind}` `` per kind otherwise), and `_buildKindSplitListTd(dts, kinds)` (generalizes the original 2-hardcoded-marker `<dd>` segmentation to any number of kinds at once, always returning a `<td>` for every EXPECTED kind — even one that happens to be empty on a particular row — so a caller iterating a fixed column set never gets a missing entry; a `kinds.size === 0` "no recognized marker at all" case, not seen in real data, falls back to cloning each `<dd>` verbatim rather than attempting to parse sub-pieces, same philosophy as `_buildLabelCreditListTd`). `_phonographicCopyrightHasKind`/`_buildPhonographicCopyrightTds` are now thin wrappers over the general functions (unconditionally split by `{artist, label}`, preserving this pair's existing independently-gated-columns behavior exactly), and the two header strings are re-derived from `_splitColumnByEntityKind('Phonographic copyright (℗) by', new Set(['artist', 'label']))` instead of being separately hardcoded, so there is exactly one implementation of the naming rule left. Verified byte-identical output against the original two-hardcoded-marker version via a standalone unit test covering `debug/double-ars.html`'s two-separate-dt/dd (artist then label) shape and a `debug/copyright.html`-style single-`<dd>`-with-3-labels shape.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
'release-tracks': added shared "Instruments" and "Vocals" columns, extracted from each track's instrument (e.g. "cello:", "harmonium, tabla and vocals:") and vocals (e.g. "vocals:", "lead vocals:", "guest background vocals:") relationship data (`debug/therising.html`) — previously only ever visible as raw text inside "ARs". New `_parseInstrumentVocalsDt(dt)` splits a `
`'s child-node stream into components at ","/"and" TEXT-node boundaries (an instrument `` is never itself a boundary, since a component can embed one), classifying each component as either an instrument credit (at most one instrument anchor, every other word a recognized attribute — Additional/Guest/Solo/Lead/Background/Spoken/Choir) or a vocals credit (last word exactly "vocals", every word before it a recognized attribute) — a single unrecognized word anywhere rejects the WHOLE `
`, not just that component, which is what correctly keeps a non-credit phrase like `
strings arranger:
` (real data) OUT of "Instruments": "arranger" isn't a recognized attribute word, so the whole `
` is left unclaimed for the dynamic-fallback classifier (9.99.804) to pick up as its own "Strings arranger" column instead. A combined credit crediting an artist with both an instrument and vocals in one relationship (e.g. "harmonium, tabla and vocals:", confirmed in `debug/therising.html`'s Asif Ali Khan and Group example) is split across both columns for the same artist rather than creating a third "combined" column. Every distinct instrument shares the ONE "Instruments" column (not one column per instrument) and every vocals variant shares the ONE "Vocals" column, each attribute word rendering inline after the artist's name via the same `.mb-credit-attr` sentinel convention every `CREDIT_ROLES` column already uses (9.99.780), so the unique-values dropdown's per-attribute filter entries (9.99.788) work identically here for free. An optional trailing `[altName]` bracket (MusicBrainz's own credited-as alternate instrument/vocal-type name, e.g. "baritone saxophone [baritone sax]") is captured per component and appended after the artist's entry. Positioned as their own block between "Recorded at place" and the `CREDIT_ROLES` columns (instrumentalists/vocalists read before production credits, matching typical liner-note ordering), gated by a new dedicated setting `sa_enable_release_tracks_instrument_vocal_columns` (default on), independent of the existing credit-role columns setting. Verified against 14 real-markup shapes captured from `debug/therising.html` via a standalone unit test, including the multi-instrument "guest harmonium, guest tabla and guest vocals:" case and the bracketed-alt-name "bell [orchestra bells] and glockenspiel:" case, plus regression checks confirming "strings arranger:"/"producer and mixer:"/"recording engineer:"/"phonographic copyright (℗) by:" are all correctly rejected by this parser.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Extracted the "find this track's bare `div.ars` (the sibling with no `AcoustID…`/`ISRC…`-prefixed class), then its direct-child `<dt>`s" lookup — duplicated verbatim across `_findRecOfDt`, `_findRecordedAtDt`, `_findPhonographicCopyrightDts`, and `_findCreditDts` — into two shared helpers, `_findBareArsDiv(titleTd)` and `_findAllArDts(titleTd)`, and rewired all four onto them with zero behavior change. Also extracted `_findCreditDts`'s per-`<dt>` role-matching body (component-splitting on ","/"and", strict attribute-word-prefix check) into a standalone `_creditDtMatch(dt, roleWords, attributeVocab)`, usable against one already-in-hand `<dt>` without re-scanning `titleTd` from scratch. Prerequisite refactor for the Instruments/Vocals (9.99.802) and dynamic-fallback (9.99.804) AR-column work — both need to walk EVERY `<dt>` on a track exactly once, classify it, and only fall back to the fixed extractors' own matching rules (via `_creditDtMatch`) for already-handled roles, rather than duplicating this lookup a fifth and sixth time.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown now offers a fourth entry category: one checkbox per distinct MusicBrainz ENTITY REFERENCE (work/place/area — including country, which MusicBrainz models as just another area — artist/label/event) found anywhere inside a cell, marked with that entity type's own MB glyph (`worklink`/`placelink`/`arealink`/`artistlink`/`labellink`/`eventlink` — the same classes `_initColHeaderGlyph()` already reuses for release-tracks column headers). Generalizes well beyond the "▤" per-`<li>`-item feature (9.99.799): it applies to ANY cell — list or not — and surfaces sub-parts of a single value, e.g. "Recorded at place" (`debug/expand.html`, `/release/52c6808b-037d-47d5-b0c7-17331c9d36cd`): "The Hit Factory in Manhattan, New York, New York, United States (from … until …) (additional)" now offers the place, each area, AND the country as five INDEPENDENTLY selectable/filterable/highlightable entries, instead of only the one giant flattened string. "Recording engineer"/"Phonographic copyright (℗) by artist" similarly offer the bare credited artist's name (e.g. "Toby Scott", "Bruce Springsteen"), letting a filter match regardless of the trailing date range/year annotation. Keyed by the entity's own href/MBID (`MB_UNIQ_ENTITY_HREF_PREFIX`, sibling to 9.99.799's `MB_UNIQ_ITEM_VALUE_PREFIX` in the same `dataset.mbUniqValues` checked-value set) rather than by display text — required for correctness, since the same entity can legitimately render under different alias text (a name-variation credit) and two different entities can otherwise share the same display text.

New shared `_findCellEntityRefs(cell)` (single source of truth for collection, matching, AND highlighting — unlike a naive implementation, this avoids three separate re-implementations of the same DOM-walk) finds every ``+`` pair in a cell, in EITHER nesting direction (`…`, the common case, or `…`, MusicBrainz's plain native "Artist" column). Deliberately never requires a glyph span to be present for detection: this script's own cell builders strip the glyph from a column's own PRIMARY entity (already shown once in the column header), so `href`+`` is the only reliable signal — confirmed against `debug/expand.html`'s real markup, where "Recorded at place"'s country entity uses a THIRD, different glyph shape again (`` WRAPPING the anchor, vs. every other area's plain empty SIBLING ``).

An entity only gets offered as its own entry when it's part of something bigger than just its own name in at least one occurrence (`ref.isBare`, computed by comparing the nearest containing `<li>`/cell's cleaned text against the bare entity name) — replaces any raw row-count threshold, and for free correctly skips a column whose cell is ALWAYS just the bare entity (e.g. "Recording of work"'s non-list cell, or MusicBrainz's plain `<bdi><a>` "Artist" column — both would otherwise just duplicate the existing whole-cell entry with an identical row-set) while still offering one for every entity in a chain or with a trailing annotation. `testRowMatch()`'s value-set filter gains a third, href-membership fallback (`f.hasEntityValues`, mirroring 9.99.799's item-membership fallback's cheap-phase-1/expensive-phase-2 shape) attempted only after the cheaper whole-cell and item checks both miss. Checking an entity entry highlights ONLY its resolved name node (e.g. just "United States", never "Manhattan"/"New York"/"The Hit Factory" in the same chain) via the existing `_buildFuzzyTextMatchRegex()`/`highlightCrossTag()` — reused as-is, no new fuzzy-matching logic needed. Verified end-to-end in an isolated jsdom harness against `debug/expand.html`'s real "Recorded at place" chain, confirming exactly one entity (the checked one) gets highlighted out of five in the same `<li>`, plus a full re-run of every 9.99.799 regression case to confirm the `combinedVals`/`renderItems()` restructuring (now a 4-way merge: whole-cell / item / entity) introduces no regressions.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: The 📊 unique-values dropdown now offers each unique `<li>` item's own text as a separate checkbox entry (marked with a "▤" glyph) for multi-row (≥2-item) list-cell columns, e.g. "Engineer" (`debug/multi-row-cell.html`: "Billy Bowers (US engineer) (additional)" and "Karl Egsieker (task: Second Engineer)" now each get their own entry, alongside the existing merged whole-cell value) — lets you filter to just the rows crediting one specific person even when they usually appear alongside others in a merged cell. Multi-select, OR'd, panel stays open — same interaction as today's plain values; item entries are stored in the same `dataset.mbUniqValues` checked-value set as whole-cell values, distinguished by a reserved-prefix encoding (`MB_UNIQ_ITEM_VALUE_PREFIX`) so no new dataset attribute or restore-on-reopen plumbing was needed. Scoped purely structurally (`_findCellListItems(cell).length >= 2`, the same threshold `_classifyCollapseCell()`'s own "isMultiRow" already uses) rather than to any specific column list, so it works generically on every list-cell column, not just credit-role ones — and correctly excludes single-item cells (whose one item is already the existing whole-cell entry) and Annotation/prose cells (no `<li>`s at all). `testRowMatch()`'s value-set filter falls back to per-`<li>` membership testing only when a checked item entry is actually present, so ordinary whole-cell filters pay zero extra cost.

Checking an item entry highlights the exact matching `<li>` (unlike whole-cell value matches, which are deliberately never highlighted). Building this exposed a real, previously-latent bug: `getCleanColumnText()` (used to compute the checkable value) normalizes whitespace across DOM-node boundaries and strips paren-adjacent spaces, while `highlightCrossTag()` (used to paint the highlight) matches against the RAW, un-normalized text — for any value spanning more than one element (which every credit `<li>` does: artist `<a>`, `<span class="comment">`, `<span class="mb-credit-attr">`/`<i class="mb-credit-task">` are all separate nodes), a literal escaped-string regex silently failed to match at all. New `_buildFuzzyTextMatchRegex()` reverses `getCleanColumnText()`'s specific whitespace/paren-space transformations into a tolerant regex so cross-node highlighting actually lands. Confirmed against the real Karl Egsieker `<li>` in an isolated jsdom harness — its raw DOM text is `"Karl Egsieker
	 (
      task: Second Engineer
      )
    "`, nothing like the cleaned, single-spaced value a naive literal-match regex would have required.

Fixed a second, harder case of the same cross-node-highlight problem, reported live: "Roger Talkov (engineer) (assistant)" checked and correctly filtering, but rendering with zero highlight anywhere in the `
  • ` (a sibling "Tim Leitner (assistant)" entry in the same cell highlighted fine). Root cause: the first fix's regex used `\s+` (one-or-more) for each normalized space, assuming a real raw whitespace character always exists at that boundary — but `…Roger Talkov (engineer)` connects the artist name to its disambiguation comment via an ISOLATED ` ` text node, which `.trim()`s to empty (non-breaking space IS whitespace) and is therefore entirely `FILTER_REJECT`ed by `highlightCrossTag()`'s own walker — contributing ZERO characters to the raw text being matched, not even one whitespace char, so the mandatory `\s+` failed outright. `_buildFuzzyTextMatchRegex()` now uses `\s*` (zero-or-more) for every normalized space instead, correctly covering both "real whitespace bridges this gap" and "the only bridging node was itself whitespace-only and vanished entirely". Verified against the actual live DOM captured from https://musicbrainz.org/release/52c6808b-037d-47d5-b0c7-17331c9d36cd's Engineer column, plus a full re-run of every earlier regression case (Billy Bowers/Karl Egsieker, both checked simultaneously) to confirm no loss of precision from the looser `\s*`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: 'release-tracks': added a "Streaming/Downloads" column, right after "ARs" (before AcoustIDs/ISRCs), sourced from the third-party "MB: Inline per-recording streaming & download links" userscript's own `<dl class="ar">` container it glues into the Title cell — one `<li>` per site (glyph + name + link, e.g. "🟢 open.spotify.com: [free streaming]"), a collapsable multi-row list when more than one site is present (`debug/streaming-downloads.html`). The userscript's own collapsed/expanded toggle state at scrape time (`<dd style="display:none">`, `debug/streaming.html`) is irrelevant — only the content is read. Same page-wide-decision reasoning as "Video"/"Disambiguation"/"Recording artist": only added once ANY track on the release actually has a link (`_pageHasStreaming`, keyed on the `<dd>` having at least one `<a>`, not on string-matching the userscript's own empty-state sentence) — a release with the userscript not installed, or that found nothing anywhere, gets zero overhead and no column at all. When only SOME tracks have data, tracks with the userscript's own "No streaming or download links found." state (`debug/streaming-downloads-empty.html`) just render an empty cell, same as any other page-wide-gated column.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed column/global filter highlighting silently never appearing on the "Length" column specifically (`debug/no-color.html`) — reproduced end-to-end in an isolated jsdom harness against the real extracted `testRowMatch()`/`highlightText()`/`highlightCrossTag()` code, which proved the highlight mechanism itself is correct; the wipe happens one step later. Root cause: jesus2099's "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL" userscript mutates the native Length `<td>` in place, setting `class="treleases"` (see `_repairTreleasesTd()`'s own JSDoc and `debug/tracklist-single-medium.html`, which shows this class co-occurring with jesus2099's own toolzone `<div>`s on a real page). The existing `'jesus2099-any'` columnEraser (9.99.759) already strips those nested toolzone/editbutt/openEdits `<div>`s from the Length column at scrape time, but never touched the `treleases` class living on the `<td>` itself — so it survived into this script's own captured row and every future `cloneNode(true)` copy of it. `runFilter()`'s multi-table path clones from that captured row on every keystroke and inserts the clone into a fresh `<tbody>`; `initTreleasesObserver()`'s `MutationObserver` cannot distinguish that routine self-triggered insertion from a genuine live jesus2099 mutation, so it fired `_repairTreleasesTd()` on our OWN freshly-highlighted cell — which rebuilds the cell from plain `textContent` (correctly preserving the visible "4:35" value and its numeric-alignment styling) but has no notion of the active filter, silently discarding the `mb-column-filter-highlight`/`mb-global-filter-highlight` `<span>` `testRowMatch()` had just added. Only the Length column is affected since it's the only column jesus2099 marks this way. Fixed by stripping `class="treleases"` (plus jesus2099's plugin `title`/inline `style`) from the cell in the SAME `'jesus2099-any'` eraser pass, once, at scrape time — this script's own rows are now permanently free of the marker, while `initTreleasesObserver()`/`_repairTreleasesTd()` still correctly react to and repair genuine future jesus2099 mutations on the live page, exactly as before.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Root-caused the "vzell" ISRC-filter injection via cross-browser testing with the user: reproduces on Chrome and Vivaldi, NOT on Firefox, Opera, or Brave — despite Opera/Brave also being Chromium-based, ruling out a generic engine quirk. Vivaldi is documented to license and use Google's own proprietary autofill/prediction backend (the same one Chrome uses); Brave and Opera implement their own independent autofill without it. Confirms this is Chrome's/Vivaldi's NATIVE, built-in credential-autofill — which has a long-standing, deliberate policy (crbug.com/468153) of ignoring `autocomplete="off"` for anything its heuristics decide looks like a login-form field, explaining why neither 9.99.795's `isTrusted` guard nor `autocomplete="off"` stopped it (both target other mechanisms — synthetic JS-dispatched events and the browser's separate form-field-history feature — not this).

Rewrote `_hardenFilterInputAgainstPasswordManagers()` into `_hardenFilterInputAgainstAutofill()`, adding two techniques specifically documented to defeat Chrome's own native credential-autofill (neither of which respects `autocomplete="off"`): (1) `type="search"` instead of `text` — Chrome's credential heuristic keys off `text`/`email`-type inputs, not `search`-type ones (also more semantically correct for a filter box); new CSS neutralizes the resulting native search-input chrome (rounded corners, native ✕ button) so the visual appearance is unchanged. (2) The field starts `readonly` and only becomes editable on a genuinely trusted `mousedown`/`focus` (gated on `event.isTrusted`, so it can't be defeated by a script/autofill mechanism synthetically dispatching those events either) — Chrome generally will not attempt to autofill a `readonly` field. The global filter's own auto-focus-after-render code (a PROGRAMMATIC, untrusted focus) now explicitly clears `.readOnly` itself right before focusing, since the trusted-only guard would otherwise leave it readonly (blocking the user's very next keystroke) until a second, real interaction. **Confirmed fixed by the user** on the real Chrome session that reproduced the bug.

'release-tracks': the yomo widget is still hidden (not removed, per 9.99.794's revision) as a first layer of defense, though the newly-confirmed native-Chrome-autofill root cause means the widget's presence/absence was likely never the actual determining factor — kept regardless since it's still a reasonable, low-risk step and satisfies keeping the widget off the final rendered page.

The `readonly`-until-interaction trick (above) has a visible side effect: Chrome/Vivaldi paint their own default grey background on any `:read-only` input, so every column filter looked greyed-out until clicked at least once (reported by the user with a screenshot right after confirming the main fix). Added a `:read-only { background-color: #fff; }` CSS override for all three filter input types — lower specificity than the yellow `sa_col_filter_active_bg` inline style applied when a filter actually has a value, so an active filter still shows its yellow highlight correctly; only the idle/empty appearance was affected.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Found the REAL cause of the "tracklist not rendering with 'Batch Add Recording Aliases' active" report (9.99.794's widget removal, while still worth keeping, was not actually the fix): the "ISRCs" column filter was silently getting populated with the user's own MusicBrainz username ("vzell") the moment that other userscript activates, filtering every row out — the table WAS rendering, just with 0 visible rows after an unwanted filter, which looks identical to "nothing rendered" at a glance. Confirmed via a real browser console capture (`debug/fail.debug`): our own filter machinery logged `Column filter updated on column 19: "vzell"` — a legitimate-looking filter update, not a crash. No Chrome-style yellow `-webkit-autofill` highlight was visible on the field, ruling out Chrome's OWN native credential autofill specifically (that highlight is painted unconditionally via a UA stylesheet no page CSS can suppress) — but not third-party password-manager browser extensions, which insert values through their own content-script logic and don't necessarily show that highlight.

Hardened all three filter input types (global filter, per-column filter, per-sub-table filter) against exactly this class of interference, three layers deep: (1) their 'input' listeners now reject any event that is neither genuinely user-triggered (`event.isTrusted`, true only for real keystrokes/paste and for events some password-manager extensions and techniques like `document.execCommand('insertText', ...)` produce — impossible to spoof via a bare JS `dispatchEvent`) nor one of our own legitimate internal re-triggers (filter-history entries, "Clear ALL filters", a unique-values dropdown entry, the Unicode character picker — all of which now dispatch their synthetic 'input' events through a new shared `_dispatchInternalInputEvent()` helper that marks the event so it still passes) — any other 'input' event is dropped and the injected value discarded before it can silently activate as an active filter; (2) `autocomplete="off"` set on all three (none had it before); (3) the widely-recognized `data-lpignore`/`data-1p-ignore`/`data-bwignore`/`data-form-type="other"`/`data-protonpass-ignore` "leave this field alone" attributes (LastPass/1Password/Bitwarden/Dashlane/Proton Pass respectively) via a new shared `_hardenFilterInputAgainstPasswordManagers()` helper — these extensions frequently ignore `autocomplete="off"` on a target field by design (treating it as a common site-authoring mistake) but DO honor their own explicit opt-out markers.

Got the other userscript's actual source (`debug/other-userscript.js`) and confirmed it contains no code that reads/writes anything resembling a username, and never touches any element outside its own `#yomo-*` fields — ruling out its own JS as the direct writer. Revised theory: a password-manager extension targets `#yomo-src` (a fresh, unlabeled input that script adds near the top of the page) for autofill; 9.99.794's `_removeYomoRecordingAliasesWidget()` used to `.remove()` that whole widget outright, and if an extension's fill attempt against `#yomo-src` gets interrupted by its removal, some extensions retry against a new nearby candidate once their original target vanishes — which could land on our column filter. Changed the function to HIDE the widget (`display: none`, DOM nodes kept, not removed) instead of deleting it, so any pending fill can complete harmlessly against a field nobody reads, rather than being forced to look elsewhere. Unconfirmed against a live password-manager extension — still being diagnosed with the user.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': when the "Batch Add Recording Aliases from another Release" userscript (by YoGo9) is active, its widget (`#yomo-src`/`#yomo-preview`/`#yomo-table`/… controls) — injected as the FIRST CHILD of `div#content`, ahead of the native release header — is now detected via its distinctive `#yomo-preview` id and hidden (`display: none`, DOM nodes kept — see 9.99.795 for why not removed) as the very first release-tracks pre-processing step, before anything else touches the DOM. Keeps the widget off the final rendered page. A safe no-op when that userscript isn't installed. See `debug/other-userscript.html`/`debug/other-userscript.js` (the widget's markup/source) and `debug/tt2a.html` (a full page capture with it present).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed the h2 "Credits" section (native `<div id="bottom-credits">`) still rendering AFTER the Tracklist section on the final page instead of before it, despite 9.99.792's fix keeping its `<h3>` sub-headings intact. Root cause: `_relocateTrailingH2Sections()`'s whole-wrapper relocation (added in 9.99.792) walked the Credits `<h2>` up to the first ancestor that is a direct child of `#content` and inserted it before the Tracklist `<h2>` — but on a real release page both the Tracklist and Credits sections share a common native `<div class="tracklist-and-credits">` wrapper several levels below `#content` (see `debug/credits.html`), so that walk produced `<div class="tracklist-and-credits">` itself — an ANCESTOR of the Tracklist `<h2>` it was about to be inserted before — throwing a DOM `HierarchyRequestError` that the function's own try/catch silently swallowed, aborting relocation for every trailing section, not just Credits. Now finds the lowest common ancestor ("LCA") the candidate `<h2>` actually shares with the Tracklist `<h2>` (rather than assuming it's always `#content`) and reorders siblings within that LCA instead — `<div id="bottom-credits">` now correctly moves as one intact unit to sit immediately before the Tracklist section.

items:
'release-tracks': the native "Release"/"Release group" `

` sub-headings inside the h2 "Credits" section are now independently collapsible by clicking their text — each toggles only its own following content (`table.details` rows, the release-group cover-art bigbox) within its own `
`/`
`, independent of the other and of the outer `

Credits

` toggle. Tooltips are toggle-aware ("Click to collapse this section" / "Click to expand this section", updated live as the section's state changes) rather than a single static label. sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': fixed the h2 "Credits" section on the final rendered page losing its native "Release"/"Release group" `<h3>` sub-headings (everything else inside — `table.details`, the release-group cover-art bigbox — stayed intact). Root cause 1: `renderGroupedTable()`'s initial-render cleanup pass swept EVERY `<h3>` on the page (not just the script's own generated `h3.mb-toggle-h3` section headers) before rebuilding, so the two native `<h3>` inside `<div id="bottom-credits">` were being deleted outright; now skipped via a targeted `el.closest('#bottom-credits')` guard alongside the existing `span.worklink` exception.

'release-tracks': fixed `_relocateTrailingH2Sections()` (which moves the native "Credits" `<h2>` to sit before the main Tracklist `<h2>` on the final page) tearing apart `<div id="bottom-credits">` in the process — it walked the Credits `<h2>`'s own `nextSibling` chain assuming the h2 was a direct child of `#content`, but the h2 is actually nested one level inside `#bottom-credits`, so its "siblings" were really `#bottom-credits`'s own children (`div#release-relationships`/`div#release-group-relationships`), which got individually re-parented onto `#content`, abandoning `#bottom-credits` empty. Now detects when the candidate h2 isn't a direct child of `#content` and relocates its whole wrapper element as one intact unit instead. See `debug/credits-original.html` / `debug/credits-final.html`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'release-tracks': before scraping a release's tracklist, now detects whether native per-track relationship credits (Recording engineer/Mixer/Engineer/Producer/Miscellaneous support) are currently rendered inline vs. consolidated into one combined block at the bottom of the page (MusicBrainz's own `#toggle-credits` control in `<span id="medium-toolbox">`, read via its own button label — "Display credits at bottom" means already inline, "Display credits inline" means currently at bottom), and if at bottom, clicks the control and awaits its re-render (`MutationObserver` on the button, idle-settle + 5s hard-timeout fallback, same shape as the existing overflow-tracks loader) before any row extraction runs — otherwise each row's own `dl.ars` credit block is missing/incomplete and the credit columns silently under-populate. See `debug/toolbox.org`.

'release-tracks': the native `<span id="medium-toolbox">` (toggle-credits/expand-all-mediums/collapse-all-mediums controls) is now stripped from the final rendered page via the existing `removeSelectors` mechanism, alongside the two other native `h2.tracklist` controls already removed there — its buttons re-render inert once the page has been restructured.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Reverted "Recording of work"'s attribute words (Acappella/Cover/Demo/Instrumental/Karaoke/Live/Medley/Partial) and "Recorded at place"'s "additional" attribute from their own separate columns (a word-per-column loop, and a standalone "Additional" column respectively) to render INLINE instead — the same `.mb-credit-attr` sentinel convention every `CREDIT_ROLES` column ("Engineer"/"Mixer"/etc.) already uses, e.g. "Rave On (live)" in "Recording of work", "Some Venue (additional)" appended to every place row in "Recorded at place" when a single relationship credits more than one place. Since the unique-values dropdown's per-attribute synthetic filter entries (9.99.788) already scan `.mb-credit-attr` generically with no column-name gating, both columns get that filtering — and its matching-text highlight (9.99.789) — for free, with zero new dropdown code. No more separate attribute-word/"Additional" columns to page-wide-gate, so that whole scan (`_presentRecOfAttributes`/`_pageHasRecordedAtPlaceAdditional`) was also removed.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Rows matching one of the new per-attribute/per-task synthetic dropdown filters (9.99.788) now get the exact matched string highlighted in the same color as any other active column filter — e.g. clicking "additional" in the "Engineer" column's dropdown highlights just the word "additional" inside each matching credit's parenthetical, not the whole cell or the whole `<li>`. A merged multi-person credit with several different attribute/task values in one cell only highlights the specific credit(s) whose own value actually matched.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added two more synthetic entries to the unique-values dropdown's "Cell structure" block, this time dynamic per-distinct-value filters rather than fixed checks: one entry per unique credit attribute word (e.g. "additional", "assistant", "co", "executive") and one per unique task string (e.g. "task: Second Engineer") actually present anywhere in a credit-role column's visible cells — e.g. the "Engineer" column on https://musicbrainz.org/release/6d19588c-0305-4fb0-b687-d4b75a75c3fd (`debug/unique-attribute-task.html`). Clicking one filters straight to every row where that specific attribute or task is credited, without typing free text. Attribute-word entries cover every credit-role column ("Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/"Engineer"/"Producer"/"Miscellaneous support") and "Produced for label"; task-value entries cover the 5 credit-role columns only ("Produced for label" has no task concept). `_buildCreditListItem`/`_buildLabelCreditListTd` now wrap attribute-word text in a `<span class="mb-credit-attr">` sentinel (and stamp the existing task `<i>` with `mb-credit-task`) so these values are reliably distinguishable from other free text sharing the same parenthetical; both new entry families reuse the exact `dataset.mbMultirowMode` → `testRowMatch()` plumbing every other synthetic entry in this block already uses, via a colon-prefixed compound mode string (`"attr:additional"`, `"task:task: Second Engineer"`) rather than a parallel filter mechanism.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added two new synthetic entries to the unique-values dropdown's optional "Cell structure" block, for additional structural filtering beyond plain text-value matching: "≠ track/recording name" for the "Title" column, matching rows where a third-party userscript (e.g. jesus2099's) has flagged the displayed track title as different from the underlying recording name — detected via the literal "≠" character in the title-anchor's own tooltip (`title="track name: …\n≠rec. name: …"`), immune to exactly which third-party script produced it; and "~ has name variation" for ANY column, matching rows where at least one credited entity (artist, label, place, …) uses a MusicBrainz `<span class="name-variation">` — the same alias/differently-spelled name rendered with a dotted underline on the live page (e.g. "Nassau Coliseum" in "Recorded at place", "Andres Bermudezat" in "Engineer"). Both entries appear even on columns that aren't otherwise collapsable (e.g. "Title"), showing a "Cell structure" header only when more than one synthetic entry would actually appear, matching the existing single-entry "○ empty cells" convention.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "extracted column" header background (9.99.785) never actually appearing on release-tracks' AR-derived columns, despite being applied at `<th>`-creation time in `applyExtractTrackTitleData()`. Root cause: that function's `<th>`s are built during pre-processing against the NATIVE page's own table, BEFORE the real `table.tbl` this script renders even exists — only their text is scraped into the final header list, and those original DOM nodes are discarded, never reused, so styling them has no visible effect. This is the exact same underlying problem 9.99.783 already diagnosed and fixed for the header glyph icons (`_initColHeaderGlyph()`), just not recognized as the same class of bug at the time. New `_stampArColumnHeaderBg(columnName)` mirrors `_initColHeaderGlyph()`'s already-proven approach: a post-render, by-name lookup against the actual rendered `table.tbl`, called from `renderGroupedTable()`'s tail alongside the glyph re-injection calls.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Every column release-tracks extracts from the Title cell's "ARs" data ("ARs"/"AcoustIDs"/"ISRCs", the "Recording of work"/"Recorded at" family and its attribute columns, and the engineer/mixer/producer/copyright credit columns) now gets the same header background color a generic synthetic column gets on other page types (`mb-extracted-column` + the existing `sa_ui_thead_th_extracted_bg` setting, default a greenish grey) instead of looking identical to the page's own native columns. "Video"/"Disambiguation"/"Recording artist" are unaffected — they're extracted from other parts of the Title/Artist cells, not from `dl.ars`.

The 📊 unique-values dropdown's flag-icon decoration (`sa_enable_dropdown_flag_icons` setting, existing feature already covering Country/Area/Locality/Region/Location/Place/Country-Date columns) now also covers release-tracks' "Recorded at place" column — each dropdown entry gets the same region/country flag icons shown in the table cell itself. No new icon-scanning logic was needed: "Recorded at place" cells already use the identical ``/`` shapes the existing scan already recognizes; the column just needed to be added to the column-name allow-list.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
