items: Fixed the credit-role columns ("Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/"Engineer"/"Producer"/"Miscellaneous support") silently dropping a credited artist's `<span class="comment">` disambiguation note entirely — e.g. a name-variation-wrapped credit's "primary alias" cross-reference (`debug/artist-name-variation-and-primary-alias.html`: "Louis Lehav" crediting engineer, with a `(Louis Lahav)` note pointing at the artist's primary alias) rendered as just the bare name, with the note gone. `_findCreditSegmentTextAnnotation` only reads a segment's own TEXT nodes, but this note's parenthesis characters live inside the `<span class="comment">` element itself, not as sibling text, so it was invisible to that lookup. New `_findCreditSegmentCommentSpan` finds this element (also covers a plain artist disambiguation with no name-variation, e.g. "Clarence Clemons (American saxophonist)") and clones it verbatim right after the artist anchor, independent of the existing attribute/instrument/task parenthetical.

Fixed a name-variation-wrapped credit (e.g. "Louis Lehav" above) losing its underline styling once extracted, even though the text/link itself was already correct — MusicBrainz underlines a `<span class="name-variation">`-wrapped credit via that span's own CSS class, to visually flag it as an alias rather than the artist's primary name, but the credit-role columns only ever cloned the bare `<a>` inside it, discarding the wrapper. `_buildCreditListItem` ("Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/"Engineer"/"Producer"/"Miscellaneous support") and the "Recorded at event" cell builder both now clone the wrapping `<span class="name-variation">` instead of the bare anchor whenever the credited artist/event uses one.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Renamed the "Recording of" column to "Recording of work" and "Produced for" to "Produced for label" (glyphs unchanged) — clarifies what each column actually links to.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Produced for" column to `release-tracks`, extracted from each track's "produced for:" relationship (`debug/copyright.html`'s "Laurel Canyon Ltd." example) — labels only, optionally prefixed with "co"/"executive" attribute words rendered inline after the label's name (e.g. "Laurel Canyon Ltd. (executive)"), matching the credit-role columns' own attribute convention. Reuses the existing `sa_enable_release_tracks_credit_role_columns` setting; positioned after both "Phonographic copyright" columns, still before "ARs".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed "Phonographic copyright (℗) by label" never appearing at all, even on a release with real label credits for it (`debug/greetings-original.html`). MusicBrainz can render a track's ARs as multiple SIBLING `<dl class="ars">` blocks inside the same bare `div.ars` — one `<dl>` crediting an artist directly, followed by a separate sibling `<dl>` crediting labels, both using the exact same `<dt>phonographic copyright (℗) by:</dt>` phrase. The lookup used a first-match-only `.find()`, so every `<dt>` after the first (the label one, in this case) was silently dropped, both in the page-wide "does this column exist" gate and in the per-row cell builder. It now collects every matching `<dt>` across every sibling `<dl>` and merges their `<dd>`s, mirroring `_findCreditDts`'s own "collect every match" convention (which was never `.find()`-based and so was unaffected by this bug).

Fixed every credit-role column header ("Recording engineer", "Mixer", "Engineer", "Producer", "Miscellaneous support") and both "Phonographic copyright" headers never actually showing MusicBrainz's marker glyph, despite that being's stated intent (`debug/greetings-rendered.html`). The glyph `<span>` was appended directly to the `<th>` at creation time, but `makeTableSortableUnified()` unconditionally rebuilds every `<th>` from a plain `textContent` string shortly after (as part of the existing sort-icon/unique-value-count UI setup), discarding any child element added before that point — the same root cause already diagnosed and fixed for "Recording of"'s own glyph in an earlier session. The glyph is now injected post-render by the existing `_initColHeaderGlyph()` helper instead, called from `renderGroupedTable()`'s tail alongside the pre-existing "Recording of"/"Recorded at event"/"Recorded at place" calls — the established, already-working pattern for this exact problem, which this feature should have reused from the start.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
Fixed the "Recorded at place" column (9.99.771/9.99.774) rendering MusicBrainz's empty `` glyph marker in front of every place, once per list item (`debug/place-icon.html`) — redundant since that same glyph is already shown once in the column header. The marker is used purely to detect where each place's own content starts (`_buildRecordedAtPlaceTd`'s per-place segmentation), but was also being appended as part of that segment's content into the rendered `
  • `. It's now dropped as soon as it's used as a segment boundary, never appended to the cell. No other content changes — area chains, flags, instrument attributions, and multi-place splitting are all unaffected.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "Engineer"/"Mixer" (and any other pair of) credit columns rendering empty for a track whose `<dt>` credits the same artists under multiple roles at once, e.g. `<dt>engineer and mixer:</dt>` (`debug/Nightshift.html`) — the whole `<dt>` was matched as one unit against a single role's `roleWords`, so `"engineer and mixer:"` matched neither the bare "engineer" role (trailing word is "mixer", not "engineer") nor the "mixer" role (leading words "engineer and" aren't recognized attribute words), leaving both columns empty despite ARs clearly crediting both. `_findCreditDts` now splits each `<dt>`'s body into role components on `,`/` and ` (the same separators MusicBrainz uses to join multiple artists in a `<dd>`) before matching, so `"engineer and mixer:"` → `["engineer", "mixer"]`, each checked independently — the same `<dd>`'s artists now correctly appear in BOTH "Engineer" and "Mixer". A `<dt>` with no `,`/` and ` (the common case) splits into one component, so single-role credits are completely unaffected; the per-component attribute-word strictness (e.g. "recording engineer" still never matching bare "engineer") is unchanged, just applied per component instead of to the whole `<dt>`.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Reverted the per-role attribute-word columns (e.g. "Mixer (Assistant)") added in 9.99.773. A credited artist's own attribute words (Additional/Assistant/Associate/Co/Executive) now render inline right after their name, inside the role's own column, instead of as a separate page-wide-gated column per attribute word — e.g. the "Mixer" cell now shows a two-item list "Paul Hamingson (assistant)" / "Bob Clearmountain" instead of a flag in a separate "Mixer (Assistant)" column (`debug/attributes.html`). Applies to every credit-role column that can have attribute words: "Recording engineer", "Mixer", "Engineer", "Producer". `_creditRoleState`'s page-wide attribute-word union tracking, and the header/row-population code that built one `<th>`/`<td>` per attribute word, are removed — the page-wide scan now only needs to know WHICH roles are used anywhere on the release, not which attribute words.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: When a credited artist has both attribute words and an instrument/task/other annotation, both now render together in one parenthetical, comma-separated, e.g. "Karl Egsieker (assistant/co, task: Second Engineer)" instead of the attribute words being dropped from the artist's own list item entirely (they only ever showed up in the now-removed separate attribute column). Multiple attribute words on one credit are joined with "/", matching the order they appear in `attributeVocab` (e.g. "assistant/co").

Any per-artist annotation whose text starts with "task:" (case-insensitive — MusicBrainz's own "miscellaneous support:" wording, but the same check applies to a task annotation on any other credit role too) now renders in italics, e.g. "Sandy Park (task: string contractor)" with the task text italicized. Every other annotation kind (a linked instrument, or other free text like "other vocals [...]") stays plain, unchanged from 9.99.777/9.99.779.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the credit-role columns (9.99.773/9.99.777/9.99.778) silently dropping a credited artist's own parenthetical note whenever it's free text rather than a linked instrument or the specific "(task: …)" wording — e.g. a bare "engineer:" credit's "(other vocals [Sam Moore vocal])" note (`debug/missing-engineer.html`/`debug/soul-days.html`) rendered as a bare artist name with the note gone. `_findCreditSegmentTaskAnnotation` (9.99.778, matched only `(task: …)`) is replaced by `_findCreditSegmentTextAnnotation`, which matches ANY `(…)` parenthetical across the segment's text nodes rather than special-casing each wording MusicBrainz happens to use — still only consulted when no instrument anchor was found in the segment, so it can't shadow the instrument case. "(task: string contractor)" still renders exactly as before; "(other vocals [Sam Moore vocal])" now renders too.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
Fixed a bare "engineer:" (and any other) credit column (9.99.773/9.99.777) silently dropping an artist entirely whenever MusicBrainz wraps that artist's anchor in `…` (an alias/disambiguated name), instead of just that one artist's instrument/task annotation being lost. `_buildCreditListTd`'s per-artist segmentation looked for the artist `` only as a direct child of the segment; a name-variation-wrapped artist's only direct child is the wrapping ``, so that segment produced no `
  • ` at all — e.g. a bare "engineer:" crediting 3 artists where the first is name-variation-wrapped rendered only the other 2, with the first missing without any indication. New `_findCreditSegmentArtistAnchor`/`_findCreditSegmentInstrumentAnchors` now search each segment node's descendants too (not just the node itself), mirroring 9.99.772's identical `_recordedAtDdAnchor` fix for the same name-variation-nesting problem in "Recorded at place".

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Miscellaneous support" credit column, extracted from `<dt>miscellaneous support:</dt>` the same way as the other 4 credit-role columns (9.99.773), reusing `CREDIT_ROLES`/`_findCreditDts`/`_buildCreditListTd` with an empty `attributeVocab` (no attribute-word prefix is recognized for this role, so it gets no attribute columns). Each credited artist is paired with their own task annotation when MusicBrainz provides one — rendered as plain parenthetical text, not a link, e.g. "(task: string contractor)" — via new `_findCreditSegmentTaskAnnotation`, appended the same way the instrument annotation already is for the other 4 roles, so an artist with a task reads as "Sandy Park (task: string contractor)". Gated by the same `sa_enable_release_tracks_credit_role_columns` setting as the other 4 credit-role columns; positioned last in that group, still before "Recorded at place"/"ARs".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
Fixed the "Recording engineer"/"Mixer"/"Engineer"/"Producer" credit columns (9.99.773) turning a credited instrument into a spurious extra list item instead of keeping it attached to the artist it belongs to. MusicBrainz renders a per-artist instrument attribution as " (strings)" right after that artist's own anchor — the previous implementation flattened every `` inside the `
` (both artist AND instrument anchors) into one `
  • ` each, so e.g. 3 credited engineers each with an instrument attribution rendered as 6 list items ("Ian Kagey", "strings", "Rob Lebret", "strings", …) instead of 3 ("Ian Kagey (strings)", "Rob Lebret (strings)", …). `_buildCreditListTd` now segments each `
    ` structurally on its own `` marker (mirroring "Recorded at place"'s (9.99.774) `span.placelink`-marker segmentation) so any instrument anchor found within an artist's own segment is appended to that artist's `
  • ` as " (strings)" instead of becoming its own item. Multiple instrument anchors within one artist's segment (e.g. "(guitar, bass)") are all kept, comma-joined — untested against real data, no such example found in any debug snapshot.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added support for individual ISRC pages (/isrc/<code>, e.g. /isrc/USSM19500019), new pageType 'isrc'. The native page already renders a fixed, fully-populated `<table class="tbl mergeable-table">` (checkbox / Title / Artist / Length) directly below its own correct `<h1>`/`<h2>`, so the new page definition needs no listToTable/insertH2/renameH2ToH3 and no fetch pagination (`non_paginated: true`) — mirrors the existing 'cd-stub'/'auto-editor-election' page definitions. Title's native `.comment` disambiguation span (often live-performance metadata, e.g. "live, 1975-10-18, early show: The Roxy Theatre, West Hollywood, CA, USA") is split into a synthetic Comment column via `extractMainColumn: 'Title'`, then further parsed by the existing `eventParts` extractor into Event-Type/Event-Date/Event-Detail/Event-Venue/Event-Venue-Detail/Event-City/Event-State/Event-Country/Event-Additional-Info columns — the same convention already used by 'work-recordings-filtered' and others. Artist's native multi-artist-credit markup is handled by the existing generic column pipeline with no new extractor; Length uses the standard `integerColumns` mm:ss sort convention. The native checkbox `<th>` carries no `checkbox-cell` CSS class (unlike other MusicBrainz merge-tables), so a small pageType==='isrc'-scoped pre-processing step stamps that class on before the header scan runs, letting the existing `sa_remove_checkbox_cell` setting govern it exactly like every other merge-checkbox column, without introducing a new removal mechanism.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added an "Additional" column, right before "Recorded at place", for that relationship's own "additional" attribute — MusicBrainz renders it as the adverb "additionally recorded at:" (confirmed via the embedded relationship-type metadata on the edit-relationships page; unlike the engineer/mixer/producer credit columns' adjective "additional recording engineer:" wording), shown here as the canonical word "additional" when present, empty otherwise, matching every other attribute column's convention. "Recorded at event" gets no equivalent column — its own "additional" attribute is never actually rendered in that direction by MusicBrainz. No real-data example of this attribute exists in any captured snapshot; verified via a synthetic jsdom test against the confirmed MB relationship-type template only.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: "Recorded at place" (9.99.771/9.99.772) now renders as a collapsible multi-row list when a single "recorded at:" relationship credits more than one place (e.g. a track recorded partly at one studio and partly at another) — one `<li>` per place, each with its own full "in <area>, <area>, <country>" chain and flags, instead of previously running every place's content together into one unreadable flat cell. Splitting is structural (a new place starts at each place's own leading glyph marker in the source markup), not by reading the "and"/"," separator text, so it's immune to wording variations. Per-place extra context (e.g. an "(<instrument>)" attribution noting which instrument was recorded at that specific place) is preserved on the correct place's row; only the literal "and"/"," joining two places is dropped. Single-place rows are unaffected in content (still exactly the place + its area chain), just now wrapped in a one-item list like every other collapsible column in this family — no behavior change for the common case.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added "Recording engineer", "Mixer", "Engineer", and "Producer" credit columns to `release-tracks`, extracted from the same bare `div.ars` as "Recording of"/"Recorded at" (9.99.770/9.99.771), sourced from sibling `<dl class="ars"><dt>recording engineer:</dt>`/`<dt>mixer:</dt>`/`<dt>engineer:</dt>`/`<dt>producer:</dt>` relationships. Each role can be prefixed with attribute words (Additional, Assistant, Associate, Co, and — Engineer/Producer only — Executive); one column per attribute word actually used on the release is added per role, header-prefixed with the role's own label to avoid collisions (e.g. "Mixer (Assistant)"), showing the attribute word when present, empty otherwise — mirrors the existing "Recording of" attribute-column pattern. When a `<dd>` credits multiple artists (comma/"and"-joined), the cell renders as a collapsible multi-row list, reusing the existing `_findCellListItems`/`initCollapsableColumns` machinery with zero new wiring. Gated by a new dedicated setting, `sa_enable_release_tracks_credit_role_columns` (default on), independent of the existing "Recording of"/"Recorded at" toggle. Positioned after "Recorded at place", still directly before "ARs", which is left completely unchanged as always.

When a track has more than one matching credit for the same role (confirmed in real data: a track with both a bare `<dt>mixer:</dt>` and a separate `<dt>assistant mixer:</dt>`), all matching credits are MERGED into one multi-person list for that role's column, rather than keeping only the first match in document order (the convention every other column in this family uses) — no credited person is silently dropped from a column literally named after their role. Attribute columns become row-level "was this attribute used by any of the merged entries" flags rather than tied to one specific person.

The bare `<dt>engineer:</dt>` role is disambiguated from the compound `<dt>recording engineer:</dt>` role via a strict prefix-word check (every word before the matched role phrase must itself be a recognized attribute word, or the whole `<dt>` is rejected for that role) — a lenient check (silently dropping unrecognized words, like the existing "Recording of" attribute parser does) would wrongly accept "recording engineer:" as a bare "engineer" credit too, since its last word literally is "engineer:". Word-splitting uses `/[\s-]+/` (whitespace OR hyphen), not just whitespace, since MusicBrainz hyphen-attaches the "co" attribute to the following word (e.g. "co-recording engineer:") — confirmed only in the spec examples (`debug/artist-roles.org`), no real-data example of any hyphenated-prefix or "co"/"executive"/"additional"/"associate" combo exists in `debug/full.html`, so this path is unit-tested synthetically only, not against real MusicBrainz markup.

Trailing dates on these credits (e.g. "(on 1975-10-18)", "(in 2015)") are dropped entirely — unlike "Recording of", which has its own "Recording date" column, these 4 roles get no equivalent; the date stays visible in "ARs" only. Achieved for free since only `<a>` anchors are ever extracted, never trailing text/comment nodes.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: "Recorded at place" (9.99.771) now includes the following "in <area>, <area>, <country>" chain (area links, region-flag image, CSS-flag-background country span) alongside the place link itself, instead of just the bare venue name — e.g. "Meadowlands Arena" now also shows "in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States" with both flags. "Recorded at event" is unchanged: its own anchor text already spells out date/venue/location, so no area chain is added there. Both cells still drop the trailing " (on YYYY-MM-DD)" (stays in "ARs" only, same as before).

Fixed "Recorded at place"/"Recorded at event" extracting nothing at all for tracks whose place/event has a name-variation (an alias name differing from the entity's canonical one — MusicBrainz wraps the link one level deeper as `...` in that case, mirroring the Title cell's own name-variation markup). The anchor lookup was scoped to `:scope > a`, a direct-child-only query that silently found nothing once the anchor sat inside that extra ``; relaxed to search any depth, since the href-prefix filter (`/place/` vs. `/event/`, disjoint from area links' `/area/`) already picks the right anchor unambiguously regardless of nesting.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added "Recorded at event" and "Recorded at place" columns to `release-tracks`, extracted from the same bare `div.ars`'s sibling `<dl class="ars"><dt>recorded at:</dt>...</dl>` relationship (a sibling of "recording of:", not nested inside it) already partly covered by the "Recording of" feature. MusicBrainz's `<dt>` wording for this relationship varies (`"recorded at:"`, `"recorded at and mixed at:"`, other "mixed at" combinations), so classification is instead by the `<dd>`'s leading native glyph span — `span.eventlink` vs. `span.placelink` — matched via a loose case-insensitive `"recorded at"` substring test against the `<dt>` rather than an exact/anchored pattern. Two separate columns (not one shared "Recorded at") because the standard sort/filter header pipeline derives each column's identity fresh from its header text on every render — two headers both showing literal "Recorded at" would collide and the second would never be created. Cell value is just the cloned event/place link (no "in <area>, <area>, <country>" chain, no trailing date — no date extraction this round, deferred). A row with more than one "recorded at" entry of the same kind only yields the first, in document order. Reuses the existing `sa_enable_release_tracks_recording_of_columns` setting (label/description updated) rather than adding a new one — same purely-additive family. Positioned after "Recording date", still directly before "ARs"; "ARs" itself is left completely untouched, same contract as "Recording of".

Generalized the post-render column-header glyph injector (`_recOfInitColHeaderGlyph` → `_initColHeaderGlyph(columnName, glyphClass)`) so the same technique now serves all three glyph columns ("Recording of"/`worklink`, "Recorded at event"/`eventlink`, "Recorded at place"/`placelink`) instead of duplicating the function body. The `height`/`margin` CSS fixes already established for `worklink` (see 9.99.770) are reused as-is for the two new glyph classes, since the root cause — any direct child of `.mb-col-hdr-flex`, a flex container, gets its outer display blockified regardless of its own `display` value — is unrelated to the specific glyph class; this is however **unverified in a live browser** for `eventlink`/`placelink` and may need the same kind of Computed-panel comparison `worklink` needed if either icon turns out missing, mis-sized, or misaligned.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
Added a new "Recording of " column (label includes MusicBrainz's own empty, CSS-styled work-glyph icon, matching the convention it's always shown with) to `release-tracks`, extracted from the "ARs" relationship data's `
recording of:
Work Name...
` block (see e.g. `/release/6d19588c-0305-4fb0-b687-d4b75a75c3fd`'s DVD-Video medium) — keeps the work link, same as every other entity reference extracted this session. Also adds one column per recording attribute actually used somewhere on the release (`Acappella`, `Cover`, `Demo`, `Instrumental`, `Karaoke`, `Live`, `Medley`, `Partial` — MusicBrainz prefixes the `
` with these, e.g. `"live cover recording of:"`), showing the attribute name itself when present (e.g. "live") and an empty cell when absent. Both gated by the existing page-wide "only render when at least one track has a value" pattern, plus a new master setting `sa_enable_release_tracks_recording_of_columns` (default **on**) for the whole feature. Positioned directly before "ARs" (not chained after Title like every other column added this session), attribute columns first, then "Recording of", then "Recording date" (see below).

Unlike every prior extraction this session, this one is purely additive: the work link is *cloned*, and the "ARs" column's underlying `div.ars` content is never touched, removed, or modified — "ARs" keeps showing the exact same full relationship data (work link included, now duplicated) it always has. Per explicit instruction, since the source `dl.ars`'s `<dd>` also holds nested writer/lyricist/publisher `dl.ars` blocks that have no column of their own and must not be lost.

Fixed the "Recording of" column's work-glyph icon not actually appearing in the rendered header — the column's `<th>` is later completely rebuilt from a plain text string by the standard sort/filter header pipeline, which destroys any child element appended to it beforehand. The glyph is now injected afterward instead, mirroring the same established pattern already used for the CAA/EAA column-header thumbnail toggle button. A second issue then surfaced: the glyph element existed in the DOM but stayed invisible, because any direct child of a flex container (`.mb-col-hdr-flex`) has its `display` forced to a block type by the CSS spec regardless of its own `display` value, which strips the line-height-derived height an inline icon normally gets from its native, non-flex context — a childless block box with no explicit height is just 0px tall. Fixed by giving the injected glyph an explicit height. A third issue then surfaced: a trailing space text node after the glyph (added so it wouldn't sit flush against the sort icons) turned out not to survive CSS whitespace-collapsing between two flex-blockified siblings — replaced with an explicit `margin-right` on the glyph itself, which isn't subject to that collapsing. A fourth, mirror-image issue then surfaced on the OTHER side of the glyph: the leading space already baked into the header template's text node (`"Recording of "`) collapses for the identical reason, leaving no gap between the label and the glyph — fixed the same way, with an explicit `margin-left` on the glyph.

Added a new "Recording date" column to `release-tracks`, positioned directly after "Recording of", extracting the optional `(on YYYY-MM-DD)` date MusicBrainz appends after the work link in the same "recording of" `<dd>` (e.g. "(on 1978-07-07)" → "1978-07-07") — same purely-additive/page-wide-gated pattern as "Recording of" itself, under the same `sa_enable_release_tracks_recording_of_columns` master setting.

Reordered the whole "Recording of"/"Recording date"/attribute-column group: the attribute columns (`Acappella`/`Cover`/…/`Partial`) now come first, followed by "Recording of", then "Recording date", then "ARs" — previously "Recording of" and (then-named) "Date" preceded the attribute columns. Renamed "Date" to "Recording date" at the same time, since a bare "Date" read ambiguously next to the release-level tracklist.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: `release-tracks`' "Disambiguation" column no longer keeps the literal `(`/`)` MusicBrainz wraps the comment's text in (e.g. "(version 1)" → "version 1", "(live, 1978‐07‐07: …)" → "live, 1978‐07‐07: …") — redundant once the comment has its own dedicated column. New `_stripSurroundingParens()` helper strips a leading `(`/trailing `)` from the cell's first/last actual text node via a `TreeWalker`, handling both structural shapes the comment can appear in (bare text directly in `span.comment`, or wrapped in a nested `<bdi>`).
`release-tracks`' `integerColumns` now also center-aligns (`align: 'C'`) the native `#` track-number column, matching `Rating`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the overflow-tracklist progress bar (9.99.766) only ever showing its static initial "medium 1 of 1..." text with no fill, instead of live progress. It was previously only updated once a medium fully finished loading — for the common case of a single overflowing medium (often the release's ONLY one), that meant the bar showed nothing but the initial text for the entire load (which can itself take as long as a whole paginated fetch), then flashed a completed state for a moment before the next phase's progress bar overwrote it. Now updates live as each medium's own AJAX response streams rows in, reusing the same `MutationObserver` that already detects completion — fill percentage, track count, and the remaining-time estimate all progress continuously during a medium's own load, not just between mediums.

Fixed the same progress bar's label text getting clipped on both ends (e.g. "Loading" losing its "Load") — its container's `min-width` (420px) was sized for the original, shorter paginated-fetch label and never grows to fit longer content since its fill/label children are both `position:absolute` and so don't contribute to the container's own auto width. Bumped to 600px, comfortably fitting the overflow-tracks label's worst case (~73 characters) while staying under the existing 750px cap.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: `release-tracks`' "Disambiguation" column is no longer unconditional — it's now only created once at least one track on the release has the parenthetical comment, same page-wide decision as "Video"/"Recording artist" (`renderGroupedTable()`'s shared header template forces this to be decided once across the whole release, not per medium). "AcoustIDs"/"ISRCs" deliberately keep their current behavior (created whenever their setting is on, independent of whether data is present yet) — their data arrives via an async third-party lookup that's often still in progress when this script runs, which is exactly why the late-arrival `MutationObserver` (added earlier this session) exists; gating their column creation on data already being present would make that observer's job impossible most of the time, since it has nowhere to place data once its destination column doesn't exist.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a progress indicator for `release-tracks`' "Load all tracks..." overflow handling (`loadAllOverflowMediumTracks`), reusing the same inline progress bar the paginated-fetch loop already shows ("Loading page X of Y... (Z rows) - Ns left"). On a release with several overflowing mediums (each its own AJAX round trip that can take a few seconds), this phase previously ran silently before the real fetch loop even started, which could look like a hang. Now shows "Loading overflow tracks: medium X of Y... (Z tracks) - Ns left", updated once per medium (not continuously during each medium's own wait).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
Added a new "Recording artist" column to `release-tracks`, extracted from the native `
Recording artist: …joined artist links…
` MusicBrainz glomms into the Title cell when a track's recording is credited to a different artist than the release itself (e.g. a live cover, a guest performance — see e.g. the "2 - DVD-Video" medium on `/release/6d19588c-0305-4fb0-b687-d4b75a75c3fd`). The whole `` — preserving every joined artist link and join phrase verbatim, same reasoning as the release-level Artist backfill — is moved (not cloned) into the new column. Like "Video", the column's presence is decided once, page-wide (any track on the release has the credit), not per medium, since `renderGroupedTable()`'s single shared header template would otherwise silently drop a `` present on only some mediums' native theads. Positioned directly after "Artist" — the release-level credit reads first, with the recording's own (possibly different) credit immediately beside it.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Renamed `release-tracks`' (9.99.761) "AcoustID"/"ISRC" columns to "AcoustIDs"/"ISRCs" (plural, since each cell can hold more than one entry).

Added a new, conditionally-created "Video" column to `release-tracks`, extracted from the native `<span class="video" title="This recording is a video">` icon MusicBrainz glomms into the Title cell for video recordings (see e.g. the "2 - DVD-Video" medium on `/release/6d19588c-0305-4fb0-b687-d4b75a75c3fd`) — reuses the existing, generic `ColumnDataExtractor.video` extractor (already used by several other pageTypes, e.g. `artist-recordings`, via a normal `columnExtractors` entry) rather than duplicating its move-the-span/audio-video-sort-key logic. Unlike a normal `columnExtractors` entry, which always creates its synthetic column, the "Video" `<th>` is only added when at least one track ANYWHERE ON THE RELEASE (any medium) has the icon, so a release with no video tracks at all never gets a permanently empty column — decided once, page-wide, not per medium: `renderGroupedTable()` builds a single header `<thead>` template from the first `table.tbl` in the document and clones it for every medium, so a `<th>` present on only some mediums' native theads would silently vanish from every rendered table (row data still carries through per group, the header does not). Positioned directly after "Title" (before "Disambiguation").

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a new (default on) `sa_enable_release_tracks_acoustid_isrc_observer` setting: a `MutationObserver`-based reactive fix for the "AcoustID"/"ISRC" columns (9.99.761) so late-arriving data from a third-party userscript's async AcoustID lookup (e.g. jesus2099's, a network round-trip to acoustid.org per recording — routinely still in progress by the time this script's own one-shot extraction pass ran) reaches those columns instead of being silently missed. Watches each medium's table for AcoustID/ISRC data appearing after the fact and relocates it into the right column reactively, mirroring the existing area-flag/region-correction observer (`initAreaFlagRegionObserver`). Only does anything when at least one of the AcoustID/ISRC column settings is on; zero overhead otherwise. Required switching `applyExtractTrackTitleData()`'s Title-cell cleanup from cloning the recording link/ARs/AcoustID/ISRC content to *moving* it — a clone would silently break this fix, since whatever the decorating userscript is tracking (a live object reference, or a re-query matching the same class/attributes) needs the actual live node to still be present in the rendered table for its own late decoration to land anywhere this observer can see it.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "ARs"/"AcoustID"/"ISRC" columns (9.99.761) never getting a collapse toggle on any release-tracks page with more than one medium, even when a cell's content clearly overflowed the clamp. Root cause: `renderGroupedTable()`'s `shouldStayOpen` heuristic (which decides whether a sub-table starts expanded or `display:none`) only recognizes a lone sub-table or the literal categories `album`/`official` — release-tracks' medium-title categories ("1 - CD", "2 - DVD-Video", …) matched neither, so every medium on a multi-medium release started hidden. `initCollapsableColumns()`/`makeColumnsResizable()` then ran immediately afterward against that still-hidden table — measuring `scrollHeight`/`clientHeight` on a `display:none` element always reads 0 in a real browser, so the overflow check permanently found nothing to add a toggle to, even after the section was later expanded by hand. This bug predates this session but was invisible until `collapsableColumns` was added to release-tracks in 9.99.761. Fixed by keeping every release-tracks sub-table expanded by default regardless of medium count — matching the feature's whole point (consolidating a release's tracklists into one always-visible view) and avoiding the hidden-at-measurement-time trap entirely.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: `release-tracks`' "Title" column no longer shows the raw glommed cell MusicBrainz (and, once it has run, the third-party jesus2099 "SUPER MIND CONTROL" script) builds it from — just the clean track title now. Everything else that used to be crammed into that cell is extracted into its own new column: a "Disambiguation" column (the parenthetical comment shown when a track's title differs from its recording, e.g. "(live, 1978‐07‐07: The Roxy Theatre, West Hollywood, CA, USA)"); an always-present, collapsible "ARs" column at the end of the table (the recording's general relationships — engineer, producer, recording-of-work, publisher, … — previously glommed into the Title cell as a `<div class="ars">`), with its own independent collapse-height settings (`sa_enable_ars_collapse`, `sa_ars_column_max_height_em`, `sa_ars_column_max_width`) rather than sharing the "Annotation" column's; and two new off-by-default multi-row columns, "AcoustID" and "ISRC" (`sa_enable_release_tracks_acoustid_column` / `sa_enable_release_tracks_isrc_column`), each entry rendered as its own list row instead of one long comma-separated line — AcoustID entries keep their native ×/+ link/unlink action link. The secondary "recording name" line MusicBrainz shows under a track's title when it differs from the underlying recording's name is dropped (not kept in any column, per explicit confirmation). Implemented via a new `applyExtractTrackTitleData()` DOM-surgery pass (mirroring the existing Artist-column backfill's approach) rather than the additive `columnExtractors` mechanism, since cleaning the Title cell in place isn't something that mechanism supports.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed `release-tracks`' backfilled "Artist" column (9.99.758) truncating a multi-artist release credit down to just the first artist — e.g. a release credited to "Bruce Springsteen & The E Street Band" rendered as just "Bruce Springsteen" in every row. `applyNormalizeMediumTracklists()` was capturing and cloning only the first `<a href="/artist/...">` found inside `p.subheader`'s `<bdi>`, dropping the join text (" & ", ", ", " feat. ", …) and any subsequent artist links; it now captures and clones the entire `<bdi>` artist-credit element, matching how MusicBrainz's own native Various-Artists per-track Artist cells already render multi-artist credits.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed `release-tracks`' "Load all tracks..." overflow handling (9.99.758) resolving after only a few milliseconds and still rendering the truncated 100-row tracklist: MusicBrainz replaces the triggering `<tr>` with a loading placeholder almost instantly on click, long before the AJAX response with the real rows has arrived, so waiting for that `<tr>` to leave the DOM (the original signal) fired a false-positive completion. `loadAllOverflowMediumTracks()` now parses the expected final track count from the overflow message ("...out of 1209 total.") and waits for the `<tbody>`'s actual data-row count to reach it, falling back to an idle-mutation heuristic only when that count can't be parsed; the per-medium timeout was also raised from 15s to 30s to give large tracklists room to load.

Fixed jesus2099 "SUPER MIND CONTROL" hover-toolzone artifacts (Merge/Edit/Open-edits quick-action `<div>`s, e.g. `<div class="jesus2099userjs81127toolzone" style="display:block">`) being cloned into the final rendered Length column with a baked-in `display:block` from whatever hover state was active at scrape time. Added a new generic `'jesus2099-any'` `columnErasers` sentinel (removes any element whose class starts with "jesus2099userjs", by prefix rather than one hardcoded suffix, since that userscript embeds an install/version-specific numeric ID) alongside the existing exact-class `'jesus2099'` sentinel, and applied it to `release-tracks`' Length column.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a new `release-tracks` pageType for bare release pages (musicbrainz.org/release/<mbid>), consolidating every medium's native tracklist into the standard filterable/sortable multi-table view via a new "Show all Tracks for Release" button (gated by the new `sa_enable_release_tracks` setting, default on). Each medium's `<thead>`-embedded title (e.g. "1 - CD") is synthesized into a sibling `<h3>` so the existing release-group h3-sibling-walk grouping pipeline can be reused unmodified; the native `<tr class="subh">` header row is promoted into a proper `<thead>`; an `Artist` column is always present, backfilled with the release's main artist credit on non-Various-Artists releases. Mediums truncated by MusicBrainz's own "Load all tracks..." overflow link (>100 tracks) are auto-loaded and awaited before the tracklist is scraped, so no tracks are missed. The native "Edit recording comments" button and settings-icon are stripped from the reused `h2.tracklist` header once it becomes the global filter/master-toggle anchor. Also adds a new additive `features.removeSelectors` (plural array) post-render step alongside the existing singular `removeSelector`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the "Relationships" column disappearing entirely (both header and data cells) after clicking "Show single-table" on an artist-relationships sub-table (e.g. "'liner notes for release' relationships"), while the same button worked correctly for artist-releasegroups/releasegroup-releases sub-tables. Root cause: the cross-tab snapshot handoff deliberately does not capture the async-populated `mb-rel-cell` data cells (they're meant to be freshly (re)built post-hydration by cleanupHeaders()/initRelationshipsColumn(), gated on the *destination* page definition's `features.injectedColumns`) — but `artist-relationships-filtered` (the tableMode:'single' definition the `?link_type_id=1`-qualified snapshot tab routes to) never declared `injectedColumns: ['Relationships']` in the first place, unlike its multi-table sibling `artist-relationships` and unlike the equivalent `label-relationships-filtered`/`place-performances-filtered` definitions (which already had it and were unaffected). With no active injected-column descriptor, cleanupHeaders()'s unconditional "always remove foreign Relationships/Release events/Tagger header text" pass still deleted the plain-text "Relationships" `<th>` that came along in the captured header HTML, but its later re-injection step (gated on the same descriptor) never ran to replace it, and initRelationshipsColumn() bailed immediately — so neither the header nor any `mb-rel-cell` `<td>` was ever (re)created. Added the missing `injectedColumns: ['Relationships']` declaration to `artist-relationships-filtered`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the overflow-button persistence added by 765edfe ("Fix overflow buttons disappearing after Load from Disk", on main) being silently dropped by the merge of main into this branch: the disk-load reconstruction loop that restores seeAllUrl/tagSeeAllUrl/ratingsViewAllUrl onto each reconstructed group had already been extracted (9.99.755 above) from loadTableDataFromDisk() into _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData(), re-indenting every line in that block — git's line-based merge treated the whole region as already changed on this branch and merged 765edfe's inserted restoration lines out without ever raising a conflict marker, even though the corresponding save-side (saveTableDataToDisk) and render-side (renderGroupedTable) halves of that same fix merged in cleanly. Re-added the three restoration blocks (seeAllUrl/seeAllCount, tagSeeAllUrl/tagSeeAllCount/tagSeeAllEntityLabel, ratingsViewAllUrl) to _grpEntry construction so the "Show all N rows"/"View all ratings" buttons survive a Load-from-Disk round trip again.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a "Show single-table" button to multi-table relationship/performance sub-sections (artist-relationships, label-relationships, place-performances) that have no MusicBrainz overflow (i.e. every row is already rendered, ≤100). Clicking it opens the currently-rendered rows as a standalone single-table view in a new browser tab via a client-side snapshot handoff (GM_setValue/GM_getValue keyed by a per-click uid, plus a `#mb-sa-snapshot=<uid>` hash marker on a `?link_type_id=1`-qualified URL) — no MusicBrainz re-fetch, unlike the existing native-overflow "Show all N rows" button. New settings: sa_ui_show_single_table_btn_bg / sa_ui_show_single_table_btn_bg_clicked.

Extended the "Show single-table" button to artist-releasegroups (e.g. an artist's bare overview page) and releasegroup-releases sub-sections, whose categories never carry a MusicBrainz overflow link at all (unlike relationships/performances, these page types accumulate every row themselves via their own multi-page fetch, so MB never imposes a per-category cap to begin with). These page types have no "-filtered" single-table sibling definition to route to via a query-param trick, so the new tab reuses the bare multi-mode URL as-is — MusicBrainz's own native table on that page already carries class="tbl" for the existing hydrate/fallback-fabrication logic to hook into. The button-eligibility whitelist and the link_type_id-routing decision are now centralized in two Sets (SA_SNAPSHOT_SUPPORTED_PAGETYPES, SA_SNAPSHOT_LINK_TYPE_ID_PAGETYPES) instead of duplicated inline conditions.

Extracted loadTableDataFromDisk()'s render/reconstruction body into a shared _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData(data, opts) function, reused by both the existing "Load from Disk" feature and the new cross-tab snapshot bootstrap, so both consumers get identical row reconstruction, render, and post-render wiring instead of two independently drifting implementations. Also hardened it with a fallback that fabricates an empty table.tbl shell when none exists natively on the page (benefits any future caller lacking a live table, not just the snapshot handoff).

Made the "Show single-table" button opt-in: new setting sa_enable_show_single_table_btn (checkbox, default OFF) gates both places the button gets created — the primary per-category button and the defensive re-injection after a filter-driven h3 re-render — since this feature is still new and hasn't shipped to main yet.

Disabled every h1 action button (e.g. "Artist RGs"/"Various Artists RGs" on an artist overview, "Show all Releases for ReleaseGroup" on a release-group overview, or the "Show all Relationships/Performances for X" buttons on relationship/performance pages) on a "Show single-table" snapshot tab, with a tooltip explaining why: clicking one would kick off a real fetch on the synthetic tab, silently replacing the frozen single-category snapshot with a completely different full multi-table view. The tooltip points the user back to the original page — refresh it and click "Show single-table" there again for a fresh version. _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData() gained an isCrossTabSnapshot opt so this only applies to the cross-tab snapshot handoff, not the general "Load from Disk" flow (which can still legitimately kick off a fresh fetch afterward).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed a "Cannot access '_filterResultCache' before initialization" crash when opening a "Show single-table" snapshot tab: the hash-marker bootstrap hook ran mid-way through the script's initial synchronous top-to-bottom execution, calling into _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData() (via runFilter()/_invalidateFilterCache()) before later module-level const/let bindings in the same top-level scope had initialized. Every other caller (a button click, a FileReader.onload) only ever fires after the whole script has finished its first synchronous pass; the bootstrap's hydrate call is now deferred one tick via setTimeout(...,0) to match.

Fixed the snapshot tab's <h2> heading always showing MusicBrainz's own native label for whichever relationship/performance type the placeholder `?link_type_id=1` happens to resolve to (e.g. "next disc" relationships) instead of the actually-captured category (e.g. "Produced release"). Added _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel(), called after hydration settles, to replace just the bare heading text node with the real category name.

Fixed inline CAA thumbnails and sticky-column not working for release/release-group snapshot tabs: reconstructed headers carried leftover uniq-value count-badge digits (e.g. "Title" -> "Title 18") baked into their captured innerHTML, which makeTableSortableUnified's colName derivation absorbed into dataset.colName (it deliberately does not strip plain 0-9, to avoid mangling genuine numeric column names like "1st seconder"), breaking every name-based column lookup downstream (caaFindColumnByName, applyStickyColumn). The header-restore step in _hydrateAndRenderFromSnapshotData now collapses an already-decorated .mb-col-hdr-flex header back to its clean name text before makeTableSortableUnified re-processes it — a general fix that also corrects the same latent bug in the existing "Load from Disk" feature.

Fixed _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel() correcting the wrong <h2> on busy pages (e.g. a release-group's bare overview, which has its own Wikipedia-extract h2 ahead of the Releases one): it now walks all h2s to find the one that actually immediately precedes table.tbl in document order (mirrors updateH2Count()'s own targetH2 resolution), instead of naively grabbing the first h2.mb-toggle-h2 on the page.

Investigated a reload race on artist-releasegroups/releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs, where a separately-installed third-party userscript (a Picard/Tagger-port integration script) auto-reloads the bare entity page shortly after load to append its own query param, wiping out the hydrated snapshot — confirmed via HAR network-log initiator trace to be that script's own reloadWithTaggerPort(), not this script's code. Added a stopOtherScripts() call (the same window.stopAllUserScripts + 'mb-stop-all-scripts' signal startFetchingProcess() already sends before every normal fetch) as early as possible in the hash-marker bootstrap, on the chance a cooperating script checks it — confirmed by testing that this specific third-party script does NOT check it, so the race remains for anyone running it alongside this one. Not fixable from here: cooperation from an independently-installed script can't be forced. Workaround: disable/adjust that script for this workflow, or use the browser's Stop button before the reload completes.

Fixed "Show single-table" on artist-releasegroups showing multiple h3-based subtables still native/unprocessed in the new tab: MusicBrainz's own artist-overview page already groups release-groups into several separate native `<h3>` + `<table class="tbl release-group-list mergeable-table">` sections (one per release-group type), and the header-restore step only ever targeted the FIRST table.tbl found, leaving the rest fully native alongside the hydrated single-table view. Added _clearNativeTableSectionsForSnapshot(), called before every snapshot hydration, which removes all such h3+table.tbl sections first (only acting on an h3 when a table.tbl is actually found in its sibling chain, so unrelated h3s — e.g. from other installed userscripts — are left alone) so the existing "no table.tbl found — fabricate a fresh shell" fallback always builds exactly one, correctly-scoped table.

Fixed _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel() stealing a release-group's native "Relationships" section heading on releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs (e.g. relabeling it to “Bootleg release” releases, with the Relationships section's own original content — e.g. its "associated singles/EPs:"/"other databases:" rows — then visibly dangling right after it): _clearNativeTableSectionsForSnapshot only ever clears h3+table.tbl "Releases" sections by design, so the Relationships h2 section survives, and once the fabricated table lands past that surviving section, "the h2 immediately preceding table.tbl" resolves to it instead of anything Releases-related. The "no table.tbl found" fabrication branch now creates its own dedicated `<h2>` (stamped `data-mb-sa-fabricated-heading`) and positions the fabricated table right after it — nothing native can ever land between them again — and _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel() targets that marker directly instead of guessing via document order. The nearest-preceding-h2 heuristic remains as a fallback for the three pageTypes that reuse an existing native table.tbl (routed via ?link_type_id=1) rather than fabricating one.

Fixed two more releasegroup-releases snapshot-tab bugs — a `<td class="relationships">` (with a discogs favicon link) appended as literally every row's 2nd cell right after the sticky column, and every release's cover-art image doubled in the big-picture stripe above the table — both traced to the separately-installed jesus2099 "mb. SUPER MIND CONTROL" userscript (already known to this codebase via its `'jesus2099'` columnEraser, its bigbox cleanup in performClutterCleanup(), and initTreleasesObserver()'s handling of its injected `<tr class="treleases">` rows). That script reacts to the page on its own schedule; the normal fetch-and-render flow's one-shot cleanup is timed after it has already run, but the snapshot-hydrate bootstrap replaces the page within one setTimeout(...,0) tick of the tab opening, so jesus2099's own injection can still be pending — it then injects its favicon-link column and a second `div.jesus2099userjs154481bigbox` into whichever rows/table it finds moments later, which are now this script's freshly-hydrated ones. Added _watchForLateJesus2099Injections(), a short-lived (5s) MutationObserver installed at the very start of the snapshot bootstrap that strips both as soon as they appear, mirroring initTreleasesObserver()'s existing childList+attributes pattern.

Fixed the jesus2099 "relationships" <td> race fix (9.99.755 above) leaving its HEADER-side twin behind: a bare `<th>Relationships</th>` (no class, no data-col-name, none of this script's own header-marker classes) landed as the table's 2nd header on releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs, right after "Release" — jesus2099 injects a whole column (one header cell, one data cell per row), and cleanupHeaders() only strips a header matching that text once, right after renderFinalTable(), before jesus2099's late injection lands on this fast bootstrap path. _watchForLateJesus2099Injections() now also matches and removes any bare foreign <th> whose text starts with "Relationships"/"Performance Attributes"/"Release events"/"Tagger" (cleanupHeaders()'s own removalMapAlways list) and carries none of this script's own header classes.

Fixed (root cause confirmed via debug logging added in the previous attempt) a release-group's native "Album" h2 (the one wrapping the Official/Promotion/Bootleg release h3+table sections) surviving on releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs as an empty, collapsed, count-less stub once _clearNativeTableSectionsForSnapshot cleared every h3+table pair beneath it. A structural analysis of an earlier debug HTML capture showed "Album" owning exactly 3 h3s, all removable — but the debug log from a live reproduction showed "h2 'Album' owns no h3" and "Cleared 1 pre-existing native table.tbl section(s) (0 h3-anchored, …)": this whole bootstrap runs within one setTimeout(...,0) tick of the tab opening — fast enough to beat MusicBrainz's OWN client-side JS splitting the release listing into its Official/Promotion/Bootleg h3 subsections, so at the moment this function actually ran, "Album" still owned a single flat table.tbl directly (no h3 wrapping yet), which the unconditional "remainingTables" sweep silently absorbed — leaving "Album" itself unaccounted for by the h3-only ownership check. _clearNativeTableSectionsForSnapshot now also records, in the same up-front walk, which table.tbl each h2 owns DIRECTLY (no h3 in between), and treats that exactly like an owned-and-removed h3 for emptiness purposes.

Fixed the fabricated heading (see the "stealing a native Relationships heading" fix above) being inserted directly after `

`, which pushed MusicBrainz's own native `

` ("~Release group by …") and `

` (Overview/Aliases/Tags/Reviews/Details/Edit) down BELOW the fabricated heading and table on releasegroup-releases snapshot tabs — that page-level chrome belongs directly under h1, not sandwiched below new content. The fabrication branch now anchors after the LAST `div.tabs` instead (the same preference order applyInsertH2 already uses for this exact problem), falling back to right after h1 only when no tabs bar exists at all.

Fixed a leftover MusicBrainz native `<h2>` (e.g. "next disc" relationships) plus its "No relationships of the selected type were found." paragraph appearing ABOVE the correctly-labeled fabricated section on artist-relationships/label-relationships/place-performances snapshot tabs, whenever the `?link_type_id=1` placeholder genuinely has zero native matches. When a native table.tbl DOES exist for the placeholder, _fixSnapshotHeadingLabel already just relabels that table's own h2 in place (no duplicate) — but with zero matches there is no native table at all, so the "no table.tbl found" branch fabricates a brand new heading+table instead of reusing the native one, leaving the old native placeholder heading and its "not found" message behind as unrelated noise. The fabrication branch now removes that native placeholder h2 (and its content, up to the next h2) first, for the 3 pageTypes routed via ?link_type_id=1, before inserting its own dedicated heading at the same anchor point.

Attempted (capture-time only — reported as still reproducing) to fix jesus2099's cover-art icon anchor (`<a href="…/cover-art"><span class="caa-icon jesus2099userjs154481">`) showing up an extra time in the sticky "Title" column and appearing at all in the synthetic "MB-Name" column on artist-releasegroups "Show single-table" snapshot tabs, by also stripping it in _stripTransientCellState() (shared by getCleanCellHtml and the disk-load path) so the STORED snapshot data is clean. That was necessary but not sufficient: unlike every other jesus2099 symptom fixed so far (all specific to releasegroup-releases table cells), this one is a generic, page-wide jesus2099 behavior — it independently scans the whole live page for release/release-group links and prepends this icon next to each one, on its own schedule, regardless of whose table those links live in. Cleaning the captured data does nothing to stop jesus2099 separately re-injecting the same icon into the DESTINATION tab's own live DOM once this script's rows exist there. _watchForLateJesus2099Injections() (the same short-lived MutationObserver already watching for the relationships td/th and the bigbox) now also detects and removes any `<a>` inside `table.tbl` that wraps a `span.caa-icon.jesus2099userjs154481`, regardless of when jesus2099 injects it.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Renamed the "(specialized)" suffix to "(complete)" on all 7 affected button labels (Area/Place/Label/Work/Artist relationships/recordings/performances pageDefinitions) for clearer wording.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the column unique-values dropdown (📊) showing entries with artificial blank spaces splitting words apart (e.g. "Illinois" rendered as "I llino is") whenever that column had an active filter whose match landed mid-word — reported on Area/Country columns of `/area/<mbid>/artists` filtering for "llino"/"it", but reproducible on any column. Root cause: `getCleanColumnText()` (used by `openUniqDrop()` to build each dropdown entry's raw value) read text directly from live table cells, which keep the matching column filter's `<span class="mb-column-filter-highlight">` wrapped around the matched substring for as long as that filter stays active (`highlightText()`/`highlightCrossTag()`). That live `<span>` split a word's text into separate before/match/after text nodes that `element.normalize()` cannot merge across an intervening element, so the TreeWalker collected them as separate fragments and `textParts.join(' ')` inserted a literal space at each boundary. Fixed by unwrapping (not stripping) any element matching the existing `_COLLAPSE_MATCH_SEL` selector — the authoritative list of all 4 filter-highlight classes (`mb-global-filter-highlight`, `mb-column-filter-highlight`, `mb-pre-filter-highlight`, `mb-subtable-filter-highlight`) — back into a plain text node before `normalize()` runs, in both `getCleanColumnText()` and `getCleanVisibleText()` (the latter shares the identical clone/strip/TreeWalker shape and feeds sort keys / the non-regex global filter, so it had the same latent bug — e.g. sorting a column while its own filter-highlight was live would have produced a corrupted, wrongly-ordered sort key).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed flagged bare states/provinces for United States and Canada (no city entered, e.g. an artist whose Area is set directly to "Illinois") landing in "MB-Locality" instead of "MB-Region" — a regression from the 9.99.752 fix, which removed those two countries from `AREA_FLAG_REGION_COUNTRIES` entirely to stop flagged CITIES being force-routed to Region. Since "MusicBrainz: More Flags Everywhere" (@Lotheric) now flags both city-level and state/province-level links for United States/Canada, flag-presence + country membership alone can no longer tell them apart. Added `AREA_FLAG_REGION_SUBDIVISIONS`, a closed allowlist of US state/district/territory and Canadian province/territory/region NAMES (sourced from that script's own non-city REGIONS sections) via a new `_flagRegionSubdivisionSet()` helper: for United States/Canada, a flagged first area link is now only forced into Region when its own name matches this allowlist, so a flagged city (not in the list) correctly stays in Locality while a flagged bare state/province (in the list) is force-routed to Region as before. United Kingdom/Australia are unaffected, still using the simpler country-membership check (`AREA_FLAG_REGION_COUNTRIES`) since that script only flags regions for them. Updated both `_routeAreaLink()` (extraction-time routing) and its deferred counterpart `_maybeCorrectAreaFlagRegion()` (pages 2..Max, async flag-decoration timing) identically.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed flagged city-level Area entries for United States and Canada landing merged into "MB-Region" (together with the state/province flag) instead of staying in "MB-Locality" — e.g. on `/area/<mbid>/artists`. `_routeAreaLink()` force-routes a flagged first area link into Region whenever its country is in the internal `AREA_FLAG_REGION_COUNTRIES` list, a rule that only made sense while "MusicBrainz: More Flags Everywhere" (@Lotheric) exclusively decorated state/province-level links for United States/United Kingdom/Canada/Australia (a flagged first link could only mean "no city entered"). Now that that userscript also flags city-level links for United States and Canada, a flagged first link there can legitimately be a real city. Removed 'United States' and 'Canada' from `AREA_FLAG_REGION_COUNTRIES` (now `['United Kingdom', 'Australia']`) so those two countries' flagged cities stay in Locality; United Kingdom/Australia are unaffected since that script still only flags regions for them.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Extended the 9.99.749 "Release country"/"Release date" collapse-toggle fix to place-performances pages: added those two columns to `collapsableColumns` on both `place-performances` and `place-performances-filtered` page definitions. They share the same `initReleaseEventsColumn()`/`applyInjectedColumnExtractors()` pipeline as label-relationships, so the underlying re-scan fix already covers them — this only extends the config.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed "Release country" and "Release date" never getting their collapse toggle on label-relationships pages, even when listed in `collapsableColumns`. `initReleaseEventsColumn()` fills those two columns' multi-row `<ul><li>` content in a third pass (`applyInjectedColumnExtractors()`, which splits the now-populated "Release events" cell), but the collapse-column scan (`initCollapsableColumns()`) was only re-run after the second pass, before that content existed. Fixed by re-running `initCollapsableColumns()` again after `applyInjectedColumnExtractors()` completes (safe/idempotent — it does its own cleanup pass before rebuilding, so "Release events"' already-installed toggle isn't duplicated). Also added "Release country" and "Release date" to `collapsableColumns` on both `label-relationships` and `label-relationships-filtered` page definitions now that the underlying bug is fixed.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the injected "Relationships" column never appearing on artist-works pages (`/artist/<mbid>/works`). Two compounding causes: the `artist-works` page definition never declared `features.injectedColumns: [ 'Relationships' ]` in the first place, so `buildActiveInjectedColumns()` — which already had dedicated `entityType: 'work'` / `inc=url-rels+artist-rels` handling for this page type — was never invoked; and even after adding that declaration, `_suppressRelationshipsIfNoReleaseOrReleaseGroupLinks()` would have immediately deleted the newly created header and cells again, because its "no /release/ or /release-group/ link in the row ⇒ nothing to show" guard — correct for release/release-group-linked pages like artist-relationships and artist-releasegroups — doesn't apply on artist-works, where the column targets each row's own Work MBID directly and a Work row never links to a release. Fixed by adding the missing `injectedColumns` declaration and gating the suppression guard to skip `entityType === 'work'`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed three related overflow-button features silently disappearing after a Save to Disk → Load from Disk round trip (and, for the latter two, after any other full re-render that happens once their source "See all"/"View all" row has already been consumed — e.g. clearing a global filter back to empty): the artist-relationships "Show all N rows" button (relationship-type sub-section exceeding the 100-row-per-page limit), the tag-value/user-tag-value/artist-credit "Show all N rows" button, and the user-ratings "View all ratings" button. All three are built purely from metadata captured once from a native placeholder row/link and were never persisted anywhere once that row was consumed — `saveTableDataToDisk()` never wrote it into the exported JSON, so the Load-from-Disk reconstruction path (and, for the latter two, `renderGroupedTable` itself on any later fresh re-render) always rebuilt the group without it. Fixed by capturing this metadata onto the group object at the point each button is first built (`group.seeAllUrl`/`seeAllCount` for relationships, `group.tagSeeAllUrl`/`tagSeeAllCount`/`tagSeeAllEntityLabel` for tag-value/artist-credit, `group.ratingsViewAllUrl` for user-ratings), persisting it in `saveTableDataToDisk()`, restoring it in the Load-from-Disk reconstruction (same conditional pattern already used there for `colName`/`entityFeatures`), and having `renderGroupedTable` fall back to it whenever the source row/link can no longer be found in the DOM.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Resynced ShowAllEntityData_HELP.txt against every user-facing change since 9.99.675, and against the live keyboard-shortcut/settings code as ground truth. Added: the report pages (/reports, /report/<Name>), edit-listing pages (edits/user-edits/user-open-edits/notes-received) as a new EDIT-LISTING PAGES section, auto-editor elections, genre/instrument/edit-types lists, CD stub pages, and privileged-accounts page to SUPPORTED PAGES; the musicbrainz.eu mirror note; unique-values dropdown multi-select checkboxes and the opt-in flag-icon decoration; the Locality/Region split of Area-family extracted columns; a new ANNOTATION COLUMNS section and ANNOTATION SECTION AUTO-EXPAND note; and the 🎨 EDITS PAGE / 📝 ANNOTATION COLUMNS / 📖 ANNOTATION SECTION settings groups. Also corrected a pre-existing keyboard-shortcuts inaccuracy found while cross-checking ctrlMFunctionMap and configSchema directly: `sa_enable_direct_ctrl_char_shortcuts` defaults to OFF, meaning every direct Ctrl+<letter> shortcut (including ones the HELP file listed as always-on, like Ctrl+G/Ctrl+C/Ctrl+K) is actually suppressed by default in favor of the Ctrl+M prefix mode — documented this plainly, added the missing Ctrl+B / prefix-mode b/g/c/q/a entries, and noted which shortcuts (Ctrl+2/3, Ctrl+,, Ctrl+Shift+G, Ctrl+↑/↓/#, Ctrl+U) are never affected by the toggle. Also added a new ACCOUNT APPLICATIONS PAGE section explaining why /account/applications gets its own callout: MusicBrainz serves /account/* with a stricter Content-Security-Policy (style-src 'self' staticbrainz.org static.metabrainz.org, no unsafe-inline) than other pages, and every dialog/tooltip/panel in this script now renders correctly there via GM_addStyle()-injected stylesheets — the subject of the 9.99.736-9.99.745 fix run — with no reduced functionality.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix the Ctrl+M shortcuts tooltip never appearing at all on page types with no `div#content` (e.g. /account/applications) — unrelated to the CSP `style-src` fixes above. `showCtrlMTooltip()` had an early `if (!contentDiv) return;` guard that skipped building the tooltip entirely whenever `#content` was absent, even though `#content` is only actually needed for the positioning step at the end of the function. Removed the early bailout and added a viewport-relative positioning fallback (anchored to the top-right corner) for when `#content` doesn't exist, instead of requiring it unconditionally.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix the remaining CSP `style-src` breakage on /account/applications in one final pass, closing out the investigation started in 9.99.736: `showRenderDecisionDialog` (the "Large Dataset Fetched" decision dialog), `showCtrlMTooltip` (the Ctrl+M shortcuts tooltip), `_saveSettingsConfig` (settings-export metadata block, now reusing the shared `.sa-meta-*` classes), `_relBuildTooltipHTML` (relationship-cell rich tooltips), `makeCollapseExpandBtnHTML` (the shared ▶/▼ collapse-toggle button label used throughout the script), and a handful of smaller 1-2-attribute sites (help-panel error fallback, resize/render progress overlays, mnemonic-underline button labels, rich hover-tooltip spans, and the release/release-group inline-expand error messages). File-wide: 0 remaining `style="..."` attributes in live code (down from ~260 at the start of this investigation) — every class referenced via `class="..."` verified to have a matching `GM_addStyle()` definition.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix the "Edit Pinned Filter List" table-editor dialog (`showEditPersistentListDialog`, opened via the ✎ Edit Pinned Filter List button inside any filter-history dropdown) rendering unstyled on /account/applications — same CSP `style-src` issue as 9.99.736-9.99.742, across 49 attributes, the biggest remaining function. Its per-row selection/mark highlighting (a dynamic `rowStyle` string computed from 3 discrete states) was converted to a base `.sa-epl-row` class plus `.sa-epl-row-sel`/`.sa-epl-row-mrk` modifier classes; the existing JS property-assignment calls that update selection after initial render are unaffected. Also reused the shared `.mb-fhw-mark` class for its quick-filter highlight.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix the generic export dialog (`showExportDialog`, the CSV/etc "Save Data" flow, distinct from `showSaveDialog`'s full-table-serialization dialog) rendering unstyled on /account/applications — same CSP `style-src` issue as 9.99.736-9.99.741, across 15 attributes. Virtually identical shell to `showSaveDialog`/`showLoadFilterDialog`, fixed with the same dedicated, id-guarded, injected-once `GM_addStyle()` stylesheet pattern.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix the statistics panel (`showStatsPanel`) rendering unstyled on /account/applications — same CSP `style-src` issue as 9.99.736-9.99.740, this time across 46 attributes in the largest single function fixed so far (~1570 lines). Almost every occurrence interpolated one of a handful of colors from the panel's own fixed, hardcoded palette (never settings-driven), so they collapsed into ~20 reusable `.sa-stats-*` classes via a new shared `_ensureStatsPanelStyle()` stylesheet. One genuinely conditional case (picking a color based on a column's sort direction) was changed to compute a class name instead of a color value, keeping it CSS-only.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix the "Save Table Data" dialog (`showSaveDialog`) and the shared "File Metadata" table it and the Load dialog both use (`buildMetaBlockHTML`) rendering unstyled on /account/applications — same CSP `style-src` issue as 9.99.736-9.99.739. `buildMetaBlockHTML`'s 10 attributes moved to a new shared, id-guarded `GM_addStyle()` stylesheet, including replacing an inline `${modeColor}`-interpolated background with two static modifier classes (`.sa-meta-mode-multi`/`.sa-meta-mode-single`) since the value is always one of exactly two options. `showSaveDialog`'s own 13 attributes moved to a dedicated, id-guarded, injected-once stylesheet (its interpolated values are settings-only, unchanged without a page reload).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix the "Load from Disk" dialog (`showLoadFilterDialog`) rendering completely unstyled/stacked on /account/applications on its very first open — same CSP `style-src` issue as 9.99.736-9.99.738, this time in the dialog's own 49 `innerHTML`-embedded `style="..."` attributes (dialog shell) plus its internal duplicate of `createFilterHistoryWidget`'s history-dropdown code, which was rewired to reuse the exact same shared `.mb-fhw-*` classes from 9.99.738 instead of duplicating them. The dialog shell itself got its own dedicated, id-guarded `GM_addStyle()` stylesheet, safe to inject once since its interpolated dynamic values (font sizes, dropdown height) only change via a settings save, which reloads the page anyway.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix `createFilterHistoryWidget()` (the Pin/History dropdown attached to every filter input, including the global filter built during initial page load) rendering unstyled if opened on /account/applications — same CSP `style-src` issue as 9.99.736/9.99.737, found via console errors present on initial page load even though nothing looked visibly broken yet (the dropdown panel stays `display:none` until clicked). Converted its 11 `innerHTML`-embedded `style="..."` attributes to a shared, page-global `GM_addStyle()` stylesheet (guarded by id so it's only injected once regardless of how many filter inputs get a history widget). Also replaced two single-letter mnemonic underline spans (`<span style="text-decoration:underline">`) with plain `<u>` tags — no CSS needed. Also fixed one missed leftover from 9.99.736's `initSaUnicodeCharsFeature` conversion: a separate inline `style="text-align:right"` on the picker's Close row that wasn't part of the `<style>` block originally converted. NOTE: an identical duplicated `_histGlyphs` badge-rendering block still exists un-fixed inside `showLoadFilterDialog` (one of the still-deferred functions, see debug/NOTES.md) — left alone per the incremental fix-as-you-test approach.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fix the settings/configuration dialog and the changelog viewer rendering broken on /account/applications (unstyled, stacked layout) by fixing the same CSP `style-src` issue as 9.99.736, this time in the shared `VZ_MBLibrary.user.js` library (`@require`d by this script): the dialog shells and per-row setting widgets were built via `container.innerHTML` templates with ~75 inline `style="..."` attributes, which are blocked by page CSP the same as `<style>` elements. Converted to id/class selectors targeted by `GM_addStyle()`-injected stylesheets, plus added `// @grant GM_addStyle` to both `VZ_MBLibrary.user.js` and `MB_PageEnhancer.user.js` (the other consumer of this library) so `GM_addStyle` exists in their sandbox. Also replaced an `onfocus`/`onblur` inline event-handler pair in the changelog search box with a CSS `:focus` rule (also CSP-restricted). NOTE: the same `innerHTML`+`style="..."` pattern still exists in ~20 more functions within ShowAllEntityData.user.js itself (dialogs, tooltips, stats panel — see debug/NOTES.md) and will be fixed incrementally as each is found broken during further pageType testing.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Replace all 9 direct `document.createElement('style')` + `document.head.appendChild()` CSS injection sites (edit-diff table colors, sticky table headers, export/save/load dialog hover states, sidebar toggle, main toolbar chrome, relationships-icon column, Unicode character picker) with `GM_addStyle()` so injected CSS is exempt from Content-Security-Policy `style-src` restrictions (no `unsafe-inline`) that MusicBrainz's backend applies to /account/* pages. This was silently dropping these stylesheets on /account/applications, causing a raw Unicode picker dump appended below the page footer and the sub-table filter row's Cc/Rx/Ex checkboxes stacking one-per-line instead of inline.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: The 📊 unique-values filter dropdown's flag-icon decoration (9.99.728-9.99.734, covering Country/Area/Locality/Region/Location/Place/Country-Date columns) is now gated behind a new 'Show Flag Icons In Unique-Values Dropdown' setting (sa_enable_dropdown_flag_icons, in the existing 'UNIQUE COLUMN VALUES DROP DOWN CONFIGURATION' settings section), default OFF. hasFlagIcons short-circuits on the setting before doing any column-name/DOM work, so the dropdown renders exactly as it did before this feature existed unless a user opts in.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'Country/Date' unique-values filter dropdown (📊, 9.99.732/9.99.733): fixed a large empty gap between multiple flag icons in a cell, and between the last flag and the value text. Confirmed against a live cell's computed style: 'release-country' spans size their box (48x14.4px) to fit BOTH the flag AND a visible country-code abbreviation (e.g. "AT") that flagIconMap's clone deliberately strips to avoid duplicating the dropdown's own value text — baking that box's full width verbatim left a large empty gap after the now-childless icon (the PNG itself is only 16x11px). flagIconMap now reads the flag's actual pixel size directly from its background-image's PNG header (when background-size is 'auto', i.e. the image already paints at its natural size — a synchronous, exact fix, not a guess) and sizes the clone to that instead of the source's content-sized box.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'Country/Date' unique-values filter dropdown (📊, 9.99.732): fixed the dropdown's value text landing on its own new line below the flag icon instead of right behind it. flagIconMap only normalized a baked 'display: none' to 'inline-block', passing every other resolved display value through verbatim — 'release-country' spans carry extra column-alignment CSS beyond the shared '.flag' sprite rule (unlike the plain '.flag.flag-XX' spans on the Country column, which is unaffected), and a layout-context-dependent display value (e.g. block/list-item/table-cell) baked onto the icon clone forces a line break once it's cloned standalone into the dropdown item. Now only inherently context-free display values (inline/inline-block/inline-flex/inline-grid) are passed through; anything else normalizes to inline-block, same as the existing 'none' case.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 'Location', source-column 'Place' (Place-category reports, e.g. AnnotationsPlaces), and 'Country/Date' unique-values filter dropdown (📊): entries now show flag icon(s) too, matching the table cells. These are the unsplit SOURCE columns splitLocation/splitCountryDate operate on, and their native markup uses the exact same two flag shapes already fixed for Country/Area (9.99.728/9.99.731) — the gap was only that the dropdown's column-name detection never recognized these three exact names. (Deliberately NOT extended to 'Release events' — that column's flag is a script-rebuilt <li class="flag flag-XX"> with no wrapping <span>/<a>, a different shape whose decoration attempt was reverted after regressing the Country column; see git history.) Because 'Location'/'Country/Date' (unlike Country/Area) can appear inside a currently-collapsed multi-event <li>, resolveFlagVisual() now also temporarily reveals a hidden ancestor <li> around the getComputedStyle() read (restored immediately after) so a collapsed-but-not-first event's flag doesn't read back as blank.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
