items: Country column unique-values filter dropdown (📊): fixed a regression from 9.99.730 where flags looked flat/washed-out again — 9.99.730's multi-flag fix wrapped icons in a <span style="display:inline-flex"> container, an extra layout context not present in the table cell that could interfere with the native flag's baked width/height/background rendering. Removed the wrapper: each icon is now stored/cloned independently and appended as its own direct sibling (matching the original, working single-flag structure), with no behavior change for the multi-flag case.

'Area'/'Begin area'/'End area' (the unsplit source columns splitArea/splitLocation operate on) unique-values filter dropdown (📊): entries now show flag icon(s) too, matching the table cells. These columns can hold BOTH icon shapes in one cell (a Locality/Region subdivision icon followed by the Country's own flag), so column-name matching now also covers an 'rea' suffix, and countryFlagMap/areaIconMap (9.99.728/9.99.729) are unified into a single flagIconMap that scans for both shapes together in document order, so a combined cell's icons come out correctly interleaved rather than grouped by shape.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Country/MB-Locality/MB-Region unique-values filter dropdown (📊): cells holding more than one flag (a multi-event Country cell, or a Region cell where a third-party userscript decorates both a subdivision AND its sovereign state with custom flag icons, e.g. "Noord-Holland, Kingdom of the Netherlands") now show all of their flags in the dropdown instead of none. countryFlagMap/areaIconMap (see 9.99.728/9.99.729) previously keyed each flag by a label parsed from that single flag's own text, but the dropdown's unique value is always the whole cell's combined text — a multi-flag cell's combined value never matched any single flag's label, so no icon was shown at all. Both maps are now keyed by the cell's full getCleanColumnText() value (exactly how the dropdown's own value list is built) and bundle every flag found in that cell into one wrapper.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: MB-Locality/MB-Region (and Begin/End variants) unique-values filter dropdown (📊): entries now show the subdivision flag icon injected by third-party userscripts like "MusicBrainz: More Flags Everywhere", matching the icon already shown in the table cells. The dropdown's flag-decoration feature previously only recognized exact Country column names, so it never ran at all for Locality/Region columns; its cell scan was also hardcoded to elements, which would have missed the markup these third-party icons actually use even if it had run. Column-name matching is now suffix-based (matching this file's own _flagRegionColumnTrios convention for the same column family), which as a side effect also fixes the Country dropdown never decorating a 'Release country' column.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Country column unique-values filter dropdown (📊): the flag icon next to each country name now renders identically to the flag in the table cell. Previously only the span's CSS class was copied into the dropdown clone, which relies on MusicBrainz's own stylesheet cascading correctly wherever the clone lands — the dropdown panel sits outside #content/table.tbl and in a smaller font-size context, so the flag could come out looking flatter/blanker than the real one. Now the resolved visual (background sprite, size, border, vertical-align, …) is read directly from the live table-cell flag via getComputedStyle() — including a ::before/::after pseudo-element fallback — and baked as inline styles onto the dropdown clone, so it is pixel-identical regardless of where MusicBrainz's CSS rule is scoped.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Auto-expand native 'Annotation' section default configuration setting changed to false.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Removed the `sa_area_flag_region_countries` settings-menu entry (and its now-empty "🌍 AREA / LOCATION COLUMN SPLITTING" section) — the countries where a flagged subdivision link forces "Region" instead of "Locality" (United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia) are no longer end-user configurable, and are now a fixed internal `AREA_FLAG_REGION_COUNTRIES` constant instead.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Auto-expand MusicBrainz's native "Annotation" section on entity pages (e.g. /work/<mbid>): the script now clicks the native `a.annotation-toggle` "Show more..." link on load, so a long annotation is fully visible immediately instead of truncated behind an extra manual click. New setting `sa_enable_annotation_auto_expand` (default: on) in a new "📖 ANNOTATION SECTION (Entity Pages)" settings section — unrelated to the existing "📝 ANNOTATION COLUMNS" section, which only affects this script's own rendered table columns.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Added "United Kingdom", "Canada", and "Australia" to the default `sa_area_flag_region_countries` list (was just "United States"), which now reads "United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia" — all three are already-supported countries per the setting's own description (matching the flag-decorating userscripts it's designed to work with, e.g. "MusicBrainz: Canadian Province Flags Everywhere").

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Changed the default `sa_ui_row_hover_bg` (table row hover background color) from `#e2e2e2` to `#c2d2e9` — both the `configSchema` default and its two JS-side fallback literals were updated together, so they stay in sync as the setting's own description already states.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
Added a `Vote` column to the `notes-received` page type (`/edit/notes-received`), positioned right before `Edit notes` — see `9.99.720`/`9.99.721`. Extracted from the note's own `

` class (`yes`/`no`/`abstain`/`approve`; `""` means no vote was cast alongside the note), the same element `User`/`Date/Time` already parse. MusicBrainz normally shows this via an adjacent empty `
` styled entirely through its own site CSS (a background-image keyed off the `

`'s class) — unavailable to a detached/fetched page, same unreliability `_editActionBgColor`'s JSDoc already documents for edit-type colors — so a new `_NOTE_VOTE_GLYPHS` lookup (👍 yes, 👎 no, ➖ abstain, ✔️ approve) supplies its own fixed glyph instead, prefixed onto the vote-outcome text. Verified via jsdom against the real `debug/notes-received.html` snapshot: all four non-empty vote classes present on that page extract correctly, and the no-vote case (empty class) correctly falls back to `N/A`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
Added `User` and `Date/Time` columns to the `notes-received` page type (`/edit/notes-received`), positioned between `Edit action` and `Edit notes` — see `9.99.720`. Both are parsed from the note's own `

` (e.g. `

…tigerman325
2025-02-04 17:29 GMT+1

`) — `User` clones the author's `` link (avatar + username, preserving the hyperlink), `Date/Time` clones the `` link (preserving its deep link to that specific edit note). Both extractions ignore the optional `
` MusicBrainz sometimes inserts between them (present when the note's `

` carries a vote-outcome class like `yes`/`no`/`abstain`/`approve`), since they query for the two anchors directly rather than relying on sibling position.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
Added a new `notes-received` page type for `/edit/notes-received` ("Recent notes left on your edits") — e.g. the "Show all Notes Received" button. This page's `div.edit-list` blocks are much sparser than every other edits-listing page: each wraps only the edit-header `

` plus a single nested `div.edit-note` — none of `.edit-description`/`p.subheader`/`.edit-details`/the multi-note `.edit-notes` wrapper — so only 3 columns exist: `Edit#`, `Edit action`, `Edit notes`. When an edit received multiple notes, MusicBrainz repeats the WHOLE `div.edit-list` block (header + that one note) once per note rather than nesting multiple notes under one heading, so this produces one row per (edit, note) pair. New `_buildNotesReceivedRow()`/`applyNotesReceivedToTable()` (gated on a new `features.notesReceivedToTable: true`, wired into the same pre-processing slot as `applyEditsToTable`/`applyListToTable`, including the fetched-page and ambiguous-pagination-early-stop handling) build this deliberately instead of reusing `applyEditsToTable`/`_buildEditRow`, which assume columns this page doesn't have. Unlike `user-edits`/`user-open-edits`, this page already has a native `

Recent notes left on your edits

`, so no `renameH2ToH1` is needed — just the usual `insertH2: 'Edit Notes'` anchor, same as base `edits`. Also extended the `@include` header's `edit/subscribed(_editors)?` alternative to `edit/(?:subscribed(?:_editors)?|notes-received)`, which didn't cover this URL before. Verified via jsdom against the real `debug/notes-received.html` snapshot, including the duplicate-block (multi-note) case.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
Fixed `user-edits`/`user-open-edits` cramming the entire action-button toolbar, row-count badge, CAA toggle, and filter bar onto the same native heading (see `debug/user-edits-wrong.org`). Both pages render no native `

` at all — their only heading is a `

Edits by

` / `

Open edits by

` — so the page-load button-toolbar injection and the post-render filter/count/CAA-toggle injection both resolved to that one element, which then also got made collapsible (every `

` is fair game for `makeH2sCollapsible()`, unlike an `

` page title). Added a new `renameH2ToH1: true` feature (mirroring the existing `renameH2ToH3: true` used by tag pages) that promotes the native `

` to `

` — carrying the already-injected button toolbar with it, since the promotion moves child nodes rather than discarding them — and gave both page types `insertH2: 'Edits'` / `insertH2: 'Open edits'` so a fresh, dedicated `

` gets injected as the actual filter/count/CAA-toggle anchor, matching every other single-table page type's h1-title/h2-anchor split. New `applyRenameH2ToH1()` (mirrors `applyRenameH2ToH3()`) excludes any `

` nested inside a `div.edit-list` block — every real edit on an as-yet-unconverted edits-listing page carries its own native `

Edit #NNNNNN - Action

` heading, and promoting those too (confirmed via a jsdom run against the real `debug/edits-by-vzell.html` snapshot: 51 `

`s instead of 1, before this exclusion was added) would have been a much worse regression than the one being fixed. Verified via jsdom against both real snapshots: exactly one `

` and one `

` result, in the correct order, before `applyEditsToTable` removes the `div.edit-list` blocks.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added two new page types for a user's own edit-listing pages: `user-edits` (`/user/<username>/edits`) and `user-open-edits` (`/user/<username>/edits/open`) — e.g. `/user/vzell/edits`, `/user/vzell/edits/open`. Both reuse the exact same `editsToTable`/`unboundedPagination`/`collapsableColumns`/`addCAA` pipeline as the existing `edits` page type (see `9.99.719` for the `renameH2ToH1`/`insertH2` heading setup these two needed on top of that, which the base `edits` page type does not). Also extended the `@include` header's `/user/<username>/...` regex to cover `edits`/`edits/open`, which it did not match before.

Fixed the two new page types failing to initialize at all ("Required elements not found. Terminating.", `hasHeader: false`) — confirmed live on `/user/vzell/edits`. Both pages render no `<h1>` whatsoever (only the native `<h2>` mentioned above), but every branch of the init header-detection chain required an `<h1>`, so `headerContainer` stayed `null` and the script aborted before doing anything. Added a `headerContainer` fallback scoped specifically to `user-edits`/`user-open-edits` (not a blanket "no h1 → use any h2" rule, to avoid masking a real missing-header case on some other page type) that falls back to the page's `<h2>` when no `<h1>` is found. Every other consumer of `headerContainer` already degrades gracefully to "use headerContainer itself" when no ancestor `<h1>` exists, so no other code needed to change.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the `edits` page type's column filter highlighting matches in the wrong column — e.g. filtering the "Edit notes" column highlighted "alias" inside "Edit details" instead, or (with a trailing comma in the filter string) narrowed to the correct row but highlighted nothing at all. `highlightText()` was scanning `row.querySelectorAll('td')` and using its flat, recursive index to find the target column's cell, but that numbering doesn't match `row.cells`-based indexing (used by `testRowMatch()`/`getColFilters`) once any earlier cell contains nested real `<td>`/`<th>` elements — which every `_detableify()`'d "Edit details" cell does (per its own JSDoc, `<td>`/`<th>` are deliberately kept real for `rowspan`/`colspan`). `highlightText()` now resolves the target column via `row.cells[targetColIndex]` directly (matching the same numbering the match logic already uses) and lets `highlightCrossTag()` walk that cell's own subtree, which still finds nested matches correctly. The global-filter case (no target column) is unchanged. Row matching itself was already correct — only the highlight placement was wrong. See `debug/filter-bug.org`, `debug/editNotes-filter-bug.html`.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Reordered the `edits` page type's columns to group related content together: `Edit#`, `Edit action`, `Edit details`, `Edit notes`, `Entered from release`, `By artist`, `Edit by`, `My vote`, `Vote count`, `Closed/Approved`, `Voting`, `Edit status` (was: `Edit#`, `Edit action`, `Edit by`, `My vote`, `Vote count`, `Closed/Approved`, `Voting`, `Edit status`, `Entered from release`, `By artist`, `Edit details`, `Edit notes` — see `9.99.715`). `_buildEditRow()`'s cell-building order was moved to match, since cells are appended positionally against the `headers` array; no other code references these columns by index (`collapsableColumns`, `addCAA`, and the prose-column checks all key off the column name), so nothing else needed to change.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added a new `edits` page type covering MusicBrainz edit-listing pages (`/search/edits`, `/<entity>/<mbid>/edits`, `/edit/subscribed`, `/edit/subscribed_editors`) — including the required `@include` header directives for all five URL shapes. Each `<div class="edit-list">` block is converted into a table row with 12 columns (Edit#, Edit action, Edit by, My vote, Vote count, Closed/Approved, Voting, Edit status, Entered from release, By artist, Edit details, Edit notes) via a new `applyEditsToTable()` DOM pre-processing step, mirroring `applyListToTable()`'s pattern. `Edit details` and `Edit notes` are collapsable/height-clamped the same way the Annotation column is — with a manual "more/less" toggle per cell plus a column-header "collapse all"/"expand all" button always available — but via independent `sa_edits_enable_details_collapse`/`sa_edits_enable_notes_collapse` settings controlling only the *initial* expand state: both default to off, so cells start expanded (unlike Annotation's default-on `sa_enable_annotation_collapse`, which starts collapsed); a fresh `Edits` `<h2>` filterline is injected so the single-table collapsible-section/filter-bar infrastructure has something to anchor to. `Entered from release`/`By artist` are populated by scanning for the entity-linked-to-artist-credit shape wherever it appears (not just the dedicated `.entered-from` block), so they cover far more edit types than just relationship edits (e.g. "Edit recording", "Edit medium", "Add cover art", ...), and get inline CAA cover-art thumbnails via `features.addCAA`. `Closed/Approved` covers both MusicBrainz's `Closed:` and `Approved:` `.edit-expiration` prefixes (the latter used for auto-editor edits that passed voting without ever being formally "closed").

Handled MusicBrainz's edit-listing pagination not always exposing a true last page. Small result sets either have no pagination at all or a complete, gap-free widget that already reveals the real last page (both handled correctly by the existing DOM-based detection); only the double-ellipsis milestone-window widget MusicBrainz shows for large/uncounted result sets ("Found at least N edits", confirmed live to keep growing past page 1000) is actually ambiguous. A new `_hasAmbiguousEditsPagination()` check now decides dynamically, per page, whether to trust the normal detection or fall back to a safety-capped fetch-until-empty-page strategy (`features.unboundedPagination`, `sa_max_page` setting) — scoped entirely to `editsToTable` pages, no behavior change for any other page type.

Colored the "Edit#" and "Edit action" columns by edit category (Add/Edit/Remove/Merge/Other) and open-vs-closed state, matching the well-known "MusicBrainz: Colourful edits" userscript's classification — but computed independently from `.edit-header`'s own class list rather than reading any inline/computed style (MusicBrainz sets no inline background there itself; visible color on a live page comes from its own class-based site CSS and/or that userscript if installed, neither of which is reliably readable from a detached, stylesheet-less fetched page). New `_editActionBgColor()` plus 11 configurable `sa_edits_color_*` color-picker settings (`🎨 EDITS PAGE COLORS` section, `sa_enable_edits_type_colors` master toggle) defaulting to that userscript's palette. `applyStickyColumn` learned a generic `data-mb-custom-cell-bg` per-cell marker — respected in both its sticky-cell and non-sticky-cell background computation — so a colored cell survives its zebra-striping-preserving cleanup pass without the function needing to know anything about the `edits` page type.

Colored old/new value diff cells inside the "Edit details" column's compare tables (e.g. a track-title edit's before/after row), matching MusicBrainz's own site CSS (`table.details td.new`/`td.old`) — which no longer matches anything once `.edit-details` has been de-tableified, since it requires a real `<table>` ancestor. `_ensureDetableifyStyle()` now also injects `!important` `.mb-dt-table td.new`/`.mb-dt-table td.old` rules (needed to reliably beat MusicBrainz's own zebra-striping CSS, which reaches these deeply-nested cells too on "even" rows) using the `.mb-dt-table` marker class `_detableify()` already stamps on the converted element. Configurable via `sa_enable_edits_diff_colors` (default on) / `sa_edits_color_diff_new` (`#e4fbe4`) / `sa_edits_color_diff_old` (`#fbe3e4`), defaults copied directly from MusicBrainz's own stylesheet.

Added zebra striping to nested compare tables inside "Edit details" (e.g. a medium edit's Old/New tracklist grid) — the `odd`/`even` classes survive `_detableify()`'s conversion untouched, but nothing colored them since MusicBrainz's own zebra CSS can't reach de-tableified content either. New `.mb-dt-tr.odd`/`.mb-dt-tr.even` rules in `_ensureDetableifyStyle()` set the background on both the row and its direct `.mb-dt-cell` children (not the row alone, which relies on painting through cells with no background of their own and silently fails to show on "even"/grey rows the moment anything sets a competing background directly on the cell) — matching how MusicBrainz's own equivalent rule always colors cells directly. Configurable via `sa_edits_color_zebra_odd` (`#ffffff`) / `sa_edits_color_zebra_even` (`#f2f2f2`).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed `applyInsertH2` failing to insert (or mis-placing) its page-level filterline heading whenever native content it runs before-processing (e.g. a wiki-formatted edit note, which can contain its own `== Edits ==` sub-heading and/or a native `<h3 class="owner">`) happened to collide with the chosen label or heading level. The idempotency guard now stamps and checks a `data-mb-injected-h2` marker instead of matching by text content (position/timing-independent, can't be fooled by unrelated headings); the "before first h3" placement fallback now also excludes headings nested inside `div.edit-list`, alongside the existing `table.tbl` exclusion. General fix to shared insertH2 infrastructure, not specific to the `edits` page type.

Fixed `rowspan`/`colspan` being silently dropped from `.edit-details` compare tables (a relationship diff's old/new values rendering side-by-side instead of stacked; a medium edit's "Old tracklist"/"New tracklist" 4-column group headers collapsing to one column each). `_detableify()` was converting `<th>`/`<td>` into `<div>`s, but `rowSpan`/`colSpan` are DOM properties only real table-cell elements expose. `<th>`/`<td>` are now left as real elements (only `<table>`/`<thead>`/`<tbody>`/`<tfoot>`/`<tr>` are converted, which is all the nested-table-corruption fix ever needed).

Fixed the "By artist" column including trailing relationship-attribute description text after the artist credit (e.g. "... has a discography entry at <url> [info]", "... can be purchased for download at <url> [info]"). `_splitEnteredFrom` now stops right after the first element following "by" (the artist-credit `<bdi>`) instead of taking the rest of the sentence.

Fixed "Edit details"/"Edit notes" having no way to manually collapse a cell (or the whole column) at all once uncollapsed-by-default landed — the earlier implementation gated off the entire clamp/toggle mechanism when the new setting was false, not just the initial visual state. The mechanism now always stays active; the setting only controls whether cells start expanded (the default) or collapsed, via a one-time `expandedCells` pre-population on the first render after a fetch that a later manual collapse correctly survives across sort/filter re-renders.

Fixed the global "collapse all"/"expand all" button and the per-column header collapse toggle both staying stuck on "Expand all" (`aria-expanded="false"`) even when a column's cells had actually started expanded — both were unconditionally hardcoded to the collapsed initial state in `initCollapsableColumns`. They now track whether any cell in the relevant column(s) started expanded and reflect that in their initial glyph/`aria-expanded`/title, same as an individual cell's own toggle already did.

Fixed `sa_ui_row_hover_bg` (the table row hover background color, used by `applyStickyColumn` for every table this script renders, not just edits) having no `configSchema` entry at all despite being read in code — it was permanently stuck on its `#e2e2e2` JS-side fallback and never actually adjustable via the settings menu. Also added a CSS `tr:hover .mb-dt-table .mb-dt-cell` rule using this setting: the existing JS-driven hover handler only ever touches a row's direct `<td>` children, so it never reached deeply-nested cells inside de-tableified "Edit details" content, which MusicBrainz's own native hover CSS was darkening instead (reaching arbitrary depth, same pattern as its zebra rule) — making their thin `#ddd` borders nearly invisible.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 9.99.713 diagnostics revealed the real root cause of `initAreaFlagRegionObserver` never finding a Locality/Region/Country column trio: on `tableMode: 'single'` pages, `startFetchingProcess()` calls `renderFinalTable()` — which called `initAreaFlagRegionObserver()` at its very end — *before* its own subsequent `cleanupHeaders()` pass, the step that actually injects the `MB-Locality`/`MB-Region`/`Country` synthetic `<th>`s. So the observer's trio-finder always scanned a thead that still only had the raw native headers (e.g. 'Area', 'Begin area'), on every page, not just page 2+ — matching the console log exactly. Moved the `initAreaFlagRegionObserver()` call out of `renderFinalTable()` and into `startFetchingProcess()`, right after its `cleanupHeaders()` pass, so the synthetic headers reliably exist first. `renderGroupedTable()`'s own call (for `tableMode: 'multi'` pages) was already correctly ordered after its per-group `cleanupHeaders()` calls and needed no change.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: 9.99.712's `initAreaFlagRegionObserver` still didn't correct page 2..Max rows even though the flag icon was confirmed to visually render for them. The observer only watched `attributes` mutations (the flag-decorating userscript setting `data-flag-processed` on the existing anchor); if it instead replaces the anchor/cell subtree wholesale (e.g. via `innerHTML`), that fires no attribute-mutation event on the new node at all, so no code path ever caught it. Now also watches `childList` mutations, and additionally runs a bounded set of full re-checks (immediately, then at 500/1500/3000/6000ms after render) as a belt-and-suspenders fallback independent of which DOM strategy the userscript uses. Also added `sa_enable_debug_logging`-gated diagnostics at each decision point (no trio found on a table, cell missing, country not resolved, country not in the list) so a next investigation has concrete evidence instead of another guess.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: The 9.99.711 country-specific Locality/Region override only worked for the current page's rows: pages 2..Max are parsed from a detached `DOMParser` document (see `fetchHtml`) that flag-decorating userscripts ("More Flags Everywhere" / "Canadian Province Flags Everywhere", @Lotheric) never touch, so `splitLocation`/`splitArea` never saw the subdivision flag icon at extraction time for those rows — even though the userscript does correctly decorate them once they're inserted into the live table. Added a `MutationObserver` (`initAreaFlagRegionObserver`, installed after every `renderFinalTable`/`renderGroupedTable`, mirroring the existing jesus2099-treleases observer) that watches for the `data-flag-processed` attribute the flag userscripts stamp on processed anchors, and moves the Locality value to Region reactively the moment it's decorated — regardless of which page it came from. The correction is applied to both the visible row and its master row (`allRows`/`groupedRows`), so it also survives later sort/filter re-renders.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: `splitLocation`/`splitArea` now apply an optional country-specific override: if the area link that would become `Locality` (the first/most specific one) is decorated with a subdivision flag icon by a separately-installed userscript (e.g. "MusicBrainz: More Flags Everywhere" or "MusicBrainz: Canadian Province Flags Everywhere", @Lotheric) — meaning no city/locality was ever entered, only a bare state/province — it is routed to `Region` instead. New setting `sa_area_flag_region_countries` (🌍 AREA / LOCATION COLUMN SPLITTING section) lists which countries this applies to, matched against the row's resolved Country; defaults to `United States` only. Leave blank to disable entirely. Fixes e.g. a US artist whose only Area is "Florida" showing up under `MB-Locality` instead of `MB-Region` on `/area/<mbid>/artists`.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `splitArea` (used on `Area`/`Begin area`/`End area`, e.g. on `/area//artists`) mis-identified the country on rows decorated by the separately-installed "Canadian Province Flags Everywhere" userscript (@Lotheric): its whole-cell scan picked the first node whose subtree contained a `.flag` class as "the country", which wrongly matched the province's sibling `` icon when it preceded the real `` country span — so `Country` showed the province flag icon and `MB-Area` ended up with the real country text stuck in it instead. Fixed by rewriting `splitArea` to route each `/area/` link individually via the same per-anchor `a.closest('.flag')` check already used by `splitLocation` (only the anchor's own ancestor chain, never a sibling), extracted into a new shared helper `_routeAreaLink`.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: `splitArea`'s synthetic `MB-Area`/`MB-Begin area`/`MB-End area` columns are now further split into `MB-Locality`/`MB-Region` pairs (and `MB-Begin locality`/`MB-Begin region`, `MB-End locality`/`MB-End region`), mirroring the `Locality`/`Region` split added to `splitLocation` in 9.99.708: the first (most specific) `/area/` link is Locality, every subsequent one is Region, comma-joined. Same positional rationale as 9.99.708 — MusicBrainz area links carry no type information and the chain depth varies per place, not per country.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: `report-detail` (e.g. `/report/AnnotationsPlaces`) now also runs `splitLocation` on the `Place` column, not just `Location` — the native `Place` cell on Place-category reports has the same "place in area-chain[, flag country]" shape. The extracted place-name column is called `MB-Place` rather than `Place` so it doesn't collide with the native `Place` column (which still carries the full place name + area/country chain unchanged); `Locality`/`Region`/`Country` are shared with the existing `Location`-based split.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: `splitLocation`'s synthetic `Area` column is now split into `Locality` and `Region`: `Locality` is the first (most specific) `/area/` link between the Place and Country — typically a city or neighbourhood — and `Region` is every subsequent `/area/` link, comma-joined in the existing broad-to-specific order (e.g. county/borough + state). MusicBrainz area links carry no type information and the hierarchy depth between Place and Country varies per place (not per country), so this is a positional split rather than a true City/County/State classification; a fully semantic split would require an MB API lookup per area (800+ distinct areas on a typical large Events table) with caching, which is out of scope for this synchronous, DOM-only extractor. Updated all 7 `splitLocation` call sites, their `collapsableColumns` lists, and the synthetic-column header tooltips accordingly.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Consolidated the 48 `@match` lines (24 path patterns × 2 domains) in the userscript header into 2 `@include` regex lines, mirroring the file's existing two `@include` lines used for MBID-entity pages. Also dropped `/cdstub/browse` as a `@match` entry since it was already a strict subset of `/cdstub/*`. No functional change — every page the script previously ran on, it still runs on.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added support for an eighth new page type: individual auto-editor election pages (`/election/<n>`), as `'auto-editor-election'`. Its "Votes cast" table is already native `table.tbl`-shaped with an existing `<h2>` label, so — like `cd-stub` — no `listToTable`/`insertH2` conversion is needed. The separate `<table class="properties">` (election details) is left untouched.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: privileged-accounts (`/privileged`, 9.99.704): the relocated intro/count paragraphs now collapse and uncollapse together with their associated sub-table when clicking the h3 header, via a new shared `_syncGroupIntroVisibility()` helper wired into every sub-table visibility toggle path (per-h3 click, Ctrl+Click toggle-all, the master toggle button, and the Ctrl+3 keyboard shortcut).

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: Renamed pageType `'cd-stub'` (`/cdstub/browse`) to `'top-cd-stub'` to free up the name for a new, more specific page type — see below.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added support for a seventh new page type: individual CD stub pages (`/cdstub/<disc-id>`), as `'cd-stub'`. Its Tracklist table is already native `table.tbl`-shaped with an existing `<h2>` label, so — unlike every other page type added this session — no `listToTable`/`insertH2` conversion is needed; the script just applies its filter/sort UI directly. The page's separate `<table class="details">` (Disc ID information) and `div#sidebar` are left untouched.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items:
privileged-accounts (`/privileged`, 9.99.703): fixed each section's descriptive/count paragraphs (e.g. "Auto-editors are trusted users who have been given …") rendering bunched together after all 7 sub-tables instead of each staying right before its own table. `renderGroupedTable`'s cleanup pass only ever removed `h3`/`table.tbl` elements, leaving those `

`s orphaned in their original position while the rebuilt h3/table pairs were inserted as one contiguous block elsewhere. Structure K now stashes them on the table's `dataset.mbIntroHtml`, `startFetchingProcess` carries that onto `group.introHtml`, and `renderGroupedTable` re-inserts them in a `.mb-group-intro` wrapper directly between each `h3` and its `table`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items:
Added support for a sixth new page type: Privileged user accounts (`/privileged`). Its 7 category sections (Auto-editors, Relationship editors, Transclusion editors, Location editors, Banner message editors, Account administrators, Bots) render each editor list as a plain `

` of comma-glued `` links rather than a `

    `, so a new Structure K was added to `applyListToTable` — it identifies the correct paragraph per section (the one containing `/user/` links, not by position) and converts it to a one-column "Editor" table, splitting by walking the `` elements rather than parsing the "," separator text (at least one MusicBrainz username itself contains a literal comma).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed native column headers containing a leading digit (e.g. auto-elections' "1st seconder" / "2nd seconder") being mangled to "st seconder" / "nd seconder" in both the rendered header text and `data-col-name`. The shared icon-stripping regex in `makeTableSortableUnified` blindly stripped ASCII `0-9` from raw, undecorated header text — removed there (only decorative icon glyphs and Unicode superscript multi-sort-order digits are stripped now) and made `getCleanColName` prefer the already-correct `th.dataset.colName` over re-deriving from text that later also carries the live uniq-count badge digits.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: cd-stub (`/cdstub/browse`): the informational "Added N years ago, last modified M years ago" row that MusicBrainz renders after every real row is no longer silently dropped — it is now folded into the preceding row as a disambiguation comment (`(…)`) appended to the Title cell, mirroring the existing `cdtoc` tracklist-row interception pattern in `startFetchingProcess`. `cd-stub` now also declares `extractMainColumn: 'Title'`, so the merged text populates dedicated MB-Name/Comment columns.

Instrument list (`/instruments`, 9.99.701): added a new `Name_Comment_Description` extractor that splits each family's combined cell (name link, optional short comment, optional longer free-text description — which may itself contain nested instrument links) into separate Name / Comment / Description columns, wired per-family via `entityFeatures` (mirrors the `tag-value` per-group columnExtractor pattern). Required extending two pageType gates in `startFetchingProcess` / `renderGroupedTable` (row-level colIdx re-resolution, and per-group thead rebuild) to also cover `instrument-list`, alongside the existing `tag-value` / `user-tag-value` / `user-ratings` pageTypes.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added support for five new page types: Auto-editor elections (`/elections`), Genre list (`/genres`), Top CD stubs (`/cdstub/browse`), Edit types (`/doc/Edit_Types`), and Instrument list (`/instruments`). All five reuse existing `applyListToTable` conversion structures — Structure G (bare `<ul>` → one-column table, extended for `genres-list`) and Structure J (repeated `<h2>+<ul>` category sections → one table per section, extended for `edit-types` and `instrument-list` with a per-section column name instead of `reports-index`'s fixed literal). `cd-stub`'s informational 'Added N years ago…' filler rows are skipped by the existing generic single-cell/colSpan>1 row-extraction guard with no new code.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Unique-value dropdown (📊): value items now render a checkbox (☑/☐) and support multi-select, OR'ing every checked value together as a single column filter. Clicking a value (or Enter on a keyboard-focused value) toggles its checkbox and keeps the dropdown open instead of replacing the filter and closing. Selecting checkboxes is mutually exclusive with typing plain text or picking a 'Cell structure' entry in the same column — whichever is used last wins and clears the other.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added support for the `musicbrainz.eu` mirror domain alongside `musicbrainz.org`: both `@include` regex directives and all 18 `@match` directives in the userscript header now cover `.eu`; the Expand Release Groups feature's absolute-href selectors (`isExpandRGsPage()`, `initExpandRGsFeature()`) now also match `musicbrainz.eu/release` links; and `_picardBuildTaggerUrl()` now builds its resource URL from `window.location.origin` instead of a hardcoded `https://musicbrainz.org`, so the Picard tagger button sends the correct domain regardless of which MusicBrainz mirror the page was loaded from.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added support for `/account/applications` (the editor's OAuth2 'Authorized applications' and 'Developer applications' page), modelled on the `user-collections` groupByH3 pattern — a 'Show all Applications' button consolidates both native h2-headed tables into one filterable/sortable view.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added `dateTimeParts` column extractor — splits a "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" timestamp (e.g. report-detail's native "Last edited" column) into separate date and time synthetic columns.

Added `numberOfChars` column extractor — counts a source cell's whitespace-normalised visible-text length into a single right-aligned numeric synthetic column (e.g. an "Annotation chars" column for sorting/filtering annotations by size).
report-detail now uses both: 'Last edited' → ['Last edited date', 'Last edited time'], 'Annotation' → ['Annotation chars'] (added to `integerColumns` for right-aligned numeric sorting).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed a syntax error (missing comma) in report-detail's `integerColumns` array introduced by a manual edit, which broke the entire userscript.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed multi-row list cells' count-based '▶ N ▤' collapse toggle (Catalog#, Label, Authors, …) becoming permanently unresponsive to clicks right after it was first built — 9.99.695's `_findCellListItems()` walked a cell's list up to the `<td>` checking for competing sibling text, but didn't exclude the toggle span it had itself just appended as a sibling of that list; the toggle's own glyph/count text (e.g. '▶3▤') was seen as competing prose on every subsequent call, so the very next click (or column-header/global mass-toggle) silently found zero list items and did nothing.

`_findCellListItems()` now excludes anything matching `_CLEAN_STRIP_SEL` (which already covers `.mb-cell-collapse-toggle` and other injected/decorative spans) from that sibling check, not just `<script>`/`<style>`/`<ul>`/`<ol>`.

Single-item list cells (e.g. a work with exactly one author) are no longer wrapped as a 'prose' cell — they render untouched with no toggle, as before this feature existed, instead of sometimes getting an incorrect 'more'/'less' toggle.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the 'Authors' column on report-detail pages (e.g. https://musicbrainz.org/report/AnnotationsWorks) regressing to the prose-cell 'more'/'less' toggle instead of its correct count-based '▶ N ▤' list toggle. 9.99.688's `:scope > ul > li` tightening assumed every script-generated multi-row column places its `<ul>` as a direct child of `<td>`, but native MusicBrainz 'Authors' markup wraps its list one level deeper (`<td><script type="application/json">…</script><div class="artist-roles-container"><ul class="artist-roles">…`), so the tightened selector no longer found it and the cell fell through to being treated as free-form prose.

Replaced the direct-child-only list lookup everywhere with a new `_findCellListItems()` that walks from a cell's first `<ul>`/`<ol>` up to the `<td>`, treating `<script>`/`<style>` tags and sibling lists as non-competing, but still correctly rejecting a wiki-rendered list embedded inside actual 'Annotation' prose text (real sibling text anywhere along that walk disqualifies it).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed the 'Annotation' column header's collapse-toggle count (`.mb-col-collapse-count`, e.g. showing '5' while its own tooltip correctly said '496') and the unique-values dropdown's 'Cell structure' collapsed/expanded counts being wrong for prose (free-text) collapsable columns. Several places independently recomputed 'is this cell multi-row?' using an unscoped `cell.querySelectorAll('ul > li')` check with no awareness of prose cells at all — it only matched cells whose Annotation text happened to contain an embedded wiki bullet/numbered list, and otherwise ignored the actual (much larger) set of collapsed prose cells entirely. Also affected — and fixed — the same way: the multi-row state column filter ('collapsed'/'expanded'/'any' entries in the unique-values dropdown actually filtering the table) and the developer stats panel's per-column multi-row count.

Added `_classifyCollapseCell()` as the single shared implementation of this check (list cells via `:scope > ul > li`, prose cells via presence of a `.mb-cell-collapse-toggle`), replacing the four independent, inconsistent implementations.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Ctrl+Click on an 'Annotation'-style cell's ▶/▼ collapse toggle now also expands (uncollapses) every nested wiki `<h2>` sub-heading inside that cell, instead of just expanding the cell's own text preview.
Ctrl+Click on the 'Annotation' column's header collapse toggle now also expands every nested wiki `<h2>` sub-heading in every cell of the column, in addition to expanding all cells.

Both toggles' tooltips now explain the Ctrl+Click behaviour — shown only when the cell/column actually contains a nested wiki sub-heading, so the hint doesn't appear on plain annotations with no headings to expand.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Added `sa_annotation_h2_bg` / `sa_annotation_h2_color` settings for the text color of wiki-rendered `<h2>` sub-headings nested inside table cells (e.g. 'Annotation' column sub-sections like '== Known performances =='), separate from the existing page-level H2 section-header colors. Defaults (#e3f2fd background / #1565c0 text) are chosen to sit quietly against the grey/white alternating row backgrounds and to read as related to (rather than compete with) the standard blue hyperlink color that often appears in annotation text.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed wiki-rendered `<h2>` sub-headings inside 'Annotation'-style column cells (e.g. '== Known performances ==') becoming permanently non-collapsible after the first sort or filter. renderFinalTable()/renderGroupedTable() replace table rows with cloneNode(true) copies on every sort/filter re-render, which copies the collapsed-h2 marker classes and icon but not the click listener — makeH2sCollapsible() (which normally sets these up) only runs after the initial full-page render and a disk-load, never after a sort/filter, so the cloned headings looked processed but were inert. A new `_rewireNestedTableH2Toggles()` re-attaches working click handlers to these nested headings after every sort/filter re-render, without touching page-level h2 sections (Genres, Tags, Relationships, …) or resetting any section's manually-toggled state.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Made the collapsed-cell clamp height of 'Annotation'-style columns configurable via a new `sa_annotation_column_max_height_em` setting (default 5.6em, ~4 lines — the same value used in 9.99.688), instead of a hardcoded CSS value.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Added a new '📝 ANNOTATION COLUMNS' settings section: `sa_enable_annotation_collapse` (checkbox, default on) toggles the 9.99.688 free-text collapse/height-clamp behaviour on/off for 'Annotation'-style columns, and `sa_annotation_column_max_width` (number, default 480) makes the auto-resize width cap configurable.

The auto-resize width cap for these columns is now always active, independent of `sa_enable_annotation_collapse` — even with collapsing disabled, a long annotation no longer stretches the column to its unwrapped width.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Annotation-style columns declared in `collapsableColumns` (report-detail's AnnotationsPlaces/AnnotationsReleases sub-reports, the instrument 'Annotations' report category) are now collapsible: free-text cells are height-clamped behind a ▶/▼ 'show more/less' toggle, sharing the same column-header and global mass-toggle buttons, filter-match highlighting, and expand-state persistence as existing list-type collapsable columns (Catalog#, Label, …).
Auto-resize (↔️ Resize / Ctrl+R) no longer sizes these free-text columns to a paragraph's unwrapped single-line width — their measured width is now capped, matching the new height-clamped rendering.

Tightened `collapsableColumns`' list-cell detection to only match a `<ul><li>` that is a direct child of the `<td>`, fixing a latent bug where a wiki-rendered bullet/numbered list embedded inside free-text annotation prose could be mistaken for a script-generated multi-row list and partially hidden.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Split 'Location' column in 'report-detail' pageTypes.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: splitLocation: the synthetic 'Area' column now preserves the Canadian-province flag icon injected by the 'MusicBrainz: Canadian Province Flags Everywhere' userscript (@Lotheric), instead of dropping it during the Location → Place/Area/Country split.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: report-detail pages: removed the native 'Show only results that are in my subscribed entities.' list item from the report description block — redundant with the existing 'Show all (subscribed only)' button.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: report-detail pages: applyInsertH2() no longer picks an <h3> nested inside table.tbl cells (e.g. wiki-rendered '=== Heading ===' markup in an Annotation-column cell on the report's native first page, before any DOM pre-processing runs) as the insertion anchor for the synthetic 'Report' <h2>. Confirmed via live debug logs as the root cause of AnnotationsPlaces/AnnotationsReleases rendering with no discoverable page-level heading: the <h2> was actually being created, but nested deep inside a table cell after the data table instead of before it, so updateH2Count's 'table follows h2' search never found it. The report-detail-scoped self-heal added in v9.99.682 remains in place as a defensive backstop.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: _relocateTrailingH2Sections() no longer treats <h2> headings nested inside table.tbl cells (e.g. wiki-rendered '== Heading ==' markup in Annotation-column text) as page-level trailing sections — previously every matching row's cell content was physically relocated out of the table to just before the page header, corrupting Annotation columns on report-detail's AnnotationsEvents/AnnotationsReleaseGroups reports and on 'search' pages for entity type Annotation.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: report-detail pages ('/report/<Name>'): CAA/EAA cover-/event-art detection now scans only the specific Release/Release group/Event column designated by the report's addCAA/addEAA feature instead of the whole row — fixes missing big-picture stripes when that column happened to become the sticky column (ReleasedTooEarlyForLabel, ReleasesWithUnlikelyLanguageScript, SetInDifferentRG, EventSequenceNotInSeries), and fixes wrong/spurious CAA or EAA indicators picked up from incidental entity links inside free-text Annotation cells (AnnotationsEvents, AnnotationsReleaseGroups). Scoped strictly to the report-detail page type; no other page definition's artwork detection changes.

report-detail pages: the 'Report' <h2> heading (and the row-count/filter-bar infrastructure anchored to it) is now defensively re-asserted if missing, mitigating a rendering issue that left some sub-reports (AnnotationsPlaces, AnnotationsReleases) without any heading at all. Scoped strictly to the report-detail page type. Root cause identified and fixed in v9.99.684; this self-heal remains as a backstop.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Merged discography view sub-tables (release-group pages) now stay fully sorted when their rows are combined from multiple underlying category groups — sorting the visible table previously only reordered one contributing group, leaving the others spliced in at their original position.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Sort keys (and the non-regex global filter) no longer include leaked inline CAA/EAA artwork markup — cache-hint emoji, thumbnail placeholders, count badges, the row-expand glyph. Whether a row's inline thumbnail had resolved from cache by render time previously determined its sort position ahead of the actual visible text, splitting otherwise-correctly-ordered rows into wrongly-ordered clusters on any table with inline cover-art/event-art thumbnails.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: report-detail pages now get a collapsible "Report" <h2> section header (row-count badge, global filter bar) matching other single-table page types, which also unlocks the CAA/EAA cover-art/event-art toggle button and big-picture image stripe above the table when a report has a Release/Release group or Event column.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: `addCAA`/`addEAA` page-definition features now accept an array of candidate column names (e.g. `addCAA: ['Release', 'Release group']`), so column-agnostic page types like `report-detail` (117 differently-shaped reports) can render inline cover/event-art thumbnails regardless of which of several possible columns a given report table actually has. `report-detail`'s `addCAA` now uses `['Release', 'Release group']`.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Add feature support for pageType 'report-detail'.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Unconditionally remove the bulk-tag checkbox column injected by the third-party "MusicBrainz Nuclear Tags" userscript (`<th class="elephant-tag-col">`) before rendering the consolidated table, so it no longer shifts column alignment on pages like series releases.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Added support for MusicBrainz report pages: the /reports index (all 117 reports across 14 categories, rendered as a filterable multi-table view) and individual /report/<ReportName> pages (paginated, with buttons to switch between all results and results limited to your subscribed entities). Column sets are report-specific and auto-detected generically; the DuplicateArtists-style 'merge queue' checkbox column renders but is non-functional (known limitation — the table is detached from its native <form>).

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed sticky column header cell remaining see-through when sort value-change shading is active (follow-up to v9.99.673 which fixed the body rows). The `mb-mscol-hdr-*` header tint classes also use `rgba() !important` (at alpha 0.60), which overrides the inline `background` shorthand set by `applyStickyColumn`'s header loop, making the sticky column header see-through on horizontal scroll. Fix: added module-level `_MSCOL_HDR_TINT_RGBA` lookup (alpha 0.60 for each of the 8 hues). In `applyStickyColumn`'s header-row loop, store `dataset.mbStickyBg = headerBg` and apply the same detect-remove-read-restore pattern as the body-row fix: if a hdr-tint class is already active, temporarily remove it, set the true header background, restore the class, compute an opaque blended colour via `_blendSortTint`, apply it with `setProperty('background-color', …, 'important')`, and record `dataset.mbStickyRestBg`. In `applyMultiSortColumnTints`, after adding `hdrCls` to the main header `<th>`, if the cell is `mb-sticky-col`, blend the header tint onto `mbStickyBg` and apply the opaque result the same way. `clearMultiSortColumnTints` already queries `thead tr:first-child th` and restores from `mbStickyRestBg`, so no change there.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed sticky column remaining see-through after sort tints are applied (complete rewrite of v9.99.672 fix). Root cause: `renderFinalTable` calls `applyTints()` on freshly cloned rows before `runFilter()` calls `applyStickyColumn`. When `applyStickyColumn` then reads `getComputedStyle(cell).backgroundColor`, the sort-tint class's `rgba() !important` rule is already winning the cascade — the browser returns the semi-transparent tint colour as the computed background, which `applyStickyColumn` stores as `mbStickyBg`. When the sort handler later calls `applyMultiSortColumnTints()`, it blends the tint onto the already-tinted rgba value, producing a doubly-wrong result, and the sticky cell stays see-through. Additionally, the `mouseleave` handler set `cell.style.background = mbStickyBg` (non-important shorthand), which cleared the cascade-winning `!important` flag previously set by `applyMultiSortColumnTints`, allowing the tint class to win again and make the cell see-through on every hover-out. Fix: (1) Move the tint RGBA lookup table to module scope as `_MSCOL_TINT_RGBA` and add a shared `_blendSortTint(tint, restBg)` helper so both `applyStickyColumn` and `applyMultiSortColumnTints` use the same data. (2) In `applyStickyColumn`'s body-row loop, detect any active tint class, temporarily remove it and any inline `background-color !important`, read the true opaque zebra background via `getComputedStyle`, then restore the tint class; if a tint was present, apply the opaque blended colour via `setProperty` and record `mbStickyRestBg`. (3) In the `mouseleave` handler, when `mbStickyRestBg` is set (tint is active), re-apply the blended colour via `setProperty('background-color', …, 'important')` after setting the background shorthand so the opaque value wins over the tint class. (4) In `mouseenter`, same treatment for the hover colour on tinted sticky cells. (5) `applyMultiSortColumnTints` now uses the shared `_MSCOL_TINT_RGBA` / `_blendSortTint` instead of its former local copies.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed sticky column becoming see-through when sort value-change shading is active. The `mb-mscol-*` tint classes use `background-color: rgba(…) !important`, which overrides the inline opaque `background` applied by `applyStickyColumn`. On a `position:sticky` cell, the browser composites that semi-transparent background against the scrolled content behind the cell (not against the DOM parent), making columns behind the sticky one visible through it. Fix: in `applyMultiSortColumnTints`, when adding a tint class to a `mb-sticky-col` cell, alpha-blend the tint's RGBA values (from a new precomputed `_tintRGBA` lookup table matching the CSS definitions) onto the cell's current opaque rest background, and apply the resulting opaque `rgb()` colour via `cell.style.setProperty('background-color', …, 'important')`. An inline `!important` declaration wins over class `!important` at the same specificity level, ensuring the sticky cell always paints opaquely. The original rest background is preserved in `dataset.mbStickyRestBg`; `dataset.mbStickyBg` is updated to the blended colour so the `mouseleave` handler continues to restore the correct tinted colour on hover-out. `clearMultiSortColumnTints` is extended to remove the inline important `background-color` and restore the original rest background for sticky cells when tints are cleared.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed collapse-toggle extra-space over-estimation in `toggleAutoResizeColumns` PASS 2. The formula `extra = max(0, toggleWidth + 16 − thPaddingRight)` subtracted the `<th>` right padding as the baseline, but since v9.99.668 `columnWidths[colIndex]` is set to `th.offsetWidth` from the live-table nowrap pass — which already includes the actual `<td>` right padding (≈22px), not the `<th>` right padding (≈5px). Subtracting the smaller `thPaddingRight` over-estimated `extra` by roughly `tdPaddingRight − thPaddingRight ≈ 17px`, making columns with collapse-toggle widgets unnecessarily wider. Fix: read `getComputedStyle(cell).paddingRight` from the sampled `<td>` cell (already available in `_colToggleSample`) and use that as the baseline (`tdPaddingRight`) instead.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Sort by column value length: Alt+Click on the ▲ or ▼ sort icon now sorts the column by the visible text length of each cell (ascending or descending) instead of by the text value. This is a single-column sort and clears any active multi-sort chain. The sort-icon tooltips for ▲ and ▼ have been updated to document the Alt+Click modifier alongside the existing Ctrl+Click multi-sort hint. The sort-status display appends '(by length)' when a length-sort is active.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed auto-resize not applying to initially-collapsed sub-tables in multi-table mode. The v9.99.668 live-table measurement reads `th.offsetWidth` directly from the live table, but a table with `style.display = 'none'` returns `offsetWidth = 0` for all cells — giving every column a 20px minimum instead of the true content width. The symptom: after the initial auto-resize, the resize button showed 'Restore' (resize appeared to succeed) but collapsed sub-tables had useless 20px column widths; expanding them produced mis-sized columns, and toggling Restore/Resize while they remained collapsed could not fix them. Fix: in the measurement loop, if `table.style.display === 'none'`, temporarily set it to `''` before adding `mb-measure-nowrap`, read `th.offsetWidth`, then restore `display: none` immediately after removing `mb-measure-nowrap`. Both mutations are synchronous with no `await` between them, so the browser never paints the intermediate visible state. This applies both to the initial `sa_auto_resize_columns` auto-trigger and to subsequent manual Resize button clicks.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed persistent line break before the last word of disambiguation comments in auto-resize mode (Bug 1) — final root cause. The v9.99.667 NBSP-outside-anchor approach correctly eliminated the `overflow-wrap:anywhere` interaction, but the bug persisted because the column minimum-width computed by the old offscreen-div measurement was too narrow. The old PASS 1 applied `getComputedStyle(th).padding` to the measurement div so that `div.offsetWidth = th_pad_left + content + th_pad_right`; it then set `th.style.minWidth` to that value. In the live table, however, `<td>` padding is larger than `<th>` padding, so `td_available_content = th.minWidth - td_pad_left - td_pad_right` was narrower than the measured content width, leaving insufficient room and forcing a wrap. Fix: replace the offscreen-div PASS 1 entirely with a live-table measurement — add class `mb-measure-nowrap` (`white-space:nowrap !important; overflow-wrap:normal !important; word-break:normal !important`) to the table itself so the browser expands every column to its single-line natural width, then read `th.offsetWidth` (border-box, includes actual TD padding from the widest cell in each column). Because `th.offsetWidth` in nowrap mode equals the max border-box width across all cells in the column, the resulting `minWidth` is always sufficient to hold the widest cell without wrapping. All mutations are synchronous (no `await` between `classList.add` and `classList.remove`), so the browser never paints the intermediate full-width state. The unused `colStyleCache` variable (a relic of the offscreen approach) was removed.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed persistent line break before the last word of disambiguation comments in auto-resize mode (Bug 1). Previous fix (v9.99.666) placed U+00A0 (NBSP) inside the anchor's `` to prevent the soft-wrap between anchor text and comment. However, `` carries `overflow-wrap:anywhere`, which Chrome can use to allow a break at any code-point boundary inside the element — including at a NBSP inside `` at a bidi-run boundary. The root fix: move the NBSP outside `` entirely. `normalizeCommentSpans` now REPLACES the whitespace text node between `` and `` with a single U+00A0 text node (or INSERTS one if none exists, covering Variant A). Because this NBSP is a sibling of `` in the `` — not inside any `overflow-wrap:anywhere` element — only the standard Unicode GL rule applies: no break before or after U+00A0. The GL SP-exception ("no break before GL unless preceded by SP") is neutralised by the companion trimEnd on the anchor ``, which removes any trailing U+0020 SPACE so the character directly before the NBSP is always a letter or punctuation. Together these two operations guarantee that anchor text and comment remain on the same line at the auto-resize minimum width.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed column resize minimum creeping upward after each drag (Bug 2). The drag-minimum width (`_minWidth`) was previously recomputed on every `mousedown` from `_hdrFlex.scrollWidth + 8`. After the user dragged a column wider, `_hdrFlex` had stretched to fill the enlarged column, so `scrollWidth` returned the CURRENT (wider) column width instead of the original header-content minimum — making it impossible to drag the column narrower again. The fix moves the computation to `makeColumnsResizable` initialisation time (before any drag has occurred), when the column is still at its natural layout width and `scrollWidth` correctly reflects the intrinsic minimum of the header widget (colName + sort icons + unique-values button + optional extras). The value is cached in `th.dataset.mbResizeMin` so that subsequent `makeColumnsResizable` calls (e.g. the re-call inside `toggleAutoResizeColumns` after auto-resize has already modified column widths, and the re-call after the Restore button removes and re-adds handles) reuse the pre-resize minimum rather than recomputing from a stretched layout.

Fixed line break before the last word of disambiguation comments in auto-resize mode (Bug 1) and residual anchor→comment line break (Bug 3). After v9.99.665 removed the whitespace text node between `` and ``, the visual gap between title and comment was still provided by the trailing `\n ` whitespace at the end of the `` element inside ``. That trailing whitespace collapsed to a regular space, which — being inside the anchor's `` boundary with `overflow-wrap:anywhere` active — was still a soft-wrap opportunity. The browser could break there, pushing the comment to a new line and potentially causing the comment text to wrap internally. The fix: `normalizeCommentSpans` now replaces any trailing whitespace in the last text node of such `` elements with a single U+00A0 (NON-BREAKING SPACE). U+00A0 has Unicode line-break class GL (Glue) — it is prohibited as a break point even under `overflow-wrap:anywhere` — so the anchor text and immediately-following comment are guaranteed to remain on the same line at the auto-resize minimum width. The visual gap is preserved (U+00A0 renders with the same metrics as a regular space). Only `` elements whose next element sibling is `` are affected. The operation is idempotent because ECMAScript `trimEnd()` treats U+00A0 as whitespace and strips it, so a second pass re-applies exactly one U+00A0.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed two remaining soft-wrap break points in `normalizeCommentSpans` that were exposed after the nowrap-style removal in v9.99.664. (1) Trailing whitespace inside `` content: MusicBrainz emits a `\n ` sequence before `` (Variant B), which collapses to a single space in rendering and creates a wrap opportunity at the end of the bdi text — causing the last word of a disambiguation comment (e.g. `reissue)`) to break to a new line in narrower columns. The fix trims trailing whitespace from the last text node inside `` after all other normalization steps. (2) Whitespace between `` and ``: MusicBrainz emits a `\n ` text node as a sibling between the closing `` and the opening `` at the `` level. That text node collapses to a space and, combined with `overflow-wrap:anywhere` on `.wrap-anywhere` anchors, created a break opportunity between the anchor text and the leading `(` of the comment — the "magic minimum column width" that prevented resize below the anchor-plus-first-word width. The fix removes that inter-element whitespace text node from every `` as a second pass in `normalizeCommentSpans`. Both fixes are pure DOM mutations with no style mutations on live elements.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Removed all `white-space: nowrap` style mutations from `normalizeCommentSpans`. Previous versions (introduced progressively in v9.99.639–9.99.651) applied `white-space: nowrap` as inline styles to live DOM elements — `span.comment`, `<bdi>`, and the containing `<td>` or `<li>` — to prevent disambiguation text from breaking away from its anchor. This forced the min-content width of every affected cell to the full single-line text width of the longest comment, making columns such as Release and Label unexpectedly wide in `table-layout:auto` even without auto-resize, and also made it impossible to drag those columns narrower than their longest single-line content (text overflowed instead of wrapping). The function now performs only the interior DOM normalisation it originally set out to do: removing pure-whitespace text nodes around `<bdi>`, consolidating Variant-A `(` / `)` orphans into `<bdi>`, and moving any trailing text node after `</bdi>` into `<bdi>` to eliminate the bidi-boundary soft-wrap point. No style properties are mutated on any live element. The auto-resize measurement sandbox is unaffected (it uses `white-space:nowrap !important` via `.mb-measure-nowrap`). At the auto-resize minimum width the full content fits on one line so the browser inserts no unnecessary breaks; if the user drags a column narrower, the browser's natural line-breaking applies — which is the intended behaviour.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed minimum drag width for the Picard tagger column. The Picard `<th>` is injected by `initPicardTaggerColumn` after `makeTableSortableUnified` runs and therefore carries no `.mb-col-hdr-flex` element. The previous fallback was 30 px, which allowed the column to be dragged to a width where the word "Picard" was completely clipped. The fallback now uses `th.scrollWidth` — the cell's natural content width including its padding — so the column name stays fully visible at minimum width.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Fixed manual column resize breaking all column widths on mousedown. Switching to `table-layout:fixed` without first locking every `<col>` to its current rendered width caused the browser to redistribute all column widths equally, making all columns jump to the same size at the moment of click. The fix snapshots every `th.offsetWidth` before any style mutation, writes those values to all `<col>` elements, clears `th.style.minWidth` (set by auto-resize) so cell constraints cannot override the explicit col widths, and removes the fixed `table.style.width`/`table.style.minWidth` set by auto-resize so the table is free to grow when a column is widened. This eliminates both the sudden jump-on-click and the zero-sum behavior where widening one column compressed all others. The fix applies equally whether auto-resize is active or not.

Replaced the hardcoded 30 px minimum drag width with a per-column header content minimum. At `mousedown`, `hdrFlex.scrollWidth + 8` is measured from the live `.mb-col-hdr-flex` element (colName + ⇅▲▼ sort icons + unique-values widget + optional collapse-toggle + optional CAA/EAA column-header button). The +8 accounts for the 8 px resizer handle. A column can no longer be dragged narrower than its own header requires. For columns without `.mb-col-hdr-flex` (e.g. the Picard tagger column, which is injected after the sort UI is built and carries only plain text), `th.scrollWidth` is used as the floor instead, ensuring the column name remains fully visible.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Reordered cover-art fetch queue so inline thumbnails (entity title column) are enqueued first, small CAA/EAA column icons second, the big-picture hover strip third, and JSON-API enrichment (count badges, multi-row art cells) last. Users who start filtering immediately now see visual feedback sooner because the most visible images load first. Implemented by extracting queue creation from `initCaaPics` into a new `_artInitQueue()` helper; all four render-completion call sites (`runFilter` single-table, `startFetchingProcess` single-table, `renderGroupedTable` tail, `_artRebuildBigPicsForTable` drain) now call `_artInitQueue()` → `initCaaInlinePics()` / `initEaaInlinePics()` → `initCaaPics()` / `initEaaPics()`.

Moved `_artEnrichTable` (JSON-API enrichment) from the first `tables.forEach` pass inside `_artInitPics` to a dedicated second pass that runs after all image-fetch tasks are enqueued. This ensures small icons, inline thumbnails, and the big-picture strip always have priority in `_caaQueue` over count-badge and multi-row-cell population.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On `releasegroup-releases` pages, inline cover art thumbnails in the first (sticky) column were absent after loading data from disk. Root cause: the disk-load path unconditionally set `group.colName = category` (e.g. `"Official release"`) for every multi-table group, but the network fetch path only sets `colName` for `listToTable`/`groupByH3` page types. For standard multi-table pages (`releasegroup-releases` uses the generic `else` fetch branch), `group.colName` is left `undefined`. When `colName` was incorrectly set on disk-load, `renderGroupedTable` patched the first `<th>` of each sub-table from `"Release"` to `"Official release"`, causing `caaFindColumnByName('Release')` to return `-1` and `_artInitInlinePics` to skip all sub-tables. Fixed by guarding the `colName` derivation behind a check for `activeDefinition.features.listToTable || activeDefinition.features.groupByH3`, mirroring the network-path condition exactly.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `applyMultiSortColumnTints` used `cell.textContent.trim()` to compare successive cell values when determining shade-flip boundaries. Cells that embed a `<script type="application/json">` block (e.g. the Country/Date column on release-group pages) produced different `textContent` strings for visually identical values because the embedded JSON uses varying property-key order, causing the shade to flip on every row even when the visible value was unchanged. Fixed by replacing `cell.textContent.trim()` with `getCleanColumnText(cell)`, which already skips `<script>` and `<style>` nodes via its TreeWalker filter.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Prefix-mode `A` (and column-filter `Ctrl+A`) now also finds EAA per-table toggle buttons (`mb-eaa-toggle-btn-N`) in addition to CAA (`mb-caa-toggle-btn-N`). Previously, on pages that show EAA event art (e.g. place/events), pressing `Ctrl+M` then `A` had no effect. Updated `ctrlMFunctionMap['a']` description to 'Toggle Cover Art Images (CAA/EAA)'.
Stop button tooltip now mentions the `Ctrl+M, then O` prefix-mode shortcut.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Global and column filter input tooltips incorrectly mentioned 'Ctrl+M then U' as an alternative for the unicode character map shortcut. The unicode picker (`Ctrl+U`) is handled in the capture phase and is never suppressed, so the tooltip now simply shows the configured `sa_shortcut_unicode_chars` shortcut (default `Ctrl+U`) without a prefix-mode alternative.

Barcode highlight button tooltip no longer shows the direct `Ctrl+B` shortcut when `sa_enable_direct_ctrl_char_shortcuts` is off. It now uses the new `buildShortcutHint` helper (same as other action buttons).

Added `buildShortcutHint(settingKey, fallback, prefixKey)` utility: always emits the prefix-mode form (`Ctrl+M, then X`); appends the direct shortcut (`or Ctrl+X`) only when `sa_enable_direct_ctrl_char_shortcuts` is on, or when the shortcut key is not a `Ctrl+<a–z>` letter (e.g. `Ctrl+,`) and is therefore never suppressed.

All action-button tooltips (Save, Load, Resize/Restore, Visible, Density, Statistics, Export, Keyboard Shortcuts, Settings) now use `buildShortcutHint` so the direct `Ctrl+X` shortcut is shown only when enabled. `Ctrl+,` (Settings) is always shown because it is not a letter shortcut. App Help shows prefix-mode only (no direct `Ctrl+H` shortcut exists).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Prefix-mode tooltip (`showCtrlMTooltip`): split the Functions list into a regular section and a 'Col-filter context' section for `o`/`q`/`a`. The column-context section is shown in green when a column filter is currently focused and grey with a '⚠ focus col filter first' warning otherwise. Added `colContext: true` flag to the `o`/`q`/`a` entries in `ctrlMFunctionMap` to enable this split.

Moved 'b — Toggle Barcode Highlighting' to appear immediately after 'v — Open Visible Columns Menu' in the prefix-mode function map (and therefore in the tooltip), matching the visual order in the controls bar.
Barcode highlight button tooltip now includes the prefix shortcut (`Ctrl+M` then `B`) and the configured direct shortcut (`Ctrl+B`) in both active and inactive states.

Global filter input tooltip now honours `sa_enable_direct_ctrl_char_shortcuts`: when the setting is off, shows the prefix-mode alternative (`Ctrl+M` then `G`) and mentions that the direct `Ctrl+G` can be re-enabled in Settings.
Column filter input tooltip similarly honours `sa_enable_direct_ctrl_char_shortcuts`: shows `Ctrl+M` then `C` prefix-mode hint when direct shortcuts are off.
Sort-icon tooltips for ⇅, ▲, ▼ now mention the keyboard shortcuts `Ctrl+#`, `Ctrl+↑`, `Ctrl+↓` (column filter focused) using `getShortcutDisplay` so they reflect any user-configured bindings.
Unique-values (📊) wrapper tooltip now mentions `Ctrl+M` then `Q` and, when direct shortcuts are enabled, also `Ctrl+Q` (col filter focused).

Multi-row collapse header button (▤) tooltip now mentions `Ctrl+M` then `O` and, when direct shortcuts are enabled, also `Ctrl+O` (col filter focused); hint is kept in sync on both creation and toggle.
Per-table CAA toggle button tooltip now mentions `Ctrl+M` then `A` (col filter focused) and, when direct shortcuts are enabled, also `Ctrl+A`; hint is kept in sync on both creation and click-toggle.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Extended `sa_enable_direct_ctrl_char_shortcuts=false` (the default) to suppress ALL `Ctrl+<a–z>` shortcuts everywhere — not just while an input field has focus or a UI dialog is open. `Ctrl+2` and `Ctrl+3` (number keys, not letters) are never affected. When a column filter is focused, `Ctrl+↑`, `Ctrl+↓`, and `Ctrl+#` are also never affected.

The configured `sa_keyboard_shortcut_prefix` (default `Ctrl+M`) is handled in the capture phase with `stopImmediatePropagation` and therefore always works — it is never suppressed regardless of the `sa_enable_direct_ctrl_char_shortcuts` setting.

Added permanent `ctrlMFunctionMap` entries for `o` (Toggle Multi-Row Cell Collapse), `q` (Show Unique Values Dropdown), and `a` (Toggle CAA Cover Art Images) — available via prefix mode (`Ctrl+M` → `o`/`q`/`a`). These operate on the last focused column filter (tracked via a `focusin` listener on `.mb-col-filter-input`). The `o` entry is temporarily overwritten by 'Stop fetching' during an active fetch and restored afterwards.

Updated the Keyboard Shortcuts help dialog and the bottom note to reflect the new global suppression behaviour, removed 'blocked while typing' wording, and added prefix-mode entries for `O`, `Q`, `A`.
Updated debug log strings in prefix-mode entry to list `o`/`q`/`a` function shortcuts with their current descriptions.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: `applyRenderMultiRowCells` did not split the 'Relationship types' column on instrument-* pages (instrument-releases, instrument-artists, instrument-recordings). Root cause: the splitting loop only recognised standalone comma text nodes (`/^\s*,\s*$/`) as separators — correct for element-separated columns like Catalog# whose HTML has `…,…` — but MusicBrainz renders Relationship types as a single plain text node (`instrument (as "lead guitar"), instrument (as "rhythm guitar")`), so no standalone comma node exists. Fixed by replacing the simple `if`/`else` check with a depth-aware top-level-comma finder: for every text node the loop now finds all comma positions at parenthesis depth 0 and splits there, creating one synthetic text node per part. Commas inside parentheses (e.g. `vocal (as "soprano, alto")`) are left intact.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Adjust 'Auto-resize columns threshold' to 10000 now that we have a much faster implementation.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Auto-resize: collapse-toggle reservation increased — the offset constant in `extra = max(0, toggleWidth + offset − thPaddingRight)` was raised from 4px (the toggle's CSS `right` value) to 16px (+12px safety buffer). v9.99.651's 4px offset left ≈1–3px of visual overlap with the closing character of long disambiguation comments; the larger offset ensures a ≥12px gap between the text right edge and the toggle left edge even with sub-pixel font rendering differences between the measurement context and the live page.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Auto-resize: collapse-toggle overlap in collapsable columns — corrected formula and added fix to sub-table resize path. v9.99.650 computed `extra = toggleWidth + 4 − cellPaddingRight` (subtracting the td's 22px), but the measurement `_div` uses the `<th>` padding, so the correct baseline is `extra = toggleWidth + 4 − thPaddingRight`. With a typical th right-padding of ~5px this raises the extra from 12px to ~29px, providing a 20px safety margin between text and toggle. The same fix is now also applied in `toggleSubTableAutoResize` (per-sub-table ↔ button on multi-table pages), which previously had no toggle compensation at all.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Three regressions from v9.99.648's DOM-wrapping approach: (1) double '▶' button — `normalizeCommentSpans` wrapped `<a>+<span.comment>` in `mb-nowrap-pair` before ERG injection ran; ERG then found the `<a>` inside the wrapper and prepended another `▶` inside it, producing two buttons; (2) `<a>+<span.comment>` pairs inside `<ul><li>` were not wrapped because Part A only walked direct `<td>` children; (3) `mb-nowrap-pair` wrapper boundaries between multiple pairs in the same cell were still wrap points. Replaced DOM-wrapping entirely with a container `white-space: nowrap` approach: Part A normalises `span.comment` interiors (same as before); Part B sets `white-space: nowrap` on each `<td>` that directly contains a `span.comment` child, and on each `<li>` that directly contains a `span.comment` child. This is safe because the measurement sandbox already uses `white-space: nowrap !important` — `th.style.minWidth` is already the full single-line width — so setting nowrap on the live container makes it match the measurement exactly, with no min-content change or re-layout.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Comment-span wrap still occurring after v9.99.647 in two new ways: (1) wrap between `` and `` — the `\n ` text node between them was not being removed reliably (Step 1's guard was too strict), causing the entire comment block to drop to a new row after the title anchor; (2) cells with multiple `+` pairs separated by `,` text nodes (e.g. Label column with CBS, Columbia, Legacy, Sony Music) — Step 1 never fires for those pairs because the preceding sibling of each `` is the `,\n ` text node (not pure-whitespace), leaving every comment wrappable. Rewrote `normalizeCommentSpans` with a new Part A: walks each ``'s direct children and wraps each `` + its immediately-following `` (plus any pure-whitespace text nodes between them) in a ``. This robustly prevents the break between any anchor and its comment, handles multiple pairs per cell, and is idempotent (guards on the `mb-nowrap-pair` class). Part B (interior normalisation of `span.comment`) is retained: removes whitespace-only child text nodes, consolidates Variant-A `(` / `)` into ``, and applies `white-space:nowrap` to `span.comment` and ``.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
